Though hundreds of thousands of rites be performed, no dam at all is set (against craving). Servant Nanak has taken the Naam as (his) support and left every other pursuit. ॥4॥
396.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I have searched through every pleasure: none is as great as the Lord; that True Master is found when the Guru is pleased. To my own Guru I am devoted, forever and ever a sacrifice; (O Guru,) bless (me) with this gift: may I not forget the Naam for a single instant, the least moment. He alone is truly rich within whom is the wealth of the Lord; he is freed from the great net, within whom the Guru's Shabad abides unbroken. What can I say of the Guru's greatness? The Guru is a lake of discernment and truth. He is the perfect Supreme God, from the beginning, from the dawn of the ages, through every age. Meditate on the Naam forever and ever, the mind dyed in the love of the Lord, Har Har. To me the Guru is soul, breath and wealth, and he is with Nanak. ॥4॥
397.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). When the Master, unseen and infinite, dwells in the mind even for a moment, my pain, my suffering and my sickness all flee, O mother. I give myself up in sacrifice to my own Master; repeating (his Name), great bliss fills mind and body. When I hear even a little talk of that True Master, I find the peace beyond all peace, O mother, whose worth I cannot reckon. He is lovely to the eyes; seeing him, I have fallen in love (with him). I am without virtue, O my mother, yet he himself has tied me to the hem of his garment. He is beyond the Vedas, the Kateb and the world, beyond them all; (yet) Nanak's King is seen, plainly manifest. ॥4॥
397.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O God,) hundreds of thousands of devotees worship (you), repeating Beloved, Beloved; by what means am I, a soul without virtue and given to vice, to meet (you)? You are (my) support, O Govind, O Gopal, O merciful God; you are the Lord of all; all creation is yours. (You are) the Sants' helper always; they see you ever present; those bereft of the Naam die grieving and grieving. Those who live as servants of (your) servants have had their wandering (through births) ended; those who have forgotten the Naam: what can be said of their plight? Like a beast that strays into green crops is the whole world; says Nanak: O God, cut (my) bonds and unite (me with you) yourself. ॥4॥
397.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Put all things out of mind and keep the One alone in your thought; cast off false pride, and lay mind and body before (him) as an offering. Praising you at all hours, O Creator, I live; (grant me) this gift of yours, be merciful to me. Do only that work by which the face is made bright; he alone is joined to the True One, O Allah, to whom you give (this gift). Set in order that house which will never fall at all; enshrine the One in your mind, who never dies. Those who have found favour with God hold the Lord dear; by the Guru's grace Nanak has spoken of the One who is beyond telling. ॥4॥
397.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Those who never forget the Naam: what are they like? Know no difference at all: they are like the Master himself. Meeting with you, (O Lord,) mind and body are filled with delight; by the grace of (your) servant, peace is found and all pain is wiped away. All the continents and worlds there are, they have carried across, those in whose minds (God) himself has come to dwell; they are the perfect devotees. The one whom (God) himself honours is the one honoured (by all); such a one is renowned and accepted, known in every place. That (Nanak) may worship (you) day and night and hold (you) dear with every breath: fulfil this longing of Nanak, O True King. ॥4॥
398.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). He, our Lord and Master, pervades every place; there is one Master, the royal canopy over his head; there is no other. As it pleases you, keep (me), O Protector; apart from you, my eyes have beheld no other. God himself cherishes (all); in every heart he takes care (of each); the one in whose mind he himself has come to dwell, he never forgets. Whatever he does, he does himself, by his own will; in every age he has been known as the helper of his devotees. Repeating the Name of the Lord over and over, one never grieves; Nanak thirsts for the sight of you: fulfil (his) longing. ॥4॥
398.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Why do you sleep, having forgotten the Naam, O heedless, careless one? How many are being swept away in this river! O mind, the Lord's feet are a (good) ship; boarding it, one crosses over, singing (his) virtues at all hours in the company of the Saadh. (People) enjoy countless pleasures, (but) without the Name they are empty; without devotion to the Lord, they die again and again, and weep. Fine clothes, pleasures, perfumes, the body rubbed with scented pastes: (yet) without Simran the body is dust, and it must surely depart. Rare is the one who has seen how very treacherous the world is; release lies in the Lord's refuge: O Nanak, this is the writ that is written. ॥4॥
398.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). No one goes along with anyone; why then be proud? With the one Naam for support, the terrifying world-ocean is crossed. For me, the poor one, you are the true support, O my Perfect True Guru; beholding the sight of you, my mind takes heart. Power and wealth are entanglements: count them as of no use in any task; the Lord's Kirtan is the (true) support; this wealth never moves. All the pleasures of Maya are but shadows; the Naam, the treasure of peace, is sung through the Guru. You are true, a treasure of virtues, O God, deep and unfathomable; in Nanak's heart is hope and trust in the Master (alone). ॥4॥
398.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The One in whose remembrance pain departs and the peace of Sahaj is found: on him, the Lord, Har Har, let us meditate night and day with palms joined. Nanak's God is he to whom everyone belongs; he fills all; he alone is True, ever True. Within and without he is with (us), our helper, the One worth knowing; worship him, O mind, and every sickness is destroyed. The infinite Protector keeps (us) safe (even) in the fire (of the womb); cooling is the Name of the Lord, Har Har; remembering it, the burning goes. Peace, Sahaj and bliss abound, O Nanak, (for one who becomes) the dust (of the feet) of the Lord's servants; meeting the Perfect Guru, all (his) tasks have been fulfilled. ॥4॥
399.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Gobind, the treasure of virtues, is known through the Guru; when he is kind and merciful, the Lord's love is enjoyed. Come, Sants, let us meet and tell the story of the Lord; night and day let us remember the Naam, casting off the shame of what people say. Repeating the Naam over and over I live, and great bliss arises; attachment is vain; the world is false and bound to perish. Only a rare one has formed a love for (God's) lotus feet; blessed and beautiful is the face of the one who has meditated on the Lord. In remembering (him), the pain of birth and death and (the dread of) Death are wiped away; for Nanak, peace is whatever pleases God. ॥4॥
399.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Come, friends, let us gather together and enjoy every flavour and relish: let us repeat the Amrit Name of the Lord, Har Har, and together cast off (our) sins. Reflect on the essence, O Sants; then no obstacle stands in the way: all the thieves (the vices) are worn down, for through the Guru one stays awake. Take a humble mind as provisions for the road; burn up the poison of Haumai; true is the shop, full the bargain: trade in the goods of the Naam. Those who have offered up soul, body and wealth are the ones with honour; pleasing to their own God, they delight (in him) always. Those who drink the wine of evil counsel turn debauched and crazed; (but) those dyed in the elixir of the Lord (Ram), O Nanak, are addicted to the True One. ॥4॥
Bikhli pati (Sanskrit vrishali-pati): the husband or keeper of a dissolute woman, a byword for a debauched man. Amali: one addicted to a drug, who cannot do without it.
399.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). As (the Guru) moved me, I made the effort and set about (the work of the Name); I repeat the Naam and live by repeating it; the Guru has fixed the mantra firm (within me). Let us fall at the True Guru's feet, who has shattered doubt; God in his mercy has set the True (Name within us) and made (our life) beautiful. The True One, the Lord of the Will, has taken (us) by the hand and made (us) his own by his Hukam; the gift God has given is complete glory. Ever and ever (his) praises are sung, repeating the Name of Murari (the Lord); God has shown his grace, and the True Guru has seen (my) vow through. The Perfect Guru has given (me) the Naam for wealth, and singing (his) praises for gain; the Sants are the traders (in the Name), O Nanak; the Banker is God, who is without limit. ॥4॥
399.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O God, the one whose Master you yourself are is greatly blessed; he lives at ease, ever at peace; all his doubt and fear have fled. We are servants of Gobind; my Master is mighty. He who does and causes all to be done, in every way, is our True Guru. There is no other, no second, whom one should fear; through the Guru's service the (Lord's) mansion is reached, and the world, so hard to cross, is crossed. (O God,) by your glance (of grace) peace is found, and the treasure (of the Name dwells) in the mind; those servants on whom you have had mercy are accepted (at your door). The Lord's Kirtan is the taste of Amrit; only a rare one drinks it; (the one who) receives the one Naam as (his) wage, O Nanak, lives by repeating it over and over in the heart. ॥4॥
400.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The God whose humble handmaid I am is higher than all; everything, little or much, is called his. My soul, my breath of life and my wealth I hold to be the Master's; through whose Name I am made radiant, his handmaid I count myself. (O Lord,) you need no one, you are all bliss; (your) Name is a jewel, a diamond; she whose King you are is sated and content, ever at peace. O companions and friends at my side, I press good counsel upon you: serve the Saadh (the Guru) with love; so it is that I find the Lord, the treasure. All (souls) are handmaids of the Master, all call (him) mine; (but) she whom (he himself) adorns, O Nanak, makes her dwelling in peace. ॥4॥
400.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Become the humble handmaid of the Sants, O friend; learn this conduct; of all virtues, this virtue is highest: do not see the Husband (Lord) as far away. Dye this mind of yours, O lovely one, in the Lord's Name, in the fast colour of madder; giving up cleverness and cunning, know Gopal (the Lord) to be with you. Whatever the Husband says should be accepted: make this your adornment, O friend; the love of another should be forgotten: chew this betel. Make the Guru's Shabad your lamp, and spread this bed of pure conduct; stay with palms joined at all hours; then the Lord King meets (you). Hers alone is good conduct, hers all adornment; she alone is beautiful, (absorbed) in the Infinite; she alone is the happy wife, O Nanak, who has pleased the Creator. ॥4॥
Betel (pan) was chewed by a bride to redden her lips, a part of her adornment for her husband. Madder (majith): a red dye from the root of a plant, a colour that never fades.
400.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Stumbling and wavering last only as long as the mind wanders in doubt; my own Guru cut away (my) doubts, and (I) found rest. Those quarrelsome foes (lust and the rest) have all, through the Guru, given up; now we are free of them, and they have let go of us. Thinking in terms of mine and yours, one is bound from that very moment; when the Guru cut away ignorance, the nooses fell loose. As long as one does not grasp the Hukam, so long is one in misery; meeting the Guru, (one) has recognised the Hukam, and from then on is at peace. (Now) no one is an enemy or a foe, no one is bad; the servant who serves the Guru, O Nanak, is the Master's own bondsman. ॥4॥
400.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Peace, Sahaj and great bliss are (mine) as I sing the Lord's Kirtan; giving (me) his own Name, the True Guru has warded off the (ill-boding) planets. To my Guru I am a sacrifice; ever and ever I offer myself to him; I give myself up for the Guru, meeting whom the True (Name) has become (my life's) aim. Good and bad omens touch the one in whose mind (the Lord) does not dwell; Jam does not come near the one who is pleasing to the Lord God. Of all the merit, charity, recitation and austerity there is, the Naam stands above all; whoever repeats (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, with the tongue has his purpose fulfilled. (Their) fears are destroyed, doubt and attachment gone; no other (than God) is seen; O Nanak, those whom the Supreme Lord has kept safe have known no sorrow again. ॥4॥
Garah: the nine planets of astrology, held to bring misfortune; sagun and apsagun: good and bad omens, signs read for good or ill luck.
401.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 9, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. I long to remember (him) and so gain every comfort; (yet who knows) whether in his presence I shall please (him) or not? There is one Giver, and all are beggars: to whom else should I go? To beg of any other puts me to shame; the one Master is sovereign over all: whom could I set beside him as (his) equal? I rise, I sit down, yet I cannot stay (without him); I search and search for the sight of him. Brahma and those like him, Sanak and his brothers, Sanak, Sanandan, Sanatan and Sanat Kumar: even for them (the Lord's) mansion is hard to reach. He is beyond reach, beyond all reach, fathomless; he cannot be grasped, nor his worth set: I cannot find it. I have sought the refuge of the True Being, and I meditate on the True Guru, the great Being. God the Master has become kind and merciful, and has cut the bond from (my) neck; says Nanak, since I found the Saadh Sangat, I shall not come into birth again. ॥4॥
Sanak and his brothers: Sanak, Sanandan, Sanatan and Sanat Kumar, in the Puranas the four sons of Brahma, sages held to remain children for ever.
401.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I sing (of him) within, I sing (of him) without, I sing awake and asleep; (the Guru) has given (me) provisions to take along (on the road); (I am) a trader in the Name of Gobind. All else I have forgotten, forgotten; the Perfect Guru granted (me) the Naam as a gift; this is all I rest on. I sing in sorrow, and I sing in joy too; walking on the road, on the way, I keep (him) in my heart; the Guru has planted the Naam firm in my mind, (and) quenched my thirst. I sing by day, I sing by night, I sing with every breath, with my tongue; in the Sat Sangat the faith takes root that the Lord is (our) companion in life and in death. Grant servant Nanak this gift, O God, that I may gain the dust (of the feet) of the Sants and keep it in my heart; that with my ears (I may hear your) praise, with my eyes behold (your) sight, (and rest my) forehead at the Guru's feet. ॥4॥
401.3: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Asa, Ghar 10, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O mind,) those you take to be lasting are guests of two days: sons, wife, house, all your goods; all love for them is false. O mind, why do you cry, Aha, aha? Look closely: (all this) is like the city of Harichand; earn the one profit, the worship of the Lord (Ram). As clothes worn on the body crumble in two or four days, (and) how far can one run along a wall? At last its end must come. As when a tank of water is set up, and salt dissolves the moment it falls in, (so,) when the order of the Supreme Lord comes, (the soul) will rise and go in an instant. O mind, by count you walk, by count you sit, by count you draw breath; ever sing the praise of the Lord, O Nanak: those who hold to the shelter of the True Guru's feet are saved. ॥4॥
The city of Harichand (Harichandauri): a city seen in the sky, a mirage that vanishes as one draws near.
402.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). What was crooked has come straight; wicked enemies have turned into friends; in the darkness a jewel has shone out; the soiled intellect has become clean. When Gobind's grace came (upon me), I found peace, riches and the fruit of the Lord's Name, meeting the True Guru. No one knew me, worthless as I was; (now I) am known in all the worlds; (once) I could find no seat beside anyone; now all serve (my) feet. (I) roamed in search of every half-penny; (now) all the craving of my mind is quenched; (once I) could not bear a single word (from anyone); (now) in the Saadh Sangat (my mind) is cooled. Which of (his) virtues can one tongue tell? (He is) beyond reach, beyond reach, beyond all reach. Make (me) the slave of the slaves of (your) slaves; servant Nanak is in your refuge, O Lord. ॥4॥
402.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O fool, you are slow, so slow, to profit, but quick to run after loss; you will not buy the cheap goods; O sinner, you are bound by debt. O True Guru, (my) hope is in you; your Name, O Supreme Lord, makes the fallen pure; this alone is my shelter. You hear foul talk and are caught up in it, (but) are idle in taking the Name; you are eager for thoughts of slander; (your) understanding is upside down. Others' wealth, others' bodies, slander of others: (like one) gone mad, you eat what should not be eaten; you take no liking to the true Dharma; hearing the truth, you are stung to anger. O God, merciful to the poor, kind Master, Lord: your devotees lean on (your) Name; Nanak has come longing to your refuge, O God: make (him) your own and keep (his) honour. ॥4॥
402.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (People) cling to false companions, bound by attachment to Maya; where (they) must go does not come to mind; they have gone blind with ego. O mind, why do you not, detached (from Maya), worship (the Lord)? You dwell in a chamber of unbaked clay (the body), with all the maladies of the vices around you. Crying, Mine, mine, day and night go by, and moment by moment life wastes away; as (a fly) is lured by the taste of sweetness, (so man is caught) in false affairs and in filth. Lust, anger, greed and attachment: in these, in the pleasures of the senses, (man) is entangled; (so) the Being, the Creator, has set (him) on the round (of births); again and again he is born. When (God), destroyer of the pains of the poor, became merciful, then meeting the Guru (I) found every comfort; says Nanak, I meditate (on him) day and night; (he) has slain and driven out all (my) vices. In this way, brother, I have meditated on the Being, the Creator: the destroyer of the pains of the poor became merciful, (and) the pains of birth and death have gone. ॥4॥
403.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O blind one,) for a moment's taste of lust you suffer pain for millions of days; for a ghari or a muhurat you revel in pleasures, then you regret it over and over. O blind one, remember the Lord King, Har Har: that day of yours has drawn near. Seeing it for a blink of the eye, you are fooled by the bitter gourd, bitter as swallow-wort and neem; as is keeping company with a snake, O man, so is this (going to) another's house (another's wife). For the sake of the enemy (Maya) you commit sins, and the real thing lies untouched, set aside; those who will leave you, with them you keep company, and with the Friend (the Lord) you are at enmity. Thus is the whole world held fast; only the one who has the Perfect Guru (for his keeper) comes through; says Nanak, (he) has crossed the world-ocean, (and his) body has become pure. ॥4॥
A muhurat is two gharis. The colocynth (tumma) is a fruit fair to look at but very bitter; swallow-wort (akk) and neem are bywords for bitterness.
403.2: Raag Asa, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O God,) what is done in secret, that very thing you have seen; yet the foolish and the senseless deny it. For their own deeds they are seized and bound, and then, too late, they repent. My God knows all (your) ways beforehand. O you, robbed by delusion, you keep a veil (before God), and behind it you do as your own heart pleases. To whatever (God) sets them, to that they are set; what can any mortal do (of himself)? Forgive (us), O Supreme Lord and Master; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to you). ॥2॥
403.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (God) himself keeps (the honour) of his servant; he himself has him repeat the Naam. Wherever his servant has some work or task, there he rises and hastens. To his servant he shows (himself) close at hand. Whatever the servant says before his Master comes about at once. To that servant who pleases his God I am devoted. Hearing of his good name, the mind turns green again; Nanak comes to touch his feet. ॥2॥
403.4: Raag Asa, Ghar 11, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The actor puts on many kinds of guise, (yet) as he is, so he remains, O brother. (So the soul,) lost in delusion, has roamed through many births, yet gains no entry into peace, O brother. O Sants, my companions and my friends, apart from the Lord, Har Har, (all) is passing, O brother. (Whoever) has joined the Saadh Sangat and sung the Lord's praises has won this precious thing, this human birth, O brother. Maya of the three qualities is of God's own making; tell me, how is it to be crossed, O brother? (It is full of) whirlpools, fathomless and hard; through the Guru's Shabad one reaches the far shore, O brother. Seeking and seeking, having sought and reflected, Nanak has come to know this essence, O brother: remembering the Naam, the priceless treasure, the mind becomes a jewel and is won over (to it), O brother. ॥3॥
404.1: Raag Asa, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). By the Guru's grace (the Lord) has come to dwell in my mind; whatever I ask for, that I receive, O brother. In the love of the Naam this mind is sated; I run off nowhere any more, O brother. My Master is higher than all; night and day I sing of him, O brother. In an instant he sets up and pulls down; it is of him I would have you stand in awe, O brother. When I behold God, my own Master, I give no place in my mind to any other, O brother. God himself has robed servant Nanak in honour; erasing doubt and fear, I engrave (his Name alone in my mind), O brother. ॥2॥
404.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (Lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride, the five,) crush the four castes, all four; the six orders (of ascetics) lie in the palm of (their) hand, O brother. the handsome, the graceful, the fair of form and the wise, the five have charmed and deceived them all, O brother. Who is so strong that, joining (the Guru), he has slain the five warriors, O brother? One who has slain the five, torn them apart and finished them, he is perfect in this Kalyug, O brother. Theirs is a great clan; they are not brought under control, nor do they flee; their army is strong and stubborn, O brother. Says Nanak, that person has trampled them down (who lives) under the shelter of the Saadh Sangat, O brother. ॥2॥
404.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The telling of the Lord is the good and sublime thing for the soul; all other tastes are flat (beside it), O brother. (It is) rich in virtues and sweet of strain; to the sages who know the six (Shastras) nothing else is worthy, O brother. (It is) the foe of the poison (of the passions), unlike any other, boundless, the bringer of Sahaj; O Nanak, (it) is drunk in the Saadh Sangat, O brother. ॥2॥
404.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (This telling of the Lord) is dear to me, a stream of Amrit; the Guru has not let it slip from (my) mind for an instant, O brother. (Through it come) the sight (of the Creator), the touch (of his feet), sweetness and delight; (it is) dyed in the Creator's love, O brother. Uttered for an instant, (it) brings one to the Guru; uttered with every breath, (it keeps) Jam away; O Nanak, (it makes) the Lord a necklace for the throat and the heart, O brother. ॥2॥
404.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Good indeed is the Saadh Sangat. (There,) every watch, every hour, every moment, singing on and on, Govind, Govind is spoken of. Walking, sitting, sleeping, the Lord's praise (goes on), and in mind and body (God's) feet are held close. (O God,) I am of little weight, you, the Master, are of great weight; Nanak has recognised (your) refuge. ॥3॥
405.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 12, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Leave all your cleverness and worship the Supreme Lord, the Formless One. Apart from the one True Name, all looks like ashes. That God is to be known as ever at one's side. By the Guru's grace (this) is understood, in the love of the one Lord. The one all-powerful (Lord) alone gives refuge; there is no other place. Sing the Lord's praises always, (and so) the great and fearsome world-ocean is crossed. (Thus) birth and death are ended, and there is no suffering in the city of Jam. That one alone gains the treasure of the Naam to whom God (himself) is gracious. The One is the prop, the One alone the support, the One the strength in the mind. O Nanak, joining the Saadh Sangat, let us repeat (his Name); there is none other but the Lord. ॥4॥
405.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Soul, mind, body and breath, and every pleasure enjoyed, are God's gifts. (He is) kin to the lowly, the Giver of life, able to protect those who come to his refuge. Meditate, O my mind, on the Name of the Lord, Har Har. (He is your) help here and hereafter, ever at (your) side; fix your loving attention on the One. To cross the world (-ocean), people ponder the Vedas and the Shastras; (they perform) rites, religious duties and many ceremonies; (but) the practice of the Naam is above them all. Lust, anger and pride perish (in one who) meets the divine True Guru. Make the Naam firm (within), worship the Lord in devotion; good is the service of God. (I have come to) the refuge of your feet, O Merciful One; you are the honour of the one without honour. Soul and breath lean on you alone; God is Nanak's strength. ॥4॥
405.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Wavering again and again, (the mind) has suffered great pain without the company of the Saadh (the Guru). (Now) earn this profit: the sweet essence of Gobind, the Lord, and the love of the one Supreme Lord. The Lord's Name should be repeated every day. With every breath meditate on that God, and give up all other love. That God is the Cause of creation, all-powerful, and himself the Giver of life. Leave all your cleverness and repeat (the Name of) God at all hours. He is friend, comrade, helper and companion, lofty, beyond reach, without end. Keep (his) lotus feet dwelling in the heart; (he) is the mainstay of the soul. Show mercy, O God, Supreme Lord, that (I) may sing your virtues and your praise. (In this) is every comfort and great glory; Nanak lives by repeating (your) Name. ॥4॥
405.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Let me strive; make me strive, O Master, beholding (you) in the company of the Saadh (the Guru). Put on (me) the dye of the Name of the Lord, Har Har; O God, dye (me) yourself (in your love). May I keep repeating the Name of Ram in my mind. Show mercy and dwell in my heart; be (my) helper yourself. Hearing your Name again and again, O beloved God, I long to see (you); be kind to this worm of yours; this alone is (my) wish, this (my) aim. Body and wealth are yours, and you are my God; nothing lies in our power. However you keep (us), so must (we) live; (we) eat what you give. Bathing in the dust (of the feet) of the Lord's servants cuts away the sins of birth after birth. Through loving devotion doubt and fear are destroyed; O Nanak, the Lord is ever present (before one). ॥4॥
406.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O God,) the sight of you is beyond reach, beyond the senses; he alone gains it on whose forehead such fortune (is written). (On whom) the merciful God himself has shown mercy, the True Guru has bestowed the Lord's Name (on him). O divine Guru, (you) have saved (the souls of) Kalyug (too); those who were filthy, foolish and witless have all taken to your service. (O God,) you yourself are the Creator, upholding all creation, pervading all. Dharam Raj is struck with wonder, for all (creation) has come and fallen at (your) feet. Satjug, Treta and Duapar are spoken of (as the good ages), (yet) of the ages Kalyug is the best: (in it) the hand that does (the deed) is the hand that reaps (its fruit); no one is seized in another's place. O dear Lord, you do just what your devotees ask of you; this is your age-old way. With palms joined Nanak begs (this) gift: O Lord, grant (me) the sight of your own Sants. ॥4॥

By an old belief (the Faridkot Teeka), in the earlier ages one person's sin brought punishment on his family, town or land as well; the line says that in Kalyug each reaps the fruit of his own deeds alone.
406.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 13, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Your words, O True Guru, have carried (even) those without virtue across. The most quarrelsome, the wicked and the foul-mouthed have become pure in (your) company. Those who wandered from birth to birth and fell into hell, (you) have saved their families too. Those whom no one knew and no one honoured stand out plainly at the Lord's door. What likeness can I give (you), what praise? Nanak is a sacrifice (to you) every moment. ॥4॥
406.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The crazed (people) lie sleeping (the sleep of attachment). Drunk on attachment to family and the pleasures of the senses, they keep their grip on what is false. False longings, joys and delights as in a dream, (these) in mind and with the mouth they call true. The Amrit Naam, that precious thing, is right beside them, yet they grasp not a sesame-seed of its secret. O Nanak, those whom (God) in his mercy has kept in the Sat Sangat have come to (his) refuge. ॥4॥
406.4: Raag Asa, Tipade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (I long for) that love of the Beloved alone. Gold, gems, great pearls and rubies: no, no, (these I) do not (want). Not kingdom, not fortune, not command, not tasty fare; nothing, nothing at all do I want. In the refuge of the Sants' feet and in bowing to them I find peace upon peace; Nanak's burning is taken away, now that the Beloved's love is found. ॥3॥
407.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Guru has shown (God) to (these) eyes of mine. Here and hereafter, in every body, in every heart, it is you, you alone, O Enchanter (Mohan). You alone, O Beautiful One, are the Maker of the cause (of all), the One alone who holds up the earth. Nanak touches (the feet of) the Sants, is a sacrifice to the sight of them, and rests in peace upon peace. ॥3॥
407.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is beyond price; (one who has it) lives at ease in Sahaj. (God) is the helper at one's side, who never goes away; he is beyond grasp and beyond weighing. My beloved, my brother, my father, my mother (is he); (he is) the shelter of his devotees. The Unseen has been made known, found through the Guru; O Nanak, this is the Lord's own marvel. ॥3॥
407.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Keep (me) true to your devotion to the end; O Master, full of longing, I have come (to your door). (Grant) the Naam, that precious thing, (so that my life) bears fruit; set (your) feet to dwell in (my) heart. This is (my) liberation, this (my) way: keep (me) in the company of the Sants. Plunging deep into the Lord's virtues, may Nanak meditate on the Naam and stay merged in Sahaj. ॥3॥
407.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Lovely are the feet of the Master; the Lord's Sants have attained them. (They) have shed their self-regard, done (his) service, and sung (his) praises, relishing them again and again. (Their) hope is in the One alone, (their) thirst is for the sight (of him); nothing else pleases (them). (This) is your mercy, (O God); what (power) have poor creatures? Nanak gives himself in sacrifice again and again. ॥3॥
407.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Remember the One within your mind. Meditate on the Naam, keep it dwelling in your heart; apart from him there is none. Coming to God's refuge, one gains every reward, and all sorrows depart. O Nanak, the Giver to all beings, the Creator, the all-pervading Being, is in every heart. ॥3॥
407.6: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Whoever forgets the Lord is dead (in spirit). Whoever meditates on the Naam obtains every reward; that person has found peace. (Whoever) calls himself a king and does deeds of ego is held fast in delusion, like a parrot on the nalini. Says Nanak, the one who has met the True Guru has become steadfast. ॥3॥

The nalini is a parrot trap: a reed that turns on a rod set over a bowl of water, with grain on it. When the parrot perches, the reed turns over; seeing the water below, the frightened bird clings to it and so is caught by its own hold.
407.7: Raag Asa, Ghar 14, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. That love is ever new which stays fixed on one's own Beloved. Whoever is pleasing to God does not come into birth (again); he stays absorbed in loving devotion to the Lord, in the Lord's love. God is met when this mind is given (to him); be merciful, (O God,) that Nanak may receive the Naam. ॥2॥
408.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Meet (me), beloved Lord (Ram): without you no one can give (my mind) comfort. (People) have performed many rites of the Simritis and Shastras, (but) without the sight of you, God, there is no peace. (They) have grown weary of keeping fasts, vows and disciplines; O Nanak, in the refuge of the Saadh (the Guru), (one) dwells with God. ॥2॥
408.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 15, Partal, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Asleep in the intoxication of vices and Maya, (man) gains no understanding; only when Jam has seized him by the hair and dragged him up does he come to his senses. Attached to greed, Maya and sensual pleasures, (they) steal (others') wealth and wound (their) hearts; drunk with pride in what perishes in an instant, these demons do not understand. The Vedas, the Shastras and (God's) servants cry it aloud, (but) the deaf one does not hear; when he has lost the game outright and reached his end, the fool repents in his mind. He pays every penalty for nothing; in the (Lord's) court it is not counted to his account; the deed by which his honour would be kept, that deed he has not done. When the Guru showed me the world to be such, then I sang the praise of the One; giving up pride, (trust in his own) strength and cleverness, Nanak has come to (his) refuge. ॥4॥
Partal: a setting in which the rhythm (taal) changes again and again as the hymn is sung.
408.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Through trade in the Name of Govind, (one) wins the favour of the Saadhs and Sants, finds the Beloved, sings (his) praises, and sounds the instruments of the five sounds. By (God's) grace he gains Sahaj, (the Lord) reveals himself, and now he is dyed in (the love of) Govind; serving the Sants, he has come to love the Master, and the colour of the Beloved has taken hold of him. The Guru's wisdom is set firm in (his) mind; joy wells up, he does not come (into birth again); Sahaj (comes), and he finds the treasure in the mind; he has given up all the cravings of the mind. It has been long, long, long, so long (without your sight); a great thirst has seized my mind. O Lord, show me the sight of you; tell me (the way) yourself. Nanak, the lowly, has come to your refuge: hold (him) to your heart. ॥2॥
The instruments of the five sounds: the five kinds of instrument (strings, metal, wind, skin drums and pots), an image of full joy within.
408.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Rare is the one who breaks down the hard fortress (of vices) and holds (his mind) back from hope, thirst, deceit, attachment and wandering. (Rare is the one who) casts off these diseases: lust, anger, greed and pride. In the company of the Sants, in love with the Naam, I sing the praises of Govind; night and day I meditate on God; I conquer the wall of delusion and pull it down. With me, Nanak, the Naam is the treasure. ॥2॥
408.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Give up lust, anger and greed; remember the Name of Gobind in your mind; through the worship of the Lord, (all) tasks bear fruit. Giving up pride, attachment, vice and falsehood, repeat Ram, Ram, Ram; O mind, fall at the feet of the Sants. Remember the feet of God, Gopal, merciful to the meek, purifier of the fallen, the Supreme Lord, Hari, and wake up (from the sleep of Maya). Practise devotion, O Nanak: (in it lies) perfect good fortune. ॥2॥
409.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Joy and grief, detachment and bliss: O friend, (the Lord) has shown (me this) play. In one moment, fears; in another, fearlessness; in a moment (one) gets up and runs off; in a moment (he) enjoys pleasures; in another he leaves them and goes. In a moment (there is) yoga, austerity and much worship; in another (he) wanders in delusion. In a moment (comes God's) grace: in the company of the Saadh (the Guru), O Nanak, the Lord has imbued (him) with his love. ॥2॥
409.2: Raag Asa Asavari, Ghar 17, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Repeat Gobind, Gobind; love the Lord, Har Har, in your mind; what the Guru has said, keep that in your consciousness; break with all others and turn (your mind) back: this is how I have found the Beloved, O friend. The lake (of the world) holds the mire of attachment; (caught in it,) the foot does not walk toward the Lord; the foolish man has sunk (his foot) in it. Make the one single-minded effort (for the One); then, by falling into (his) refuge, (the foot) comes out, O friend. Make the mind steady, steady, steady, (so that) forest and home are the same (to you); within, (keep) the One Husband; outwardly, take up many (tasks); practise Raj Jog. Says Nanak, (thus one lives) among people (yet) apart from people, O friend. ॥2॥
Haan, at the end of the lines of these Asavari shabads, is a syllable sung to the song's measure; it is not rendered.
409.3: Raag Asavari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Hold firmly to one longing (for the One); joined to the Guru, stay ever in meditation; be firm in understanding the teaching of the Sant (the Guru); (do) service at the Guru's feet; then, by the Guru's grace, (God) is met, O my mind. Other wanderings have broken off; (the Lord is seen) pervading every place; (the dread of) fearsome Jam has lifted; a place has been found at the Root (the Lord, trunk of the world's tree); then all dependence (on others) has ended. One on whose forehead (this) destiny (is written) crosses over the fire of fear; he finds a place in his own home (within); he savours the relish of the Lord; his thirst and hunger have gone; O Nanak, he is merged in Sahaj, O mind. ॥2॥
409.4: Raag Asavari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Lord, Har Har Har, the Master of all virtues: let us repeat (his Name) in the strain of Sahaj; the Saadh (the Guru) has uttered (it) with his tongue; (from him) I have heard the way to be set free; it is found through great merit, O my mind. The sages search for him, God, the Master of all; he is hard to find in the world of Kali Yuga; he is the destroyer of pain; God fulfils (all) hopes, O my mind. O mind, he is the one to serve, the unseen, the unfathomable; love him; he does not perish, nor does he die. (Whoever) has come to know (him) through the Guru, O Nanak, that one's mind is won over (to him), O my mind. ॥2॥
410.1: Raag Asavari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Hold to the support of the One alone; utter the Guru's Shabad; accept (God's) command as true; find the treasure within your mind: (thus) one is absorbed in peace, O my mind. Whoever dies while living crosses (the world-ocean) so hard to cross; (whoever) becomes the dust of all, him I call fearless. Anxieties are erased (for one) whom the Sant (the Guru) has taught, O my mind. The person who has the peace of the Naam: pain never comes near him. Whoever hears the praise of the Lord, Har Har, everyone honours him. Fruitful is the coming (into the world) of the one who, O Nanak, is pleasing to God, O my mind. ॥2॥
410.2: Raag Asavari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Coming together, let us sing the Lord's praise: (so) the supreme state is attained. Whoever is pierced by that relish gains every siddhi; he stays awake (and on guard against Maya) night and day; O Nanak, he is greatly fortunate, O my mind. Let us wash the feet of the Sants and cast off evil-mindedness. Become the dust of (the Lord's) servants, (and) no pain afflicts (you). Take refuge with the devotees, (and) you shall never (again) be born and die. They have become steadfast who have meditated on the Lord, Har Har, O my mind. (O God,) you are my friend and companion; fix the Naam firmly in me. Without him there is no other; worship him in the mind. Let him not be forgotten even for an instant; how can one get by without him? I am a sacrifice to the Guru; (by his grace) Nanak repeats the Name, O my mind. ॥2॥
410.3: Raag Asavari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (O God,) you are the first Cause and the Maker of all; no one else comes to my mind (but you). What you do, that alone comes to be; (so) we sleep in Sahaj and in peace; patience has come into (our) minds since we fell at God's door, O my mind. In the company of the Saadh (the Guru) there is perfect self-restraint. Since (our) self-conceit left (us), from then on (our) torments have ended. (O Lord,) show mercy, keep (our) honour, O Banwari (the Lord); (so pray,) O my mind. Let us know this as peace: whatever the Lord does, let us accept it (as good). No one (seems) bad to the one who becomes the dust of the Sant's feet. The one whom (the Lord) himself protects alone tastes the Lord's Amrit, O my mind. One left with no one (to lean on) has that God as his own. (God) knows the state within (each one); everything is plain to him. (O God,) lift up and save the fallen; this is Nanak's prayer, O my mind. ॥3॥
Banwari (wearer of the garland of forest flowers, a name of Krishna): in Gurbani, a name of God.
410.4: Raag Asavari, an Iktuka, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). O sojourner (soul), hear the message: the things (people) were wrapped up in, all of them they left behind and went; (those things) have become as a dream for the one who has taken the Lord's Name. Those who left the Lord and clung to others run on, being born and dying (from birth to birth). The servants who have found the Lord, Har Har, live on (for ever). The one on whom (God) has mercy, O Nanak, he alone is the devotee. ॥2॥
411.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Asa, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji). To whom shall I tell the plight of the mind? Gripped by greed, (this mind) runs in all ten directions, held by the hope of wealth. For the sake of comfort it suffers much pain, waiting on one man after another; like a dog it roams from door to door, with no thought of the worship of the Lord (Ram). It throws away the human birth for nothing, and feels no shame when people laugh. O Nanak, why does it not sing the Lord's praise, by which the body's evil understanding would be destroyed? ॥2॥
411.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 2, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (The true yogi) comes down from the hard pass (of ego) and bathes in the pool (of the holy company); he does not babble idly; he sings the Lord's praises; as water (rising) is lost in the sky, he is absorbed in Sunn (the stillness where no worldly thought stirs); savouring the essence of truth, swirling it (like a drink), he obtains the supreme essence. Hear such wisdom as is in my heart: filling all, (God) is upholding every place. Truth (the eternal Lord) is (his) fast and (his) daily rule; death does not torment him; through the True Guru's Shabad he burns away anger; dwelling in the sky (of the higher spirit), he enters Samadhi; touching the Paaras (the Guru), he attains the supreme state. For the sake of (mastering) the mind he churns the True One, the very essence; bathing in the brimming pool, he has no filth (left) to wash; he becomes like the One he is dyed in; that alone comes to be which the Creator himself does. Through the Guru, cool as ice, he puts out the fire (of craving); the ashes he smears on are attention fixed in service; his own garb (darsan) is to come into the home of Sahaj; the pure Bani is the horn (nad) he sounds. Within him is (divine) wisdom, the finest, supreme essence; reflection on the Guru('s word) is (his) bathing at the tiraths; his worship is within, (where) Murari (the Lord) dwells; he merges (his) light in the Light (of the Lord). Steeped in the essence (of the Name), his understanding rests in love of the One; having stilled the five (passions), he dwells on the throne (within); (living in) the Master's will is his work and his earning; the unmanifest Nath (Master) cannot be comprehended. (As the sun) appears in the water and yet is far from the water, and its light fills the water, (so is the Lord); whom shall I call near (to him), and whom far? Seeing him ever present, I sing the praises of the treasure of virtues. Within and without, there is no other; whatever pleases him, that alone comes to pass. Listen, Bharthari (the yogi): Nanak speaks (this) reflection: the pure Naam is my support. ॥8॥

The yogis' terms: darsan is the garb of a yogi order (yogis call taking the garb taking darsan); bibhut is the ash smeared on the body; nad is their horn; Gagan (the sky) is the highest plane of the mind.
Paaras: the philosopher's stone, held to turn iron into gold at a touch.
412.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). With all the chanting, all the austerities and every kind of cleverness, (one) wanders in the wilds and does not come onto the road. Without understanding, none is accepted; on the brow of one empty of the Naam falls ash. The Master is eternal; the world comes and perishes. The mortal who becomes (the Lord's) servant through the Guru is set free. The world is bound by attachment and by many hopes; through the Guru's teaching some have become detached; within (them) is the Naam, and (the heart's) lotus has blossomed; they have no fear of Jam. The world is conquered by desire for woman, and dotes on the wife; attached to son and wife, it has forgotten the Naam; it has wasted its life for nothing and lost the game. Whoever serves the True Guru, (his) way of life is the best. Outwardly he may speak, and be spoken of, in the terms of Haumai, (but) inwardly he is free, and never lets (Maya's) stain cling to him; through the Guru's Shabad he burns away attachment to Maya; and in his heart he ever meditates on the pure Naam. He holds back the running (mind) and keeps it still — the Sikh whom (the Lord) in his grace joins to the Sangat. Without the Guru (one) strays, and comes and goes; when (the Lord) casts his glance of grace, he brings about the union and joins (him to himself). (O Lord,) I call (you) beautiful, (but your beauty) cannot be told; I speak of the Unspeakable, (yet your) worth cannot be found. All sorrows are sent by you, and joys come by (your) will; through the glory of the True One all sorrows are erased. (Within him) music plays without hands, and the beat is kept without feet; if (one) understands the Shabad, then he beholds the True One. (one who has) the True One within has every comfort with him; casting his glance of grace, the Protector protects (him). One who loses self-conceit comes to see (the Lord in) the three worlds; he understands the Bani and merges in the True One; he reflects on the Shabad, his attention held on the One in an unbroken line. O Nanak, blessed is (the Lord) who adorns (lives). ॥8॥
412.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Writing countless writings, again and again, (breeds only) pride; when the mind is won over (to God), the True One in (one's) attention is (the real) exposition. Telling and talking, reading again and again, (are only) a burden; writings are countless, (but the Lord) is beyond all writing and without end. Know the One alone to be such, the eternal (Lord); recognise birth and death as (his) Hukam. Through attachment to Maya the world is held bound by Jamkaal (death); the bound one is freed by cherishing the Naam. The Guru is the giver of peace; seek no other; in this world and the next (his friendship) will stand by you. When (one) dies (to self) through the Shabad, then he fixes his attention on the One; when he devours what cannot be devoured (the passions none can master), then he ends his doubt; one who enshrines the Naam in the mind is liberated while yet alive; if (he) becomes Gurmukh, then he merges in the True One. He who fashioned the earth, the heavens and the sky, who set up all (creation) and, having set it up, pulls it down, is himself, he alone, within all, through and through; he asks no one; he himself bestows his grace. (O Lord,) you are the brimming ocean, (you) the ruby and the diamond; you are pure and eternal, a fathomless (ocean) of virtues; one who meets the Guru, the Pir, enjoys peace; (you) alone are the Sovereign, (you) alone the minister. The world is in prison; (those who) have killed the ego are free; in the world, rare is the wise man who lives by (his wisdom); in the world, rare is the pandit who truly reflects; without meeting the True Guru, all go about full of pride. The world is in sorrow; only some (rare) one is at peace; the world is sick; given to pleasures, it weeps for (lost) virtues; the world is born and dies, losing its honour; one who becomes Gurmukh understands (this). (The Lord) is costly beyond price, beyond measure in weight; immovable, beyond deceit; through the Guru's teaching, enshrine him (in the heart). he is met through love; work done in (his) fear pleases him; lowly Nanak speaks this thought. ॥8॥
413.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (When) one dies, the five (nearest kin) gather and weep; (but those whose) Haumai departs wash off (the mind's) filth through the Shabad, (and,) understanding and seeing, they abide in the home of Sahaj; without this understanding, (the mourners) lose all their honour. Who dies, and who is it that weeps, wailing for him? O Creator, root of the whole world, over the head of each one are you alone. Whoever weeps for the dead weeps (his own) sorrow; he alone weeps who has (some) pain (of his own). What befalls the one (who has died), that God knows; that alone comes to be which the Creator himself does. To die while living is to cross over, carried across (by the Lord); victory to the Lord of the world! In his refuge is the supreme state. I am a sacrifice to the True Guru's feet; the Guru is the ship; through (his) Shabad the (ocean of) fear is crossed. (The Lord) himself is fearless, (his) light (within all) unbroken; without (his) Name, (the notion of) Sutak and of defilement by touch holds the world. Those who perish through evil-mindedness: what is one to say, weeping for them? Without devotion, without hearing (his praise), they are born and die. For the dead, friends weep in earnest; those of the three qualities weep, day after day. (But I,) casting off (all thought of) pain and pleasure, alert in Sahaj, surrender body and mind to the love of Krishna (the Lord). (Beings are) many, beyond count, (yet) within (all) is the One; rites and religious duties are many, past counting. Without (the Lord's) fear and devotion, life is wasted; those who join together and sing the Lord's praises (attain life's) supreme aim. (The Lord) himself dies, and he himself also kills; he himself creates; he sets up and pulls down. Know this: the world was created by the Light (that is the Lord); reflecting on the Shabad, (one) meets (him); there is no doubt (of it). Sutak is (even) in fire, which blazes and devours the world; Sutak is in water, on land, in every place. O Nanak, (the world) is born and dies in Sutak; by the Guru's grace, the Lord's sweet essence is to be drunk. ॥8॥
The five: the nearest kin of the one who dies, mother, father, brother, wife and son; some take them to be the five passions, lust and the rest.
Sutak: in Hindu custom, the impurity held to fall on a household for some days after a birth or a death; chhot is defilement by touch.
413.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). One who reflects on his own self assays the diamond (of the Naam); with a single glance (of grace) the Perfect Guru carries (him) across; (one who) trusts the Guru with all his heart has a mind held steady. Such is the Banker (the Guru), and such the assaying he does, that by (his) unerring glance (one), attuned to the One, crosses over. (One whose) capital is the sublime Name of Niranjan, is pure, dyed in the True One, a paikar (who sifts the true from the false); through praise (of the Lord), in the home of Sahaj, (he finds) the Guru, the Creator. Through the Shabad he burns away hopes and the mind's desires; he utters (the Name of) Ram Narayan, and leads (others) to utter it; from the Guru he finds the way, (the Lord's) mansion, (his true) home. (The Lord) whose being is gold, whose light is beyond compare, the God of the three worlds, whose form is every form: that wealth, eternal and inexhaustible, is in my lap. (He) pervades the five (elements), the three (qualities), the nine (regions) and the four (directions); by his power he holds up the earth and the sky; (the mind) that runs outward he turns and brings back (within). He is a fool, (who) does not see (the Lord) with his eyes, (whose) tongue knows no relish (of the Name), (who) does not understand what he is told; drunk on the poison (of Maya), he quarrels with the world. In noble company one becomes noble; (he) runs after virtues and washes away faults; (but) without serving the Guru, Sahaj does not come. The Naam is a diamond, a jewel, a ruby, (and) the mind (made pure) is a pearl: this is the wealth of such a one. O Nanak, (the Guru) assays (him), and with (his) glance of grace makes (him) blissful. ॥8॥
414.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Through the Guru, savour in your mind the knowledge (of God) and meditation (on him); through the Guru, recognise (within you) the mansion of the Master of the mansion; through the Guru, (hold) the Shabad in your awareness: (this is the) seal of passage. In this way, through loving devotion, (one) becomes wise in reflection, (and) through the Guru (gains) the eternal Name of Murari. Day and night (he keeps) in (his heart's) place the pure and sublime abode (of the Lord); (he gains) knowledge of the desireless (Lord who pervades) the three worlds. From the True Guru, recognise (the Lord's) Hukam. (His) joy is lasting; no grief touches him; the Amrit (Naam), knowledge (of God) and the supreme sweet essence are his food; with the five (passions) brought to an end, all people are at peace. (O Lord,) your light is in all (creation); everyone is yours; he himself joins, and he himself separates; that alone comes to be which the Creator himself does. He pulls down and builds, and by (his) Hukam (all) merge (in him again); his Hukam alone prevails, as pleases him; without the Guru, none attains the Perfect (Lord). Neither in childhood nor in old age is the mortal aware (of the Lord); in the full flush of youth he drowns in pride; without the Name, what will he earn in the end? He has not known in Sahaj the One whose grain and wealth (he lives on); led astray by doubt, he repents afterwards; with a noose around his neck, the madman wanders, crazed. (Those who,) seeing the world drowning, fled in fear, (and) whom the True Guru saved, are greatly fortunate; O Nanak, they cling to the Guru's feet. ॥8॥
414.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (Some) sing songs (of devotion), but in their minds is wickedness; reciting (talk of freedom from) attachment and aversion, they have themselves called (men who have) gone beyond them; without the Name, (their) minds hold falsehood and wickedness. Where are you wandering, O mind? Stay in (your own) home (within). Through the Guru, (people) are fulfilled in the Name of Ram; searching (thus), you will find the Lord in Sahaj. Lust and anger are in the mind, attachment in the body, and greed, avarice and pride: these are (the real) pain; without the Name of Ram, how can the mind take heart? One who recognises the True One bathes within; the Gurmukh knows the state within; without the true Shabad, (none) recognises (the Lord's) mansion. (One who) merges the visible form (of the world) in the Formless, (and,) through the True (Name), fixes (in his heart) the eternal One, whose power is beyond measure, that man does not come into the womb and the round of births. Where the Naam is to be found, there would I go; by the Guru's grace, (those) deeds would I do; (and,) dyed in the Naam, sing the Lord's praises. One who has recognised his own self through serving the Guru, (in him) the Amrit Naam, the giver of peace, has come to dwell; night and day, through the Bani, he is dyed in the Naam alone. When my God attaches (one to the Naam), then alone is anyone attached; (such a one) kills Haumai and is awakened through the Shabad; here and hereafter, peace is ever before him. The fickle mind does not know the way (to kill Haumai); the manmukh is filthy, (and) does not recognise the Shabad; the Gurmukh is pure, (and) utters the Naam. I offer my prayer before the revered Lord, that I may dwell in the company of the holy (Saadhs), (where) sins and sorrows are cut away, and the Lord's Name shines. One who, by reflection, has recognised (true) conduct, (and) through the True Guru's words has known the One — O Nanak, (his) mind is dyed in the Name of Ram. ॥10॥
415.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The Saakat's mind is (like) a crazed elephant; in the forest (of the world) it wanders, bewildered by attachment to Maya. (Such ones,) pressed down by death, go this way and that; the Gurmukh searches and finds the home (of the Lord) within himself. Without the Guru's Shabad the mind finds no resting place. Remember the utterly pure Name of Ram; give up other (tastes) and bitter Haumai. Tell me, how will this foolish mind be steadied? Without understanding, it will suffer the pain (inflicted by) Jam. (Whom the Lord) himself forgives, him the True Guru unites (with him); (he) slays death, the thorn, and the True One urges (him on, towards himself). This mind (performs) rites, this mind (keeps) religious duties; this mind is born of the five elements; this mind of the Saakat is greedy and foolish; through the Guru, repeating the Naam, the mind becomes beautiful. Through the Guru, the mind gives a place (within) to that very One; through the Guru, understanding (of him who pervades) the three worlds comes. This mind (is now) a yogi, (now) a pleasure-seeker, (now) one who practises austerities; the Gurmukh recognises the Lord God within himself. The mind (at times) turns renunciate, giving up Haumai; (yet) desire and double-mindedness cling to every heart. (One who), through the Guru, tastes Ram, the home of all delights, the Lord, the Master of the mansion, keeps his honour at (his) door and in (his) home. This mind (is now) a king, (now) a hero in battle; through the Guru, in the Naam, this mind becomes fearless; it kills the five (passions) and brings them under its sway; devouring Haumai, it holds them (bound) in one place. Through the Guru, (this mind) gives up other melodies and tastes; through the Guru, this mind awakens in devotion. Hearing the Anhad (melody) and reflecting on the Shabad, it is won over; recognising the self, (such ones) have become one with the Formless. This mind, made pure, (sees) that One at the door and in the home; through the Guru, devotion, love and longing arise (in it); day and night, by the Guru's grace, (it sings) the Lord's praise; God, (who was) at the beginning and from the start of the ages, (it sees) in every heart. In Ram, the home of all delights, this mind is intoxicated; through the Guru, it has known the home of all delights. For love of devotion, it dwells at the Guru's feet; Nanak is a servant of the servants of the Lord's devotees. ॥9॥
416.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). When the body perishes, whose can its wealth be called? Without the Guru, where can the Lord's Name be found? The wealth of the Lord's Name is the companion and helper (that goes) along; night and day, (one) who fixes loving attention on the Lord (becomes) pure. Without the Name of the Lord, who is ours? Holding pleasure and pain alike, I will not let go of the Naam; (the Lord) himself forgives and unites (me with himself). Fools are attached to gold and women; caught in duality, they have forgotten the Naam. Whom you forgive, (him) you make to repeat the Naam; singing (your) praises, (he) cannot be touched by Jam's servant. O Lord, great Giver, O Ram, O Gopal, keep (me) as it pleases you, O Merciful One. Through the Guru, Ram has become dear to my mind; (my) ailments are gone, and pain has been held back. There is no other medicine, no charm and no mantra; the Simran of the Lord, Har Har, destroys sins. You yourself lead (beings) astray, making them forget the Naam; you yourself save (them), showing grace. (Theirs is) the disease of doubt, of separateness, of another in the mind; without the Guru, in doubt, they chant the chant of another. They do not behold the Guru, the Primal Being; without the Guru's Shabad, of what account is (their) life? Beholding the Wonder (that you are, we) are struck with awe; (you are) in every heart, in gods and men, in Sahaj Samadhi (steady absorption). You fill every mind and uphold (all); there is no other equal to you. Ram, for devotion to whom (the Sants) have love, and whose Name is on their lips, is (found) in the company of the Sants and devotees. They break (their) bonds and (hold God) in meditation in Sahaj; through the Guru, (one) is set free, (gaining) the Guru's knowledge of the Lord. The pain (dealt) by Jam's servants does not touch him, the servant who stays awake, attuned in love to the Lord's Name. The Lord, Lover of devotion, is with his devotees; O Nanak, (they) are liberated in the Lord's love. ॥8॥
416.2: Raag Asa, an Iktuki, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). One who serves the Guru knows the Master; (his) sorrow is erased; through the Shabad he recognises the True One. Repeat the name of Ram, my friends and companions; serve the True Guru, and see God with your own eyes. In the world, mother and father are bonds; son, daughter and wife are bonds. Rites and religious deeds done in ego are bonds; son and wife are bonds (when) another (love) is in the mind. The farmers who till the land are in bonds: (one) bears the penalty of Haumai, (and) the king demands (his) due. Trade done without reflection is a bond; in the spread of attachment to Maya there is no contentment. The bankers who hoard wealth are in bonds; the wealth goes; without devotion to the Lord, (none) is accepted. The Vedas and debate (done) in pride are bonds; in the bond of attachment and vice, (one) perishes. O Nanak, (those who) take the refuge of the Lord's Name, the True Guru has saved (them), and no bond binds them. ॥8॥
417.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 3, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Those on whose heads the smoothly dressed hair looked lovely, with vermilion in the parting, those heads are now shorn with shears, and dust fills their throats. They lived inside palaces; now they are not allowed even to sit near them. Salutation, O Father, salutation! O Primal Being, no one has found your limit; you make form after form and watch them. When they were wed, their bridegrooms looked splendid beside them; they came riding in palanquins inlaid with ivory; water was waved over their heads (in welcome), and fans glittered beside them. They received a lakh (in gifts) when they sat, and a lakh when they stood; they ate coconut and dates, and enjoyed their beds. Now ropes are put round their necks, and their strings of pearls are breaking. Wealth and youth, which kept them steeped in delight, have both become their enemies; the order was given to the henchmen, and they carried them off, robbed of honour. If it pleases him, (the Lord) gives greatness; if it pleases him, he gives punishment. If one remembers (the Lord) beforehand, why should one receive punishment? The rulers had lost their senses in revelry, in shows and in pleasures; now that Babur's rule has been proclaimed, even a prince gets no bread to eat. Some (the Muslims) lose the times of their prayers; some (the Hindus) lose their worship; without their sacred cooking squares, how can the Hindu women bathe and put on the frontal mark? They never remembered Ram; now they are not allowed even to say Khuda. Some come back to their homes, and meeting one another ask how each one fares; for some this is what was written: they sit and weep over their sorrows. Whatever pleases him comes to pass; O Nanak, what can mortals do? ॥7॥
This shabad and the next are held to tell of the sack of Saidpur and the slaughter there by Babur's army.
Babarvani: Babur's rule proclaimed. Kuir (kunwar): a prince. Chauka: the purified square of the kitchen, in which Hindus cooked and ate after bathing.
417.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Where are those games, the stables and the horses? Where are the kettledrums and the shehnais? Where are those sword-belts of fine wool? Where are those red tunics? Where are those mirrors and the handsome faces? They are not seen here (any more). This world is yours; you are its Master. In a moment (the Lord) sets up and pulls down; he shares out wealth and gives it to others. Where are those houses, gateways, pavilions and palaces? Where are those handsome serais? Where is that easeful bed, and the woman the sight of whom kept sleep away? Where are the betel leaves and the betel-sellers, and the women of the harem? They have vanished like shadows. Many have been ruined on account of this wealth; this wealth has brought many to ruin. It cannot be amassed without sin, and at death it does not go with (anyone). Whom the Creator himself would lead astray, he first takes away (his) goodness. When they heard that the Mir was marching on them, millions of pirs tried to hold (him) back; (yet) shrines and abodes and mansions solid as stone were burnt, and the princes were cut to pieces and left in the dust. Not one Mughal went blind, and no one worked any miracle. There was battle between the Mughals and the Pathans, and the sword was wielded on the field; they (the Mughals) aimed and fired their guns, they (the Pathans) drove on their elephants. Those whose letter was torn in the (Lord's) court had to die, brother. The Hindu women and the Muslim women, the wives of the Bhattis and of the Thakurs: some had their robes torn from head to foot, some came to dwell in the cremation ground; those whose handsome (husbands) did not come home, how did they pass the night? The Creator himself does and causes (all) to be done; to whom should (this) be told? Pain and pleasure come in your will; to whom should we go and weep? The Lord of the Hukam drives (all) by his Hukam and is pleased; O Nanak, what is written is received. ॥7॥
The Mir is Babur; the Pathans then ruled Hindustan. A torn letter is a summons to death (a letter bearing news of a death was torn at one edge). The Bhattis and the Thakurs are Rajput clans.
418.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Asa Kafi, Ghar 8, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). As the herdsman (stays a while) at the pasture, so is (our stay in) the world; men practise falsehood when they build houses and homes. Wake up, wake up, you sleepers; the trader is departing. Houses would be built to last for ever if one were to stay (here for ever); the body falls, the soul will depart; if only one understood! Why do you cry, alas, alas? (The Lord) who is, he alone will be. You will weep for him (who has died); who will weep for you? You beat (your breasts) in vain, O brothers; you practise falsehood. He (the dead one) does not hear (you) at all; you only make the people hear. O Nanak, the one by whom (the soul) sleeps, he alone wakes it; if (one) understands his own home, then sleep does not come. If the one departing has taken any wealth along with him, then gather wealth (too): look, reflect and understand. Trade, and gain (life's) purpose, lest you regret; give up faults and practise virtues; in this way gain the essence. Make dharma the soil and truth the seed: farm such a crop; then you will be known as (true) traders, and take your profit with you. If (God's) grace comes, the True Guru is met, and (one) understands this teaching; he utters the Name, hears the Name, and deals in the Name alone. As there is profit and loss (in trade), so has (the world's) way always gone on; O Nanak, whatever pleases him is (true) greatness. ॥10॥
Goil: a pasture to which herdsmen bring their cattle to graze for a season, and then leave.
418.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). I have searched the four directions; no one is mine. If it pleases you, O Master, you are mine and I am yours. I have no second door; before whom should I bow in salutation? You alone are my Master; your True Name is on my lips. (Some) serve the Siddhas, (wishing to be) Siddhas and pirs, and beg for riddhis and siddhis (riches and miraculous powers); may I never forget the one Name, through the wisdom of the True Guru. Yogis, pleasure-seekers and wearers of patched coats, why do they roam through foreign lands? They do not recognise the Guru's Shabad, the sublime essence that pervades all. Pandits, teachers and astrologers read the Puranas every day; they do not know the treasure within: Brahm (God) is hidden in the heart. Some ascetics practise austerities in the forest, and ever dwell at tiraths (places of pilgrimage); in their dark (tamasi) nature they do not know themselves; why have they become renunciants? Some hold back their seed with effort and call themselves jatis (celibates); without the Guru's Shabad they are not set free; in doubt they come and go. Some householders, servants (of the Lord) and seekers hold to the Guru's teaching; they keep the Naam, giving and purity firm, and stay awake in the Lord's devotion. Through the Guru (the Lord's) door and home are known; one who goes (to the Guru) recognises (them). O Nanak, (such a one) does not forget the Name; his mind is content in the True One. ॥8॥

Several words of this shabad are of the Lahnda (western Punjabi) speech: maida mine, taida yours, nimhi not, bibha another, hiko the one. Naam, daan, isnaan: remembering the Name, giving, and purity of life.
419.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Merge desire into the mind itself; through the True One the terrifying world-ocean is crossed. From the beginning, through the ages, you are merciful; O Master, (I seek) your refuge. You are the Giver, we are beggars; O Lord, grant (us) the sight of you. Meditate on the Naam through the Guru, and the temple of the mind is drenched (in love). If false greed is given up, then (one) recognises the True One; if one merges in the Guru's Shabad, one knows the highest aim. This mind is a king, greedy, lured on by greed; through the Guru greed is driven out, and (one comes into) harmony with the Lord. If a crop is sown in saline soil, how can (one) reap a profit? The manmukh is not drenched in the True One; the false (one) is sunk in falsehood. Give up greed, you blind ones; in greed there is great pain. (When) the True Master dwells in the mind, the poison of Haumai is destroyed. Give up duality, the crooked path, or you will be robbed, brother; night and day, praise the Naam in the refuge of the True Guru. The manmukh is a stone, a rock; cursed (is his) insipid life: however long (a stone) is kept in water, it stays dry within. The Lord's Name is the treasure; the perfect Guru has given (it); O Nanak, (one who has it) does not forget the Name; he churns and drinks the Amrit. ॥8॥
419.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Those bound to depart are going on their way, having left the (true) road; the world toils and frets over its affairs; the True One has not pleased it. Why wander now, what is there to search for? The Guru's Shabad has shown (the Lord); (I) have cast off possessiveness and attachment, and come into (my) own home. The True One is met through truth; through falsehood he is not found; fixing the mind on the True One, one does not come (into birth) again. Why do you weep for those who have died? You do not know how to weep. Weep as you praise the True One, and recognise (his) Hukam. Know that (each one) has come with his allowance written by the Hukam; if the Hukam is recognised, the profit (of life) comes into one's hands. By the Hukam (one) goes (from here) robed in honour, and is pleasing in the Lord's court; by the Hukam too, in God's prison, blows fall on the head. This is the profit: let truth and justice dwell in the mind; what is written is what one receives; (so) let pride be cast away. The self-willed are struck on the head and worn away in strife; the false (world), plundered by the cheat (Maya), is bound and driven off. Those who enshrine the Master in the heart do not repent; (he) is the forgiver of sins, and they live by the Shabad. Nanak begs for the True (Naam), which is earned by toil through the Guru; (O Lord,) I have none but you; look on (me) with your glance of grace. ॥9॥
420.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Why should I go and search the forest? In my own home is a green forest. Coming home through the Shabad, (the mind) quickly settles in the True One. Wherever I look, there he is; no other is known. By doing the Guru's work, (the Lord's) mansion is recognised. When the True One himself unites (one with himself), then he is dear to the mind; (one) walks ever in (his) will, and merges in (his) embrace. When the True Master dwells in the mind, he alone stays dwelling in the mind; he himself bestows glories, and however much he gives, (his store) does not run short. Waiting on this one and that, how is (one) to reach the Lord's court? If one boards a boat of stone, it sinks him in the sea. Let us sell our own mind (to the Guru), and give our head along with it; (then), searching our own home, we recognise through the Guru the real thing (the Naam). What is called birth and death was made by that Creator; those who lost self-conceit and stayed dead (to self while living) have not had to die again. That work alone is to be done which is ordained from the Source; if, giving the mind to the True Guru, one meets (the Lord), who has ever put a price on (such a one)? That Master is the assayer of jewels; it is he who has set (their) worth. O Nanak, (one in whose) mind the Master dwells (receives) true glory. ॥8॥
420.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Those who have forgotten the Naam, led astray by the doubt of duality, have left the root and clung to the branches; what will they gain? Ashes. How can one be set free without the Naam? If anyone would understand (this): become Gurmukh, and one is set free; the manmukh has lost (his) honour. Those who have served the One, O brother, have perfect understanding; (such) servants stay in the refuge of the Lord, the Pure One, who is from the beginning, from the start of the ages. My Master is One; there is no other, O brother; by (his) grace, through the True One, peace has been found. Without the Guru none has found (the Lord), however many may say (otherwise) and have it said; (the Guru) himself shows the way, and makes true devotion firm (in the heart). Even if the manmukh is taught, he still goes off into the wilds. Without the Lord's Name he will not be set free; he dies and sinks into hell. He is born and dies and is made to wander, (yet) does not take the Lord's Name; without serving the Guru, he is of no worth. As is the service (the Lord) makes one do, such too are (one's) deeds; he himself does (all); whom else can one tell? He beholds his own greatness. The Guru's service is done only by the one whom (the Lord) himself has do it; O Nanak, by giving one's head one is set free, and (such a one) gains honour in the Lord's court. ॥8॥
421.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O Master, you are beautiful and wise; beautiful (too) is the Guru's Bani; it is by great good fortune that the True Guru is met, and (through him) the state of nirvana, where desire is stilled, is attained. I am the servant of (your) servants; we are your little servants; as you keep me, so I live; (let your) Name be in my mouth. Great is the thirst for the sight of (you); by (your) will alone does one please (your) mind; glories are in my Master's hands; by (his) will alone is honour obtained. The True One is not to be thought far away; he is within (all). Wherever I look, there he pervades; by whom can (his) worth be told? He himself makes, he himself destroys, and he beholds his own greatness. Becoming Gurmukh, one beholds (him); in this way (his) worth is known. One who does the Guru's work gains the profit while still alive; if it is written (in one's lot) from the past, only then is the True Guru found. The manmukhs suffer loss every day; led astray, they wander about. the manmukh, blind, does not remember (the Lord); how can he gain the sight of (him)? Only then is one's coming into the world (counted worth while), when one fixes one's attention on the True One; meeting the Guru, they become the Paaras, and merge (their) light in the (Lord's) Light. Day and night (such a one) stays unattached, doing the work given from the Source. O Nanak, contented in the Naam, they are dyed in (love of) the Lord's feet. ॥8॥
421.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). However much is said of (the Lord), I do not know his limit. For me who have no support, you alone are the support; you are my mighty strength.
