Nanak's prayer is this: to live at peace in the True Naam. When self-conceit goes, understanding dawns, and through the Guru's Shabad comes union (with the Lord). When Haumai and pride are cast away, true understanding is gained; when the mind is won over to the Master, he gives the support of the True (Naam). To stay contented in the Naam day and night: that is the true service. No obstacle comes in the way of one who walks in the Hukam of the Lord of the Will. Whoever walks in the Hukam of the Lord of the Will is placed in (his) treasury; the counterfeit find no place (there), and stay mixed with the impure. Day by day let the Genuine One be cherished (in the heart); (so) the true merchandise is gained. The counterfeit do not come into (his) sight; they are taken and burnt in the fire. Those who have recognised their own self are one with the Supreme Self; the One alone is the tree of Amrit, and its fruit is Amrit. Those who have tasted the fruit of Amrit stay fulfilled in the True One; they have neither doubt nor separation (from him); their tongues are steeped in the Lord's savour. (O mortal,) by the Hukam, through the joining of (your past deeds), you have come (into the world); walk ever in (the will of) the Lord of the Will. May Nanak, who is without virtue, be given virtue, the True (Naam) and glory. ॥8॥
421.3: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (One whose) mind is dyed in the Lord's Name, (who) has spoken (the praise of) the True One, what do people lose when (such a one) has become pleasing to you? As long as there is life and breath, let us meditate on the True One; by singing the Lord's virtues the profit is gained, and peace is found. Your service is true; grant (it to me), O Merciful One. Praising you, I live; you are my prop and my support. (I am) a servant at (your) door, a doorkeeper; you know (my) pain. Devotion to you is a wonder; (through it) you take away pain. Through the Guru one comes to know that in the Lord's court, in (his) presence, (it is) the Naam (that is accepted). the time (of one's life) is true and accepted, (if) one recognises the Shabad. They practise truth, contentment and love, and (take) the Lord's Name as provisions for the road; they cast vices out of the mind, (and) the True One gives (them) the True (Naam). True love for the True One, the True One himself has kindled; he himself does justice, as it pleases him. O True One, give (me) the true gift; (the Lord) is merciful; I serve him day and night; (his) Name is priceless. You are exalted and I am lowly, (yet) I am called (your) servant. Says Nanak: (O Lord,) cast your glance of grace, that I, who am separated, may find the True One. ॥8॥
422.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). How can coming and going cease? How can union (with the Lord) take place? Great is the pain of birth and death, (with) constant dread in duality. Without the Naam, what life is it? Shame on (such) cleverness; it is cursed, (for one who) has not served the True Guru, the Saadh, and has not loved devotion to the Lord. Coming and going ceases only when the Perfect Guru is found; (he) gives as capital the wealth that is the Lord's Name, and false doubt perishes. (Such a one) stays joined with the Sants, and sings (the Lord's) praise, (saying), Blessed, blessed; through the Guru he finds the Lord, the Primal Being, beyond the farthest beyond. An actor has put on a show: the world is (such) a play; the play is watched for an instant, a moment; it takes no time to be swept away. The game of chaupar is being played in Haumai, with falsehood and pride (for pieces); all the world loses; only he wins who reflects on the Guru's Shabad. Like the stick in a blind man's hand is the Lord's Name to me; the Name of the Lord, of Hari, is (my) prop, by night, by day and at dawn. As you keep me, so I live; the Lord's Name is (my) support. I have found the friend who stands by (me) at the end, the gateway of liberation for (your) servant. Repeating the Name of Murari, (I) have erased the pains of birth and death. O Nanak, (one to whom) the Naam is never forgotten, the Perfect Guru carries across. ॥8॥
422.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 2, Ashtapadis, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (O Lord,) the Shastras, the Vedas and the Simritis are your pool; the Ganga is merged in your feet; the intellect dwells on the three branches (the three qualities of Maya) and their root; but you are wondrous through and through. Servant Nanak contemplates his feet, and speaks the Bani that is Amrit. The thirty-three crore (gods) are your servants; (you are) the support of riddhis and siddhis (wealth and miraculous powers) and of the breath of life. His forms cannot be discerned; what can I say, what can I reflect (of them)? Within the world the three qualities (of Maya) are yours; yours are the four sources of life. When there is (your) grace, the supreme state is attained, and (one) tells the story of the Untellable. You are the Creator; everything is your doing; what can any mortal do? She alone on whom you cast your glance of grace merges in the True One. Everyone takes your Name, all the (creation) that comes and goes; (but) when it pleases you, then (one) understands, through the Guru; the rest, self-willed, wander about in folly. The four Vedas were given to Brahma; reading them again and again, he reflects (on them); (yet) the poor one does not understand his Hukam, and is born now into hell, now into heaven. (The Lord) made the kings of age upon age, whom (people) sing of as incarnations; even they did not find his limit; what can I say, what can I reflect (of him)? You are true; everything you have made is true; if you grant it, I speak of the True One. She to whom you make your Truth known merges in the Naam, in Sahaj. ॥8॥
Sursari (the river of the gods): the Ganga, which by the Puranas flows from the feet of Vishnu.
423.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The True Guru has driven out my doubt, and has made the immaculate Name of the Lord dwell in (my) mind; recognising the Shabad, (I) have found peace that lasts for ever. Hear, O my mind, the wisdom that is the essence: the Giver knows every way; the treasure of the Naam is found through the Guru. Such is the greatness of meeting the True Guru that he has put out the fire of the sense of mine and of craving; absorbed in Sahaj, (I) sing the virtues of the Lord. Without the Perfect Guru, none has known (this wisdom); (the world) is lured by attachment to Maya, by the love of another; through the Guru (alone) the Naam is received, and the Lord's Bani. Service of the Guru is the excellent austerity, crowning all austerities; (through it) the Lord, who takes away all sorrows, comes to dwell in the mind, and (one) is seen to be truthful at the True One's door. Through service of the Guru comes understanding of (the Lord in) the three worlds; recognising his own self, he finds the Lord; through the True Bani (the Lord's) mansion is attained. Through service of the Guru (one) saves all his family lines; (he) keeps the pure Naam enshrined in his heart; true glory is (his) at the True One's door. Fortunate are those whom the Guru has set to service; night and day (the Guru) makes devotion and the True Naam firm (in them); through the Naam all (their) family lines have been saved. Nanak speaks a true reflection: keep the Name of the Lord fixed in your heart; those dyed in devotion to the Lord (find) the door of liberation. ॥8॥
423.2: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Everyone lives on hope upon hope; one who understands (the Lord's) Hukam is freed from hope. Many people lie asleep in (the sleep of) hope; he alone wakes whom (the Lord himself) awakens. The True Guru has given (me) understanding of the Naam; without the Name, the hunger (for Maya) does not go. only through the Naam is the fire of craving put out; (but) the Naam is received only by the will of that (Lord). In Kalyug, (the Lord's) praise (is the way); recognise the Shabad. This is devotion; (by it) pride comes to an end. By serving the True Guru, (one) is accepted (at the Lord's door); know him who made hope. What should be offered to (the Guru) who makes (us) hear the Shabad, (and) in his grace makes the Naam dwell in the mind? Let this head be offered (to him), losing self-conceit; one who understands (his) Hukam has peace for ever. (The Lord) himself does (all), and himself causes (all) to be done; he himself, through the Guru, makes the Naam dwell (in the mind); he himself leads astray, and himself sets (one) on the path; through the True Shabad (one) merges in the True One. The Shabad is true, the Bani is true, which Gurmukhs in every age have uttered and expounded. The self-willed (world) is led astray by attachment and doubt; without the Name, all (the world) wanders about crazed. In all three worlds (spreads) the one Maya; the fool, reading and reading, has made firm (only) the love of another (than God); he performs many rites, (yet for him) it is all sorrow. Serving the True Guru, (the Gurmukh) has found lasting peace. Reflecting on the Shabad, (one gains) the sweet Amrit; having killed Haumai, (he) enjoys (it) night and day; when (the Lord) shows grace, (he abides) in Sahaj and in bliss. Those dyed in the Naam ever (abide) in the True One, in (his) love. Reflecting on the Guru's Shabad, let us repeat and read of the Lord; killing Haumai, let us repeat and read of the Lord; let us repeat (the Name of) the Lord in (his) fear and in true love. O Nanak, through the Guru's teaching, enshrine the Naam in the heart. ॥8॥
424.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Asa Kafi, Ghar 8, Ashtapadis, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). From the Guru springs (the) calm that has put out the fire of craving; from the Guru the Naam is received, (which is) the highest glory. Remember the one Name, O my brother. Seeing the world burning, (I) have run to the shelter (of the Guru). From the Guru springs wisdom, (and) reflection on the supreme essence; from the Guru (the Lord's) house and door are found, (and) the storehouses of devotion are filled. Through the Guru the Naam is meditated on, (and one) grasps the reflection; through the Guru (come) devotion and praise, (and) within (dwells) the Shabad of the Infinite. Through the Guru peace springs up, and sorrow never comes; through the Guru Haumai is killed, (and) the mind becomes pure. When the True Guru is met, self-conceit departs, (and) one comes to understand (the Lord in) the three worlds; (one sees that) the pure Light is spread (everywhere), (and one's) light is merged in the Light. (The one whom) the Perfect Guru has taught, (his) understanding has become sublime; (his) inner self becomes cool and calm, (and) through the Naam there is peace. The Perfect True Guru is met only when (the Lord) casts his glance of grace; (then) all sins and wrongs are cut away, (and) then no sorrow or hindrance comes. Glories are in (the Lord's) own hands; giving (them), he joins (one) to the Naam. O Nanak, (the one in whose) mind the treasure of the Naam has come to dwell receives glory. ॥8॥
425.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Listen, O mind: make (the Naam) dwell within you; (the Lord) himself will come and meet (you), O my brother. Night and day perform true devotion, (and) fix (your) consciousness on the True One. Meditate on the one Name, and you will find peace, O my brother; cast out Haumai and (the love of) another, (and) great will be (your) glory. This devotion gods, men and silent sages long for, (but) without the True Guru it cannot be had. Pandits and astrologers read (their books), (but) they gain no understanding (of it). (The Lord) has kept everything in his own hands; nothing can be said. what he himself gives, that alone is received; the Guru has given (me) this understanding. All beings and creatures are his; he alone is (the Master) of all; whom should one call bad? (One might,) if there were any other (than him). The Hukam of the One alone prevails; the task (set) by the One alone is on (every) head. (Those whom) he himself has set wandering have greed and vice within. Some he himself has made Gurmukh; (they) grasp the (true) reflection; on them he has also bestowed devotion; within (them) is the storehouse (of the Naam). To those who have wisdom, all is the True One; understanding of the True One has dawned (on them); though anyone try to mislead them, they are not misled, (for) they know that True One. In the house (of the heart of the wise) the five (passions) are at work too, (but there) the five become discerning (and keep within bounds). O Nanak, without the True Guru (these five) are not brought under control; through the Naam Haumai is killed. ॥8॥
425.2: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). All the treasure is within the home (of the heart); outside there is nothing; (it) is found by the Guru's grace, (when) the doors within are opened. From the True Guru the Lord is found, O brother. The treasure of the Naam lies within; the Perfect True Guru has revealed (it). One who becomes a buyer of the Lord('s Name) takes (it), (and) gains the jewel of reflection; (he) opens (his) inner self, (and) with divine sight beholds the storehouse of liberation. Within (the body) are many mansions, (in which) the soul makes its dwelling; (it) will obtain the fruit the mind longs for, (and) there will be no more round (of birth and death). The assayers have taken good care of the treasure (of the Naam); understanding has come (to them) from the Guru; the Naam is a priceless treasure; some (rare) one obtains it through the Guru. What will one find who searches outside? The treasure is within the home, O brother. Led astray by doubt, the whole world wanders; the manmukh has lost (his) honour. The false one, (who) leaves his own house and door (and) goes into another's house, is caught like a thief; without the Name (he) suffers blows. Those who have come to know their own home are at peace, O brother; (they) have recognised Brahm (God) within; (this is) the greatness of the Guru. (The Lord) himself makes the gift; to whom (else) can one speak? He himself gives understanding. O Nanak, meditate on the Naam, (and) you will win glory at the True One's door. ॥8॥
426.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Those who have recognised their own self have found (the Naam's) taste sweet, O brother; tasting the Lord's elixir, those to whom the True One is dear have become free. The Lord is pure, wholly pure; his dwelling is in the pure mind. When (he) is praised through the Guru's teaching, (one stays) detached in the midst of Maya. Without the Shabad one's own self is not known; all (the world) is blind, O brother. Through the Guru's teaching there is light in the heart, (and) the Naam is a companion at the last. (They) move in the Naam, in the Naam alone; (their) dealings are with the Naam alone. Within (them) is the Naam, in (their) mouth is the Naam; through the Shabad (they) reflect on the Naam alone. Let the Naam be heard, let the Naam be accepted; through the Naam alone comes glory. One who praises the Naam for ever and ever finds (the Lord's) mansion through the Naam. Through the Naam alone there is light in the heart; through the Naam alone glory is won; through the Naam alone peace springs up; through the Naam alone (one finds) refuge (in the Lord). Without the Name no one is accepted; the manmukh has lost (his) honour. (Manmukhs) are bound and beaten in the city of Jam; (they) have wasted (their) life for nothing. All (the world) serves the one of the Naam; through the Guru understanding of the Naam is given. Through the Naam alone (one's) name is honoured; through the Naam alone comes glory. He to whom (the Lord himself) gives (it) receives (the Naam); through the Guru's teaching (he) gives understanding of the Naam. O Nanak, everything is in the power of the Naam; some (rare) one obtains (it) by perfect fortune. ॥8॥
426.2: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). The forsaken soul-brides do not reach (the Husband's) mansion, nor do (they) know the delight of the Husband; (they) speak harshly and do not bow; the love of another is (their only) relish. How can this mind be brought under control? By the Guru's grace (it) is held back, (and) through an understanding lit by wisdom it comes (back to its) home. The happy soul-brides (the Lord) has himself adorned, instilling love and affection (in them); (they) walk in the will of the True Guru; through the Naam, Sahaj is (their) adornment. (They) ever enjoy their own Husband, on the true bed, in love; enchanted by the Husband's love, (they) find peace in meeting the Beloved. (She whose) adornment is boundless wisdom is a woman of honour; she is blessed with brothers, she is beautiful, (steeped) in the Husband's affection and love. In the happy soul-brides the True, the Unseen, the Infinite (Lord) has placed (his) love; with true love and affection (they) serve their own True Guru. The happy soul-brides have made (this) their adornment: round the neck a necklace of virtues; on the body, the fragrance of love applied; (and) within, the jewel of reflection. Those dyed in devotion are exalted; (their) caste and honour come through the Shabad alone. Without the Name, all are of low caste; (one without the Name) becomes a worm of filth. All (the world) goes about crying I, I; without the Shabad the I does not go. O Nanak, those dyed in the Naam have lost their Haumai; (they) remain merged in the True One. ॥8॥
Sabhraaee (sa, with; bhraa, brother): a bride with brothers, and so held in honour in her husband's home.
426.3: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Those dyed in the True One are pure; their glory is true for ever. Here they are known in house after house; hereafter (their glory) shines out age after age. O fair mind, so fond of colour, take on the true colour. If you are dyed with the beautiful Bani, this colour will neither fade nor leave. We are lowly, soiled and very proud; in the love of another (we are caught) in vices. Meeting the Guru, the Paaras, (we) have turned to gold; the pure Light of the Infinite (shines within). Without the Guru no one is dyed (in this colour); when the Guru is met, the colour takes. Those dyed in the Guru's fear and love are merged, through praise, in the True One. Without (the Lord's) fear the mordant (that fixes the colour) does not take, nor does the mind become pure. Deeds done without fear are false; (such a one finds) no place at all. He alone will be dyed whom (the Lord) himself dyes, joining (him) to the Sat Sangat. The Sat Sangat springs from the Perfect Guru, (and in it one abides) in Sahaj, in the True One, in love. Without the Sangat all live like beasts and cattle; they do not know their Maker; without the Name all are thieves. Some buy virtues, and (their) faults are sold off; through the Guru (they abide) in Sahaj and in love. Through service of the Guru (they) have found the Name, which has come to dwell within (them). The Giver of all is the One (Lord); (he) sets each one to (his) work. O Nanak, (those whom) he has adorned by joining (them) to the Naam he unites (with himself) through the Shabad. ॥8॥
427.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). All (the world) longs for the Name, (but) he alone obtains (it) to whom (the Lord) is gracious. Without the Name all is sorrow; peace is his in whose mind (the Lord) makes (the Name) dwell. (O Lord,) you are infinite and merciful; (I am in) your refuge. From the Perfect Guru (your Name) is received, (and) through the Naam alone comes glory. Within and without is the One (Lord); (he) has made the creation in many forms. By his Hukam alone (he) has (all) work done; whom else could we name, O brother? (O Lord,) understanding and the lack of it are your making; this work is in your charge. Some you forgive and unite (with yourself); some, the false, are beaten and thrown out of the Lord's court. Some are pure and holy from the very start; you have joined (them) to the Naam. Through service of the Guru peace springs up (in them); through the True Shabad (the Guru) gives (them) understanding. Some are of crooked ways, unclean and debauched; (the Lord) himself has made them miss the Name. They have neither attainment nor understanding, nor are they self-disciplined; they wander about unsteady and bewildered. On whom (the Lord) casts his glance of grace, in him he instils faith. Truth and contentment are (his) self-discipline; (his) mind is pure, (for the Lord) lets (him) hear the Shabad. Reading accounts, one cannot reach (him); by telling and describing, (his) end is not found. From the Guru (his) worth is known; through the True Shabad understanding comes. Search and set right this mind and body, reflecting on the Guru's Shabad. O Nanak, the treasure of the Naam lies within this very body; (it) is found through boundless love for the Guru. ॥8॥
427.2: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Dyed in the True One are the happy soul-brides whose adornment is the Guru's Shabad; reflecting on the True Shabad, (they) have found that Husband in (their own) home. (She who) through virtues has had (her) faults forgiven, (and) has fixed loving attention on the Lord, that bride has found the Lord as (her) Husband; the Guru has brought (her) into union (with him). Some, led astray by the doubt of duality, do not know the Husband to be ever present; how can (those) forsaken soul-brides find (the Husband)? (Their) night passes in pain. Those in whose mind the True One has come to dwell do the true work; night and day (they) serve (him) in Sahaj, (and) stay merged in the True One. The forsaken soul-brides are led astray by doubt; speaking falsehood, (they) eat poison. (They) do not know their own Husband, (and) on an empty bed they suffer. The True Master is One; O mind, see that (you) are not led astray by doubt. (If you) serve (him) by asking the Guru, (you will) enshrine the pure True One in (your) mind. The happy soul-bride, shedding Haumai and self-conceit, has found the Husband for ever; night and day (she) holds fast to the Husband, (and) finds peace on the true bed. (Those who) went (from the world) crying mine, mine got nothing in their hands. The forsaken soul-bride has no (place in the Husband's) mansion; at the last (she) went away repenting. That Husband of mine is the One; fix loving attention on the One alone. Says Nanak: O bride, if (you) long for peace, enshrine the Name of the Lord in (your) mind. ॥8॥
428.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Those whom he has given the Amrit to taste have found its savour, in Sahaj and in love. The True One is carefree; he has not a speck of greed. The true Amrit is raining down; (he) puts (it) into the mouths of the Gurmukhs. (Their) mind stays ever green, (and they) sing the virtues of the Lord in Sahaj. The self-willed (brides) are ever forsaken soul-brides; standing at the door, (they) wail. Those who have not known the delight of the Husband do just what was written (for them) from the start. The Gurmukh sows Truth, (and in him) Truth springs up; the True Name is (his) trade. Those whom he has set to this profit, (to them he) gives the storehouses of devotion. The Gurmukh (brides) are ever happy soul-brides; (the Lord's) fear and devotion are (their) adornment. Night and day (they) enjoy their own Husband, (and) keep the True One fixed in (their) heart. Those who have enjoyed their own Husband, to them I offer myself; shedding self-conceit from within, (they) stay ever with the Husband. In the Husband's love and affection, (their) body and mind are cool (and their) faces bright. Having killed Haumai and craving, (their) bed is a bed of ease, (and) the Husband delights in (them). (She into whose heart's) home (the Lord), in his grace, has come through boundless love for the Guru, (that) happy soul-bride has found as Husband the one Murari alone. He has forgiven all (her) sins; the Uniter has united (her with himself). O Nanak, let us speak only such words that, hearing them, (the Lord) may bear (us) love. ॥8॥
428.2: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Virtue springs from the True Guru when that God unites (one with the Guru); (then) the Naam is meditated on in Sahaj, (and) wisdom is revealed (within). O mind, do not think the Lord is far away; see (him) ever present. (He) ever hears and ever sees; he is wholly present in the Shabad. Those who have recognised their own self through the Guru have meditated (on the Lord) with a single mind; (they) ever enjoy their own Husband, (and) have found peace through the True Name. O mind, no one is yours; reflect through the Shabad and see. Run and fall into the Lord's refuge; (you) will find the door of liberation. Through the Shabad (the Naam) is heard, through the Shabad it is understood, (and one) stays lovingly attuned to the True One. Through the Shabad alone Haumai is killed, (and one) finds peace in the True mansion. In this age the glory belongs to the Naam; without the Name there is no glory. This glory of Maya is for four days; it is gone without delay. Those who have forgotten the Naam are dead, (and) they go on dying. (They) have not tasted the savour of the Lord's elixir; (they) stay sunk in filth. Some (the Lord) himself has forgiven and united (with himself), joining (them) to the Naam night and day; (they) live the Truth, abide in the True One, (and) merge in the True One alone. Without the Shabad (the Lord) is neither heard nor seen; deaf and blind, the world wanders astray. Without the Name (it) will suffer pain; (but) the Naam is received only by the will of that (Lord). Those who have joined their mind to the Bani are pure people, and accepted (at the Lord's door). O Nanak, they never forget the Naam; at the door of the True One they are renowned. ॥9॥
429.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Through the Shabad alone are the devotees known, whose speech is true; self-conceit has gone from within (them), (they) have accepted the Name, (and their) union with the True One comes about. The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is the honour of (his) servants; fruitful is their life, (and) everyone honours them. Haumai and the sense of mine are (the world's) caste, (and with them) great anger and pride; if one dies through the Shabad, then (this) caste goes; (one's) light merges in the Light, (and) the Lord is met. (I) have met the Perfect True Guru, (and) my life has borne fruit; (I) have found the Naam, the nine treasures, (and my) storehouses are full, never to run out. The traders in this capital who come are (those) to whom the Naam is dear; one who becomes Gurmukh obtains (this) wealth; within such ones (dwells) reflection on the Shabad. The proud manmukhs do not know the worth of devotion; (the Lord) himself has led (them) astray from the start; (they) have lost the game (of life) in a gamble. Without love there is no devotion, nor is there peace in the body. The gift of love is received (from the Guru); through devotion as the Guru teaches, the mind is steadied. He alone performs devotion, reflecting on the Guru's Shabad, whom (the Lord himself) moves to it; with Haumai and duality killed, the one Name dwells in (his) heart. The caste and honour of the devotees is the one Name; (the Lord) himself adorns (them). (They) are ever in his refuge; as it pleases (him), so (he) brings (their) task to fulfilment. Wondrous is devotion to Allah, the Lord; (it) is understood through reflection on the Guru('s word). O Nanak, (one in whose) heart the Naam dwells is adorned by (the Lord's) fear, devotion and the Naam. ॥9॥
430.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Led astray by other pleasures, (one) suffers pain without the Naam; (he) has not met the True Guru, the Purakh, who imparts true understanding. O my crazed mind, taste the Lord's elixir (and) enjoy its savour. Clinging to other pleasures, you wander about, wasting (your) life for nothing. In this age the Gurmukhs are pure; (they) stay lovingly attuned to the True Name. Without (the Lord's) grace nothing is obtained; what can one say? (Those on whom it falls) recognise their own self, (and) die through the Shabad, casting the vices out of (their) mind; (they) have run to the Guru's refuge, (and) the Forgiver has forgiven (them). Without the Name peace is not found, nor does sorrow leave from within; (yet) this world is gripped by attachment to Maya, led astray by the doubt of duality. The forsaken soul-brides do not know the Husband's worth; what use is the adornment they put on? Night and day (they) go about ever burning; the Husband does not delight in (them) on the bed. The happy soul-brides, shedding self-conceit from within, have reached (the Husband's) mansion; adorned with the Guru's Shabad, (they) have been united (with himself) by their own Husband. (The manmukh) has put death out of (his) mind; attachment to Maya is pitch darkness. The manmukhs die and die and are born, and die again, (and) are disgraced at the door of Jam. Those whom he himself has united are united (with him), reflecting on the Guru's Shabad. O Nanak, (those) merged in the Naam have bright faces in that True Court. ॥8॥
430.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 2, Ashtapadis, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (I) have won over the five (virtues), (and) turned away the five (passions); (the first) five (I) have settled (within), (the other) five (I) have driven out. In this way the city (of my body) has come to be peopled, O my brother; sin has gone, (for) the Guru has made wisdom firm (within). (The Guru) has set a fence of true dharma (around it); its strong gates (are) reflection on the Guru's wisdom. Sow the crop of the Naam, O brothers and friends; trade in (it), and serve the Guru every day. All the shops (of this city) are of calm, Sahaj and peace; the banker and the traders (live) together in one place. (Here) no one takes jizya, fine or toll, (for) the True Guru has set the seal of the Lord's own court. Load the merchandise of the Naam and send off (your) consignment; through the Guru, earn the profit and come (to your true) home. The True Guru is the banker, the Sikhs are the travelling traders; (their) capital is the Naam, (and) cherishing the True One (in the heart) is (their) account. He dwells in this house whom the Perfect Guru (blesses with) service; O Nanak, (that house becomes) the unshakeable city of the Lord. ॥8॥
The five won over and settled within are the virtues (truth, contentment, compassion, dharma, patience); the five turned away and driven out are the passions (lust, anger, greed, attachment, pride).
Pharhe: gates of planks or bars that close the way into a village or a cattle-pen; muhkam (Persian): firm, strong. Jizya: the poll tax taken from non-Muslims under Muslim rule.
431.1: Raag Asavari, Ghar 3, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O my mind, love for the Lord has taken hold; repeating (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, in the Saadh Sangat: (this is) the pure and true way of life. (O Lord,) great is (my) thirst for the sight of you, as I think (of you) in countless ways; be gracious, O Supreme Lord, O Lord; show mercy, O Murari. The mind, a stranger (wandering through many births), has come and joined the Saadh's company; the merchandise it wanted, it has found in the love of the Naam. However many the pleasures and relishes of Maya, they perish in an instant; (but) the devotees dyed in your Name enjoy peace in every place. The whole world is seen to be passing; the Name of the Lord is unshakeable. Make friends with the Saadh, and you will find an unshakeable place. Friends, companions, sons and kin: none of them goes along (with you); the Name of Ram alone stands by (one to the end); God is the Master of the lowly. The lotus feet have become the ship; clinging to them, (one) has crossed the ocean (of the world). (the one who) has met the Perfect True Guru (has) true love for God. (O Lord,) this is the plea of your Saadh: may you not be forgotten with any breath or morsel; whatever pleases you is good; in your will (all) affairs are set right. The Beloved, the ocean of peace, has been met, and great bliss has welled up; says Nanak, all sorrows are erased: God, (the Lord of) supreme bliss, has been met. ॥8॥
Murari (the foe of the demon Mur): a name of God.
431.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 4, Birhare, to the measure of the Chhants, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Let us remember the Supreme Lord God, O dear one; I am a sacrifice to the sight of him. He by remembering whom sorrows are forgotten, O dear one: how can he be forsaken? I would sell this body to the Sant, O dear one, (who) unites (me with) the Beloved. The pleasures and adornments of Maya are insipid; I have given them up, O my mother. Lust, anger and greed have left (me), O dear one, as (I) fell at the True Guru's feet. Those humble ones who are dyed in (the love of) Ram, O dear one, go nowhere else. Those who have tasted the essence of the Lord('s Name), O dear one, remain sated and fulfilled. O Nanak, (one who) has grasped the hem of the Saadh's robe crosses the terrifying ocean (of the world). The pain of birth and death is cut away, O dear one, when the Lord King is met. Beautiful, refined and wise is my God; when he shows (me) his sight, (that is) life (to me). Beings parted from you, O Beloved, go on being born and dying, having eaten the poison (of Maya). Only the one you unite (with yourself) meets (you), O Beloved; I fall at his feet. The peace (that comes) in beholding your sight, O Beloved, cannot be told by the mouth. True love does not break, O Beloved; it stays contained (in the heart) age after age. Whatever pleases you is good, O Beloved; undying is your will. O Nanak, those dyed in the love of Narayan, O Beloved, are intoxicated in Sahaj and in love. You alone know all the ways (of things), O Beloved; to whom else should I speak and tell (it)? You are the Giver of all beings; (all) wear and eat what you have given. Pleasure and pain (come) by your order, O Beloved; there is no other place (to turn). What you have me do, that I do, O Beloved; nothing else can be done. All the days and nights are beautiful, O Beloved, in which the Lord's Name is repeated. That alone is the work (one) does, O Beloved, (whose) writ (one) has had inscribed on the forehead from the start. The One himself is at work (in all), O Beloved; he is contained in every heart. Draw (me) up out of the well of the world, O Beloved; Nanak (has come to) the Lord's refuge. ॥8॥
Birhare: songs of birha, the pain of separation from the Beloved; these three are sung to the measure (jat) of the chhants.
In the first Birhara, and in the first line of the second, O dear one addresses a dear Sikh; after that, O Beloved addresses God (Bhai Vir Singh's Santhya).
432.1: Raag Asa, Patti Likhi, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Sassa: he who created the universe is the one Master of all; those whose minds were attached (to him) kept serving (him); their coming (into the world) has borne fruit. ॥1॥
Patti: the wooden slate on which children learn to write their letters.
432.2: O mind, why do you go astray, O foolish mind? When you can render the account (of your deeds), O brother, then (are you truly) learned.
432.3: Eevri: the Primal Being is the Giver (of all); he himself alone is the True One. One who, through the Guru, understands (him) in these letters has no account (standing) on his head. ॥2॥
432.4: Oora: let us praise him whose limit has not been found. They alone who serve (him) obtain the fruit, they who have practised the Truth. ॥3॥
432.5: Nganga: if anyone understands (true) knowledge, he alone is learned, a pandit; if he knows the One (Lord) in all beings, then he utters no (word of) Haumai. ॥4॥
432.6: Kaka: when the hair has turned white (as the white lotus), shining without soap, the scouts of Jam the King have come, and (one is) held bound by the chain of Maya. ॥5॥
432.7: Khakha: Khundkar (the Lord) is the King of the world, who has bought (all beings as his own) and given (them) their keep; in whose bond the whole world is held; no one else's command holds sway. ॥6॥
Khundkar (Persian khudavandgar): the Lord; Shah Alam: the King of the world.
432.8: Gaga: (the one who,) by mere talk of Gobind, who has kneaded and worked (the clay of the world), has grown proud, for such a one, he (Gobind) who shaped the pots and built the kiln (of the world) has made ready the putting in (the kiln) and the taking out. ॥7॥
The image is the potter's: the Lord has kneaded the clay and shaped the pots (beings); the kiln is the world, and putting the pots in and taking them out is birth and death (the Darpan).
432.9: Ghagha: if the servant toils at (true) labour and stays attached to the Guru's Shabad, if he knows bad and good as alike: in this way he keeps the Master in remembrance. ॥8॥
432.10: Chacha: he who created the four Vedas, the four sources (of life) and the four ages has himself, age after age, been the yogi, the enjoyer (in the beings of) the sources, the learned one and the pandit. ॥9॥
433.1: Chhachha: the shadow (of ignorance) spreads within all; (O Lord,) doubt is of your making. Having created doubt, he himself has led (beings) astray; (O Lord,) those on whom your grace has fallen have met the Guru. ॥10॥
433.2: Jaja: the humble beggar begs for knowledge (of God); for these alms he has wandered through the eighty-four lakh (forms of life). The One alone takes, the One alone gives; I have heard of no other, a second. ॥11॥
433.3: Jhajha: why do you fret yourself to death, O mortal? Whatever (God) is to give, he goes on giving. Giving and giving, he watches over (all) and runs his command, as the sustenance of beings is allotted. ॥12॥
433.4: Nyanya: when I look with attention, there is no other at all; the One is present in every place; the One dwells in the mind. ॥13॥
433.5: Tatta: why do you busy yourselves with vain affairs, O mortal? In a ghari or a muhurat you must rise and depart. Do not gamble away your (human) life; run and fall into the Lord's refuge. ॥14॥
433.6: Thattha: coolness has come within those whose minds are fixed on the Lord's feet; those humble ones whose minds are so fixed have been carried across; (O Lord,) by your grace they have found peace. ॥15॥
433.7: Dadda: why do you make a show, O mortal? Whatever has come into being must all depart. Worship him, and you will find peace; he pervades all, without a gap. ॥16॥
433.8: Dhaddha: he himself pulls down and builds up; as it pleases him, so he does. Making (creation) again and again, he watches over it and runs his command; he carries across the one on whom he casts his glance of grace. ॥17॥
433.9: Nanna: the one in whose heart (the Lord) stays pervading, he alone sings the Lord's virtues; the Creator himself unites (him with himself), and he is not born again. ॥18॥
433.10: Tata: the world-ocean is too deep to wade, and its far shore has not been found; we have neither boat nor raft, (and) we will drown; carry us across, O King who carries (all) across. ॥19॥
433.11: Thatha: he is in place after place, he by whom all that is was made. What can be called doubt, what Maya? Whatever pleases him, that alone is good. ॥20॥
433.12: Dada: let me blame no one; the fault is in my own deeds. Whatever I did, that I received; blame should not be laid on other people. ॥21॥
433.13: Dhadha: the Lord, who has set his power (in all), the doer of wonders who made (the world's many) colours: what he gives, all have received; according to each one's deeds his command operates. ॥22॥
433.14: Nana: (everyone) daily enjoys the gifts of the Husband (Lord); (yet I) have neither seen him nor kept him in (my heart). In talk alone am I a happy soul-bride, O sister; (yet) the Husband has never met me. ॥23॥
433.15: Pappa: the Supreme God is the King; he made this expanse (of the world) to behold (it). He sees, understands and knows everything; he pervades within and without. ॥24॥
433.16: Phapha: all the world is caught in the noose (of Maya), held bound by the chain of Jam; by the Guru's grace those men have escaped who have run to the Lord's sanctuary. ॥25॥
433.17: Babba: (the Lord) has begun to play the game (of chaupar), making the four ages the (four arms of the) board; all beings and creatures he has made the pieces, and he himself casts the dice. ॥26॥
434.1: Bhabha: those who seek (him) obtain the fruit, in whom, by the Guru's grace, the fear (of God) has taken root; the manmukhs wander, the fools, and do not remember (him); the round of the eighty-four lakh (forms of life) is their lot. ॥27॥
434.2: Mamma: attachment (to Maya) is death; only when death came did he think of Madhusudan. While in the body, he read (of) other things, and forgot the letter Mamma. ॥28॥
Madhusudan (the slayer of the demon Madhu): a name of God. The letter Mamma begins both maran (death) and Madhusudan.
434.3: Yaya: one is never born again, if one recognises the True One; through the Guru he speaks (of him), through the Guru he understands, through the Guru he knows the One. ॥29॥
434.4: Rara: he pervades within all, all the creatures he has made; having created the creatures, he has set them all to their tasks; those on whom (his) grace fell have taken the Naam. ॥30॥
434.5: Lala: he who has set (beings) to their tasks, who has made the love of Maya sweet (to them): eating and drinking, and bearing (pain) alike: by his will (this) command is laid down (for each). ॥31॥
434.6: Vava: Vasudev, the Supreme God, who put on this guise (of the world) to behold (it), sees and tastes (all), knows everything; he pervades within and without. ॥32॥
Vasudev: a name of Krishna, son of Vasudeva; in Gurbani it names God, who dwells in all.
434.7: Rarra: what is (the use of) quarrelling, O mortal? Meditate on him who is deathless; meditate on him, merge in the True One; (I) have made (myself) a sacrifice to him. ॥33॥
434.8: Haha: there is no other giver (but him) who created beings and gave (them) sustenance. Meditate on the Lord's Name, merge in the Lord's Name; (so) night and day the profit of the Lord's Name is earned. ॥34॥
434.9: Aira: he who himself made (the world) is doing whatever is to be done; he acts and causes (all) to act, and knows everything; so has Nanak the poet said. ॥35॥
434.10: Raag Asa, Patti, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Ayo Angai: the whole world has come (into being); Kakhai Ghangai: it is under (the sway of) death. Riri Lali: (people) commit sins; reading (what breeds) vices, they have forgotten virtue. ॥1॥
Ayo Angai, Kakhai Ghangai, Riri Lali: names of letters as children recited them in order: a, i, u … ang; k, kh, g, gh, ng; and ri, li, vowels of the Devanagari alphabet (the Darpan).
434.11: O mind, to what end have you read such accounts? The account (of your deeds) still stands on your head, to be given.
434.12: Sidhan-ngaiai: you do not remember (the Lord); Nana: you have not taken the Name. Chhachha: you are wasting away night and day, you fool; how will you get free when Jam has seized you? ॥2॥
Sidhan-ngaiai (siddham, may it be accomplished): the words of blessing the teacher wrote at the head of the slate before the letters (the Darpan).
434.13: Babba: you fail to understand, you fool; lost in doubt, your life has slipped away. Unworthy (of it), you have had yourself named a teacher; you have taken on yourself the load of others. ॥3॥
434.14: Jaja: your light (of understanding) has been stolen, you fool; at the end, as you go, you will repent. You do not recognise the One Shabad; again and again you will come into births. ॥4॥
434.15: O pandit, read what is written on your own head; do not teach others (the reckonings of) Maya. The noose has fallen first (on the neck) of the teacher; afterwards he puts (it) on the pupils' necks. ॥5॥
435.1: Sassa: your self-restraint is gone, you fool; you have taken a gift from the wrong place. The daughter of your patron is your own (daughter); by eating this grain, your life has gone (to waste). ॥6॥

The yajman (jajman) is the patron for whom a priest performs rites. The gift taken from the wrong place is, by the Darpan and the Faridkot Teeka, the gift taken at the wedding of the patron's daughter, who is to the priest as his own daughter.
435.2: Mamma: your understanding has been stolen, you fool; the great disease of Haumai has seized you. Within your inner self you have not recognised Brahm (God); you have become dependent on Maya. ॥7॥
435.3: Kaka: you have strayed in lust and anger, you fool; clinging to (the thought of) mine, you have let the Lord slip from your mind. You read, you ponder, you proclaim much aloud; (but) without understanding you have drowned and died. ॥8॥
435.4: Tata: you are burnt up in tamas (anger), you fool; Thatha: the place (of your heart) has been defiled. Ghagha: you wander from house to house, you fool; Dada: (yet) you have not received the gift (of the Name). ॥9॥
435.5: Pappa: you will not reach the far shore, you fool; you are entangled in the world's show. The True One himself has led you astray, you fool; this is the writ set on your head. ॥10॥
435.6: Bhabha: you are drowning in the world-ocean, you fool; you are sunk deep in Maya. (One who,) by the Guru's grace, knows the One crosses over in a single ghari. ॥11॥
435.7: Vava: your turn (of human birth) has come, you fool, (yet) Vasudev has slipped from your mind. You will not find this time (again), you fool; then you will fall into Jam's power. ॥12॥
435.8: Jhajha: you will never (have to) grieve, you fool; listen to the True Guru's teaching, and see. Without the True Guru there is no Guru; the one without a Guru bears an evil name. ॥13॥
435.9: Dhadha: hold back (the mind) that runs about, you fool; the treasure lies within you. If you become Gurmukh, you will drink the Lord's essence, and feed on (the treasure) lying (within) age after age. ॥14॥
435.10: Gaga: keep Gobind in your mind, you fool; no one has ever found (him) by talk. Enshrine the Guru's feet in your heart, you fool, (and) all past sins are forgiven. ॥15॥
435.11: Haha: understand the telling of the Lord's praises, you fool; then there will be peace for ever. However much the manmukhs read, so much suffering clings to them; without the True Guru there is no liberation. ॥16॥
435.12: Rara: keep Ram in your mind, you fool. Those in whose hearts he dwells, who by the Guru's grace have recognised Ram, have understood and found Ram, who is beyond the three qualities. ॥17॥
435.13: (O Lord,) your limit cannot be perceived; the Lord, who is beyond telling, cannot be told. O Nanak, those who have met the True Guru have had their account settled. ॥18॥
435.14: Raag Asa, Ghar 1, Chhants, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O innocent bride, a young girl in the bloom of youth, my Husband is full of delight. Deep is the love between bride and Husband; with delight she loves the Merciful One. The bride's union with her Husband comes about (when) God, the Master, himself shows grace. With the Husband, the bed (of her heart) is made beautiful, and the seven pools (within her) brim with Amrit. O merciful True One, show kindness and mercy, that joined to the Shabad (I) may sing (your) praises. O Nanak, seeing the Lord, her Groom, the young bride has blossomed; there is joyous eagerness in her mind. O young bride, made lovely in Sahaj, (hear) one prayer of love: To my mind and body the Lord is dear; I am dyed in union with God. Dyed in God's love, (I) make my prayer to the Lord; in the Lord's Name (the bride) dwells in peace. (O Lord,) (the brides) recognise your virtues, and then they know God; under the sway of virtue, fault flees. (O Lord,) without you I cannot live even a moment; by (mere) talk and hearing (my mind) finds no comfort. O Nanak, (she who) calls out, Beloved, Beloved, has her mind drenched in the delight her tongue tastes. O my friends and companions, my Husband is a trader. (From him I) have bought the Lord's Name, boundless in its relish and its worth. Priceless beyond any price, the Beloved (dwells) in the true home; if she pleases God, then the bride is good. Some (brides) revel in delight with the Lord; I stand at the door, calling out. The cause of all creation, the all-powerful Sridhar (the Lord), himself brings the task to fulfilment. O Nanak, by his gracious glance the bride is a happy wife, and the Shabad gives her heart support. In my home (of the heart) the true song of joy (is sung); God, my Friend, has come. He enjoys (me), dyed in (his) love; (I) gave (my) mind, and (he) took it. I gave my own mind and took the Lord as my Groom; as it pleases him, so he enjoys (me). Placing body and mind before the Husband, through the Shabad she gains the fruit of Amrit in the fortunate home (of her heart). He is not found by intellect, by reading of texts or by much cleverness; he is met through love, when the mind holds him dear. Says Nanak: the Master is our Friend; we do not belong to the world's people. ॥4॥
Ram at the end of many lines of these Chhants is a sung word of the measure, a calling on the Lord; it is not rendered.
The seven pools (ਸਾਤ ਸਰ): the five senses, the mind and the intellect.
436.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The unstruck music, the unstruck music plays, with a ringing, tinkling chime. My mind, my mind is dyed in the love of the darling Beloved. Night and day, dyed (in love), the detached mind has found its home in the realm of Sunn. The Primal Being, beyond all that is beyond, the Beloved, the Unseen: the True Guru has made (me) see him. Narayan is ever steady on his seat, in his dwelling; through reflection (on the Guru's Shabad) the mind is dyed in him. O Nanak, within the detached ones dyed in the Name is the ringing, tinkling chime of the unstruck music. (O friend,) tell me, by what way can one go to that city beyond reach, beyond reach? By truth and self-restraint, by cherishing (his) virtues, the Guru's Shabad is to be lived. Living the true Shabad, one goes to one's own home and finds the treasure of virtues. He has no branch, no root, no leaf, no bough; he is supreme over the heads of all. (The world) has grown weary of chanting, austerity and self-restraint, done again and again; by stubborn effort and forced control (of the senses) he is not found. O Nanak, the Life of the world is met in Sahaj, (when) understanding is given by the True Guru. The Guru is the ocean, a mine of jewels; in him are jewels in abundance. Bathe in the seven pools, O my mind, and be pure. One bathes in the pure water when it pleases God; through reflection (on the Guru's Shabad) the five (virtues) are gained. Giving up lust, anger, deceit and Maya, he holds the True Name in his heart. Haumai, the wave of greed, and avarice are stilled; he finds the One who is merciful to the meek. O Nanak, no place of pilgrimage equals the Guru; the Guru is the True Gopal. I have looked through forest after forest, and looked at all the green growth. The three worlds, the whole world, all of it, you yourself have made. All is of your making; you remain steadfast; there is none like you. You are the Giver, and all are beggars at your door; whom but you should I praise? You give gifts unasked, O Giver; the storehouses are full of devotion to you. Without the Name of Ram there is no liberation: Nanak says this after reflection. ॥4॥
The five (ਪੰਚ) here are five virtues: truth, contentment, compassion, dharma and patience.
437.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). My mind, my mind is dyed in the love of Ram, the Beloved. The True Master, the Primal Being, beyond all that is beyond, upholds (all). Beyond reach, beyond the senses, boundless, without limit, the Supreme Lord is foremost of all. He was from the beginning, from the start of the ages; he is, and he will be; know all else to be false. (The mind) does not know the essence of rites and deeds of dharma; how then are awareness and liberation to be gained? O Nanak, through the Guru (the mind) recognises by the Shabad (that) night and day the Name is to be meditated on. My mind, my mind is convinced (that) the Name is the (true) friend. Haumai, possessiveness and Maya do not go along (at the end). Mother, father, brother, son, cleverness, wealth and wife: (none of these) goes along. Through reflection (I) have cast off and forsaken the daughter of the ocean (Maya), (keeping her) under (my) feet. The Primal Being has shown a wondrous play: wherever I look, there he is. Nanak does not let go of the Lord's devotion; whatever comes to be in Sahaj, let it be. My mind, my mind is pure, cherishing the True One. Erasing faults, (I) walk on, with virtues as companions beside (me). Casting off faults, (one whose) conduct is excellent is found true at the door of the True One. (He) puts a stop to coming and going, and through the Guru reflects on the essence (of all). (O Lord,) you are (my) friend, beloved, all-knowing companion; in the True One glory is gained. Says Nanak: the jewel of the Name has shone forth (within); such is the Guru's teaching (I) have received. The True One is the collyrium; applying that collyrium, (the mind) is dyed in the Niranjan (the One untouched by Maya's stain). The Life of the world, the Giver, pervades mind and body. The Lord, the Life of the world, the Giver, in whom the mind is dyed, is met in Sahaj when (the Guru) brings about the meeting. In the gathering of the Saadh, in the company of the Sants, by God's gracious glance, peace is found. The detached ones, dyed in the Lord's devotion, are rid of attachment and thirst. O Nanak, rare are the servants, detached (from the world), who have killed Haumai and are content (in the Name). ॥4॥
The daughter of the ocean (ਸਾਇਰ ਕੀ ਪੁਤ੍ਰੀ): Lakshmi, who in the Puranas rose from the churning of the ocean; here, Maya.
438.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 2, a Chhant, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Wherever I go, you are in every place, O true Creator. (You are) the Giver of all, who shapes (each) by their deeds, the One who takes sorrows away. The Master who takes sorrows away, by whose doing (all) comes to pass, destroys in a single moment sins by the millions upon millions. The swan as a swan, the heron as a heron: he weighs every heart. Wherever I go, you are in every place, O true Creator. Those who meditated (on him) with one-pointed mind found peace; such are rare in the world. Jam does not come near them; they live the Guru's Shabad and never come back defeated. They never lose; they cherish the virtues of the Lord, Har Har; Jam does not come near them. Birth and death are ended for those who have fallen at the Lord's feet. Through the Guru's teaching they have gained the Lord's essence, the Lord's fruit, keeping in their hearts the Name of the Lord, Har Har. Those who meditated (on him) with one-pointed mind found peace; such are rare in the world. To the One who created the world and set it to its work, (I am) a sacrifice. Serve him and earn (this) profit; (so) honour is gained in the Lord's court. In the Lord's court, honour is gained only by the one who recognises the One. He gains the nine treasures, who through the Guru's teaching meditates on the Lord and daily speaks and tells of the Lord's virtues. Night and day take the Name of him alone: the Lord, the most exalted, the all-pervading Being, foremost of all. To the One who created the world and set it to its work, I am a sacrifice. Those who take the Name look beautiful; to them come the fruits of peace; those who believe (in it) go having won (life's game). When it pleases him, their fruit does not run short, though ages upon ages pass. Though ages upon ages pass, O Master, their fruit does not run short. Those who meditate on the Lord's Name know no old age, no death, no fall into hell. Those who repeat Har Har do not wither; O Nanak, they suffer no pain. Those who take the Name look beautiful; to them come the fruits of peace; those who believe (in it) go having won (life's game). ॥4॥
438.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Asa, Ghar 3, a Chhant, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Listen, O black deer: why are you lost in delight in the garden (of the world)? The poisonous fruit is sweet for four days, then it turns hot (and painful). (That in which you are) so drunk turns hot then; without the Name it brings torment. It is like the waves the sea throws up, like the flash of lightning (gone in a moment). Without the Lord there is no protector, and him you have forgotten. Says Nanak: O mind, remember the True One, (or) you will die, O black deer. O bumblebee, hovering over the flowers, very heavy is the pain (to come). I have asked my own Guru, true and wise in reflection. Having reflected, I asked the True Guru about the bumblebee (of the mind), lost in delight among the creepers. (The answer:) when the sun rises (and the night of life is over), the body falls, and (the soul) is heated like oil in the pan. Bound on Jam's road, you take blows, O ghoul, without the Shabad. Says Nanak: O mind, remember the True One, (or) you will die, O black bumblebee. O my soul, a stranger (here), why do you fall into entanglements? If the True Master dwells in the mind, why would you be caught in Jam's net? The fish, parted (from the water), weeps from its eyes when the fisher has cast his net. The world, Maya's attachment, seems sweet; at the end this illusion is shattered. Worship (him) with devotion, fixing your mind on the Lord, and cast anxiety from your mind. Says Nanak: O mind, remember the True One, O soul, a stranger (here). When the currents of rivers are parted, they meet again only by destiny. Age after age (this attachment) is sweet, (yet) filled with poison; a rare yogi (one detached) knows (it). Some (rare) one knows (it) in Sahaj and recognises the Lord: the one who has kept the True Guru in mind. Without the Lord's Name, heedless fools, strayed in doubt, waste away. Those in whose hearts are not the Lord's Name, devotion and the True One, at the end weep and wail aloud. Says Nanak: through the true Shabad the True One unites those long parted. ॥4॥
439.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Asa, Ghar 1, Chhants, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). In my home (of the heart) is the true song of joy, made beautiful by the true Shabad. The bride's union with her Husband has come about; God himself has united (her with him). God himself united (her) and set the True (Name) in (her) mind; the bride is rapt in Sahaj. The Guru's Shabad has adorned her, truth has made her beautiful; dyed in love, she ever delights in (her Husband). When she sheds self-conceit and finds the Lord as her Groom, then she sets the Lord's essence in her mind. Says Nanak: (she who is) made beautiful by the Guru's Shabad has her whole life made fruitful. Caught in (the love of) another, the bride, strayed in doubt, does not find the Lord as her Groom. That bride has no virtue; she wastes her life in vain. She wastes her life in vain; the manmukh, ignorant, full of faults, pines in grief. Serving her own True Guru, she found lasting peace; then she met the Husband, present before her. Seeing the Husband, she blossomed, delighted within; through the true Shabad she is (absorbed) in love. O Nanak, without the Name the bride strays in doubt; meeting her Beloved, she finds peace. The bride whom the Guru has brought into union knew the Husband to be with her. Within, through the Shabad, she met (him), and in Sahaj quenched (her) burning. The Shabad quenched the burning; peace came within, and in Sahaj she tasted the Lord's essence. Meeting her own Beloved, she ever enjoys his love; through the true Shabad her speech is sweet. The pandits and the silent sages have worn themselves out with reading and reading; those who wear religious garb have not found liberation. O Nanak, without devotion the world has gone mad; through the true Shabad (one) is united (with God). Bliss has come into the mind of that bride whom the beloved Lord has united (with himself). That bride is steeped in the Lord's essence through the Guru's boundless Shabad. Through the boundless Shabad she has met the Beloved; ever she cherishes (his) virtues, and they dwell in (her) mind. The bed (of her heart) became beautiful when the Husband enjoyed her; meeting the Beloved, her faults fled. In the home where the Lord's Name is ever meditated on, the song of joy (resounds) through all four ages. O Nanak, those dyed in the Name are ever in bliss; meeting the Lord, (all) tasks are fulfilled. ॥4॥
440.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Asa, Ghar 3, a Chhant, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). O my friends, my dear ones, keep up devotion to the Husband Lord. Serve your own Guru always, and receive the precious gift of the Naam. Practise devotion to the Husband Lord, (the devotion) that pleases the beloved Husband. If you do as you yourselves will, then the Husband's favour does not come (your way). This path of devotion and love is hard; some rare one finds it at the Guru's door. Says Nanak, the one on whom (the Lord) shows grace fixes his mind on devotion to the Lord. O my mind, you who have turned renunciant, to whom do you show off your detachment? The Lord's song of joy (sounds) ever and always within those who sing the Lord's virtues. Practise (true) detachment, give up pretence: that Husband Lord knows everything. In the water, on the land and in the sky, he alone is (present); the Gurmukh recognises (his) Hukam. One who has recognised the Lord's Hukam, he alone finds every comfort. Thus says Nanak: he is the (true) renunciant who night and day keeps his mind attuned to the Lord. O mind, wherever you run, there the Lord is with you. O mind, cleverness should be given up; cherish the Guru's Shabad. That Husband Lord is ever with you; if you hold the Name of the Lord in your heart even for a moment, your sins of birth after birth will be cut away, and in the end you will attain the supreme state. Your bond with the True One will be tied; through the Guru, cherish (him) always. Thus says Nanak: O mind, wherever you run, there the Lord is ever with you. When the True Guru is met, the wandering (mind) is held still, and comes to dwell in its own home (within). It buys the Naam, utters the Naam, and stays merged in the Naam. The wandering (mind) is held still when the True Guru is met, and it reaches the Tenth Gate. There the Amrit (of the Naam) is its food, and the strain of Sahaj wells up; through that Shabad (the pull of) the world is held in check. There countless instruments (play), there is bliss for ever, and (the mind) stays merged in the True One. Thus says Nanak: when the True Guru is met, the wandering (mind) is held still, and comes to dwell in its own home (within). O mind, you are the very form of the Light; recognise your own source. O mind, the dear Lord is at your side; following the Guru's teaching, take delight in his love. If you recognise your source, you will know the Husband Lord, and understanding of death and of life will come. If by the Guru's grace you know the One, then the love of another does not arise. Peace has come into the mind, the music of rejoicing has sounded, and so (the mind) has been accepted. Thus says Nanak: O mind, you are the very form of the Light; recognise your own source. O mind, you are smeared with pride; laden with pride you will depart. Bewitched by enchanting Maya, you will be made to wander through births again and again. Clinging to pride you will go, O foolish mind, and at the last, when you are gone, you will repent. The disease of pride and craving has seized you; you are wasting your life in vain. O foolish, self-willed (mind), you do not remember (the Lord); gone on to the next world, you will repent. Thus says Nanak: O mind, you are smeared with pride; laden with pride you will depart. O mind, take no pride (in thinking) that you know something; through the Guru, become humble. Within you are ignorance and an intellect of ego; through the True Shabad, wash away this filth. Be humble before the True Guru; do not make any show of yourself. The world is burning in its own pride; see that you do not ruin your own self (in it as well). (Only) if you do your work in the True Guru's will (are you safe); so stay attached to the True Guru's will. Thus says Nanak: give up self-conceit and you will find peace; O mind, remain humble. Blessed is that moment when I met the True Guru, and that Husband Lord came into my mind. Great bliss and Sahaj came about, and (my) mind and body found peace. That Husband Lord came into my mind; I enshrined him in my heart, and put all my faults out of mind. When it pleased him, virtues became manifest (in me); the True Guru himself adorned (my life). Those people are accepted who have held fast to the one Naam and have ended the love of another. Thus says Nanak: blessed is that moment when I met the True Guru, and that Husband Lord came into my mind. Some beings are lost in doubt; that Husband Lord has himself led them astray. In the love of another they wander about, doing their deeds in Haumai. That Husband Lord has himself led them astray and set them on the wrong path; nothing is in their power. Their good state and their bad you alone know, you who made this creation. Your Hukam is very weighty; to some rare one you make it understood through the Guru. Thus says Nanak: what can helpless beings do, when you lead them astray in doubt? O my True Master, true is your greatness. You are the Supreme Lord, the infinite Master; your power cannot be told. True is your greatness; those in whose minds you have made it dwell sing your virtues for ever. They sing your virtues when they are pleasing to you, and they fix their minds on the True One. One whom you yourself unite (with you) stays absorbed (in you) through the Guru. Thus says Nanak: O my True Master, true is your greatness. ॥10॥
The closing figures count the Chhants of Raag Asa so far: five by the First Guru and two by the Third, seven in all.
442.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 1, Chhants, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. I have found life, the true life: through the Guru (the Lord) has become dear to me. (The Guru) gives the Lord's Name, the Lord's Name, and makes it dwell in my every breath. He has made the Name of the Lord, Har Har, dwell in my every breath, and has taken away all my fear and sorrow. Through the Guru's word I have meditated on the Unseen One, beyond the reach of the senses, and have attained the pure, supreme state. With unstruck melody, instruments play (within me) day after day, as I sing the True Guru's Bani. O Nanak, God the Giver has given (this) gift, and (my) light has merged in the Light. The self-willed, the manmukhs, have died (a spiritual death), holding Maya to be their own. (Their mind) is buoyed one moment and sinks the next; they have fixed their minds on the stinking carcass (of the body). They have fixed (them) on the stinking carcass, and their minds cling to what shows itself like the safflower's colour (bright, and soon gone). Like a shadow (their mind) falls one moment to the east and the next to the west, and turns like the wheel the potter spins. They eat sorrow, gather sorrow and live on sorrow; they have made sorrow grow and grow. O Nanak, the hard (ocean of the world) is crossed with ease when one comes to the Guru's refuge. My Master, my Master is beautiful, unreachable and unfathomable. I ask for the capital of the Lord, the capital of the Lord, O my True Guru, my Banker. One who has sought the Lord's capital and bought the Naam sings (his) virtues, and through those virtues is dear (to him). He casts off sleep and hunger altogether, and stays absorbed in the stillness of Sunn. Traders of one kind come (to the Guru) and take away the Lord's Name as their profit. O Nanak, offer your mind and body to the Guru; he finds (the Name) in whose lot it is. The ocean (of the body) is full of jewels upon jewels, of countless precious things. Those who are attached to the Bani, the Guru's Bani, have it come into their hands. Those attached to the Guru's Bani have the priceless, boundless jewel come into their hands. They have found the Name of the Lord, Har Har, beyond all weighing; (O Lord,) their storehouses are full of devotion to you. I have churned the ocean of the body and searched it, and a thing of matchless beauty has come into sight. The Guru is Govind, and Govind is the Guru; says Nanak, there is no difference (between them), O brother. ॥4॥
442.2: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Gently, gently, drop by drop, the stream of Amrit rains down. To the Gurmukh, to the Gurmukh, the beloved Lord comes into sight. The Name of Ram, the saviour of the world, is dear (to him); in the Name of Ram is (his) glory. In Kalyug the Name of Ram is the ship; through the Guru it carries (one) across. In this world and the next, through the Name of Ram (they) live at ease; the Gurmukh's way of life is excellent. O Nanak, (the Lord) in his mercy gives this gift, and through the Name of Ram carries (one) across. (I) have repeated the Name of Ram, of Ram, and sorrows and sins have been destroyed and driven away. In close bond with the Guru, in close bond with the Guru, I have meditated (on him), and have made Ram dwell in my heart. Ram has been remembered in the heart, and the supreme state attained, since (I) came to the Guru's refuge. The boat (of life), sinking in greed and vice, came out (safe), when the True Guru made the Naam firm (within). The Perfect Guru has given the gift of (spiritual) life, and has fixed (my) mind on the Name of Ram. The Merciful One himself gives (this) in his mercy; O Nanak, (it comes) in the Guru's refuge. Hearing the Bani of the Name of Ram, (I) have won success; all (my) affairs are made fair. With every hair, every single hair, through the Guru I meditate on Ram. Meditating on the Name of Ram, (I) have become pure; he has no form or feature at all. Ram, Ram alone is remembered within the heart, and all craving and hunger have been taken away. Mind and body have grown cool, and all is adorned, (now that) through the Guru's teaching Ram has shone forth. O Nanak, (the Lord) himself has shown grace; I am the slave of the slaves of (his) slaves. They who have forgotten the Name of Ram, of Ram, are foolish, unfortunate manmukhs. Within them attachment holds sway; moment after moment Maya holds on (to them). Maya's filth has stuck (to them); they have become foolish and unfortunate, those to whom the Name of Ram is not pleasing. The proud perform countless rites, but keep (their minds) stolen away from the Name of the Lord, of Ram. Very hard and painful is the path of Jam, (full of) the blackness and darkness of attachment. O Nanak, when (one) has meditated on the Naam through the Guru, then (one) finds the door of liberation. The Name of Ram, of Ram, and Ram himself, one who is a Gurmukh comes to know through the Guru. This mind, which wanders one moment up high and (the next) down in the netherworld, he brings into the one home. He brings the mind into the one home, knows every state and bound (of the spiritual life), and relishes the Name of the Lord, of Ram. The Name of Ram keeps the honour of the Lord's servant; it saved Prahlad and carried him across. Ram, Ram, the all-pervading, the beautiful, is high above; telling his virtues, none has found their end. O Nanak, hearing the Name of Ram, (they) are drenched (in it), and merged in the Name of Ram. Those within whom the Name of Ram dwells have cast away all anxiety. All wealth and all dharma have come to them, and they have found the fruit their minds longed for. They have found the fruit the mind longed for, meditating on the Name of Ram and singing the praises of Ram's Name. Evil thinking and bad sense have gone and understanding has come, as they fix their minds on the Name of Ram. Fruitful has become the life, and the whole body, in which the Name of Ram has shone forth. O Nanak, worship the Lord always, day and night; through the Guru, (one) comes to dwell in one's own home (within). Those who have come to have faith in the Name of Ram do not fix their minds on another. Even if the whole earth were turned to gold and given (to them), nothing but the Name pleases them. The Name of Ram pleases their minds; they have found supreme peace, and (the Name) goes with them as their companion at the last, when they depart. They have gathered the wealth of the Name of Ram as their capital; it neither sinks nor is lost. In this age the Name of Ram is the raft; Jamkaal does not come near. O Nanak, (one who) has recognised Ram through the Guru, (Ram) in his grace himself unites (him with himself). The Name of Ram, of Ram, is true, ever true; the Gurmukh has come to know it. That servant is engaged in the Guru's service who has offered up his mind and body. He has given his mind and body, with great faith in his mind; for the love of the servant, the Guru unites (him with the Lord). The Master of the meek, the Giver of all beings, is found through the Perfect Guru. The Guru is the Sikh, and the Sikh is the Guru; (the two) are one, (and the Sikh) carries on the Guru's teaching. (The Guru) places the mantra of the Name of Ram in the heart; O Nanak, the union (with the Lord) comes through love. ॥8॥
444.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Asa, Ghar 2, Chhants, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Lord, Har Har, the Creator, is the destroyer of sorrow; the Lord's Name purifies the fallen. One to whom the Lord's service is pleasing has attained the supreme state; (remembering) the Lord, Har Har, is the most excellent work. The Lord is the excellent work: let the Lord's Name be repeated; by repeating the Lord, one becomes steady. (That one) wipes out the sorrows of both birth and death, and in Sahaj sleeps in peace. O Lord, Har Har, O Master, show your grace, that (we) may repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Atam Ram, the all-pervading. The Lord, Har Har, the Creator, is the destroyer of sorrow; the Lord's Name purifies the fallen. In Kalyug the treasure of the Lord's Name is the most excellent; let the Lord be repeated in love of the True Guru. Through the Guru, read of the Lord; through the Guru, hear of the Lord; repeating and hearing of the Lord, sorrow departs. Repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har, sorrow has been destroyed; through the Lord's Name, supreme peace has been found. The True Guru's wisdom has blazed up, there is light in the heart, and the darkness of ignorance is dispelled. They alone have worshipped the Name of the Lord, Har Har, on whose foreheads (this) was written from the very beginning. In Kalyug the treasure of the Lord's Name is the most excellent; let the Lord be repeated in love of the True Guru. One in whose mind the Lord, Har Har, has become dear has found supreme peace, and earned the Lord as profit: the state beyond all desire. He has formed love for the Lord, the Lord's Name is his companion, and doubt and coming and going are ended. Coming and going, doubt and fear have fled, as he has sung the virtues of the Lord, Har Har Har. The sins and sorrows of birth after birth have been washed away, and he is absorbed in the Name of the Lord, Har Har. Those who have meditated on the Lord, as was written in their lot from the beginning: their life is fruitful and accepted. One in whose mind the Lord, Har Har, has become dear has found supreme peace, and earned the Lord as profit: the state beyond all desire. Those to whom the Lord seems sweet are the foremost of people; they are the exalted ones, the people of the Lord, Har Har. Their greatness is the Lord's Name, their companion the Lord's Name; through the Guru's Shabad, they enjoy the Lord's delight. Enjoying the Lord's delight, they stay wholly unattached; by great good fortune they have found the Lord's delight. Blessed are they, great, true and perfect beings, who through the Guru's teaching have meditated on the Naam. Servant Nanak begs for the dust of the Saadh's (the Guru's) feet; grief and separation in the mind are ended. Those to whom the Lord seems sweet are the foremost of people; they are the exalted ones, the people of the Lord, Har Har. ॥4॥
445.1: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). In Satjug everyone was contentment embodied; dharma stood on all four feet, and (hearts) dwelt in meditation (on the Lord). (People) sang the Lord with mind and body, and found supreme peace; in their hearts was the Lord, and the knowledge of the Lord's virtues. The knowledge of (his) virtues was their wealth; through the Lord, Har Har, their lives were fulfilled, and glory came through the Guru. Within and without (they saw) the one Lord God alone, and no other besides. One who fixed loving attention on the Lord, Har Har, with the Lord's Name as companion, gains honour in the Lord's court. In Satjug everyone was contentment embodied; dharma stood on all four feet, and (hearts) dwelt in meditation (on the Lord). (Then) came the age of Treta; force took hold within (people), and they practised the disciplines of chastity and self-restraint. The fourth foot (of dharma) slipped, and it stood on three; anger blazed in mind and heart. In mind and heart was anger, a deadly poison; kings marched against (one another), and by fighting they reaped pain. The sickness of possessiveness took hold within (them), and Haumai and pride grew great. (Those on whom) my Master, the Lord, Har Har, showed grace have the poison removed through the Guru's teaching, through the Lord's Name. (Then) came the age of Treta; force took hold within (people), and they practised the disciplines of chastity and self-restraint. (Then) came the age of Duapar; (people) were led astray by doubt; the Lord created the gopis and Kaanh (Krishna). They practised austerities, enduring the heat (of fires), began sacrifices and works of merit, and performed rituals and rites in plenty. With rituals and rites performed, two feet (of dharma) slipped away, and it stood held up on two. Warriors fought many mighty wars; in Haumai one burns and sets others burning. (One whom) the Lord, merciful to the meek, brings to the Guru, the Saadh, has his filth washed away on meeting the True Guru. (Then) came the age of Duapar; (people) were led astray by doubt; the Lord created the gopis and Kaanh (Krishna). (Then) the Lord made Kalyug; three feet (of dharma) slipped away, and it stands held up on the fourth foot (alone). (One who) lives the Guru's Shabad has found the medicine, the Lord; through the Lord's praise, the Lord bestows peace. The season of the Lord's praise has come; the Lord's Name is (true) glory; (the Gurmukh) has made the crop of the Name of the Lord, Har Har, spring up.
