In Kalyug, (whoever) sows a seed other than the Name loses all the profit and the capital (too). Servant Nanak has found the Perfect Guru, who has made the Name shine forth in (his) mind and heart. (Then) the Lord made Kalyug; three feet (of dharma) slipped away, and it stands held up on the fourth foot (alone). ॥4॥

Satjug, Treta, Duapar and Kalyug are the four ages of the Puranas; dharma, pictured as a bull, stands on four feet in Satjug and loses one in each age after. Kaanh is Krishna, whom the Puranas place in Duapar among the gopis, the herdswomen of Braj.
446.1: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). One whose mind loves the Lord's praise has attained the supreme state; to mind and body the Lord has grown sweet. He has found the relish of the Lord, Har Har, and through the Guru's teaching meditated on the Lord; the fortune written of old on his forehead from the start (has awoken). Such was the fortune on his forehead from the start: through the Lord's Name he found the Husband, and through the Name he sang the Lord's virtues. On his forehead the jewel of deep love has shone out; through his Name the Lord has made him beautiful. His light has merged in the Light; he has found God; meeting the True Guru, his mind is won over. One whose mind loves the Lord's praise has attained the supreme state; to mind and body the Lord has grown sweet. Those who sang the praise of the Lord, Har Har, attained the supreme state; those servants are excellent and foremost. We wait upon their feet and wash their feet moment by moment, those to whom the Lord is sweet. (Those to whom) the Lord is sweet have found supreme peace; on their faces glows the lovely bloom of good fortune. Through the Guru's teaching they sang of the Lord, put the Lord's garland upon their breast, and kept the Lord's Name at their throat. He looks on all with one eye, seeing all alike, and recognises the all-pervading Lord (Atam Ram) in all. Those who sang the praise of the Lord, Har Har, attained the supreme state; those servants are excellent and foremost. One whose mind loves the Sat Sangat has a tongue steeped in the Lord; in the Sangat the Lord's relish is found. He has worshipped the Lord, Har Har, and blossomed through the Guru's Shabad; (for him) there is no other, no second. There is no other: the Lord alone is Amrit; one who has drunk it knows what it is. Blessed, blessed is the Perfect Guru, (through whom) God is found; held to the Sangat, one recognises the Name. He serves the Name alone and worships the Name alone; without the Name he has no other. One whose mind loves the Sat Sangat has a tongue steeped in the Lord; in the Sangat the Lord's relish is found. O Lord, O God, show mercy: carry us stones across, and lift us out through the Shabad, in your love. Caught in the mire of attachment, we are sinking down; O Lord God, give (us) your arm to hold. (The one to whom) God gave his arm gained the highest understanding, and that servant clung to the Guru's feet. He repeated and worshipped the Name of the Lord, Har Har; on his face and forehead good fortune (awoke). The Lord has shown grace to servant Nanak, and made the Lord, Har Har, sweet to his mind. O Lord, O God, show mercy: carry us stones across, and lift us out through the Shabad, in your love. ॥4॥
447.1: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). In their minds they repeat the Naam; the Lord, Har Har, is dear to their minds; in the minds of the Lord's devotees is eager longing. Those who have died (to self) and live (anew) drink Amrit; through the Guru's teaching, love (for the Lord) has taken hold in their minds. In the mind is love for the Lord, Har Har, (when) the Guru shows grace; one is liberated while yet alive, and there is peace. In life and in death they are at ease through the Lord's Name; in their minds and hearts is that Lord, Har Har. The Lord, Har Har, has come to dwell in their minds; through the Guru's teaching the Lord has become their delight; they drink the relish of the Lord in deep draughts. In their minds they repeat the Naam; the Lord, Har Har, is dear to their minds; in the minds of the Lord's devotees is eager longing. In the world no one likes to die; each keeps hiding himself, lest Jam seize him and take him away. (But) within and without is the one Lord God; this life cannot be kept (hidden from him). How can the life be kept, when the Lord wants back what is his? The One whose thing it is takes it away. The manmukhs wander about wailing piteously, trying every medicine and cure. God, the Master, whose thing it is, takes it; his servants are saved (from the fear of death) by living the Shabad. In the world no one likes to die; each keeps hiding himself, lest Jam seize him and take him away. Death is written from the start; through the Guru it is made beautiful; the servants are saved by meditation on the Lord, Har Har. Through the Lord they gained honour, through the Lord's Name glory; robed (in honour), they go to the Lord's court. Robed in honour in the Lord's court, made whole through the Lord's Name, they have found peace from the Lord's Name. The sorrows of both birth and death are wiped away (for them), and they are merged in the Name of the Lord, of Ram. The Lord's servants and God have blended into one; the Lord's servants and God are alike. Death is written from the start; through the Guru it is made beautiful; the servants are saved by meditation on the Lord, Har Har. The world is born and perishes, perishing again and again; clinging (to the Lord) through the Guru, one becomes steady. The Guru makes the mantra (of the Name) firm (within), and makes one savour the Lord with delight; the Lord lets his Amrit trickle into the mouth. (One who) has found the relish of the Lord's Amrit is brought back to life from death, and never dies again. Through the Name of the Lord, Har Har, he has attained the deathless state; he remains merged in the Lord's Name. For servant Nanak the Name is the support and the prop; without the Name there is no other. The world is born and perishes, perishing again and again; clinging (to the Lord) through the Guru, one becomes steady. ॥4॥
448.1: Raag Asa, a Chhant, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Great is my Govind, beyond reach, beyond the senses, the Primal, Stainless and Formless One. His state cannot be told; his greatness is beyond measure; my Govind is unseen and boundless. Govind is unseen, boundless, beyond the farthest beyond; he alone knows himself. What can these poor creatures be called, that any could speak of you and describe you? (O Lord,) one on whom you cast your gracious glance reflects (on you) through the Guru. Great is my Govind, beyond reach, beyond the senses, the Primal, Stainless and Formless One. You are the Primal Being, beyond the farthest beyond, the Creator; your far shore cannot be found. You dwell in every heart, through all without a break, pervading all. The Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, is within every heart; no one has found his end. He has no form and no feature; he is unseen, beyond the senses; through the Guru the Unknowable is made known. (Such a one) lives in bliss always, day and night, and is absorbed in the Name in Sahaj. You are the Primal Being, beyond the farthest beyond, the Creator; your far shore cannot be found. You are the True One, the Supreme God, imperishable for ever; O Lord, Har Har, (you are) the treasure of virtues. The Lord God, Har Har, is One; there is no other; you yourself are the all-pervading, all-knowing Being. You are the all-knowing Being, you are foremost; no other is as great as you. Your Word (your Hukam) is everywhere, and you alone are at work in all; what you yourself do, that comes to pass. The One Lord alone pervades all; through the Guru the Lord's Name is perceived. You are the True One, the Supreme God, imperishable for ever; O Lord, Har Har, (you are) the treasure of virtues. O Creator, you yourself are all, and all glory is yours; as it pleases you, so make (us) walk. As it pleases you yourself, so you make (all) walk; all are held within your Word. When it pleases you, all merge in the Word; through your Word comes glory. Through the Guru understanding is gained and self is lost, and one stays absorbed in the Word. Your Word is beyond the senses; it is found through the Guru; O Nanak, (the one who finds it) merges in the Name. O Creator, you yourself are all, and all glory is yours; as it pleases you, so make (us) walk. ॥4॥
448.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Asa, Ghar 4, Chhants, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). (My) eyes are moist with the Lord's Amrit, and (my) mind is dyed in (his) love. The Lord put (my) mind to the touchstone, and it (proved) pure gold. Through the Guru (I) am dyed deep red (with love); my mind and body are drenched (in that colour). Servant Nanak is steeped in the musk (of the Name); his whole life is blessed, blessed. The Lord's Bani of love has pierced my mind, like arrows with keen points. Only one struck by the pang of the Beloved's love knows how it is borne. He is called liberated while yet alive, who dies (to self) and, so dead, lives. O Lord, unite servant Nanak with the True Guru, (by whom) the world (-ocean), so hard to cross, is crossed. We, foolish and ignorant, have come to your refuge; meet (us), O Govind, whose plays are many. Through the Perfect Guru I have found the Lord; one thing I ask: devotion to the Lord. My mind and body have blossomed through the Shabad, repeating (the Name of) the Lord of endless waves. Meeting the Sants, in the Sat Sangat, the Lord is found, O Nanak. Hear (my) plea, O Lord God, kind to the lowly, O Lord King. I beg for the shelter of the Lord's Name, that I may take the Lord, Har Har, into my mouth. To love devotion is the Lord's age-old way; the Lord has kept (his devotees') honour. Servant Nanak has come to (the Lord's) refuge; through the Name the Lord has carried him across. ॥4॥
449.1: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Through the Guru, searching and searching, (I) have found the Lord, my Friend. Within the fortress of the body, (now) gold, the Lord, Har Har, is made manifest. The Lord, Har Har, is a diamond, a jewel, and my mind and body are pierced through (by him). By great fortune written from the start (I) have found the Lord; Nanak is steeped in (his) relish. Every day I stand and ask the way (to my Husband), a young bride in the bloom of youth. O Guru, make (me) remember the Name of the Lord, Har Har, (that I may) walk the Lord's path. In my mind and body the Name is the support; (it) has burnt away the poison of Haumai. O Lord, unite servant Nanak with the True Guru; (through him) the Lord, Har Har, Banwali, is met. O Beloved, come and meet me through the Guru; I have been parted (from you) so long. My mind and body are deeply forlorn; O Lord, (my) eyes are wet with (tears of love). O Guru, show me the beloved Lord God, that meeting the Lord (my) mind may be content. (The Guru) has set me, the fool Nanak, to a task: the Lord's work. The Guru's frame is steeped in Amrit; he sprinkles Amrit (all around). Those whose minds love the Guru's Bani drink deep of the Amrit and are fulfilled. The Guru being pleased, they have found the Lord, and their being pushed about (from birth to birth) is ended. The Lord's servant has become the Lord, Har Har; Nanak and the Lord are one. ॥4॥
449.2: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The storehouses of the Lord's devotion, which is Amrit, are with the Guru, the True Guru. The Guru, the True Guru, is the Banker, ever true; to the Sikh he gives the Lord as his stock. Blessed, blessed is the trader, (and blessed his) trade; the Guru, the Banker, praises him. Says servant Nanak: they alone have found the Guru on whose foreheads (this) was written from the start. (O Lord,) you are our true Banker, our Master; the whole world is (your) trader. All the vessels (bodies) you yourself have fashioned; what lies within (them), O Lord, is yours. What you put in the vessel, that alone comes out; what can any poor creature do? On servant Nanak the Lord has bestowed the treasure of the Lord's devotion. Which of your virtues can we tell, O Master? You are boundless, without limit. Let (us) praise the Lord's Name day and night; this is (our) hope and support. We are fools and know nothing at all; how can we find (your) far shore? Servant Nanak is the Lord's slave, a water-carrier for the Lord's slaves. Save (us) as it pleases you; we have come to your refuge, O God. We go astray and spoil (our lives) day and night; O Lord, keep our honour. We are children; you are (our) Guru and Father: give (us) counsel and make (us) understand. Servant Nanak is called the Lord's slave; O Lord, keep his honour. ॥4॥
450.1: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Those on whose foreheads the Lord wrote (this) from the beginning have met the True Guru. (Their) darkness of ignorance is cut away, and the Guru's wisdom has been lit (like a lamp) in the heart. (They) have found the Lord, the precious jewel, which never leaves (them) again. O servant Nanak, they have worshipped the Naam, and worshipping, have met the Lord. Those who have not remembered such a Name of the Lord: why did they come into the world? This human birth is so hard to obtain; without the Name it all goes to waste. One who has not sown the Lord's Name now, in the sowing season, what will he eat hereafter, when hungry? For the manmukhs there is birth again; O Nanak, this is what pleases the Lord. O Lord, you (are the Master of all); everyone is yours; you have created all. Nothing at all is in anyone's hands; all walk as (you) make them walk. Those whom you unite (with yourself), O Beloved, they alone meet you, those who are pleasing to your mind, O Lord. O servant Nanak, (those who) have met the True Guru, (he) carries (them) across through the Lord's Name. One sings in raags, one with the sounds of instruments, one with the Vedas, in many ways, (yet so) the Lord is not won over. Those who have deceit and vice within: what is gained by their weeping? The Lord, the Creator, knows everything, though one put a hand over the head of the disease (to hide it). O Nanak, those whose hearts are made pure through the Guru win the Lord by devotion to the Lord. ॥4॥
450.2: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Those within whom is the love of the Lord, Har Har, are people of refined and wise mind. Even if outwardly they speak with a slip or a mistake, they are still most pleasing to the Lord. The Lord's Sants have no other place (but the Lord); the Lord is the honour of those without honour. O servant Nanak, (for the Sants) the Naam is the court where they plead; the Lord is the strength by which they are strong. Wherever my True Guru goes and sits, that place becomes beautiful. The Guru's Sikhs sought out that place, and took its dust and put it on their faces. The toil of the Guru's Sikhs who meditated on the Lord's Name was accepted. Those who have worshipped the True Guru, Nanak: the Lord makes (all the world) worship them. O Lord, in the minds of the Guru's Sikhs is love for you, love for your Name. They serve (him), knowing (him) for the Perfect True Guru, and (their) hunger and possessiveness depart. All the hunger of the Guru's Sikhs is gone, and following them, many others eat (the food of the Name). O servant Nanak, (those who) have sown the merit of the Lord, never again run short of the Lord's merit. There is rejoicing in the minds of the Guru's Sikhs who have seen my True Guru. If someone tells them anything of the Lord's Name, he seems sweet to the minds of the Guru's Sikhs. The Guru's Sikhs with whom my True Guru is pleased are robed in honour in the Lord's court. Servant Nanak has become (one with) the Lord, Har Har; the Lord, Har Har, has come to dwell in his mind. ॥4॥
451.1: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Those who have met my Perfect True Guru, he makes the Lord's Name firm within them. All the craving and hunger of one who meditates on the Lord's Name are taken away. Jam does not come near any who keep meditating on the Name of the Lord, Har Har. O Lord, show mercy to servant Nanak, that he may repeat the Lord's Name day after day, and through the Lord's Name carry (others) across. Those who have meditated on the Naam through the Guru meet no obstacle again. Those who have won the favour of the True Guru, the mighty one, are honoured by everyone. Those who have served the beloved True Guru have peace for ever. Those who have met the True Guru, Nanak, have met the Lord himself. Those within whom is love (for the Lord) through the Guru: the Lord is their protector. What slander can anyone speak of those to whom the Lord's Name is dear? Those whose minds are reconciled with the Lord: all the wicked strike out (at them) in vain. O servant Nanak, (those who) have meditated on the Naam: the Lord is (their) protector. Age after age the Lord creates devotees, and has ever kept their honour. The Lord killed the wicked Harnakhash and carried Prahlad across. (He) turned his back on the proud and the slanderers, and turned his face to Namdev. Servant Nanak has served such a Lord, who delivers (him) at the last. ॥4॥

Prahlad was the son of the demon king Harnakhash (Hiranyakashipu) and held to devotion to God through all his father's torments; in the Puranas, God took the form of Narasimha, the Man-Lion, and killed Harnakhash.
By tradition, the priests of a temple (at Aundha) put Bhagat Namdev, a calico printer by caste, out from before it; he sat singing God's praises at the back, and the temple turned round to face him.
451.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 5, a Chhant, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O my mind, wanderer in strange lands, O beloved, come home. Meet the Guru, the Lord's own form, O my beloved, and the Lord will dwell in (your) home. Enjoy delight in (his) love, O my beloved, (if) the Lord shows grace. Guru Nanak, when pleased, O my beloved, unites (one) with the Lord. I have not loved (him) and tasted (his) love, O my beloved. Craving in the mind is not quenched, O my beloved; ever it hopes (for more). Day by day youth passes, O my beloved, and Jam watches the breaths. She is the happy bride with the jewel of fortune, O my beloved, who, O Nanak, keeps the Lord in her heart. My eyes are steeped in (love of) the Husband, O my beloved, as the chatrik (rain-bird longs) for the raindrop. The mind has grown cool, O my beloved, drinking the drop of the Lord (the Name). The pain of parting in the body keeps (me) awake, O my beloved; sleep does not come at all. I have found the Lord, my Friend, O my beloved; O Nanak, (it is) through the attunement the Guru gives. Chet has come, and spring, O my beloved, a fine season. Without the Husband, O my beloved, dust blows in (my) courtyard. With hope in (my) mind, O my beloved, (I am) downcast, and (my) two eyes are fixed (on his path). Seeing Guru Nanak, O my beloved, I have blossomed, as a mother (at the sight of) her son. The True Guru has told (me) the stories and discourses of the Lord, O my beloved. To the Guru I am a sacrifice, O my beloved, who has brought about (my) union with the Lord. The Lord has made all (my) hopes come true, O my beloved; I have found the fruit the mind longed for. The Lord is pleased, O my beloved, and servant Nanak is absorbed in the Name. Without the beloved Lord, I will not play the game of love (with anyone). How may I find the Guru, holding on to whom I may see the Beloved? O Lord, dear Giver, unite (me) with the Guru; through the Guru I shall meet (you) face to face. I have found Guru Nanak, O my beloved; such was the writ on (my) forehead from the beginning. ॥6॥
The chatrik (rain-bird, the pied cuckoo) is held in Indian poetry to drink only the raindrop that falls under the Swati star, and no other water, and to cry out for it.
452.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Raag Asa, Ghar 1, Chhants, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Bliss upon bliss, great bliss (is within me): I have seen that God. I have tasted, tasted the Lord's sweet essence. The Lord's sweet essence has come to dwell in the mind; the True Guru is pleased, and Sahaj has come. The home (of the heart) is peopled, songs of joy are sung, and those five villains have fled. (We) are cooled and satisfied by the Amrit Bani; the friend, the Sant, has been the go-between (to unite us with God). Says Nanak, my mind is reconciled with the Lord; I have seen that God with my eyes. Adorned, adorned are my splendid doors. My guests, my guests are the beloved Sants. The beloved Sants have set (my) affairs right; bowing (to them), (we) have taken up (their) service. He himself is the groom's party, himself the bride's kin, himself the Master (the groom), himself the deity (before whom the wedding is made). He himself sets his own affair right; he himself gives the support. Says Nanak, the Husband is seated in (my) home, and the splendid doors are adorned. The nine treasures, the nine treasures have come into my home. I have found everything, everything, meditating on the Naam. I meditate on the Naam of Govind, my companion for ever, who brings Sahaj and love. (My) anxious reckoning is wiped out, (my) running about is ended; anxiety of mind never besets (me). Govind resounds (within), unstruck music plays, a wondrous splendour has been made. Says Nanak, the Husband is with me; so I have found the nine treasures. Delighted, delighted are my brothers and all my friends. Meeting the Guru, I have won the hardest, hardest arena. Meeting the Guru I have won; I have repeated (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, and the wall of the fortress of doubt has broken. I have found the treasure, a vast store of wealth; (God) himself stands by me to help me. He alone is wise, he alone is foremost, whom God has taken as his own. Says Nanak, when the Master is on (one's) side, then brothers and friends rejoice. ॥4॥
The nine treasures (nidhis): by tradition, the nine treasures of Kuber, the god of wealth; that is, all the riches of the world.
Janji: one of the groom's wedding party (janj); manji: one of the bride's people, the hosts who serve the party.
453.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Beyond telling, beyond telling is the story of the Lord; nothing of it can be known. Men of godly nature and silent sages utter (his praise), resting in Sahaj. In Sahaj they have uttered the Amrit Bani, and fixed their love on (his) lotus feet. Repeating (the Name of) the One God, unseen and stainless, they have found the fruit the mind longed for. Casting off pride, attachment, vice and duality, (their) light has merged in the Light. Nanak prays: by the Guru's grace, the Lord's love is enjoyed for ever. The Lord's Sants, the Lord's Sants are my friends, companions and helpers. By great fortune, by great fortune I have found the Sat Sangat. One who finds it by great fortune meditates on the Naam, and (his) pains and torments are lifted. (One who) clings to the Guru's feet: doubt and fear flee, and he has wiped out self-conceit from within himself. (One whom) God in his grace has united with himself never parts (from him) to go anywhere. Nanak prays: (I am) your servant, O Lord, for ever in your refuge. At the Lord's door, at your door, O Lord, your beloved devotees look beautiful. To them I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, ever a sacrifice. Ever a sacrifice, I bow to them, meeting whom God is known. The Perfect Purakh, the Maker of all, pervades every heart and every place. (One who) has found the Perfect Guru and meditated on the Naam does not lose (his) life in the gamble. Nanak prays: (I am) in your refuge; show mercy and save (me). Endless, endless are your virtues; how many can I sing? Your feet, the dust of your feet I gain by great fortune. Bathing in the dust of the Lord's (feet), filth is washed away and the pains of birth and death are lifted. Within and without, the Supreme God is ever present, ever with (us). Through Kirtan sorrows are erased and well-being comes; (so) I shall not be cast into a womb again. Nanak prays: in the Guru's refuge one crosses over; (so) may I be pleasing to my God. ॥4॥
453.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 4, a Chhant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The mind pierced by the Lord's lotus feet finds nothing else sweet. Joining the company of the Sants, (one) has worshipped (him), and has seen the Lord in every heart. (One) has seen the Lord in every heart, Amrit has come to dwell (within), and the pains of birth and death have fled. (One) has sung of the treasure of virtues, has erased all pain, and the knot of Haumai has come undone. The Beloved, full of Sahaj and love, does not leave (him) to go away; the mind is dyed the fast colour of madder. O Nanak, (the mind) pierced by the Lord's lotus feet finds nothing else sweet. As the fish is steeped in water, so (the Sants) are intoxicated with the essence of Ram. (Those whom) the Perfect Guru has taught are pleasing to (the Lord), the life and liberation (of all). The Master, the life and liberation (of all), the Knower of hearts, has himself attached (them) to his hem. The Lord, the precious jewel, has shone forth (in them); he fills all, and does not leave (them) to go anywhere. God the Master is accomplished, beautiful in form and all-knowing; his gifts never run out. As the fish is steeped in the company of water, (so,) O Nanak, (the Sants) are intoxicated with the Lord. As the chatrik begs for the raindrop, (so to them) the Lord is the support of life. More than wealth, treasure, sons, brothers and friends, more than all, (the Lord) is dear (to them). Dearer than all is (he,) the Purakh beyond all, whose state cannot be known. (For them) the Lord is never forgotten with any breath or morsel; through the Guru's Shabad (his) love is enjoyed. God, the Purakh, is the life of the world; the Sants drink (his) essence, and repeating (his Name), cast off doubt, attachment and pain. As the chatrik begs for the raindrop, (so,) O Nanak, the Lord is dear (to them). (Those who) have met their Narayan have their heart's desire fulfilled. Meeting the valiant Guru, (their) wall of doubt has fallen. (They) have found the Perfect Guru, as was written before (in their lot) by the Merciful to the meek, the treasure of all. In the beginning, the middle and the end there is that God alone, the beautiful, the great Gopal. The dust (of the feet) of the Saadh, which purifies the fallen, (brings) abundant peace, Sahaj and bliss. O Nanak, (those who) have met the Lord Narayan have their heart's desire fulfilled. ॥4॥
454.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 6, Chhants, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Those on whom God becomes merciful, they alone repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har. O Nanak, as soon as they meet the Saadh Sangat, their love is drawn to Ram. ॥1॥
454.2: Such is the way of water's love for milk: then, (on the fire,) it lets no heat touch the milk; O mind, such is love for the Lord. Then the bumblebee is caught in the lotus, absorbed in its fragrance, and does not stir from it for even a moment. (So) one should not stir from love for the Lord for even a moment; all adornments and all pleasures should be offered up (to it). Where cries of pain are heard and the path of Jam is spoken of, there, in the Saadh Sangat, one knows no fear. Sing the praise of Govind, (sing) his virtues: he takes away all sins and sorrows. Says Nanak: O mind, (sing) the chhants of praise of Govind, the Lord, and keep love for the Lord; O mind, such is love for the Lord. As the fish (loves) the water and, (without it,) has no peace for even a moment, O mind, love (the Lord) like that. As is the thirst of the chatrik, which every moment begs for the drop and calls: Rain, O beautiful cloud! (So) one should love the Lord, give him this mind, and fix one's consciousness wholly on Murari. One should not be proud, but fall into his refuge and be a sacrifice to the sight of him. When the Guru is well pleased, the bride sends her true message: Meet me, my Husband, from whom I am parted. Says Nanak: (sing) the chhants of praise of the infinite Master; one should love the Lord. O mind, love (the Lord) like that. The chakvi loves the sun and keeps it in her thoughts; great is her longing: when shall the sun be seen? The koel loves the mango and sings sweetly; O mind, (so) love the Lord. One should love the Lord and not be proud; all (here) are guests for one night. Why then have you now taken to pleasures and built up attachment? Naked (all) come and (naked they) go. One should take the Saadh's refuge and fall at his feet, (and the mind is) steady; then the attachment you have formed will break. Says Nanak: (sing) the chhants of praise of the merciful, all-pervading Lord; O mind, love the Lord (as the chakvi longs): when shall the sun be seen? As the deer at night, hearing the sound (of the hunter's bell) with its ears, gives its heart (to it), O mind, love (the Lord) like that. As a young wife, bound in love to her husband, serves her beloved, (so) one should give this mind to the Beloved. One should give the mind to the Beloved and enjoy (union with him); (she who does so) delights in all joys and pleasures. She has found her own Husband, has dyed herself the deep red (of love), and the Friend of ages long past has met (her). (She says:) When the Guru became the go-between, I saw (him) with my eyes; none is seen like the Husband. Says Nanak: O mind, (sing) the chhants of praise of the merciful, enchanting Lord; one should grasp the Lord's feet. O mind, love (him) like that. ॥4॥
The chakvi (ruddy shelduck), parted from her mate at night, waits all night for the sunrise.
Hunters draw the deer at night with the sound of a bell (ghanda hera); the deer gives up its life to that sound.
455.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (The bride) wandered from forest to forest, searching, and grew weary of searching deep. O Nanak, when the Saadh was met, the Lord was found within the mind. ॥1॥
455.2: He whom countless munis (silent sages) and many ascetics search for, whom millions of Brahmas and men of knowledge worship, chanting their chants; with chants, austerities, self-restraint, rites, worship, countless purifications and prostrations, journeying over the whole earth and bathing at tiraths, (people strive) to meet him, the Immaculate One: (O Lord,) humans, forests, grasses, beasts and birds, all of them worship you. O merciful, beloved Gobind! O Nanak, join the Saadh Sangat: (there) liberation is gained. Millions of Vishnu's incarnations, and Shivas with matted hair, long for you, O merciful one; in mind and body (they feel) a boundless yearning. O infinite, inaccessible Gobind, Master, God who fulfils all, Lord! Gods, Siddhas, ganas and gandharvas meditate on you; yakshas and kinnars (beings of the heavens) utter your praises. Millions of Indras and countless gods repeat (your Name), O Master, and hail your victory. O Master of the masterless, merciful one! O Nanak, joining the Saadh Sangat one is saved. He whom millions of goddesses serve, and Lakshmi in countless ways; whom the hidden and the manifest worship, (and) wind and water, day and night; on whom the stars, the moon and the sun meditate, (of whom) earth and sky sing; on whom all the sources of life and all the tongues ever meditate; whose Name is chanted by the Simritis and Puranas, the four Vedas and six Shastras: he, the purifier of the fallen, Lover of devotion, O Nanak, is met in the true company. As much as God has made known (to me), so much has (my) tongue spoken. Those beyond (my) knowing who serve (him) cannot be counted. The Master is unmanifest, countless, unfathomable; he is within all and outside all. All are beggars, he alone the Giver; he is not far, but with (all), plain to see. He has come under the sway of his devotees; those beings who have met (him), how is their glory to be reckoned? May Nanak receive this gift and this honour: to place (his) head at the feet of the Saadhs. ॥4॥
456.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Make the effort, O fortunate ones: remember the Lord King, Har Har, by remembering whom, O Nanak, all comforts come, and pain, suffering and wandering doubt depart. ॥1॥
456.2: In repeating the Name of Gobind, one should never be slothful. Meeting the company of the Saadh, one does not have to go to the city of Jam. Pain, suffering and fear do not seize (one); remembering the Naam, (one is) ever at peace. With every breath worship the Lord, Har Har; meditate on that God in the mind and with the mouth. O kind, merciful one, home of all delight, treasure of virtues: in your mercy, set (me) to your service. Nanak makes his plea and meditates on (your) feet: in repeating the Name of Gobind, one should never be slothful. Pure is the Name of the Immaculate One, the purifier of the fallen. The salve of the Guru's wisdom destroys the darkness of doubt. With the salve of the Guru's wisdom (one sees that) God, the Immaculate, fills water, land and sky. One in whose heart (he) dwells for even an instant, his every grief is wiped away. The Master, of unfathomable wisdom, all-powerful, is the destroyer of the fear of all. Nanak makes his plea and meditates on (his) feet: pure is the Name of the Immaculate One, the purifier of the fallen. I have taken your shelter, O Gopal, merciful one, treasure of grace. My support is your feet; in your refuge is (my) fulfilment. The feet of the Lord, the Master, the Cause of causes, Har Hare, are the saviour of the fallen; they carry (beings) across the dreadful world-ocean; remembering the Name, many have crossed. (You are) at the beginning and at the end; beings without number search for (you). (I) have heard that the company of the Sants is the way of deliverance. Nanak makes his plea and meditates on (your) feet: I have taken your shelter, O Gopal, merciful one, treasure of grace. The Lord is the Lover of devotion: he himself has made this his pledged way. Wherever the Sants worship (him), there he becomes manifest. God himself has merged (them in himself), and with natural ease has accomplished the tasks of his devotees. (Singing) the Lord's praise (they know) bliss and great joy, and all sorrows are forgotten. He whose wondrous light shines in the ten directions, the One alone, is seen there. Nanak makes his plea and meditates on (his) feet: the Lord is the Lover of devotion: he himself has made this his pledged way. ॥4॥
457.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Lasting is the marriage of the Sants: (their Husband) neither dies nor goes away. She in whose home the Lord is the Husband enjoys (his union) for ever. That God is imperishable, unmanifest, ever new and pure. The Master is not far, he is ever present; he fills the ten directions, for ever and ever. (He is) the Lord of the breath of life, from whom (the high) state and understanding come; through love for the Beloved, the Beloved grows ever dearer. Nanak says, and through the Guru's word one comes to know it: lasting is the marriage of the Sants: (their Husband) neither dies nor goes away. She whose Husband is Ram has great bliss (within). Happy is that wife, and her glory is full and complete. Honour, greatness, well-being and the Lord's praise (are hers); that God, the noble one, is with her. All siddhis and the nine treasures are in that home; nothing is lacking, everything is (there). Sweet is her speech, the Husband honours her; her marriage is made lasting. Nanak says, and through the Guru's word one comes to know it: she whose Husband is Ram has great bliss (within). Come, my friend, let us go to the Sant and give ourselves to (his) service. I would grind (corn for him) and wash (his) feet; let us give up the self. Giving up the self, anguish ends; let us make no show of ourselves. Let us take (his) refuge and accept (his will): whatever he does, in that let us find comfort. Becoming the handmaid of (his) servants, giving up listlessness, with palms joined let us keep awake day and night. Nanak says, and through the Guru's word one comes to know it: come, my friend, let us go to the Sant and give ourselves to (his) service. Those on whose foreheads (good) fortune (is written) are set to (his) service. Fulfilled is the hope of those who have found the Saadh Sangat. In the Saadh Sangat, in the Lord's love, they take to the remembrance of Gobind. Doubt, attachment, vice and duality: all of these they have given up. Peace, Sahaj and love have come to dwell in (their) minds; in bliss and joy they have sung (his) praises. Nanak says, and through the Guru's word one comes to know it: those on whose foreheads (good) fortune (is written) are set to (his) service. ॥4॥
457.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Jamkaal says nothing to one who repeats the Name of the Lord, Har Har. O Nanak, mind and body are at peace, and in the end Gopal is met. ॥1॥
457.3: (O Lord,) may I join the company of the Sants; save me. With palms joined I make my plea: give (me) the Name of the Lord, Har Har. By your mercy, may I beg for the Lord's Name, fall at (your) feet and give up pride. May I run nowhere (else), but find (your) refuge; O God, embodiment of compassion, show mercy. O all-powerful, indescribable, infinite, pure Master, hear this my plea. With palms joined Nanak begs for (this) gift: put an end to (my) birth and death. (O God, I am) a wrongdoer, without understanding, without virtue, without a protector, and lowly. (I am) foolish, hard of heart and of no lineage; the mire of attachment has seized (me). (On me is) the filth of deeds done in doubt, of ego and of mine-ness; death does not come to (my) mind. (I) cling to the play of women, the pleasures of Maya and ignorance. Youth is fading, old age grows; death, standing by, watches (my) days. Nanak humbly prays: my hope is in you; keep (me), the lowly one, in the refuge of the Saadh. (I) have wandered through countless births and suffered the great hardships of the life-forms. (I) have stayed clinging to sweet pleasures and gold. Carrying countless burdens (of sin), (I) have come wandering, and have run through many foreign lands. Now (I) have taken the shelter of God, Murari; in the Name of the Lord are all comforts. O beloved God, the Protector: nothing has been done, nor can be done, by me. Says Nanak: (O God,) by your grace come peace, Sahaj and bliss, and (one) crosses the world (-ocean). (God) has saved even those who were (devotees) in name alone; what doubt (then) for (true) devotees? By whatever means (you can), hear the praise of the Lord, Har Har, with your ears. O man of understanding, hearing with your ears the Bani (of his praise), you will find the treasure within your mind. (Those) dyed in the love of the Lord, God, the Maker, sing the virtues of Ram. If the earth were paper, the forests pens, and the wind the writer, (even then) the end of the Infinite cannot be found. Nanak has taken the refuge of (his) feet. ॥4॥
458.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Lord, the Master of all beings: (I) have taken his refuge. (My) life has become fearless, (and) all anxiety has lifted. (Him I) have known as mother, father, son, friend, well-wisher, beloved and kin. The Guru brought (me) to meet (him), and he took (me) by the hand and held (me) to his breast; the Sants speak his spotless praise. Infinite are (his) virtues, countless his glories; (his) worth cannot be told at all. God is One (and) many, the unseen Master; Nanak has taken his shelter. When (God) himself became (my) helper, the world (-ocean) became the water of Amrit. The Name of Ram is the necklace of (my) heart; the days of poison are gone. Doubt is gone, attachment and vices are destroyed, (and) all coming into births has ceased. The oceans of fire have become cool, holding on to the hem of the Saadh. Govind, Gopal, the merciful, the all-powerful: with the Saadh, proclaim the Lord's victory, hail, hail. O Nanak, meditating on the Name of the Perfect (Lord), the supreme state is gained in the Saadh Sangat. Wherever I look, there the One alone is with (me), pervading. He himself dwells in every heart; some rare one has realised (this). Filling water, land and sky completely, he is contained in the worm and the elephant (alike). In the beginning, the end and the middle he alone (is); by the Guru's grace (this) is known. Brahm has spread out (all this), (all) is the play of Brahm; (his) servant has spoken (thus) of Govind, the treasure of virtues. O Nanak, remember the Master, the Knower of hearts: the One Lord alone pervades (all). Day and night have come beautiful, remembering the Name of the Lord. With love for (his) lotus feet, impurities and sins are driven away. Sorrow, hunger and poverty have fled; (the Guru) has shown the plain path. Joining the Saadh Sangat, dyed in the Name, (I) have found what the mind longed for. Seeing the sight of the Lord, the wish is fulfilled, and all the generations of the family are carried across. Day and night there is bliss, O Nanak, remembering the Lord, Har Hare, night and day. ॥4॥
459.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 7, Chhants, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Good thoughts, the uttering of Gobind's praises, the pure company of the Saadh (be mine); have mercy, O Lord, that I, Nanak, may not forget the Naam for even a moment. ॥1॥
459.2: In the lovely dew-soaked night the stars glitter; (then) the Sants, the beloved ones of my Ram, are awake. The beloved ones of Ram are ever awake, and remember the Naam night and day. In their hearts is meditation on (God's) lotus feet; (they say:) O God, do not slip from (our) minds for even an instant. Casting off the mind's pride, attachment and vice, they burn away sins and sorrows. Nanak prays: the Lord's servants, (his) beloved Sants, stay awake for ever. My lovely bed has been adorned; joy has come to my mind on hearing that God is coming. God, the Master who leads to peace, has met (me); (I am) brimming with eagerness, gladness and delight. (I) have clung to (his) side, sorrows have fled, and breath, mind and body have all turned green. Meditating on God, I have gained my heart's wish; the union and the saha (the wedding day) were reckoned auspicious. Nanak prays: Sridhar (the Lord) has met (me), and every joy and delight has come about. Gathering together, my friends ask: tell (us) some sign of the Husband. Filled with the delight of (his) love, I cannot put anything into words. The Creator's virtues are deep, hidden and boundless; even the Vedas do not find their end. (His devotees,) meditating on the Master with devotion and love, ever sing the Lord's virtues. Full of every virtue and of true wisdom, (the soul-bride) is pleasing to her God; Nanak prays: dyed in (his) colour, she stays merged in love, in Sahaj. (When his servants) begin to sing the Lord's soothing songs of joy, (their) friends flourish, and sorrows and enemies run away. The comforts of Sahaj bloom, and they rejoice in the Lord's Name; God himself has shown (this) mercy. They have come to the Lord's feet, are ever awake, and have met God, Banwari. Blessed days have come (to them); in Sahaj they have reached the feet of God, (master of) all treasures. Nanak prays: in the Master's refuge, the Lord's servants keep (their love) to the end, for ever. ॥4॥
459.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Rise and get going, O traveller; why have you lingered? Your allotted time is up; in what falsehood are you lured? You are lured by what is false; Maya is a fraud, (yet) you commit countless sins. The body (is to be) a heap of ashes; Jam has his eye on it; death has conquered the poor creature. Leaving wealth and youth, you will go; your clothes and your food stay behind. O Nanak, what one has earned goes along (with one); the record of past deeds cannot be erased. You are caught like the deer that sees at night (the hunter's) moon-like light; out of comforts sorrows have come, (yet) you commit sins every day. You do not give up committing sins; with a halter round the neck, (you) are being led away. Seeing the city of Harichand, you are cheated; on your bed you have enjoyed only what is false. Drunk with craving, greed and ego, you are lost in pride. O Nanak, (such) deer perish through ignorance, and (their) coming and going does not end. The fly is dead in the sweet; how can it take flight? The elephant lies fallen in the pit; how can it swim across? Crossing over has become hard, (for) not for an instant did the Master come to mind. There is no counting the pains and punishments; (one) has reaped what one did. What was done in secret has come to light; there is disgrace here and hereafter. O Nanak, the proud manmukh is plundered for want of the True Guru. The Lord's servants have come to life, clinging to God's feet; in the refuge of that Master, (he) has hugged them to his breast. Strength, understanding, knowledge and meditation on himself (he gave), and himself had them repeat the Naam. (God) himself became the Saadh Sangat, and himself carried the world across. The Protector has kept them safe; (their) conduct is ever pure. O Nanak, the Lord's Sants never go to hell; (they are) in the Lord's refuge. ॥4॥
460.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Be gone, my laziness; (my) plea is before the Lord, that I may enjoy my own dear Husband; at God's side I am made beautiful. At the side of the Husband, the Master, (the soul-bride) is beautiful; let us enjoy him day and night. Calling (him) to mind with every breath, I live; beholding God, let us sing the Lord's praises. Separation is put to shame; (I) have found (his) sight; (his) glance sprinkles Amrit. Nanak prays: my wish is fulfilled; he whom I was searching for has met (me). Flee, O sins: the Creator has come into the home (of the heart). The fiends (the vices) are burned up, (for) Govind has become manifest. The beloved Gopal, Gobind, has become manifest; (his praise) is spoken in the Saadh Sangat. A wonder has been seen: Amrit has come to dwell (within); by the Guru's grace (God) is known. Peace has come to the mind, the songs of rejoicing ring out; (God's) end cannot be found. Nanak prays: in peace and Sahaj, God himself has brought about (this) union. Remembering Narain, (one) does not see hell; Dharam (Raj) hails (such a one), and (Jam's) messengers flee. Worshipping the Lord in the Saadh Sangat, (they) have found contentment in dharma, patience and Sahaj. In his kindness (God) has saved them; they have given up all attachment and possessiveness. (God) has taken hold of them and hugged them close; the Guru has united (them with him); repeating Govind, they are satisfied. Nanak prays: by remembering the Master, every hope is fulfilled. When (one) has grasped the feet of (the Lord of) treasures and siddhis, what worry is left? The God in whose power everything lies is ours. Taking (us) by the arm, he has made (us) his own, given (us) the Naam, and, placing his hand on (our) forehead, kept (us) safe. The world-ocean does not overpower (us): we have tasted the Lord's essence, the Amrit. In the Saadh Sangat, dyed in the Naam, (we) have won the battle, the great wrestling ground (of the world). Nanak prays: in the Master's refuge, (one) is not uprooted by Jam again. ॥4॥
461.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). What you have done, day and night, has come (written) upon your forehead. He from whom you hide (your deeds) is beside you, watching. The Maker watches from close by; why commit sin? Let us do good deeds and take the Naam; then one never goes to hell at all. At all hours remember the Lord's Name: (it) goes along with you. Says Nanak: worship (God) ever in the Saadh Sangat; the faults you have committed are wiped away. O foolish, ignorant one, you fill your belly by cheating, while the Lord, the Giver, goes on giving everything. The bountiful Master is ever merciful; why forget him from the mind? Join the Saadh Sangat and worship (him) without hesitation; so all one's generations are carried across. For Siddhas, seekers, gods, sages and devotees, the Naam is the support. Nanak prays: let us ever worship God, the One, the Maker (of all). Let no falseness be practised: God is the one who tests (all). Those who deal in falsehood and fraud are born into the world (again and again). They alone have crossed the world-ocean who have meditated on the One, (and,) giving up lust, anger and the slander of the blameless, have come to God's refuge. The Master pervades the water, the land and the sky; (he is) lofty, unreachable and boundless. Nanak prays: (he) is his servants' prop; (his) lotus feet are what they lean on. See, (this world) is the city of Harichand; nothing (in it) is lasting. All the pleasures of Maya, as many as there are, do not go along (with anyone). Ever at your side, the Lord is your companion; let us cherish him day and night. Apart from the one Lord there is nothing else; let the love of duality be burned away. Friend, youth, wealth, everything: hold in your mind that the one God is (all of these). Nanak prays: (God) is found by great good fortune; (those who find him) remain merged in peace and Sahaj. ॥4॥
461.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 8, a Chhant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Maya (Kamla) is a wall of delusion, Maya is a wall of delusion; its intoxication is sharp and leads the wrong way; (in it) life is passing in vain. (The world) is a dense, dreadful forest, a dense, dreadful forest; the thief, the mind, is plundering the house (of the heart), and night and day the sun devours (one's life). The days devour (it) and slip away, passing without God; meet (me), O God, Lord of compassion. Countless births and deaths have gone by; without the Beloved's company there is no liberation. I am without lineage, beauty, fragrance or wisdom; without you, who is a mother to me? With joined palms Nanak has come to your refuge; O beloved Master, O Narhar (the Lord), grant (me) liberation. A fish without water, a fish without water: parted from it, its mind and body waste away; how can there be life without the beloved? Facing (the hunter), the deer takes the arrow, facing him takes the arrow; it gives up mind, body and breath, pierced by (the hunter's) soothing sound. O Beloved, love (for you) has taken hold; meet (me), I am forlorn; cursed is the body that stays an instant without him. The eyelids do not close; (the mind is) at the Beloved's feet in love; night and day, O God, the mind dwells on (you). Those dyed in (the love of) Sri Rang (the Lord) and drunk with the Naam have lost all fears and the wandering after duality. Show kindness and mercy, O merciful, all-pervading (Lord), (that) Nanak may stay immersed in the Lord's love. The bees hum, the bees hum, drunk on the nectar's taste and fragrance; for love they let themselves be bound in the lotus. The chatrik's heart thirsts, the chatrik's heart thirsts; its mind hopes for the lovely drop from the cloud; drinking that heady (drop), its fever is gone. O destroyer of fever, remover of pain, meet (me); in my mind and body the love is very deep. O beautiful, clever, all-wise Master, with what tongue can I tell (your) virtues? Take (me) by the arm, give (me) the Naam; as soon as you cast your glance, sins are erased. Nanak prays: O Lord, purifier of the fallen, beholding your sight there is no anguish. I dwell on you in my mind, O Master, I dwell on you in my mind, O Master; keep me, who have no one, in your refuge; meet (me), my breath is full of longing. (My) attention is on (your) beautiful form, on (your) beautiful form; my mind craves the knowledge of Gopal; (you) keep the honour of the servants who beg (at your door). God gives honour in full and tears pain away; every wish is fulfilled. (I) am clasped to the Lord's neck, and the days are blessed; now that (I) have met the Husband, the bed is made beautiful. God cast his glance; Murari has met (me), and all sins are destroyed. Nanak prays: my hope is fulfilled; Sridhar (the Lord), the treasure of virtues, has met (me). ॥4॥
462.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). A Vaar with saloks; the saloks too were written by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji); (to be sung) to the tune of Tunda Asraja. Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). To my Guru I am a sacrifice, each day a hundred times over, who made gods out of men, and took no time in doing it. ॥1॥

A vaar is a hymn of pauris (stanzas); the pauris of this vaar are the First Guru's, and each is preceded by saloks, a few of them the Second Guru's (marked Mahla 2). Tunda Asraja: by tradition a prince whose hand was cut off (tunda, maimed) and who later became a king; the bards sang a vaar of him, and this vaar is set to its tune (dhuni).
463.1: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). Were a hundred moons to rise and a thousand suns to come up, even with so much light, without the Guru there is pitch darkness. ॥2॥
463.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O Nanak, those who do not keep the Guru in mind, and are clever in their own eyes, are like barren sesame plants left forsaken in an empty field. Left in the field, says Nanak, such plants have a hundred masters; the poor things flower and bear pods, yet inside their bodies is only ash. ॥3॥
Naah here is the plural of naahu (master), not the negative: barren plants left in a harvested field have no one owner, so anyone who passes may cut them and carry them off.
463.3: (God) himself made himself, and himself fashioned his Name (his glory). Second, he made the creation, and taking his seat (within it), watched its play. You are the Giver, you yourself the Maker; when pleased you give and bestow grace. You know all; having given life and its garment (the body), you will take (them) back. Taking your seat (within the creation), you have watched its play. ॥1॥
463.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). True are your lands (khand), true the universes. True are your worlds, true the forms (in them). True are your works, and all your thought. True is your rule, true your court. True is your Hukam, true your decree. True is your grace, true its token. True are the hundreds of thousands, the millions, who call on you. All rest on the True One's strength, all on the True One's might. True is your praise, true your acclaim. True is your creation, O True King. O Nanak, those who meditate on the True One are true; those who die and are born (again) are raw, raw through and through. ॥1॥
True (sacha) here means what truly is and abides: by the Darpan the salok says that God's creation is real, not an illusion, and its order lasting, though its single forms pass away.
463.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). His greatness is great, for his Name is great. His greatness is great, for his justice is true. His greatness is great, for his seat is unshakeable. His greatness is great: he knows what (all) say. His greatness is great: he grasps the feelings (of every heart). His greatness is great, for he consults no one before he gives. His greatness is great, for he is all by himself. O Nanak, (his) work cannot be told; all that he has made, the whole creation, is within his will. ॥2॥
463.6: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). This world is the chamber of the True One; the True One dwells in it. Some, by his Hukam, he takes into himself; some, by that same Hukam, he brings to ruin. Some, as it pleases him, he draws out (of Maya); others he keeps dwelling in Maya. Nor can it be told whom he will bring through. O Nanak, (this) is understood through the Guru by the one in whom he himself makes light. ॥3॥
463.7: O Nanak, having created the beings, (God) has seated Dharam Raj to write (their) accounts. There (each case) is settled by truth, truth alone; those foul with sin (jajmale) are picked out and set apart. The false find no place (there); with blackened faces they are sent off to hell. Those dyed in your Name go (from here) having won; the cheats go having lost. (God) has seated Dharam Raj to write (their) accounts. ॥2॥
Jajmale (from jazam, leprosy): the leprous; here, those foul with evil deeds.
463.8: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Wondrous are the sounds (naad), wondrous the Vedas. Wondrous are the beings, wondrous their kinds. Wondrous are the forms, wondrous the colours. Wondrous are the creatures that roam naked. Wondrous is the wind, wondrous the water. Wondrous are the fires that play their strange games. Wondrous is the earth, wondrous the sources of life (khaani). Wondrous it is that mortals cling to tastes. Wondrous is union, wondrous parting. Wondrous is hunger, wondrous the eating. Wondrous is (his) praise, wondrous (his) acclaim. Wondrous is the trackless waste, wondrous the road. Wondrous it is (that he is) near, wondrous (that he is) far. Wondrous it is (that he), ever present, watches over (all). Seeing (his) marvels, (the mind) is lost in wonder (vismaad). O Nanak, to understand (it) comes by perfect fortune. ॥1॥
Vismaad: the wonder and awe that rise in the mind at the marvels of God's creation.
464.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). (Your) Kudrat is what is seen, (your) Kudrat what is heard; (your) Kudrat is fear, the essence of peace. (Your) Kudrat is in the netherworlds and the skies; (your) Kudrat is all that has form. (Your) Kudrat are the Vedas, the Puranas and the Kateb; (your) Kudrat is all thought. (Your) Kudrat is eating, drinking and clothing; (your) Kudrat is all love. (Your) Kudrat is in castes, kinds and colours; (your) Kudrat is in the beings of the world. (Your) Kudrat are the good deeds, (your) Kudrat the evil; (your) Kudrat is honour and pride. (Your) Kudrat are wind, water and fire; (your) Kudrat the earth and the dust. All is your Kudrat; you are its Master (Kadir), the Creator; pure is your glory, (and you yourself are) pure. O Nanak, (God) watches over (all) within his Hukam, and he alone, himself, pervades (all). ॥2॥

Kudrat (Arabic qudrat): power, and the creation in which God's power is at work; Kadir (Qadir) is its Master. The Kateb: the scriptures of the Semitic faiths (the Torah, the Psalms, the Gospel and the Quran).
464.2: (Man) himself enjoyed his pleasures; (then the body) became a heap of ashes, and the bhaur (the soul) departed. The worldly man died (vadda hoa); a chain was put round his neck, and he was driven off. Hereafter his deeds and his repute are read out; seated, he is made to understand the reckoning of his account. As the blows fall he finds no place (of shelter); what wailing of his is heard now? His blind mind has wasted (this human) birth. ॥3॥
The bhaur (the black bee) is a name of the soul in Gurbani. Vadda hona (to become great) is an old Punjabi idiom for dying (the Darpan).
464.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). In (God's) fear the wind blows for ever. In (God's) fear hundreds of thousands of rivers run. In (God's) fear fire does its forced labour (begaar). In (God's) fear the earth is pressed down under (its) load. In (God's) fear Indra (the god of rain) goes about on his head. In (God's) fear is the door of Dharam Raj. In (God's) fear is the sun, in (God's) fear the moon; travelling crores of kos, (their journey) has no end. In (God's) fear are the Siddhas, the Buddhas, the gods and the Naths. In (God's) fear the skies are stretched out. In (God's) fear are warriors, the mighty and the brave. In (God's) fear boatloads (of beings) come and go. Upon the heads of all, fear is written as their lot. O Nanak, only the One, the True, the Formless, is without fear. ॥1॥
Bhau (fear) in Gurbani is awe of God and of his Hukam, under which all creation keeps its course. Begaar: labour forced from one without pay. A kos is an old measure of distance, about two miles.
464.4: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O Nanak, the Formless One (alone) is without fear; so many other Rams are (but) dust (before him). So many are the tales of Kaanh, so many the reflections on the Vedas. So many beggars dance, and wheeling round and round keep the beat. The players (bajaari) come into the bazaar and set out their show. They sing (as) kings and queens, and talk wild nonsense. (They wear) earrings worth a lakh of takas, necklaces worth a lakh of takas; (but) the bodies they are put on, O Nanak, those bodies turn to ash. Wisdom is not found by talk; to tell of it is as hard as iron. It is gained only when it comes by (his) grace; all other cleverness and command come to nothing. ॥2॥

Bajaari (by the Darpan, the raasdharis): troupes who staged the raas in the bazaars for a living, acting out in song and dance the stories of Krishna and the gopis, and of Ram and Sita; the two saloks at 465.2 and 465.3 also speak of the raas. A taka was a coin.
465.1: If you cast your glance of grace, then by (your) grace the True Guru is found. This soul roamed through many births; then the True Guru made it hear the Shabad. None is a giver as great as the True Guru; listen, all you people, every one. Those who rid themselves of self within have found the True One by meeting the True Guru, (the Guru) who has made (them) understand the True One, Truth itself. ॥4॥
465.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The gharis are all gopis, the pahars (of day and night) Kaanh, Gopal; wind, water and fire are the ornaments, the moon and the sun the avatars; the whole earth is (the play's) goods and wealth, and all the world's entanglements are the things it uses. O Nanak, (the world,) empty of wisdom, is being robbed; Jamkaal has devoured it. ॥1॥
465.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The disciples play (the instruments), and the gurus dance; they jig their feet and toss their heads; the dust flies up and settles in their hair. The onlookers watch, laugh, and make for home. For the sake of bread they keep the beat, and fling themselves upon the ground. They sing as the gopis, they sing as Kaanh, they sing as Sita and as Ram the king. The Fearless, the Formless, whose Name is True, whose making is all the world: him those servants serve whom (his) grace has uplifted; for those whose minds are eager (for him), the night (of life) is dew-soaked and sweet. Those who have learned this teaching through reflection on the Guru's word, the Gracious One, in his kindness, carries (them) across. The oil-press, the spinning wheel, the grindstone, the potter's wheel, the whirlwinds of the desert, many beyond count, tops, churning-staves, threshing frames, birds that wheel without pausing for breath, creatures set on a spike and spun round: O Nanak, of those that go round there is no count and no end. Binding (beings) in bonds, he spins them round; everyone dances by the deeds that have fallen to his lot. Those who laugh as they dance depart in tears. (Dancing,) they neither take flight (to a higher state) nor become Siddhas. Dancing and leaping are (but) the mind's fancy; O Nanak, those whose minds hold (God's) fear hold (his) love in their minds. ॥2॥
465.4: Your Name is Nirankar (the Formless); taking (your) Name, one does not go to hell. Soul and body, all is his; give (of what he gives) and then eat; speak of (the giving), and (its merit) is lost. If you want your own good, do good deeds and (still) be called lowly. Even if a mighty man would cast it off, old age comes on, putting on its garb. No one stays (here) when the measure (paai) of life is full. ॥5॥
465.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). With the Muslims it is the praise of the Shariat (the Islamic law); reading it again and again, they reflect: (God's) servants are those who enter its bond (bandi) to behold (his) vision. The Hindus praise the Praiseworthy One, through the darshans (their schools of scripture), as beautiful and boundless; they bathe at the tiraths, make offerings (to images) and worship (them), with the scent of aloe-wood and perfumes. The yogis, all of them, meditate on the Creator in Sunn, naming him Alakh (the Unseen); (yet in their meditation) the One of subtle form, whose Name is Niranjan, takes the shape of a body. In the minds of the charitable, contentment springs up at the thought of giving; (but) giving and giving, they ask a thousandfold (in return), and the world sings their praise. Thieves, adulterers and liars, the wicked and the sinful: some use up what they had and go from here; they too have some task (given them). In water and on land are beings, in the realms and the worlds, form upon form: what they say, you alone know; they too are in your care. O Nanak, the devotees hunger to praise (you); the True Name is (their) support. Ever in bliss they live, day and night, (as) dust beneath the feet of the virtuous. ॥1॥
The salok first tells the ways of the Muslims, the Hindus, the yogis, the givers and the wicked; the Guru's own conclusion is in its last two lines (the Darpan, the Santhya).
466.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The clay of a Muslim('s grave) may come to lie in the potter's lump; shaping it, (he) makes pots and bricks of it, and as it burns (in the kiln) it cries out. The poor thing weeps as it burns and burns, and embers keep dropping from it. O Nanak, the Creator who made the creation, he alone knows (its secret). ॥2॥
The salok answers a belief held among Muslims, that those whose bodies are burnt burn in the fire of hell (the Darpan).
466.2: Without the True Guru no one has found (God); without the True Guru no one has found (him). (God) has placed himself within the True Guru, and has made this plain and proclaimed it. One who has rid himself of attachment within is free for ever, when the True Guru is met. Best of all is this understanding: one who has fixed his mind on the True One has found the Giver, the Life of the world. ॥6॥
466.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). In Haumai (ego) one comes (into the world), in Haumai one goes. In Haumai one is born, in Haumai one dies. In Haumai one gives, in Haumai one takes. In Haumai one earns, in Haumai one loses. In Haumai one is (now) truthful, (now) false. In Haumai one weighs sin and merit. In Haumai one falls (now) into hell, (now) into heaven. In Haumai one laughs, in Haumai one weeps. In Haumai one is soiled (with sin), in Haumai one washes (it off). In Haumai, (proud of) caste and kind, one loses (oneself). In Haumai one is (now) a fool, in Haumai (now) wise, (but) does not grasp what liberation and release are. In Haumai one (chases) Maya, in Haumai (lives under) its shadow. Acting in Haumai again and again, beings are born (again and again). When one understands Haumai, then the (Lord's) door comes into sight. Without this knowledge, one only quarrels, talking and talking. O Nanak, this record is written by the Hukam: as (beings) look (upon others), so their own form becomes. ॥1॥
Hau (I) and Haumai (I-am-ness): the sense of a self apart from God.
466.4: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). Such is the nature of Haumai: (beings) do the deeds of Haumai. These are the bonds of Haumai: (beings) fall into the life-forms again and again. Where does Haumai spring from? By what discipline does it go? Haumai is by this very Hukam: driven by their past deeds, (beings) wander. Haumai is a long, lingering disease, but it has a cure as well. If (God) shows his grace, then (beings) live by the Guru's Shabad. Nanak says: hear, O people; by this discipline the pains (of Haumai) go. ॥2॥
466.5: Service has been done by the contented, who have meditated on none but the True One. They have not set foot on (the path of) evil; doing good deeds, they have lived by dharma. They have broken the world's bonds, and have taken little of grain and water. (O Lord,) you are the great Giver of gifts; you give each day, and (your giving) ever grows. By praising (you), they have found (you), the Great One. ॥7॥
467.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Of men, trees, tiraths, riverbanks, clouds and fields, of islands, worlds, spheres, continents and universes, of the sources of life, egg-born, womb-born, earth-born and sweat-born, of lakes, mountains and creatures, he knows the measure, O Nanak. O Nanak, having brought forth the beings, (God) takes care of them all. The Creator who made the creation must also see to its care. That Creator who brought forth the world takes thought for it. To him I bow, hail to him; his court stands for ever unbroken. O Nanak, without the True Name, what is the frontal mark, what the sacred thread? ॥1॥
467.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Lakhs of good deeds and kindnesses, lakhs of acts of merit approved (by the world), lakhs of austerities at tiraths, yoga in the stillness of Sahaj in the wilds, lakhs of feats of valour, the breath of life let go on the field of battle, lakhs of ways of fixing the attention, lakhs of (discourses on) knowledge and of meditations, and the Puranas read and recited: (before) the Creator who made the creation and wrote down (all) coming and going, O Nanak, (all these) clevernesses are worthless; his grace is the true mark (of acceptance). ॥2॥
467.3: (O Lord,) you alone are the True Master, who have made Truth, nothing but Truth, prevail. Whoever you give it to receives Truth; then such ones live the Truth. Those in whose hearts (the Guru) has set Truth to dwell have found Truth through meeting the True Guru. Fools do not know the Truth; the manmukhs have wasted their lives. Why did (such a one) come into the world? ॥8॥
467.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). One may read and read till carts are loaded, read and read till caravans are filled (with books); read and read till a boat is laden, read and read till pits are packed full; one may read for as many years as there are, year upon year, read for as many months as there are; one may read for as long as life lasts, read for as many breaths as there are: (Even so,) O Nanak, in (God's) reckoning one thing alone counts; all else is the idle babble of Haumai. ॥1॥
467.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). However much one writes and reads, so much does one fret and burn (within). However many tiraths one tours, so much the more one prattles. (One) has put on many guises and given the body pain: endure, O soul, what you have done yourself. (One who) has eaten no grain has lost the taste (of life); he has suffered much pain, for something other (than the Name) has pleased him. (One) wears no clothes, and is in torment day and night. (One) has gone astray in silence: asleep, how can he wake without the Guru? (One) goes barefoot, and reaps what he has done. (One) has eaten what is foul and put ash on his head: the blind fool has lost his honour. Without the Name, nothing is accepted. (One) lives in the wilds, at tombs and cremation grounds: the blind man does not know (the way), and afterwards repents. One who meets the True Guru finds peace, and enshrines the Lord's Name in the mind. O Nanak, one on whom (God) casts his glance of grace finds (the Guru); free from hope and anxiety, he burns away Haumai through the Shabad. ॥2॥
468.1: (O Lord,) your devotees are dear to your mind; singing (your) praises, they look beautiful at (your) door. O Nanak, those without (his) grace find no shelter at the door; they wander about. Some do not understand their own origin, and, having nothing, make much of themselves. I am a humble minstrel (dhadhi) of low caste; others call themselves high-born. (The company of) those who meditate on you is what I ask for. ॥9॥
468.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The king is falsehood, the subjects are falsehood, all the world is falsehood. Pavilions are falsehood, palaces are falsehood, and he who sits in them is falsehood. Gold is falsehood, silver is falsehood, and he who wears them is falsehood. The body is falsehood, clothes are falsehood, and beauty beyond measure is falsehood. Husband is falsehood, wife is falsehood; worn out (in it), they come to ruin. The false one's love is fixed in falsehood, and he has forgotten the Creator. With whom should one make friends? The whole world is passing away. Falsehood is sweet, falsehood is honey; falsehood drowns the whole boatload (of beings). Nanak humbly prays: without you, (all) is falsehood, nothing but falsehood. ॥1॥
Kur in this salok is a noun: not a lie told, but what is unreal and passes away, the world's show of illusion; kurai: of the false one, the being caught in it.
468.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Truth is known only when the True One is in the heart; (then) the filth of falsehood comes off, and (one) washes the body clean. Truth is known only when (one) bears love for the True One; hearing the Name, the mind blossoms with joy, and then one finds the door of liberation. Truth is known only when the soul knows the (true) way of life: making ready the earth of the body, it puts into it the Creator's seed (the Name). Truth is known only when (one) takes true teaching (from the Guru), knows how to show compassion to living beings, and gives something in charity and good works. Truth is known only when (one) dwells at the tirath of the soul within, and, having asked the True Guru, stays seated (there) and makes his home (there). Truth is the cure for all (ills); it washes sins away and drives them out. Nanak humbly prays before those who have Truth in their lap. ॥2॥
468.4: For me the gift (to ask for) is the dust from beneath (the Sants') feet; if it is obtained, let it be put to the forehead. Let false greed be given up, and, single-minded, let the Unseen One be meditated on. Such fruit is reaped as is the work one does. If it is so written from the start, then the dust of such ones is obtained. (Leaning on one's) small understanding, service is lost. ॥10॥
468.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). A famine of Truth has come, falsehood holds sway; in the blackness of Kalyug, (people have become) ghouls. Those who sowed the seed (of the Name) have gone with honour; how now can split grain sprout? Seed sprouts if it is whole, and the season too is the best of seasons. O Nanak, without the mordant, raw cloth does not take the (fast) colour. In the fear (of God) let (the mind) be set on the khumb, and let effort be the mordant for the cloth (of the body). O Nanak, if (the mind) is dyed in devotion, not a trace of falsehood (remains). ॥1॥
Khumb: the dyer's vat in which cloth is steamed clean before dyeing. Saram here is effort, as in the Saram Khand of the Japji.
468.6: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Greed and sin are the two, king and minister (mahta), and falsehood has become the chief (sikdar). Lust is the deputy (naib), summoned and consulted; he sits with them, deliberating again and again. The subjects, blind and without knowledge, stuff the fire (of the rulers' craving) with carrion (bribes). Those (called) wise dance, play instruments, put on guises and adorn themselves. They shout aloud, sing of battles, and expound the tales of warriors. Foolish pandits love to amass (wealth) by cunning and argument. The pious do pious deeds and waste them, asking (in return) for the door of liberation. (Some) call themselves celibates but do not know the way; they leave hearth and home and sit (apart). Everyone is perfect in his own eyes; no one calls himself lacking. O Nanak, only when the weight of honour (from God) is put in the other pan does (one) prove truly weighed. ॥2॥
469.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). What is ordained, O Nanak, shall sound forth (come to light); the True One himself watches over (all). All have made their leaps (and tried their strength), but what the Creator does, that comes to pass. Hereafter there is no caste and no force; hereafter the beings (one meets) are new (strangers). Those few whose honour counts in the reckoning, they alone are good. ॥3॥
469.2: Those on whom you cast your grace from the very first have then meditated on the Master. It is not in these creatures' power to do anything; you have brought forth a world of many kinds. Some you unite (with yourself); others you have led astray from yourself. By the Guru's grace you are known (by the one) to whom you have made yourself understood, and (that one) has merged, in Sahaj, in the True One. ॥11॥
469.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Sorrow has become the remedy and comfort the disease, for when there is comfort, then (your remembrance) is not there. You are the Creator, the Doer (of all); I am nothing; when I would do (anything) myself, it does not come about. ॥1॥
469.4: I am a sacrifice to you, who dwell within your creation; your limit cannot be perceived.
This salok has a Rahao line of its own between its two parts, as a shabad has; it holds the salok's central thought.
469.5: Your light is in the creation, and in every light you are known; undivided and whole, you fill all things. You are the True Master, and lovely is your praise; whoever has offered it has crossed over. Says Nanak, (all these are) the Creator's doings: whatever is to be done, he is doing. ॥2॥
469.6: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). The way of the yogi is knowledge; the way of the Brahmins is the Veda; the way of the Khatri is valour; the way of the Shudra is the service of others; the way of all is (the remembrance of) the One; if anyone knows this secret, Nanak is his servant; he himself is (the image of) Niranjan, the Lord. ॥3॥
Sabadam here is the way, the duty (dharma), laid down for each.
469.7: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji). The one Krishna (the Lord) is the soul of all the gods, and the soul too of the gods of the gods; (in all) is the soul of Vasudev (the Lord); if anyone knows this secret, Nanak is his servant; he himself is (the image of) Niranjan, the Lord. ॥4॥
Krishna here is a name of the one God.
469.8: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Water stays held only within a pitcher, (yet) without water no pitcher is made; (so) the mind stays steady only when held by wisdom, (yet) without the Guru there is no wisdom. ॥5॥
469.9: If the learned one is a sinner, the unlettered one who is good is not punished. As are the deeds one labours at, so is the name one comes to be known by. Let no such game be played as would make one lose on reaching the Lord's court. Of the learned and the unlettered alike, the case is weighed hereafter; whoever goes headstrong, by his own will, is punished hereafter. ॥12॥
Omi (Arabic ummi): unlettered, one who cannot read or write.
470.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). O Nanak, the body that is the meru (the crown of all bodies, the human one) has one chariot and one charioteer; age after age they are changed again; the wise understand this. In Satjug the chariot is of contentment, and dharma the charioteer in front; in Treta the chariot is of continence, and might the charioteer in front; in Duapar the chariot is of austerity, and sat (upright conduct) the charioteer in front; in Kalyug the chariot is of fire, and falsehood the charioteer in front. ॥1॥
