For lakhs and crores (of coins) no one obtains it;
(O Lord,) you give it to the one whose lot it is to receive it.
Tasting it, Nanak is lost in wonder;
O Nanak, this savour has come from the Guru.
here and hereafter, (he) does not leave it to go anywhere else;
Nanak is steeped in the Lord's sweet essence. ॥3॥
377.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O soul-bride,) if you wipe out lust, anger, greed and attachment, the evil-mindedness you have taken up yourself falls away;
if, becoming humble, you serve, you will be dear to your Beloved's heart.
Listen, O lovely one: the words of the Saadh (the Guru) bring rescue;
your pain, hunger and dread will be gone, and you will find peace, O woman who longs for a mind at peace.
Wash (his) feet and serve the Guru: the soul grows pure, and the poison and the thirst (of Maya) are driven out.
If you become the handmaid, the lowly handmaid, of (the Lord's) servants, you will win honour at the Lord's door.
This alone is right conduct, this alone the daily way: obey (the Lord's) command, and your devotion is fulfilled.
Whoever lives by this mantra (teaching), O Nanak, is carried across the terrifying world-ocean. ॥3॥
378.1: Raag Asa, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
You have received this lovely human body;
this is your turn to meet Gobind (the Lord of the universe).
All other tasks are of no use to you at all;
join the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) and remember the Naam alone.
Set yourself to the task of crossing the ocean of the world;
your life is passing in vain in the love of Maya.
(O Lord,) I have practised neither repetition (of the Name), austerity, self-restraint nor any deed of dharma;
I have not served the Saadh (the holy one), nor have I known you, O Lord, my King.
Says Nanak, we are of lowly deeds;
save the honour of one who has come into your refuge. ॥2॥
378.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) apart from you I have no other at all; you are within my mind.
You are (my) friend, my companion, my God; why then, O my soul, are you afraid?
Yours is my shelter, in you my hope;
sitting or rising, sleeping or waking, with every breath and every morsel, may I never forget you.
Keep me, keep me in your refuge, O God; (this world) is a fearsome ocean of fire.
O True Guru, Giver of peace to Nanak, we are your children, O Gopal. ॥2॥
378.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
God has set the Lord's servants free;
my mind is at one with the Beloved; the fever has died, as if it had eaten poison.
Neither chill nor heat touches (one) at all who sings the praises of the Name of Ram;
the witch has no hold at all on the mind that is in the refuge of the lotus feet.
By the grace of the Sant (the Guru), (the Lord) has become merciful and has himself become (my) help.
Nanak sings ever of the Treasure of virtues, dread and pain wiped away. ॥2॥
378.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I have taken the medicine of the Lord's Name;
I have found comfort, and the very seat of pain is destroyed.
The fever has left, by the word of the Perfect Guru;
there is joy, and all sorrows are wiped away.
All beings and creatures have found peace
who, O Nanak, have meditated on the Supreme Lord in their minds. ॥2॥
378.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
That hour (of death), which no one wishes for, arrives;
without (the Lord's) Hukam, how can one understand, though it be explained?
(The body) is consumed by the cold (water), the hot (fire) or the earth;
(but) that (soul) is neither child nor old, O brother.
Servant Nanak is in the refuge of the Saadh (the Guru);
by the Guru's grace (he) has crossed beyond fear. ॥2॥
378.6: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
For ever and ever the soul is lit up
in one who, in the Saadh Sangat, dwells at the Lord's feet.
Repeat the Name of Ram every day, O my mind;
you will find coolness, calm and lasting peace, and all your sins will go, O mind.
Says Nanak, one whose destiny is perfect
meets the True Guru, and meets the perfect Supreme Lord.
The thirty-four (shabads) of the Second Ghar.
378.7: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
She whose friend is the Lord, the Master, God:
her pain is gone, and never again is she in misery.
In his mercy he has joined her to his feet;
she is at ease, in comfort, Sahaj and bliss.
Singing (his) virtues in the Saadh Sangat, she has grown beyond all weighing;
remembering the Lord, O Nanak, she has become priceless. ॥2॥
379.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Lust, anger, Maya, pride and envy: all these (we) have gambled away and lost;
truth, contentment, compassion, dharma and truthful living: these (we) have brought into our own home.
All the burdens of birth and death are ended;
joining the company (of the holy), the mind has become pure; the Perfect Guru has taken (us) along and carried (us) across in an instant.
The mind remains the dust (of the feet) of all, and all appear as dear friends.
My Master pervades all; giving his gifts, he takes care of all beings.
He himself is the One, the One alone, only the One; the whole expanse is the One's alone.
Repeating (the Name) again and again, all have become holy; meditating on the one Name, they have saved a great many.
The Lord of the world is deep, profound and boundless; he has no end at all, no near shore and no far shore.
By your grace, (O Lord,) Nanak sings (your) praises, and, meditating again and again, bows before God. ॥4॥
379.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) you are infinite, unmanifest, beyond the reach of the senses; all this (visible) form is yours.
What cleverness can we creatures show, when everything is within you?
O my True Guru, by your wondrous play keep your children safe;
give (me) good understanding, that I may ever sing (your) virtues, O my Master, inaccessible and infinite.
As the mortal in the mother's womb lives on the support of the Name:
he is in bliss, keeps (the Lord) in mind with every breath, and the fire (of the womb) cannot touch him.
Another's wealth, another's wife, the slander of others: take away (my) love for these;
may I serve (your) lotus feet within my heart, upheld by the Perfect Guru.
Home, mansions and palaces, whatever is seen: none of them goes along;
as long as you live in this age of Kalyug, O servant Nanak, cherish the Naam (in your heart). ॥4॥
379.3: Raag Asa, Ghar 3, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Rule, lands, the bloom of youth, home, renown, a handsome form, youthful vigour,
great wealth, elephants and horses, rubies bought for lakhs and brought home:
hereafter, in the Lord's court, (none of it) is of use; the proud man departs and leaves (it all) behind.
Why should the mind be set on anything but the One?
Rising, sitting, sleeping and waking, let us meditate on the Lord for ever and ever.
One may win marvellous, splendid contests in the arena and win the fights on the battlefield,
and brag with his mouth like this: I kill, I bind, I let go;
(yet when) the Hukam of the Supreme Lord came, he left (it all) one day and was gone.
One may perform religious rites and duties in many ways, yet not know the Creator;
he preaches but does not practise it himself, and does not recognise the Shabad, the essence;
naked he came and naked he will go, like an elephant that (bathes and then) scatters dust over itself.
Listen, Sants, good people, all my friends: this expanse is false (it perishes).
Crying mine, mine, the fools have drowned; they have wasted away and died.
O Nanak, (whoever) has met the Guru and meditated on the Naam has been carried across through the True Name. ॥4॥
380.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 5, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The whole world lies asleep in delusion, blinded by its worldly affairs; only some servant of the Lord stays awake.
It is engrossed in the great enchantress (Maya), her love dearer to it than life; some rare one renounces her.
The peerless lotus feet of the Lord, the mantra of the Sants: to these some Saadh holds fast.
O Nanak, in the company of the Saadh (the Guru) they awake, dyed in divine knowledge; this is (the Lord's) grace on the most fortunate. ॥4॥
380.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, Ghar 6, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) whatever pleases you is accepted (by your servants); that alone is peace and Sahaj in (their) minds.
(You are) the Cause of creation, all-powerful, infinite; O brother, there is no other (like God).
Your servants sing your praises, relishing them again and again.
What you yourself do and have (others) do is your servant's counsel, resolve and wisdom.
Your Naam is Amrit, O Beloved; in the Saadh Sangat (your servants) have found its taste.
Those servants alone are filled to contentment and made whole who have sung of the Lord, the treasure of peace.
O Master, one who leans on you has no anxiety.
Those on whom your mercy has fallen are worthy bankers, rich in good fortune.
From the moment (one) has had the sight (of God), doubt, attachment and deceit have all gone out (of him);
O Nanak, he has made the True Naam the stuff of his daily life, and is merged in love of the Lord's Name. ॥4॥
380.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The slanderer) washes off the grime others gathered birth after birth, but reaps what he himself has done.
Here he has no peace, in the Lord's court no shelter; he goes to the city of Jam and burns there.
The slanderer has squandered his precious life.
In nothing can he reach (his aim), and hereafter he finds no place.
The hapless slanderer's own past deeds have come upon him; what can the poor man do?
He is brought to ruin where no one shields him; to whom can he cry for help?
Nowhere is there release for the slanderer; so it has pleased the Master.
As each one slanders the Sants, so the Sants find comfort in it.
The Sants lean on you, O Master; you are the Sants' helper.
Says Nanak, the Lord has kept the Sants safe and swept the slanderers away. ॥4॥
381.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(One who) washes the outside while the mind within stays filthy has lost both his places (this world and the next).
Here he is gripped by lust, anger and attachment; hereafter he sobs and weeps.
The understanding that worships Govind is of another kind.
Beating its hole does not kill the snake; the deaf one does not hear the Naam.
(One) gives up and throws away the labour of earning a living, yet does not know the worth of devotion;
he takes to arguing over the Vedas and Shastras, but does not recognise the essence, union (with God).
As a false coin is laid bare when it comes under the eye of the money-testers,
(so) the Knower of hearts knows everything; what can be hidden from him?
Cheated in falsehood and fraud, the (mortal) whose days are few perishes in an instant.
Nanak has spoken the truth, the truth, the truth: keep (God) in your own heart and see. ॥4॥
381.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
As he strives, (the servant's) mind grows pure; he dances by casting out his self-conceit.
He seizes the five (passions) and keeps them under control, and (keeps) Ekankar, the One Creator, in his mind.
(O God,) your servant dances (thus): he sings (your) praises,
and plays the unstruck Shabad as his rebab, pakhavaj, cymbals and ankle-bells.
First he awakens his own mind, and then he delights others.
He repeats the Name of Ram in his heart, and with his mouth recites it to all.
With his hands he washes the feet of the Saadhs, and puts the dust of the Sants on his body.
He offers up his mind and body, laying them before the Guru, and obtains the true treasure.
Whoever hears and beholds (this dance) with faith is rid of the pain of birth and death.
Such a dance wards off hell; O Nanak, (by it) the Gurmukh awakens. ॥4॥
381.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The mind's bent, once) a lowly Chandal woman, has become a Brahmin woman; from a Shudra woman she has risen to the highest, O brother.
The flame (of craving), left empty though (it took in) the underworlds and the skies, is quenched and spent, O brother.
The cat of the house (the mind's greed) has learnt another lesson; seeing the mouse (of worldly things), she takes fright, O brother.
The Guru has put the lion (of pride) in the power of the goat (of humility), and set the dog (of the senses) to (eating) grass, O brother.
With no props the thatch is held up; the homeless (wandering mind) has gained a home, O brother.
With no setter the jewelled ornament has been set, and a wondrous gem fixed in it, O brother.
The complainant could never reach justice; once silent, he has received the verdict, O brother.
She who sat in state upon the carpet (in pride) now seems as one dead; the glaring of eyes (at others) has fled, O brother.
Ignorant is he who says, I know; one who (truly) knows does not stay hidden, O brother.
Says Nanak, one whom the Guru has given the Amrit (of the Naam) to drink blossoms, relishing it again and again, O brother. ॥4॥
382.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Cutting (their) bonds, (God) has forgotten (their) faults; he has kept to his age-old way.
Like a mother and father he has been merciful, and has cherished (them) as his children.
The great Gopal has kept the Guru's Sikhs safe;
looking on (them) with his gracious eye, he has drawn (them) out of the vast ocean of the world.
He by whose Simran one is freed from Jam, and finds peace in this world and the next:
with every breath and every morsel repeat (his Name) with your tongue; let his praises be sung day after day.
Through loving devotion (they) have attained the supreme state; in the Saadh Sangat (their) sorrows have fled.
Nothing wears away or is lost, and no fear takes hold: the pure wealth of the Lord is tied in (their) knot.
At the last moment God has been (their) help; here and hereafter he is the protector.
(God is) my life, my friend, my well-wisher and my wealth; Nanak is for ever a sacrifice (to him). ॥4॥
382.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When you are (my) Master, what fear can there be? Whom but you should I praise?
If you alone are (mine), I have everything; for me there is no other but you.
O Father (God), I have seen the world to be poison.
Protect (me), my Lord of the world; your Naam is my support.
You know all the pain of the mind; to whom else should it be told?
Without the Name the whole world has gone mad; when the Naam is found, peace is found.
What is there to say, and to whom should it be told? Whatever is to be said is (to be said) to God.
All that comes to pass is your doing; for ever and ever my hope is in you.
If you grant (me) greatness, that greatness is yours; here and hereafter I meditate on you alone.
O God of Nanak, ever the Giver of peace, my strength is your Name alone. ॥4॥
382.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Your Naam is Amrit, O Master; this supreme essence (your) servant has drunk.
The fears and burdens of birth after birth are ended; sin is destroyed, and the doubt of duality (is gone).
Beholding the sight of you, I have come alive;
hearing your words, O True Guru, my mind and body have grown cool and calm.
By your grace (I) came to the Saadh Sangat; this work you yourself have done.
I have clasped your feet firmly, O God; with ease the poison (of Maya) has withered away.
Your Naam, O God, is the treasure of peace; this imperishable mantra I have received;
the True Guru in his grace gave it to me; my fever, my anguish and my enmity are gone.
Blessed is the human body (I) have been given, through which God has united (me) with himself.
Blessed is that Kalyug (too), if Kirtan is sung in the Saadh Sangat and, O Nanak, the Naam is the heart's support. ॥4॥
383.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Everything has come about from the very first (by his will); what other knowledge can anyone have?
For all (its) slips and failings, the Supreme Lord God has forgiven his own child.
My True Guru is merciful for ever; he has kept me, poor and lowly, safe.
The sickness is cut away and I have found supreme peace; (the Guru) has put the Lord's Amrit Naam in my mouth.
(The Guru) has cast away my countless sins; my bonds are cut, and I am free.
Seizing (my) arm, the Guru has lifted (me) out of the blind well, deep and dreadful.
I have become fearless, all fear is erased; the Protector has protected (me).
Such is your gift, my God, that all (my) affairs are set right.
In my mind I have met the Master, the treasure of virtues;
Nanak has sought (his) refuge and is at ease. ॥4॥
383.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When I forget you, everyone turns against me; when you come to mind, (all) serve me.
No other, no second, do I see, O True One, unseen and unfathomable.
When (he) comes to mind, he is ever merciful; what can poor people do?
Tell me, whom should one call bad, and whom good? All beings are yours.
Yours is my support, yours my mainstay; giving (your) hand, you protect (me).
No one speaks an ill word to the person on whom your grace rests.
That alone is peace, that alone is greatness, which pleases God's mind.
You are wise, you are ever kind; if I am given the Naam, I revel in joy.
Before you is my prayer: soul and body, all is yours.
Says Nanak, all greatness is yours; no one even knows my name. ॥4॥
383.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Show mercy, O God, Knower of hearts; in the Saadh Sangat the Lord is found.
Opening the doors, he shows the sight of himself, and one does not come into birth again.
May I meet my beloved Master and be rid of all my sorrows, O brother;
in the company of one who has worshipped the Supreme Lord in the heart, may I swim across, O brother.
(The world) has become a great wilderness, an ocean of fire, where one dwells amid joy and grief;
meeting the True Guru, the mind has become pure, repeating with the tongue the Lord's Amrit (Name).
(Man) has set up body and wealth, all of it, as his own, and is bound in soft bonds (of attachment);
by the Guru's grace those servants are set free who have worshipped the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
God the Protector has saved those who are pleasing to their God.
Soul and body, all is yours, O Giver; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to you). ॥4॥
383.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
You have broken free of the foul sleep of attachment, O friend; what grace has come upon you?
The great enchantress (Maya) has no hold on you; where has your sloth gone, O friend?
Lust, anger and pride are hard to master; by what discipline have you escaped them, O friend?
(They) have plundered good men, gods, demons, the beings of the three qualities, the whole world, O friend.
Fire in the forest has burnt up much of the grass; only some rare green plant is left, O friend.
I cannot describe one so mighty; no words can tell that one's worth, O friend.
(She answers:) In a room of lamp-black I was not blackened; my colour has stayed spotless, O friend.
The Guru's great mantra has come to dwell in (my) heart; I have heard the wondrous Naam, O friend.
God in his mercy cast (his) gracious glance and joined (me) to his feet.
Through loving devotion, O Nanak, (I) have found peace, and am absorbed in the company of the Saadh. ॥4॥
384.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, Ghar 7, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The red gown looks lovely on your body, (O friend);
you have pleased the Beloved, and so you have won (his) heart.
How did this glow of yours come about, O friend?
With what dye have you turned so rosy red?
You alone are beautiful; yours alone is the married bliss;
in your house is the Beloved, in your house is good fortune.
You are pure in conduct, you are foremost;
you have pleased the Beloved, you alone have lofty wisdom.
(She answers:) I pleased the Beloved, and so (I am dyed) in the deep red (of his love);
says Nanak, (he) has looked on (me) with a kindly eye.
Listen, my friend: this is all my labour:
God, who adorns and makes beautiful, has himself adorned (me). ॥1॥
384.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When I was far (from him), the pain was great;
now, by (the Guru's) counsel, I have been brought into his presence.
My complaining is over, my friends and companions;
my doubt is gone; the Guru has united me with my Husband Lord.
Bringing (me) near, (he) has placed (me) on the Beloved's bed;
I am freed from bowing in deference (to others).
Through the Shabad there is light in the mansion (of my heart);
my Master is full of bliss and play.
Good fortune is on my forehead: my Husband has come home;
servant Nanak has gained a wedded bliss that endures. ॥4॥
384.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
My mind is joined to the Name of the True One;
with people, my dealings go only as far as need requires.
Outwardly I am on easy terms with all, and glad with them,
yet I stay untouched, as the lotus does in the water.
With my mouth I talk with everyone,
but my God I hold close to my heart.
(To others my mind) seems very hard and cold,
(yet) this mind (of mine) is the dust of everyone's feet.
Servant Nanak has found the Perfect Guru,
(who) has shown (me) the One (Lord), within and without. ॥4॥
385.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Strong in his youth, (a man) revels in pleasures;
(but) without the Name he mingles with the dust.
He wears rings in his ears and fine clothes on his body,
(sleeps on) a soft bed, and is proud in his mind.
Elephants beneath him, a golden canopy over his head;
(yet) without devotion to the Lord, he is taken and buried in the earth.
(There may be) many women of beautiful form,
(but) without the Lord's sweet essence all tastes are insipid.
Maya is a deceiver, and the vices are poison;
O God, merciful Being, Nanak has come to your refuge. ॥4॥
385.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
There is a garden, in which very many trees have been planted;
in it the Amrit of the Naam has come to fruit.
O wise one, reflect in such a way
that the state beyond all desire may be reached.
All around are pools of poison, (but) in the middle is the Amrit, O brother.
The one who waters it is the one Gardener alone;
he looks after every leaf and every branch.
He has brought every kind of plant and set it (in this garden);
all of it has flowered; not one is without fruit.
The one who has received from the Guru the Amrit fruit, the Naam:
O servant Nanak, he has crossed over (the ocean of) Maya. ॥4॥
385.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) your Name has made (for me) the delights of a kingdom;
as I sing your Kirtan, yoga too is attained.
In your shelter every comfort has come about;
the True Guru has drawn back the curtains of doubt.
Understanding (your) Hukam, I enjoy every joy and delight;
through the True Guru's service (I) have become wholly free of desire.
One who has known you is approved, whether householder or renunciant;
the one dyed in the Naam is the one free of desire.
The one who has received the treasure of the Naam:
says Nanak, that one's treasury is full. ॥4॥
385.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
If I go to a place of pilgrimage, (I find people) crying I, I;
if I ask the pandits, they are steeped in Maya.
O friend, tell me of that place
where the Lord's Kirtan, Har Har, goes on day after day.
The Shastras and the Vedas (teach) the reckoning of sin and merit,
(by which) one is born again and again in hell and in heaven.
In the householder's life there is anxiety, in renunciation there is pride;
doing rituals, the soul is caught in entanglements.
(The one whose) mind has come under control by God's grace:
O Nanak, through the Guru that one has crossed over (the ocean of) Maya.
In the Saadh Sangat let us sing the Kirtan of the Lord;
this place is found through the Guru. ॥7॥
385.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
There is peace at home, and peace outside too;
remembering the Lord, all sorrows are destroyed.
(O Lord,) when you come into the mind, there is every comfort;
(but) only the one who pleases you repeats the Naam.
Repeating your Name, body and mind are cooled and calmed;
repeating (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, the camp of sorrow is torn down.
Only one who understands (God's) Hukam is approved,
one who bears the True Shabad as his seal of passage.
The Perfect Guru has made the Name of the Lord firm (within me);
says Nanak, my mind has found peace. ॥4॥
386.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O Lord,) where you send me, there I go;
what you give me, in that I find my comfort.
O Govind, Lord of the world (Gosain), I am your servant for ever;
by your grace I am filled and content.
What you have given, that I wear and eat;
by your grace, O God, I spend (my days) in comfort.
Within my mind and body I meditate on you alone;
I set no one beside you as your equal.
Says Nanak: (grant that) I may meditate (on you) thus for ever,
(and) attain the highest state, falling at the feet of the Sants. ॥4॥
386.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Rising, sitting and sleeping, let us meditate (on the Lord);
walking on the road, let us sing of the Lord, Har Har.
With the ears, let us listen to the Amrit account (of the Lord's praises),
hearing which there is bliss in the mind, (and) all the sorrows and sicknesses of the mind are lifted away.
In every task and every work, on the road and at the river crossing, let us repeat (his Name);
by the Guru's grace, let us drink the Lord's Amrit (of the Name).
Day and night let us sing the Kirtan of the Lord;
(the one who sings it,) that person is not set on the road of Jam.
(O Lord,) the one who does not forget you at any hour:
O Nanak, falling at that one's feet, the highest state is attained. ॥4॥
386.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Remember the Lord,) through whose remembrance peace comes to dwell (in the mind);
there is well-being, and sorrows are destroyed.
Live in bliss; sing the praises of God;
for ever and ever win the favour of your True Guru.
Live by the True Guru's true Shabad;
(so,) steady and seated in your own home (within), you will find your God.
Do not hold ill will for another in your mind;
(then) no sorrow (will come) to you, O brother, O friend.
The Guru has given the Lord, Har Har, as the charm and the mantra;
O Nanak, (the one who received it) has come to know this peace, night and day. ॥4॥
386.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The lowly one, whom no one even knows,
is honoured in the four directions by repeating the Naam.
I beg for the sight of you: grant it, O Beloved;
whom has your service not carried across?
The one whom no one would come near:
the whole creation rubs and washes that one's feet.
The mortal who was of use to no one:
by the grace of the Sant (the Guru), that one's name is (now) repeated (by all).
In the Saadh Sangat the mind that slept wakes up;
then, O Nanak, God seems sweet. ॥4॥
386.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
With my eyes I behold the One, the One alone,
(and) ever and ever keep the Name of the Lord treasured (in my heart).
I sing the praises of Ram, of Ram the beautiful;
by the power of the Sant (the Guru), in the Saadh's company, I meditate, O brother, on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
The One on whose thread all creation is strung:
In an instant he brings about the creation and the dissolution (of the world),
(yet) himself stays untouched, beyond (Maya's three) qualities.
He does and causes all to be done; he is the knower of hearts;
387.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The wanderings of millions of births have ended;
(the game of) this human body, so hard to come by, is won, not lost.
Sins are wiped out, sorrow and pain are far away;
by the dust of the Sants' feet (they) have become pure.
God's Sants have the power to save;
(but) they meet only the one for whom such union was written from the very start.
The Guru has given the mantra (of the Name), and there is bliss in the mind;
craving is quenched, and the mind has become steady.
The Name, that precious thing, is the nine treasures and the siddhis;
O Nanak, (this) understanding is received from the Guru. ॥4॥
387.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Thirst (for Maya) and the darkness of ignorance are gone;
serving the Saadh (the Guru), a host of sins has been cut away.
There is peace, Sahaj, and abundant bliss;
through the Guru's service, minds have become pure, hearing the Name of the Lord, Har Har, Har Har.
The folly and the stubbornness of the mind are destroyed;
God's will has come to seem sweet.
The feet of the Perfect Guru were grasped,
(and) the sins of millions of births were washed away.
This life, a jewel, has borne its fruit;
says Nanak, God has shown mercy. ॥4॥
387.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Keep your True Guru treasured (in the heart), ever and always;
dust the Guru's feet with (your) hair.
Wake up, O mind, you who can wake!
Without the Lord nothing else will be of use (to you); attachment is false, (the world's) spread is perishable.
Fall in love with the Guru's Bani;
(when) the Guru is merciful, sorrow goes.
Apart from the Guru there is no other resting place;
the Guru is the Giver, and it is the Guru who gives the Name.
The Guru is himself the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God;
at all hours, O Nanak, meditate on the Guru. ॥4॥
387.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
God himself is the trunk (of the tree of the world), and he himself has spread out its branches;
he himself is the keeper of his own crop.
Wherever I look, there is that One alone;
within each and every heart it is he himself (who dwells).
He himself is the sun, and the reach of its rays;
he is the unseen, and he is the visible form.
Sargun and Nirgun: he (himself) sets up these two names;
the two together have made their dwelling in the One.
Says Nanak, the Guru has rid (me) of doubt and fear;
(now) with (my own) eyes I have seen him whose form is bliss, everywhere. ॥4॥
387.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I know nothing at all of reasoning or cleverness;
day and night I utter your Name.
I am without virtue; there is no virtue (in me) at all;
O God, you are the one who does and causes all to be done.
I am foolish, dull, ignorant and thoughtless;
(yet) I hold in my mind the hope of your Name.
I have practised neither chanting, austerity, self-restraint nor (any) ritual deed;
in my mind I have contemplated only God's Name.
I know nothing, my understanding is small;
Nanak prays: O God, your shelter is all I have. ॥4॥
388.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Har Har: these two words are (my) rosary;
telling it again and again, (God) becomes merciful to the lowly.
O True Guru, I make this plea of mine:
be merciful and keep (me) in your refuge, and give me the rosary of the Lord's Name, Har Har.
One who keeps the Lord's rosary within the heart
is rid of the pain of birth and death.
One who cherishes (the Lord) in the heart and with the mouth speaks Har Har:
that person never wavers anywhere, here or hereafter.
Says Nanak, one who is absorbed in the Name:
the Lord's rosary goes along with him (into the hereafter). ॥4॥
388.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
One who becomes his to whom all this belongs:
no taint (of Maya) clings to that servant.
The Lord's servant is ever free;
whatever (God) does seems good to (his) servant; the servant's way of life is utterly pure.
One who has left all else and come to the Lord's refuge:
how can Maya take hold of that servant?
One in whose mind is the treasure of the Name
knows no anxiety, even in a dream.
Says Nanak, (the one who) has found the Perfect Guru:
has had all (his) doubt and attachment destroyed. ॥4॥
388.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When my God has become fully pleased,
then tell me, how can sorrow or doubt come near?
Hearing of your glory again and again, I live;
save me, who am without virtue.
Sorrow is gone and anxiety forgotten;
(this) fruit I have gained by repeating the True Guru's mantra.
He alone is true, ever true is he;
remember him again and again, and keep him strung (like a garland) about your neck.
Says Nanak, what (other) deed (is left to do)
for one in whose mind the Lord's Name has come to dwell? ॥4॥
388.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(People) are ruined in lust, anger and ego;
the Lord's servants, doing the Lord's Simran, have escaped.
Drunk on the wine of Maya, (people) lie asleep;
the devotees are awake, remembering the Lord, steeped (in his love).
In attachment and doubt (people) are made to wander through many births;
the devotees, who have meditated on the Lord's feet, stand firm.
(The thought) this house is mine is bondage, a blind well;
the Sants are free, for they know the Lord to be close by.
Says Nanak, one who is in God's refuge
has found peace here and the highest state hereafter. ॥4॥
389.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) you are my water, and I am your fish;
you are my Master, and I lie at your door.
You are my Creator, I am your servant;
O God, deep (ocean) of virtues, I have taken hold of your refuge.
You are my life, you are (my) support;
at the sight of you the lotus (of my heart) opens.
You are my highest state and my honour; it is you who accept (me);
you are all-powerful, and your strength is what I lean on.
Night and day may I repeat (your) Name, O treasure of virtues:
this is Nanak's prayer to God. ॥4॥
389.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The one who weeps (for the dead) is only acting out a falsehood;
the stranger offers his sorrow laughing all the while.
Someone has died, (while) in someone's house there is singing;
one weeps, another bursts out laughing.
(man) does not reach (his goal), (his round) does not end, and then he repents.
The world goes about within the three qualities (of Maya);
again and again it is born into hell and heaven.
Says Nanak, one whom (God) has joined to the Name:
that one's life is fruitful and accepted. ॥4॥
389.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The soul-bride) slept on and knew nothing of God;
Through love of the Beloved, in Sahaj, I keep bliss in my mind, O friend;
I long to meet God, so how could I be idle, O friend?
(God) brought Amrit and poured it into (her) hand;
(but) it slipped away and fell upon the ground.
(She) was weighed down with relish (for pleasures), attachment and ego;
the fault is not God's, the Doer of all.
In the Saadh Sangat the darkness of doubt was dispelled,
(and) O Nanak, the Creator united (her with himself). ॥4॥
389.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(When) there is hope in (your) lotus feet, O Beloved,
the wretched servants of Jam take flight.
It is by your mercy that you come to mind;
remembering (your) Name, every ailment is destroyed.
(Jam's servants) inflict countless pains on others,
(One in whose) mind a thirst for the sight of you has arisen
dwells, detached, in Sahaj and bliss.
give (him) the Name alone, (to dwell) in (his) heart. ॥4॥
389.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The mind is satisfied, its entanglements are gone,
(for) my own God has become merciful.
By the grace of the Sant (the Guru), it has gone well (with me):
the fearless Master, in whose house everything is in full, has met (me).
The merciful Saadh (the Guru) has made the Name firm (within),
(and) the most dreadful hunger is gone.
the burning (of craving) is quenched, and there is peace in the mind.
The searching is over, the mind is merged in Sahaj;
Nanak has found the treasure of the Name. ॥4॥
390.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
One whose (bond) with the Master is made
stays content with the perfect food (of the Name).
The Lord's devotees are short of nothing:
not to eat, nor to spend, nor to enjoy, nor to give (to others).
One whose Master is the unreachable Lord of the world:
tell me, how far can any man's (power) prevail (against him)?
Him by whose service the eighteen siddhis are gained
in the twinkling of an eye: cling to his feet.
Those on whom you show mercy, my Lord,
390.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When I meditated on my True Guru,
then my mind found great peace.
Anxious reckoning has ended, and doubt is destroyed;
the servants (of God) steeped in the Name have become fortunate.
When I (kept) my Lord in my mind,
then, my friend, (my) fear was gone.
When I took hold of your shelter, O God,
then the longing of my mind was fulfilled.
Seeing (your) wondrous play, the mind has taken heart;
your servant Nanak trusts in you. ॥4॥
390.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Night and day the mouse (of time) gnaws at the rope (of life);
falling into the well, (you) go on eating sweets.
In worrying and scheming the night (of life) has passed;
dwelling on the many pleasures of Maya, (man) never remembers the Lord, Saringpani.
He has made his home in a tree's shade, taking it to be lasting;
(he is) in the noose of death, and a mighty arrow is drawn (at him).
A bank of sand has come into the mouth of the waves,
(yet) the fool has taken that place to be firm.
One who has repeated (the Name of) the Lord King in the Saadh Sangat:
O Nanak, (that one) lives, singing the Lord's praises. ॥4॥
390.4: Raag Asa, nine Dutuke, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O body,) in the company of that (soul) you play and delight;
in its company you mingle with one and all;
in its company everyone wants you;
without it, no one so much as turns a face towards you.
Where has that detached one (the soul) gone to merge?
Without it, O (body), you are wretched.
In its company you are held capable in the home;
in its company you have become well known;
in its company you are kept and tenderly cherished;
without it you are cast off and left to lie in the dust.
In its company you have honour and greatness;
in its company the world is your kin;
in its company you are provided for in every way;
without it you have become dust.
That detached one neither dies nor is born;
bound by (God's) Hukam, it does its work.
O Nanak, having set (the body) up, (God) joins (the soul to it) and parts them again;
he alone knows his own creative power. ॥4॥
390.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
He (God) does not die, and we do not fear (death);
he does not perish, and we do not fret;
he is not poor, and we are not hungry;
he has no pain, and no pain troubles us.
There is no other who can kill (us);
the Giver of our life lives for ever.
He has no bonds, and we are not bound;
he has no entanglements, and we are not entangled;
he has no filth, and no filth stains us;
he is in bliss, so we too are ever joyful.
He has no anxiety, and we have no anxiety;
no (Maya's) stain clings to him, and no smear to us;
he has no hunger, and we have no craving;
since he is pure, we too are pure.
We are nothing; he alone, the One, is (all);
before and after, there is only he.
O Nanak, the Guru has done away with the doubts that stood in the way;
we and he have met and become of one hue. ॥4॥
391.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In many ways one should serve (her);
life, breath and wealth should be laid before (her);
giving up pride, I would carry water and wave the fan (for her);
again and again one should be a sacrifice (to her).
Only she who pleases God is the happy soul-bride;
O my mother, may I come to be in her company.
(I would be) the water-carrier of the maid of (their) maids;
may the dust (of their feet) dwell with my very life;
if fortune is (written) on my forehead, I shall find (their) company;
(through it) the Master, in his own love, comes to meet.
Chanting, austerities and all observances I would give (for it);
rites, religious duties and all fire-offerings I would offer up;
shedding pride and attachment, I would become the dust (of their feet);
in their company I would see God with my own eyes.
Every moment, this alone is what I pray for:
that day and night I may carry out this service.
Gopal, Gobind, has become merciful;
O Nanak, the Forgiving One (has been found) in the Saadh Sangat. ॥4॥
391.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Through the love of God there is always peace;
through the love of God no sorrow touches (one);
through the love of God (one) sheds the filth of Haumai;
through the love of God (one) becomes pure for ever.
Listen, friend: such is loving devotion (to God)
that it is the support of life and breath, of each and every heart.
Through the love of God all treasures have come;
through the love of God the pure Naam (dwells) in the heart;
through the love of God (one) is glorious for ever;
through the love of God all anxiety is erased.
Through the love of God (one) crosses this world-ocean;
through the love of God (one) does not fear Jam;
through the love of God (one) saves all (others too);
the love of God goes along with (one).
By one's own doing no one meets (God), nor goes astray;
the one to whom (he) is merciful he blends into the Saadh Sangat.
Says Nanak, (O God,) I am a sacrifice to you;
the Sants have your shelter, O God, and your strength. ॥4॥
391.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Someone) became a king and ruled;
doing wrong upon wrong, he acquired wealth;
hoarding and hoarding, he filled a purse;
(but) God snatched it from him and handed it to another.
(This body is) a pitcher of unbaked clay set in water;
swelling with pride again and again, it sinks into that same (water).
He grew fearless and reckless;
the Creator, who is with him, never came to his mind;
he gathered armies and massed a great host;
(but when) the breath went out of him, he turned to ash.
Lofty mansions, palaces and a queen,
elephants, horses and garments that please the mind,
a large family, sons and daughters:
consumed again and again in attachment (to them), the blind one died.
He who created him destroyed him;
the pleasures and delights (were) like a dream.
He alone is liberated, his are the kingdom and the wealth,
O servant Nanak, on whom the Master is merciful. ॥4॥
392.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The soul) formed a great love for her (Maya);
the more one meets her, the more (that love) grows;
when, clinging to the neck, she will not let go,
(one) is set free by falling at the True Guru's feet.
I have renounced and cast away the enchantress of the world;
the Lord beyond (Maya's three) qualities has met me, and songs of rejoicing ring out.
She is such a beauty that she enchants the mind;
on the road, at the ferry, in the home, in forest after forest, she lies in wait;
seeming sweet, she clings to mind and body;
(but) by the Guru's grace I have seen that she is false.
Her chief attendants, who go before her, are great swindlers;
they spare neither father nor mother;
those who keep company with them, they have seized and bound;
(but) by the Guru's grace I have subdued them all.
Now there is bliss in my mind;
fear is gone, and all the nooses are broken.
Says Nanak, now that I have found the True Guru,
I have settled my whole house in peace. ॥4॥
392.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The Sant) knows (God) to be near at all hours,
and accepts what God does as sweet.
The one Naam is the Sants' support;
they stay as the dust beneath everyone's feet.
Listen, my brother, to the way the Sants live;
its glory cannot be told.
(The Sant is one) whose daily dealing is the Naam alone,
whose resting place is the Kirtan of the One who is bliss itself,
to whom friend and foe are one and the same,
(and who) knows no other than his own God.
(The Sant) cuts away sins by millions upon millions;
(the Sants) take sorrow away and are givers of (true) life;
they are brave warriors, strong in (keeping) their word;
poor Kaula (Maya) has been outwitted by the Sants.
The gods long for the company of such a one,
the sight of whom never fails to bear fruit, and serving whom is fruitful.
With joined hands Nanak offers his prayer:
grant me the service of the Sants, O treasure of virtues. ॥4॥
392.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
All comforts (come) by repeating the Name of the One;
all righteous deeds (lie) in singing the Lord's virtues.
Most holy is the Saadh's company,
on meeting whom one is dyed in the love of God.
By the Guru's grace, such joys are attained by the one
whose mind is lit up by remembering (God); his state and its measure cannot be told.
Fasts, observances, holy baths and worship are all his,
he has heard the Vedas, the Puranas and the Simritis,
whose dwelling (the heart) is most holy and spotless,
(and) within whom, through the Saadh Sangat, is the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
That person becomes known in all the worlds;
the dust of his feet makes the fallen pure.
The one who has met the Lord King, Har Har:
his state and its measure cannot be told.
At all hours, with joined hands, I would meditate (on God),
(and) receive the sight of those Saadhs.
(O God,) take me, the lowly one, and blend me in (with them);
Nanak has come and fallen into your refuge. ॥4॥
393.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Our Salagram, the Lord,) bathes in the waters at all hours;
the all-knowing one ever takes the food offered to him;
he lets no one go away empty;
again and again we fall at his feet.
In our house the Salagram is the service (of the Lord);
our worship, our offering of fragrance and our obeisance are to the Divine Lord.
He whose bell is heard in the four directions,
whose seat is for ever in Baikunth,
whose fly-whisk waves over all,
his incense is ever in bloom (in all that flowers).
He whose casket, O brother, is every heart,
with whom is the assembly of the Saadhs that never breaks up:
(his) aarti is the Kirtan, ever full of bliss;
his glory is beautiful and ever without end.
Only the one whose lot it is to receive him finds him;
that one comes to the refuge of the Sants' feet.
The Lord, the Salagram, has come into (his) hands;
says Nanak, the Guru has given (him) this gift. ॥4॥
393.2: Raag Asa, a Panchpada, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The road on which the water-carrier (the soul-bride) is robbed:
that road lies far away from the Sants.
The Perfect True Guru has made known the Truth (the Name of the eternal Lord);
(O God,) the lane of your Name is open, and the road of Jam is left far behind.
Where the greedy toll-collectors keep their crossing,
that road stays far from (the Lord's) servant.
(there) the Saadhs are in the company of the Supreme Lord.
Chitr and Gupt write the account of all,
(but) on the Lord's devotees they do not so much as cast an eye.
Says Nanak: the one who has the Perfect True Guru,
within him the unstruck trumpets play. ॥5॥
393.3: Raag Asa, one Dupada, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Those who) are taught the Naam in the company of the Saadh (the Guru)
have all their longings and tasks fulfilled;
(their) thirst is quenched, and they are sated with the Lord's praise.
Repeating (the Name of) Saringpani again and again, I live.
(Whoever) has fallen at the refuge of the One who does and causes all to be done
by the Guru's grace has found the home of Sahaj: the darkness is gone, the moon has risen.
The storehouses are full of rubies and jewels;
repeating (the Name of) the Formless One, they never run short.
Any servant who drinks the Amrit of the Shabad,
O Nanak, he attains the supreme state. ॥2॥
394.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 7, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I meditate on the Lord's Name in my heart every day,
(and so) I carry all my companions and comrades across.
The Guru is with me always, ever at my side;
(by his grace,) remembering (God) again and again, I keep him always in my heart.
(O God,) what you do seems sweet (to me);
Nanak begs for the Lord's Name, that precious thing. ॥2॥
394.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Through the company of the Saadh (the Guru), the world has crossed over;
the Lord's Name is the mind's support.
The lotus feet of the beloved Divine Guru
the Lord's Sants worship with love and affection.
The one on whose forehead good fortune is written:
says Nanak, that one's wedded bliss endures. ॥2॥
394.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Since) my Husband's command has come to seem sweet (to me),
my Husband has cast the co-wife out of the house (of my heart).
The Beloved has made (me) his happy bride and adorned (me),
and has taken away the burning of my mind.
It went well that I obeyed what my Beloved said;
(now) I have come to know the peace and Sahaj of this house (of the heart).
I am my Beloved's handmaid, the one who waits on him;
he is imperishable, beyond reach, infinite.
Taking a fan, I fan my Beloved, (standing) at his feet;
the five enemies, the reapers (of my spiritual life), have fled.
I have no (high) family, nor any glory;
what do I know of how I came to please my Husband?
Me, without a protector, poor and without honour,
my Husband took (by the arm) and made his queen.
When my Beloved, my Friend, met me face to face,
(I found) peace and Sahaj, and blessed is my wedded bliss.
Says Nanak, my hope is fulfilled;
the True Guru has joined (me) with God, the treasure of virtues. ॥4॥
394.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
A frown is on her brow, her look is cruel;
she speaks bitter words, her tongue is harsh;
she is ever hungry, and thinks her Husband far away.
Such a woman the Lord has created:
she has eaten up the whole world, (but) the Guru has kept me safe, O my brother.
Giving her thugs' drug, she has the whole world in her sights;
she has bewitched Brahma, Vishnu and Mahadev (Shiva).
Those who, through the Guru, are joined to the Name are made beautiful.
(People) have worn themselves out with fasts, observances and acts of atonement;
they have roamed the banks of holy rivers and tiraths over all the earth.
Only they are saved who are in the True Guru's refuge.
The whole world is bound in attachment to Maya;
the foolish manmukh is consumed in Haumai.
O Nanak, the Guru has taken me by the arm and saved me. ॥4॥
394.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When you are forgotten, O Master, all sorrows (come);
(such) a mortal is of no use, here or hereafter.
The Sants are content, meditating on the Lord, Har Har;
(O God,) in your mercy you have joined (them) to your Name; all comfort, O God, is in your will.
(Whoever) thinks the One who is with him far away
(Those who) do not call to mind the One who gave everything
pass their days and nights in the great poison (of Maya).
Says Nanak: remember the One God;
in the shelter of the Perfect Guru the highest state is attained. ॥4॥
395.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Repeating the Naam, mind and body all grow green;
all sins and faults are cast away.
Blessed is that day alone, O my brother,
(on which), singing the Lord's praises, the supreme state is attained.
(The one who) has worshipped the feet of the Saadhs:
the troubles and the hatreds have gone from (his) mind.
(The one who), meeting the Perfect Guru, has ended the strife (within):
the five enemies have all come under (his) control.
The one in whose mind the Lord's Name has come to dwell:
Nanak is a sacrifice to him. ॥4॥
395.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Sing (his praises), you who can sing:
(of him who is) the support of soul, body and breath;
serving him, you will obtain every comfort
and never again go to anyone else.
The Master is ever in bliss, the source of bliss, the treasure of virtues; (his Name) is to be repeated day after day.
I am a sacrifice to that beloved Sant (the Guru) by whose grace God is made to dwell in the mind.
He whose giving never runs out,
(enshrining whom) all are well absorbed in Sahaj,
whose grace no one can undo:
that True One is to be enshrined in the mind.
He in whose house every good thing is in full store,
the servants of that God do not pine in sorrow;
(in whose) shelter the state without fear is gained:
with every breath, that treasure of virtues is to be sung.
He is not far away; where should one go (to seek him)?
When he looks with grace, then the Lord, Har Har, is found.
I offer my prayer to the Perfect Guru:
Nanak begs for the wealth of the Lord, (his) capital. ॥4॥
395.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
First, the pain of the body was ended;
(then) the whole mind found peace.
In his mercy the Guru gave (me) the Name:
over and over I am a sacrifice to that True Guru.
I have found the Perfect Guru, O my brother;
in the True Guru's refuge, disease, grief and all pain are destroyed.
I have enshrined the Guru's feet in my heart
(and) have obtained all the fruits my mind longed for.
The fire (of craving) is quenched, all is cool and calm;
the Guru, in his mercy, has bestowed (this) gift.
To one who had no place, the Guru has given a place;
to one without honour, the Guru has given honour;
cutting (my) bonds, (the Guru) has kept (me) as his servant;
(my) tongue tastes the Amrit Bani.
By great good fortune (I) worshipped the Guru's feet,
(and) giving up all (else), have found God's refuge.
O Nanak, the one to whom the Guru has become merciful
has become happy for ever. ॥4॥
396.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The True Guru has sent (this child);
by the union (God) ordained, one who will live long has come into being.
When he came and made his dwelling in the womb,
great was the gladness in the mother's heart.
A son is born, a devotee of Govind;
what was written at the Source has become manifest among all.
By (God's) Hukam the child was born in the tenth month;
grief is gone, and there is great joy.
The companions sing the song of joy, Gurbani,
which is pleasing to the mind of the True Master.
The vine has spread, and the line runs on through many generations;
the Lord has bound the power of dharma fast and set it in place.
What the mind longed for, the True Guru has obtained (for us);
(we) are free of care, our loving attention fixed on the One.
As a child counts greatly on his father,
(so the Guru's servant) speaks as he is bidden, in the Guru's will.
This is no hidden or secret matter:
Guru Nanak, well pleased, has bestowed this gift. ॥4॥
396.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Giving (his) hand, the Perfect Guru has kept (his servant) safe,
and the servant's glory has become plain to all.
I keep repeating Guru, Guru; I keep meditating on the Guru, the Guru;
the prayer of my heart I lay before the Guru.
(We) have come to the refuge of the True Gurdev,
and the servant's service has come to fruition.
(The Guru) protects soul and body, youth and the breath of life.
Says Nanak, I give myself in sacrifice to the Guru. ॥3॥
396.3: Raag Asa Kafi, Ghar 8, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
I am a slave bought for a price; my Master is the True One.
Soul and body, all is his; (O Lord,) everything is yours.
O Master, you are the honour of (me), the one without honour; my trust is in you.
One who leans on any support but the True One, know him to be unripe.
Your Hukam is boundless; no one finds its end.
Whoever meets the Perfect Guru walks in (your) will.
Cleverness and shrewd ways are of no use at all;
the only peace (we) receive is what the Master, well pleased, gives.
Though hundreds of thousands of rites be performed, no dam at all is set (against craving).
Servant Nanak has taken the Naam as (his) support and left every other pursuit. ॥4॥
396.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I have searched through every pleasure: none is as great as the Lord;
that True Master is found when the Guru is pleased.
To my own Guru I am devoted, forever and ever a sacrifice;
(O Guru,) bless (me) with this gift: may I not forget the Naam for a single instant, the least moment.
He alone is truly rich within whom is the wealth of the Lord;
he is freed from the great net, within whom the Guru's Shabad abides unbroken.
What can I say of the Guru's greatness? The Guru is a lake of discernment and truth.
He is the perfect Supreme God, from the beginning, from the dawn of the ages, through every age.
Meditate on the Naam forever and ever, the mind dyed in the love of the Lord, Har Har.
To me the Guru is soul, breath and wealth, and he is with Nanak. ॥4॥
397.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
When the Master, unseen and infinite, dwells in the mind even for a moment,
my pain, my suffering and my sickness all flee, O mother.
I give myself up in sacrifice to my own Master;
repeating (his Name), great bliss fills mind and body.
When I hear even a little talk of that True Master,
I find the peace beyond all peace, O mother, whose worth I cannot reckon.
He is lovely to the eyes; seeing him, I have fallen in love (with him).
I am without virtue, O my mother, yet he himself has tied me to the hem of his garment.
He is beyond the Vedas, the Kateb and the world, beyond them all;
(yet) Nanak's King is seen, plainly manifest. ॥4॥
397.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) hundreds of thousands of devotees worship (you), repeating Beloved, Beloved;
by what means am I, a soul without virtue and given to vice, to meet (you)?
You are (my) support, O Govind, O Gopal, O merciful God;
you are the Lord of all; all creation is yours.
(You are) the Sants' helper always; they see you ever present;
those bereft of the Naam die grieving and grieving.
Those who live as servants of (your) servants have had their wandering (through births) ended;
those who have forgotten the Naam: what can be said of their plight?
Like a beast that strays into green crops is the whole world;
says Nanak: O God, cut (my) bonds and unite (me with you) yourself. ॥4॥
397.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Put all things out of mind and keep the One alone in your thought;
cast off false pride, and lay mind and body before (him) as an offering.
Praising you at all hours, O Creator,
I live; (grant me) this gift of yours, be merciful to me.
Do only that work by which the face is made bright;
he alone is joined to the True One, O Allah, to whom you give (this gift).
Set in order that house which will never fall at all;
enshrine the One in your mind, who never dies.
Those who have found favour with God hold the Lord dear;
by the Guru's grace Nanak has spoken of the One who is beyond telling. ॥4॥
397.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those who never forget the Naam: what are they like?
Know no difference at all: they are like the Master himself.
Meeting with you, (O Lord,) mind and body are filled with delight;
by the grace of (your) servant, peace is found and all pain is wiped away.
All the continents and worlds there are, they have carried across,
those in whose minds (God) himself has come to dwell; they are the perfect devotees.
The one whom (God) himself honours is the one honoured (by all);
such a one is renowned and accepted, known in every place.
That (Nanak) may worship (you) day and night and hold (you) dear with every breath:
fulfil this longing of Nanak, O True King. ॥4॥
398.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
He, our Lord and Master, pervades every place;
there is one Master, the royal canopy over his head; there is no other.
As it pleases you, keep (me), O Protector;
apart from you, my eyes have beheld no other.
God himself cherishes (all); in every heart he takes care (of each);
the one in whose mind he himself has come to dwell, he never forgets.
Whatever he does, he does himself, by his own will;
in every age he has been known as the helper of his devotees.
Repeating the Name of the Lord over and over, one never grieves;
Nanak thirsts for the sight of you: fulfil (his) longing. ॥4॥
398.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Why do you sleep, having forgotten the Naam, O heedless, careless one?
How many are being swept away in this river!
O mind, the Lord's feet are a (good) ship; boarding it, one crosses over,
singing (his) virtues at all hours in the company of the Saadh.
(People) enjoy countless pleasures, (but) without the Name they are empty;
without devotion to the Lord, they die again and again, and weep.
Fine clothes, pleasures, perfumes, the body rubbed with scented pastes:
(yet) without Simran the body is dust, and it must surely depart.
Rare is the one who has seen how very treacherous the world is;
release lies in the Lord's refuge: O Nanak, this is the writ that is written. ॥4॥
398.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
No one goes along with anyone; why then be proud?
With the one Naam for support, the terrifying world-ocean is crossed.
For me, the poor one, you are the true support, O my Perfect True Guru;
beholding the sight of you, my mind takes heart.
Power and wealth are entanglements: count them as of no use in any task;
the Lord's Kirtan is the (true) support; this wealth never moves.
All the pleasures of Maya are but shadows;
the Naam, the treasure of peace, is sung through the Guru.
You are true, a treasure of virtues, O God, deep and unfathomable;
in Nanak's heart is hope and trust in the Master (alone). ॥4॥
398.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The One in whose remembrance pain departs and the peace of Sahaj is found:
on him, the Lord, Har Har, let us meditate night and day with palms joined.
Nanak's God is he to whom everyone belongs;
he fills all; he alone is True, ever True.
Within and without he is with (us), our helper, the One worth knowing;
worship him, O mind, and every sickness is destroyed.
The infinite Protector keeps (us) safe (even) in the fire (of the womb);
cooling is the Name of the Lord, Har Har; remembering it, the burning goes.
Peace, Sahaj and bliss abound, O Nanak, (for one who becomes) the dust (of the feet) of the Lord's servants;
meeting the Perfect Guru, all (his) tasks have been fulfilled. ॥4॥
399.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Gobind, the treasure of virtues, is known through the Guru;
when he is kind and merciful, the Lord's love is enjoyed.
Come, Sants, let us meet and tell the story of the Lord;
night and day let us remember the Naam, casting off the shame of what people say.
Repeating the Naam over and over I live, and great bliss arises;
attachment is vain; the world is false and bound to perish.
Only a rare one has formed a love for (God's) lotus feet;
blessed and beautiful is the face of the one who has meditated on the Lord.
In remembering (him), the pain of birth and death and (the dread of) Death are wiped away;
for Nanak, peace is whatever pleases God. ॥4॥
399.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Come, friends, let us gather together and enjoy every flavour and relish:
let us repeat the Amrit Name of the Lord, Har Har, and together cast off (our) sins.
Reflect on the essence, O Sants; then no obstacle stands in the way:
all the thieves (the vices) are worn down, for through the Guru one stays awake.
Take a humble mind as provisions for the road; burn up the poison of Haumai;
true is the shop, full the bargain: trade in the goods of the Naam.
Those who have offered up soul, body and wealth are the ones with honour;
pleasing to their own God, they delight (in him) always.
Those who drink the wine of evil counsel turn debauched and crazed;
(but) those dyed in the elixir of the Lord (Ram), O Nanak, are addicted to the True One. ॥4॥
399.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
As (the Guru) moved me, I made the effort and set about (the work of the Name);
I repeat the Naam and live by repeating it; the Guru has fixed the mantra firm (within me).
Let us fall at the True Guru's feet, who has shattered doubt;
God in his mercy has set the True (Name within us) and made (our life) beautiful.
The True One, the Lord of the Will, has taken (us) by the hand and made (us) his own by his Hukam;
the gift God has given is complete glory.
Ever and ever (his) praises are sung, repeating the Name of Murari (the Lord);
God has shown his grace, and the True Guru has seen (my) vow through.
The Perfect Guru has given (me) the Naam for wealth, and singing (his) praises for gain;
the Sants are the traders (in the Name), O Nanak; the Banker is God, who is without limit. ॥4॥
399.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O God, the one whose Master you yourself are is greatly blessed;
he lives at ease, ever at peace; all his doubt and fear have fled.
We are servants of Gobind; my Master is mighty.
He who does and causes all to be done, in every way, is our True Guru.
There is no other, no second, whom one should fear;
through the Guru's service the (Lord's) mansion is reached, and the world, so hard to cross, is crossed.
(O God,) by your glance (of grace) peace is found, and the treasure (of the Name dwells) in the mind;
those servants on whom you have had mercy are accepted (at your door).
The Lord's Kirtan is the taste of Amrit; only a rare one drinks it;
(the one who) receives the one Naam as (his) wage, O Nanak, lives by repeating it over and over in the heart. ॥4॥
400.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The God whose humble handmaid I am is higher than all;
everything, little or much, is called his.
My soul, my breath of life and my wealth I hold to be the Master's;
through whose Name I am made radiant, his handmaid I count myself.
(O Lord,) you need no one, you are all bliss; (your) Name is a jewel, a diamond;
she whose King you are is sated and content, ever at peace.
O companions and friends at my side, I press good counsel upon you:
serve the Saadh (the Guru) with love; so it is that I find the Lord, the treasure.
All (souls) are handmaids of the Master, all call (him) mine;
(but) she whom (he himself) adorns, O Nanak, makes her dwelling in peace. ॥4॥
400.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Become the humble handmaid of the Sants, O friend; learn this conduct;
of all virtues, this virtue is highest: do not see the Husband (Lord) as far away.
Dye this mind of yours, O lovely one, in the Lord's Name, in the fast colour of madder;
giving up cleverness and cunning, know Gopal (the Lord) to be with you.
Whatever the Husband says should be accepted: make this your adornment, O friend;
the love of another should be forgotten: chew this betel.
Make the Guru's Shabad your lamp, and spread this bed of pure conduct;
stay with palms joined at all hours; then the Lord King meets (you).
Hers alone is good conduct, hers all adornment; she alone is beautiful, (absorbed) in the Infinite;
she alone is the happy wife, O Nanak, who has pleased the Creator. ॥4॥
400.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Stumbling and wavering last only as long as the mind wanders in doubt;
my own Guru cut away (my) doubts, and (I) found rest.
Those quarrelsome foes (lust and the rest) have all, through the Guru, given up;
now we are free of them, and they have let go of us.
Thinking in terms of mine and yours, one is bound from that very moment;
when the Guru cut away ignorance, the nooses fell loose.
As long as one does not grasp the Hukam, so long is one in misery;
meeting the Guru, (one) has recognised the Hukam, and from then on is at peace.
(Now) no one is an enemy or a foe, no one is bad;
the servant who serves the Guru, O Nanak, is the Master's own bondsman. ॥4॥
400.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Peace, Sahaj and great bliss are (mine) as I sing the Lord's Kirtan;
giving (me) his own Name, the True Guru has warded off the (ill-boding) planets.
To my Guru I am a sacrifice; ever and ever I offer myself to him;
I give myself up for the Guru, meeting whom the True (Name) has become (my life's) aim.
Good and bad omens touch the one in whose mind (the Lord) does not dwell;
Jam does not come near the one who is pleasing to the Lord God.
Of all the merit, charity, recitation and austerity there is, the Naam stands above all;
whoever repeats (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, with the tongue has his purpose fulfilled.
(Their) fears are destroyed, doubt and attachment gone; no other (than God) is seen;
O Nanak, those whom the Supreme Lord has kept safe have known no sorrow again. ॥4॥
401.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 9, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
I long to remember (him) and so gain every comfort; (yet who knows) whether in his presence I shall please (him) or not?
There is one Giver, and all are beggars: to whom else should I go?
To beg of any other puts me to shame;
the one Master is sovereign over all: whom could I set beside him as (his) equal?
I rise, I sit down, yet I cannot stay (without him); I search and search for the sight of him.
Brahma and those like him, Sanak and his brothers, Sanak, Sanandan, Sanatan and Sanat Kumar: even for them (the Lord's) mansion is hard to reach.
He is beyond reach, beyond all reach, fathomless; he cannot be grasped, nor his worth set: I cannot find it.
I have sought the refuge of the True Being, and I meditate on the True Guru, the great Being.
God the Master has become kind and merciful, and has cut the bond from (my) neck;
says Nanak, since I found the Saadh Sangat, I shall not come into birth again. ॥4॥
401.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I sing (of him) within, I sing (of him) without, I sing awake and asleep;
(the Guru) has given (me) provisions to take along (on the road); (I am) a trader in the Name of Gobind.
All else I have forgotten, forgotten;
the Perfect Guru granted (me) the Naam as a gift; this is all I rest on.
I sing in sorrow, and I sing in joy too; walking on the road, on the way, I keep (him) in my heart;
the Guru has planted the Naam firm in my mind, (and) quenched my thirst.
I sing by day, I sing by night, I sing with every breath, with my tongue;
in the Sat Sangat the faith takes root that the Lord is (our) companion in life and in death.
Grant servant Nanak this gift, O God, that I may gain the dust (of the feet) of the Sants and keep it in my heart;
that with my ears (I may hear your) praise, with my eyes behold (your) sight, (and rest my) forehead at the Guru's feet. ॥4॥
401.3: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, Ghar 10, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O mind,) those you take to be lasting are guests of two days:
sons, wife, house, all your goods; all love for them is false.
O mind, why do you cry, Aha, aha?
Look closely: (all this) is like the city of Harichand; earn the one profit, the worship of the Lord (Ram).
As clothes worn on the body crumble in two or four days,
(and) how far can one run along a wall? At last its end must come.
As when a tank of water is set up, and salt dissolves the moment it falls in,
(so,) when the order of the Supreme Lord comes, (the soul) will rise and go in an instant.
O mind, by count you walk, by count you sit, by count you draw breath;
ever sing the praise of the Lord, O Nanak: those who hold to the shelter of the True Guru's feet are saved. ॥4॥
402.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
What was crooked has come straight; wicked enemies have turned into friends;
in the darkness a jewel has shone out; the soiled intellect has become clean.
I found peace, riches and the fruit of the Lord's Name, meeting the True Guru.
No one knew me, worthless as I was; (now I) am known in all the worlds;
(once) I could find no seat beside anyone; now all serve (my) feet.
(I) roamed in search of every half-penny; (now) all the craving of my mind is quenched;
(once I) could not bear a single word (from anyone); (now) in the Saadh Sangat (my mind) is cooled.
Which of (his) virtues can one tongue tell? (He is) beyond reach, beyond reach, beyond all reach.
Make (me) the slave of the slaves of (your) slaves; servant Nanak is in your refuge, O Lord. ॥4॥
402.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
O fool, you are slow, so slow, to profit, but quick to run after loss;
you will not buy the cheap goods; O sinner, you are bound by debt.
O True Guru, (my) hope is in you;
your Name, O Supreme Lord, makes the fallen pure; this alone is my shelter.
You hear foul talk and are caught up in it, (but) are idle in taking the Name;
you are eager for thoughts of slander; (your) understanding is upside down.
Others' wealth, others' bodies, slander of others: (like one) gone mad, you eat what should not be eaten;
you take no liking to the true Dharma; hearing the truth, you are stung to anger.
O God, merciful to the poor, kind Master, Lord: your devotees lean on (your) Name;
Nanak has come longing to your refuge, O God: make (him) your own and keep (his) honour. ॥4॥
402.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(People) cling to false companions, bound by attachment to Maya;
where (they) must go does not come to mind; they have gone blind with ego.
O mind, why do you not, detached (from Maya), worship (the Lord)?
You dwell in a chamber of unbaked clay (the body), with all the maladies of the vices around you.
Crying, Mine, mine, day and night go by, and moment by moment life wastes away;
as (a fly) is lured by the taste of sweetness, (so man is caught) in false affairs and in filth.
Lust, anger, greed and attachment: in these, in the pleasures of the senses, (man) is entangled;
(so) the Being, the Creator, has set (him) on the round (of births); again and again he is born.
When (God), destroyer of the pains of the poor, became merciful, then meeting the Guru (I) found every comfort;
says Nanak, I meditate (on him) day and night; (he) has slain and driven out all (my) vices.
In this way, brother, I have meditated on the Being, the Creator:
the destroyer of the pains of the poor became merciful, (and) the pains of birth and death have gone. ॥4॥
403.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O blind one,) for a moment's taste of lust you suffer pain for millions of days;
for a ghari or a muhurat you revel in pleasures, then you regret it over and over.
O blind one, remember the Lord King, Har Har:
that day of yours has drawn near.
Seeing it for a blink of the eye, you are fooled by the bitter gourd, bitter as swallow-wort and neem;
as is keeping company with a snake, O man, so is this (going to) another's house (another's wife).
For the sake of the enemy (Maya) you commit sins, and the real thing lies untouched, set aside;
those who will leave you, with them you keep company, and with the Friend (the Lord) you are at enmity.
Thus is the whole world held fast; only the one who has the Perfect Guru (for his keeper) comes through;
says Nanak, (he) has crossed the world-ocean, (and his) body has become pure. ॥4॥
403.2: Raag Asa, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) what is done in secret, that very thing you have seen; yet the foolish and the senseless deny it.
For their own deeds they are seized and bound, and then, too late, they repent.
My God knows all (your) ways beforehand.
O you, robbed by delusion, you keep a veil (before God), and behind it you do as your own heart pleases.
To whatever (God) sets them, to that they are set; what can any mortal do (of himself)?
Forgive (us), O Supreme Lord and Master; Nanak is ever a sacrifice (to you). ॥2॥
403.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God) himself keeps (the honour) of his servant; he himself has him repeat the Naam.
Wherever his servant has some work or task, there he rises and hastens.
To his servant he shows (himself) close at hand.
Whatever the servant says before his Master comes about at once.
To that servant who pleases his God I am devoted.
Hearing of his good name, the mind turns green again; Nanak comes to touch his feet. ॥2॥
403.4: Raag Asa, Ghar 11, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The actor puts on many kinds of guise, (yet) as he is, so he remains, O brother.
(So the soul,) lost in delusion, has roamed through many births, yet gains no entry into peace, O brother.
O Sants, my companions and my friends, apart from the Lord, Har Har, (all) is passing, O brother.
(Whoever) has joined the Saadh Sangat and sung the Lord's praises has won this precious thing, this human birth, O brother.
Maya of the three qualities is of God's own making; tell me, how is it to be crossed, O brother?
(It is full of) whirlpools, fathomless and hard; through the Guru's Shabad one reaches the far shore, O brother.
Seeking and seeking, having sought and reflected, Nanak has come to know this essence, O brother:
remembering the Naam, the priceless treasure, the mind becomes a jewel and is won over (to it), O brother. ॥3॥
404.1: Raag Asa, Dupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
By the Guru's grace (the Lord) has come to dwell in my mind; whatever I ask for, that I receive, O brother.
In the love of the Naam this mind is sated; I run off nowhere any more, O brother.
My Master is higher than all; night and day I sing of him, O brother.
In an instant he sets up and pulls down; it is of him I would have you stand in awe, O brother.
When I behold God, my own Master, I give no place in my mind to any other, O brother.
God himself has robed servant Nanak in honour; erasing doubt and fear, I engrave (his Name alone in my mind), O brother. ॥2॥
404.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(Lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride, the five,) crush the four castes, all four; the six orders (of ascetics) lie in the palm of (their) hand, O brother.
the handsome, the graceful, the fair of form and the wise, the five have charmed and deceived them all, O brother.
Who is so strong that, joining (the Guru), he has slain the five warriors, O brother?
One who has slain the five, torn them apart and finished them, he is perfect in this Kalyug, O brother.
Theirs is a great clan; they are not brought under control, nor do they flee; their army is strong and stubborn, O brother.
Says Nanak, that person has trampled them down (who lives) under the shelter of the Saadh Sangat, O brother. ॥2॥
404.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The telling of the Lord is the good and sublime thing for the soul; all other tastes are flat (beside it), O brother.
(It is) rich in virtues and sweet of strain; to the sages who know the six (Shastras) nothing else is worthy, O brother.
(It is) the foe of the poison (of the passions), unlike any other, boundless, the bringer of Sahaj; O Nanak, (it) is drunk in the Saadh Sangat, O brother. ॥2॥
404.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(This telling of the Lord) is dear to me, a stream of Amrit; the Guru has not let it slip from (my) mind for an instant, O brother.
(Through it come) the sight (of the Creator), the touch (of his feet), sweetness and delight; (it is) dyed in the Creator's love, O brother.
Uttered for an instant, (it) brings one to the Guru; uttered with every breath, (it keeps) Jam away; O Nanak, (it makes) the Lord a necklace for the throat and the heart, O brother. ॥2॥
404.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Good indeed is the Saadh Sangat.
(There,) every watch, every hour, every moment, singing on and on, Govind, Govind is spoken of.
Walking, sitting, sleeping, the Lord's praise (goes on), and in mind and body (God's) feet are held close.
(O God,) I am of little weight, you, the Master, are of great weight; Nanak has recognised (your) refuge. ॥3॥
405.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 12, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
