Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Leave all your cleverness and worship the Supreme Lord, the Formless One.
Apart from the one True Name, all looks like ashes.
That God is to be known as ever at one's side.
By the Guru's grace (this) is understood, in the love of the one Lord.
The one all-powerful (Lord) alone gives refuge; there is no other place.
Sing the Lord's praises always, (and so) the great and fearsome world-ocean is crossed.
(Thus) birth and death are ended, and there is no suffering in the city of Jam.
That one alone gains the treasure of the Naam to whom God (himself) is gracious.
The One is the prop, the One alone the support, the One the strength in the mind.
O Nanak, joining the Saadh Sangat, let us repeat (his Name); there is none other but the Lord. ॥4॥
405.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Soul, mind, body and breath, and every pleasure enjoyed, are God's gifts.
(He is) kin to the lowly, the Giver of life, able to protect those who come to his refuge.
Meditate, O my mind, on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
(He is your) help here and hereafter, ever at (your) side; fix your loving attention on the One.
To cross the world (-ocean), people ponder the Vedas and the Shastras;
(they perform) rites, religious duties and many ceremonies; (but) the practice of the Naam is above them all.
Lust, anger and pride perish (in one who) meets the divine True Guru.
Make the Naam firm (within), worship the Lord in devotion; good is the service of God.
(I have come to) the refuge of your feet, O Merciful One; you are the honour of the one without honour.
Soul and breath lean on you alone; God is Nanak's strength. ॥4॥
405.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Wavering again and again, (the mind) has suffered great pain without the company of the Saadh (the Guru).
(Now) earn this profit: the sweet essence of Gobind, the Lord, and the love of the one Supreme Lord.
The Lord's Name should be repeated every day.
With every breath meditate on that God, and give up all other love.
That God is the Cause of creation, all-powerful, and himself the Giver of life.
Leave all your cleverness and repeat (the Name of) God at all hours.
He is friend, comrade, helper and companion, lofty, beyond reach, without end.
Keep (his) lotus feet dwelling in the heart; (he) is the mainstay of the soul.
Show mercy, O God, Supreme Lord, that (I) may sing your virtues and your praise.
(In this) is every comfort and great glory; Nanak lives by repeating (your) Name. ॥4॥
405.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Let me strive; make me strive, O Master, beholding (you) in the company of the Saadh (the Guru).
Put on (me) the dye of the Name of the Lord, Har Har; O God, dye (me) yourself (in your love).
May I keep repeating the Name of Ram in my mind.
Show mercy and dwell in my heart; be (my) helper yourself.
Hearing your Name again and again, O beloved God, I long to see (you);
be kind to this worm of yours; this alone is (my) wish, this (my) aim.
Body and wealth are yours, and you are my God; nothing lies in our power.
However you keep (us), so must (we) live; (we) eat what you give.
Bathing in the dust (of the feet) of the Lord's servants cuts away the sins of birth after birth.
Through loving devotion doubt and fear are destroyed; O Nanak, the Lord is ever present (before one). ॥4॥
406.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) the sight of you is beyond reach, beyond the senses; he alone gains it on whose forehead such fortune (is written).
(On whom) the merciful God himself has shown mercy, the True Guru has bestowed the Lord's Name (on him).
O divine Guru, (you) have saved (the souls of) Kalyug (too);
those who were filthy, foolish and witless have all taken to your service.
(O God,) you yourself are the Creator, upholding all creation, pervading all.
Dharam Raj is struck with wonder, for all (creation) has come and fallen at (your) feet.
Satjug, Treta and Duapar are spoken of (as the good ages), (yet) of the ages Kalyug is the best:
(in it) the hand that does (the deed) is the hand that reaps (its fruit); no one is seized in another's place.
O dear Lord, you do just what your devotees ask of you; this is your age-old way.
With palms joined Nanak begs (this) gift: O Lord, grant (me) the sight of your own Sants. ॥4॥
406.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 13, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
have carried (even) those without virtue across.
The most quarrelsome, the wicked and the foul-mouthed have become pure in (your) company.
Those who wandered from birth to birth and fell into hell, (you) have saved their families too.
Those whom no one knew and no one honoured stand out plainly at the Lord's door.
What likeness can I give (you), what praise? Nanak is a sacrifice (to you) every moment. ॥4॥
406.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The crazed (people) lie sleeping (the sleep of attachment).
Drunk on attachment to family and the pleasures of the senses, they keep their grip on what is false.
False longings, joys and delights as in a dream, (these) in mind and with the mouth they call true.
The Amrit Naam, that precious thing, is right beside them, yet they grasp not a sesame-seed of its secret.
O Nanak, those whom (God) in his mercy has kept in the Sat Sangat have come to (his) refuge. ॥4॥
406.4: Raag Asa, Tipade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(I long for) that love of the Beloved alone.
Gold, gems, great pearls and rubies: no, no, (these I) do not (want).
Not kingdom, not fortune, not command, not tasty fare; nothing, nothing at all do I want.
In the refuge of the Sants' feet and in bowing to them I find peace upon peace; Nanak's burning is taken away, now that the Beloved's love is found. ॥3॥
407.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Guru has shown (God) to (these) eyes of mine.
Here and hereafter, in every body, in every heart, it is you, you alone, O Enchanter (Mohan).
You alone, O Beautiful One, are the Maker of the cause (of all), the One alone who holds up the earth.
Nanak touches (the feet of) the Sants, is a sacrifice to the sight of them, and rests in peace upon peace. ॥3॥
407.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is beyond price;
(one who has it) lives at ease in Sahaj.
(God) is the helper at one's side, who never goes away; he is beyond grasp and beyond weighing.
My beloved, my brother, my father, my mother (is he); (he is) the shelter of his devotees.
The Unseen has been made known, found through the Guru; O Nanak, this is the Lord's own marvel. ॥3॥
407.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Keep (me) true to your devotion to the end;
O Master, full of longing, I have come (to your door).
(Grant) the Naam, that precious thing, (so that my life) bears fruit; set (your) feet to dwell in (my) heart.
This is (my) liberation, this (my) way: keep (me) in the company of the Sants.
Plunging deep into the Lord's virtues, may Nanak meditate on the Naam and stay merged in Sahaj. ॥3॥
407.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Lovely are the feet of the Master;
the Lord's Sants have attained them.
(They) have shed their self-regard, done (his) service, and sung (his) praises, relishing them again and again.
(Their) hope is in the One alone, (their) thirst is for the sight (of him); nothing else pleases (them).
(This) is your mercy, (O God); what (power) have poor creatures? Nanak gives himself in sacrifice again and again. ॥3॥
407.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Remember the One within your mind.
Meditate on the Naam, keep it dwelling in your heart; apart from him there is none.
Coming to God's refuge, one gains every reward, and all sorrows depart.
O Nanak, the Giver to all beings, the Creator, the all-pervading Being, is in every heart. ॥3॥
407.6: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Whoever forgets the Lord is dead (in spirit).
Whoever meditates on the Naam obtains every reward; that person has found peace.
(Whoever) calls himself a king and does deeds of ego is held fast in delusion, like a parrot on the nalini.
Says Nanak, the one who has met the True Guru has become steadfast. ॥3॥
407.7: Raag Asa, Ghar 14, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
That love is ever new which stays fixed on one's own Beloved.
Whoever is pleasing to God does not come into birth (again); he stays absorbed in loving devotion to the Lord, in the Lord's love.
God is met when this mind is given (to him); be merciful, (O God,) that Nanak may receive the Naam. ॥2॥
408.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Meet (me), beloved Lord (Ram): without you no one can give (my mind) comfort.
(People) have performed many rites of the Simritis and Shastras, (but) without the sight of you, God, there is no peace.
(They) have grown weary of keeping fasts, vows and disciplines; O Nanak, in the refuge of the Saadh (the Guru), (one) dwells with God. ॥2॥
408.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 15, Partal, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Asleep in the intoxication of vices and Maya, (man) gains no understanding;
only when Jam has seized him by the hair and dragged him up does he come to his senses.
Attached to greed, Maya and sensual pleasures, (they) steal (others') wealth and wound (their) hearts;
drunk with pride in what perishes in an instant, these demons do not understand.
The Vedas, the Shastras and (God's) servants cry it aloud, (but) the deaf one does not hear;
when he has lost the game outright and reached his end, the fool repents in his mind.
He pays every penalty for nothing; in the (Lord's) court it is not counted to his account;
the deed by which his honour would be kept, that deed he has not done.
When the Guru showed me the world to be such, then I sang the praise of the One;
giving up pride, (trust in his own) strength and cleverness, Nanak has come to (his) refuge. ॥4॥
408.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Through trade in the Name of Govind,
(one) wins the favour of the Saadhs and Sants, finds the Beloved, sings (his) praises, and sounds the instruments of the five sounds.
By (God's) grace he gains Sahaj, (the Lord) reveals himself, and now he is dyed in (the love of) Govind;
serving the Sants, he has come to love the Master, and the colour of the Beloved has taken hold of him.
The Guru's wisdom is set firm in (his) mind; joy wells up, he does not come (into birth again); Sahaj (comes), and he finds the treasure in the mind;
he has given up all the cravings of the mind.
It has been long, long, long, so long (without your sight); a great thirst has seized my mind.
O Lord, show me the sight of you; tell me (the way) yourself.
Nanak, the lowly, has come to your refuge: hold (him) to your heart. ॥2॥
408.4: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Rare is the one who breaks down the hard fortress (of vices)
and holds (his mind) back from hope, thirst, deceit, attachment and wandering.
(Rare is the one who) casts off these diseases: lust, anger, greed and pride.
In the company of the Sants, in love with the Naam, I sing the praises of Govind;
night and day I meditate on God;
I conquer the wall of delusion and pull it down.
With me, Nanak, the Naam is the treasure. ॥2॥
408.5: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Give up lust, anger and greed;
remember the Name of Gobind in your mind;
through the worship of the Lord, (all) tasks bear fruit.
Giving up pride, attachment, vice and falsehood, repeat Ram, Ram, Ram;
O mind, fall at the feet of the Sants.
Remember the feet of God, Gopal, merciful to the meek, purifier of the fallen, the Supreme Lord, Hari, and wake up (from the sleep of Maya).
Practise devotion, O Nanak: (in it lies) perfect good fortune. ॥2॥
409.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Joy and grief, detachment and bliss: O friend, (the Lord) has shown (me this) play.
In one moment, fears; in another, fearlessness; in a moment (one) gets up and runs off;
in a moment (he) enjoys pleasures; in another he leaves them and goes.
In a moment (there is) yoga, austerity and much worship; in another (he) wanders in delusion.
In a moment (comes God's) grace: in the company of the Saadh (the Guru), O Nanak, the Lord has imbued (him) with his love. ॥2॥
409.2: Raag Asa Asavari, Ghar 17, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Repeat Gobind, Gobind;
love the Lord, Har Har, in your mind;
what the Guru has said, keep that in your consciousness;
break with all others and turn (your mind) back:
this is how I have found the Beloved, O friend.
The lake (of the world) holds the mire of attachment;
(caught in it,) the foot does not walk toward the Lord;
the foolish man has sunk (his foot) in it.
Make the one single-minded effort (for the One);
then, by falling into (his) refuge, (the foot) comes out, O friend.
Make the mind steady, steady, steady,
(so that) forest and home are the same (to you);
within, (keep) the One Husband;
outwardly, take up many (tasks);
practise Raj Jog.
Says Nanak, (thus one lives) among people (yet) apart from people, O friend. ॥2॥
409.3: Raag Asavari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Hold firmly to one longing (for the One);
joined to the Guru, stay ever in meditation;
be firm in understanding the teaching of the Sant (the Guru);
then, by the Guru's grace, (God) is met, O my mind.
(the Lord is seen) pervading every place;
(the dread of) fearsome Jam has lifted;
a place has been found at the Root (the Lord, trunk of the world's tree);
then all dependence (on others) has ended.
One on whose forehead (this) destiny (is written)
crosses over the fire of fear;
he finds a place in his own home (within);
he savours the relish of the Lord;
his thirst and hunger have gone;
O Nanak, he is merged in Sahaj, O mind. ॥2॥
409.4: Raag Asavari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Lord, Har Har Har, the Master of all virtues:
let us repeat (his Name) in the strain of Sahaj;
the Saadh (the Guru) has uttered (it) with his tongue;
(from him) I have heard the way to be set free;
it is found through great merit, O my mind.
he is hard to find in the world of Kali Yuga;
he is the destroyer of pain;
God fulfils (all) hopes, O my mind.
O mind, he is the one to serve,
he does not perish, nor does he die.
(Whoever) has come to know (him) through the Guru,
O Nanak, that one's mind is won over (to him), O my mind. ॥2॥
410.1: Raag Asavari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Hold to the support of the One alone;
find the treasure within your mind:
(thus) one is absorbed in peace, O my mind.
crosses (the world-ocean) so hard to cross;
whom the Sant (the Guru) has taught, O my mind.
The person who has the peace of the Naam:
Whoever hears the praise of the Lord, Har Har,
Fruitful is the coming (into the world) of the one
who, O Nanak, is pleasing to God, O my mind. ॥2॥
410.2: Raag Asavari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Coming together, let us sing the Lord's praise:
(so) the supreme state is attained.
Whoever is pierced by that relish
gains every siddhi;
he stays awake (and on guard against Maya) night and day;
O Nanak, he is greatly fortunate, O my mind.
Let us wash the feet of the Sants
and cast off evil-mindedness.
Become the dust of (the Lord's) servants,
(and) no pain afflicts (you).
Take refuge with the devotees,
(and) you shall never (again) be born and die.
They have become steadfast
who have meditated on the Lord, Har Har, O my mind.
(O God,) you are my friend and companion;
fix the Naam firmly in me.
Without him there is no other;
worship him in the mind.
Let him not be forgotten even for an instant;
how can one get by without him?
I am a sacrifice to the Guru;
(by his grace) Nanak repeats the Name, O my mind. ॥2॥
410.3: Raag Asavari, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(O God,) you are the first Cause and the Maker of all;
no one else comes to my mind (but you).
What you do, that alone comes to be;
(so) we sleep in Sahaj and in peace;
patience has come into (our) minds
since we fell at God's door, O my mind.
In the company of the Saadh (the Guru)
there is perfect self-restraint.
Since (our) self-conceit left (us),
from then on (our) torments have ended.
(O Lord,) show mercy,
keep (our) honour, O Banwari (the Lord); (so pray,) O my mind.
Let us know this as peace:
whatever the Lord does, let us accept it (as good).
No one (seems) bad to the one
who becomes the dust of the Sant's feet.
The one whom (the Lord) himself protects
alone tastes the Lord's Amrit, O my mind.
One left with no one (to lean on)
has that God as his own.
(God) knows the state within (each one);
everything is plain to him.
(O God,) lift up and save the fallen;
this is Nanak's prayer, O my mind. ॥3॥
410.4: Raag Asavari, an Iktuka, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
the things (people) were wrapped up in,
all of them they left behind and went;
(those things) have become as a dream
for the one who has taken the Lord's Name.
Those who left the Lord and clung to others
run on, being born and dying (from birth to birth).
The servants who have found the Lord, Har Har,
The one on whom (God) has mercy,
O Nanak, he alone is the devotee. ॥2॥
411.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, by the Ninth Guru (Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji).
To whom shall I tell the plight of the mind?
Gripped by greed, (this mind) runs in all ten directions, held by the hope of wealth.
For the sake of comfort it suffers much pain, waiting on one man after another;
like a dog it roams from door to door, with no thought of the worship of the Lord (Ram).
It throws away the human birth for nothing, and feels no shame when people laugh.
O Nanak, why does it not sing the Lord's praise, by which the body's evil understanding would be destroyed? ॥2॥
411.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 2, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(The true yogi) comes down from the hard pass (of ego) and bathes in the pool (of the holy company);
he does not babble idly; he sings the Lord's praises;
as water (rising) is lost in the sky, he is absorbed in Sunn (the stillness where no worldly thought stirs);
savouring the essence of truth, swirling it (like a drink), he obtains the supreme essence.
Hear such wisdom as is in my heart:
filling all, (God) is upholding every place.
Truth (the eternal Lord) is (his) fast and (his) daily rule; death does not torment him;
through the True Guru's Shabad he burns away anger;
dwelling in the sky (of the higher spirit), he enters Samadhi;
touching the Paaras (the Guru), he attains the supreme state.
For the sake of (mastering) the mind he churns the True One, the very essence;
bathing in the brimming pool, he has no filth (left) to wash;
he becomes like the One he is dyed in;
that alone comes to be which the Creator himself does.
Through the Guru, cool as ice, he puts out the fire (of craving);
the ashes he smears on are attention fixed in service;
his own garb (darsan) is to come into the home of Sahaj;
the pure Bani is the horn (nad) he sounds.
Within him is (divine) wisdom, the finest, supreme essence;
reflection on the Guru('s word) is (his) bathing at the tiraths;
his worship is within, (where) Murari (the Lord) dwells;
he merges (his) light in the Light (of the Lord).
Steeped in the essence (of the Name), his understanding rests in love of the One;
having stilled the five (passions), he dwells on the throne (within);
(living in) the Master's will is his work and his earning;
the unmanifest Nath (Master) cannot be comprehended.
(As the sun) appears in the water and yet is far from the water,
and its light fills the water, (so is the Lord);
whom shall I call near (to him), and whom far?
Seeing him ever present, I sing the praises of the treasure of virtues.
Within and without, there is no other;
whatever pleases him, that alone comes to pass.
Listen, Bharthari (the yogi): Nanak speaks (this) reflection:
the pure Naam is my support. ॥8॥
412.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
With all the chanting, all the austerities and every kind of cleverness,
(one) wanders in the wilds and does not come onto the road.
Without understanding, none is accepted;
on the brow of one empty of the Naam falls ash.
The Master is eternal; the world comes and perishes.
The mortal who becomes (the Lord's) servant through the Guru is set free.
The world is bound by attachment and by many hopes;
through the Guru's teaching some have become detached;
within (them) is the Naam, and (the heart's) lotus has blossomed;
they have no fear of Jam.
The world is conquered by desire for woman, and dotes on the wife;
attached to son and wife, it has forgotten the Naam;
it has wasted its life for nothing and lost the game.
Whoever serves the True Guru, (his) way of life is the best.
Outwardly he may speak, and be spoken of, in the terms of Haumai,
(but) inwardly he is free, and never lets (Maya's) stain cling to him;
through the Guru's Shabad he burns away attachment to Maya;
and in his heart he ever meditates on the pure Naam.
He holds back the running (mind) and keeps it still —
the Sikh whom (the Lord) in his grace joins to the Sangat.
Without the Guru (one) strays, and comes and goes;
when (the Lord) casts his glance of grace, he brings about the union and joins (him to himself).
(O Lord,) I call (you) beautiful, (but your beauty) cannot be told;
I speak of the Unspeakable, (yet your) worth cannot be found.
All sorrows are sent by you, and joys come by (your) will;
through the glory of the True One all sorrows are erased.
(Within him) music plays without hands, and the beat is kept without feet;
if (one) understands the Shabad, then he beholds the True One.
(one who has) the True One within has every comfort with him;
casting his glance of grace, the Protector protects (him).
One who loses self-conceit comes to see (the Lord in) the three worlds;
he understands the Bani and merges in the True One;
he reflects on the Shabad, his attention held on the One in an unbroken line.
O Nanak, blessed is (the Lord) who adorns (lives). ॥8॥
412.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Writing countless writings, again and again, (breeds only) pride;
when the mind is won over (to God), the True One in (one's) attention is (the real) exposition.
Telling and talking, reading again and again, (are only) a burden;
writings are countless, (but the Lord) is beyond all writing and without end.
Know the One alone to be such, the eternal (Lord);
recognise birth and death as (his) Hukam.
Through attachment to Maya the world is held bound by Jamkaal (death);
the bound one is freed by cherishing the Naam.
The Guru is the giver of peace; seek no other;
in this world and the next (his friendship) will stand by you.
When (one) dies (to self) through the Shabad, then he fixes his attention on the One;
when he devours what cannot be devoured (the passions none can master), then he ends his doubt;
one who enshrines the Naam in the mind is liberated while yet alive;
if (he) becomes Gurmukh, then he merges in the True One.
He who fashioned the earth, the heavens and the sky,
who set up all (creation) and, having set it up, pulls it down,
is himself, he alone, within all, through and through;
he asks no one; he himself bestows his grace.
(O Lord,) you are the brimming ocean, (you) the ruby and the diamond;
you are pure and eternal, a fathomless (ocean) of virtues;
one who meets the Guru, the Pir, enjoys peace;
(you) alone are the Sovereign, (you) alone the minister.
The world is in prison; (those who) have killed the ego are free;
in the world, rare is the wise man who lives by (his wisdom);
in the world, rare is the pandit who truly reflects;
without meeting the True Guru, all go about full of pride.
The world is in sorrow; only some (rare) one is at peace;
the world is sick; given to pleasures, it weeps for (lost) virtues;
the world is born and dies, losing its honour;
one who becomes Gurmukh understands (this).
(The Lord) is costly beyond price, beyond measure in weight;
immovable, beyond deceit; through the Guru's teaching, enshrine him (in the heart).
he is met through love; work done in (his) fear pleases him;
lowly Nanak speaks this thought. ॥8॥
413.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(When) one dies, the five (nearest kin) gather and weep;
(but those whose) Haumai departs wash off (the mind's) filth through the Shabad,
(and,) understanding and seeing, they abide in the home of Sahaj;
without this understanding, (the mourners) lose all their honour.
Who dies, and who is it that weeps, wailing for him?
O Creator, root of the whole world, over the head of each one are you alone.
Whoever weeps for the dead weeps (his own) sorrow;
he alone weeps who has (some) pain (of his own).
What befalls the one (who has died), that God knows;
that alone comes to be which the Creator himself does.
To die while living is to cross over, carried across (by the Lord);
victory to the Lord of the world! In his refuge is the supreme state.
I am a sacrifice to the True Guru's feet;
the Guru is the ship; through (his) Shabad the (ocean of) fear is crossed.
(The Lord) himself is fearless, (his) light (within all) unbroken;
without (his) Name, (the notion of) Sutak and of defilement by touch holds the world.
Those who perish through evil-mindedness: what is one to say, weeping for them?
Without devotion, without hearing (his praise), they are born and die.
For the dead, friends weep in earnest;
those of the three qualities weep, day after day.
(But I,) casting off (all thought of) pain and pleasure, alert in Sahaj,
surrender body and mind to the love of Krishna (the Lord).
(Beings are) many, beyond count, (yet) within (all) is the One;
rites and religious duties are many, past counting.
Without (the Lord's) fear and devotion, life is wasted;
those who join together and sing the Lord's praises (attain life's) supreme aim.
(The Lord) himself dies, and he himself also kills;
he himself creates; he sets up and pulls down.
Know this: the world was created by the Light (that is the Lord);
reflecting on the Shabad, (one) meets (him); there is no doubt (of it).
Sutak is (even) in fire, which blazes and devours the world;
Sutak is in water, on land, in every place.
O Nanak, (the world) is born and dies in Sutak;
by the Guru's grace, the Lord's sweet essence is to be drunk. ॥8॥
413.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One who reflects on his own self assays the diamond (of the Naam);
with a single glance (of grace) the Perfect Guru carries (him) across;
(one who) trusts the Guru with all his heart has a mind held steady.
Such is the Banker (the Guru), and such the assaying he does,
that by (his) unerring glance (one), attuned to the One, crosses over.
(One whose) capital is the sublime Name of Niranjan,
is pure, dyed in the True One, a paikar (who sifts the true from the false);
through praise (of the Lord), in the home of Sahaj, (he finds) the Guru, the Creator.
Through the Shabad he burns away hopes and the mind's desires;
he utters (the Name of) Ram Narayan, and leads (others) to utter it;
from the Guru he finds the way, (the Lord's) mansion, (his true) home.
(The Lord) whose being is gold, whose light is beyond compare,
the God of the three worlds, whose form is every form:
that wealth, eternal and inexhaustible, is in my lap.
(He) pervades the five (elements), the three (qualities), the nine (regions) and the four (directions);
by his power he holds up the earth and the sky;
(the mind) that runs outward he turns and brings back (within).
He is a fool, (who) does not see (the Lord) with his eyes,
(whose) tongue knows no relish (of the Name), (who) does not understand what he is told;
drunk on the poison (of Maya), he quarrels with the world.
In noble company one becomes noble;
(he) runs after virtues and washes away faults;
(but) without serving the Guru, Sahaj does not come.
The Naam is a diamond, a jewel, a ruby,
(and) the mind (made pure) is a pearl: this is the wealth of such a one.
O Nanak, (the Guru) assays (him), and with (his) glance of grace makes (him) blissful. ॥8॥
414.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Through the Guru, savour in your mind the knowledge (of God) and meditation (on him);
through the Guru, recognise (within you) the mansion of the Master of the mansion;
through the Guru, (hold) the Shabad in your awareness: (this is the) seal of passage.
In this way, through loving devotion, (one) becomes wise in reflection,
(and) through the Guru (gains) the eternal Name of Murari.
Day and night (he keeps) in (his heart's) place the pure and sublime abode (of the Lord);
(he gains) knowledge of the desireless (Lord who pervades) the three worlds.
From the True Guru, recognise (the Lord's) Hukam.
(His) joy is lasting; no grief touches him;
the Amrit (Naam), knowledge (of God) and the supreme sweet essence are his food;
with the five (passions) brought to an end, all people are at peace.
(O Lord,) your light is in all (creation); everyone is yours;
he himself joins, and he himself separates;
that alone comes to be which the Creator himself does.
He pulls down and builds, and by (his) Hukam (all) merge (in him again);
his Hukam alone prevails, as pleases him;
without the Guru, none attains the Perfect (Lord).
Neither in childhood nor in old age is the mortal aware (of the Lord);
in the full flush of youth he drowns in pride;
without the Name, what will he earn in the end?
He has not known in Sahaj the One whose grain and wealth (he lives on);
led astray by doubt, he repents afterwards;
with a noose around his neck, the madman wanders, crazed.
(Those who,) seeing the world drowning, fled in fear,
(and) whom the True Guru saved, are greatly fortunate;
O Nanak, they cling to the Guru's feet. ॥8॥
414.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(Some) sing songs (of devotion), but in their minds is wickedness;
reciting (talk of freedom from) attachment and aversion, they have themselves called (men who have) gone beyond them;
without the Name, (their) minds hold falsehood and wickedness.
Where are you wandering, O mind? Stay in (your own) home (within).
Through the Guru, (people) are fulfilled in the Name of Ram; searching (thus), you will find the Lord in Sahaj.
Lust and anger are in the mind, attachment in the body,
and greed, avarice and pride: these are (the real) pain;
without the Name of Ram, how can the mind take heart?
One who recognises the True One bathes within;
the Gurmukh knows the state within;
without the true Shabad, (none) recognises (the Lord's) mansion.
(One who) merges the visible form (of the world) in the Formless,
(and,) through the True (Name), fixes (in his heart) the eternal One, whose power is beyond measure,
that man does not come into the womb and the round of births.
Where the Naam is to be found, there would I go;
by the Guru's grace, (those) deeds would I do;
(and,) dyed in the Naam, sing the Lord's praises.
One who has recognised his own self through serving the Guru,
(in him) the Amrit Naam, the giver of peace, has come to dwell;
night and day, through the Bani, he is dyed in the Naam alone.
When my God attaches (one to the Naam), then alone is anyone attached;
(such a one) kills Haumai and is awakened through the Shabad;
here and hereafter, peace is ever before him.
The fickle mind does not know the way (to kill Haumai);
the manmukh is filthy, (and) does not recognise the Shabad;
the Gurmukh is pure, (and) utters the Naam.
I offer my prayer before the revered Lord,
that I may dwell in the company of the holy (Saadhs),
(where) sins and sorrows are cut away, and the Lord's Name shines.
One who, by reflection, has recognised (true) conduct,
(and) through the True Guru's words has known the One —
O Nanak, (his) mind is dyed in the Name of Ram. ॥10॥
415.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The Saakat's mind is (like) a crazed elephant;
in the forest (of the world) it wanders, bewildered by attachment to Maya.
(Such ones,) pressed down by death, go this way and that;
the Gurmukh searches and finds the home (of the Lord) within himself.
Without the Guru's Shabad the mind finds no resting place.
Remember the utterly pure Name of Ram; give up other (tastes) and bitter Haumai.
Tell me, how will this foolish mind be steadied?
Without understanding, it will suffer the pain (inflicted by) Jam.
(Whom the Lord) himself forgives, him the True Guru unites (with him);
(he) slays death, the thorn, and the True One urges (him on, towards himself).
This mind (performs) rites, this mind (keeps) religious duties;
this mind is born of the five elements;
this mind of the Saakat is greedy and foolish;
through the Guru, repeating the Naam, the mind becomes beautiful.
Through the Guru, the mind gives a place (within) to that very One;
through the Guru, understanding (of him who pervades) the three worlds comes.
This mind (is now) a yogi, (now) a pleasure-seeker, (now) one who practises austerities;
the Gurmukh recognises the Lord God within himself.
The mind (at times) turns renunciate, giving up Haumai;
(yet) desire and double-mindedness cling to every heart.
(One who), through the Guru, tastes Ram, the home of all delights,
the Lord, the Master of the mansion, keeps his honour at (his) door and in (his) home.
This mind (is now) a king, (now) a hero in battle;
through the Guru, in the Naam, this mind becomes fearless;
it kills the five (passions) and brings them under its sway;
devouring Haumai, it holds them (bound) in one place.
Through the Guru, (this mind) gives up other melodies and tastes;
through the Guru, this mind awakens in devotion.
Hearing the Anhad (melody) and reflecting on the Shabad, it is won over;
recognising the self, (such ones) have become one with the Formless.
This mind, made pure, (sees) that One at the door and in the home;
through the Guru, devotion, love and longing arise (in it);
day and night, by the Guru's grace, (it sings) the Lord's praise;
God, (who was) at the beginning and from the start of the ages, (it sees) in every heart.
In Ram, the home of all delights, this mind is intoxicated;
through the Guru, it has known the home of all delights.
For love of devotion, it dwells at the Guru's feet;
Nanak is a servant of the servants of the Lord's devotees. ॥9॥
416.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
When the body perishes, whose can its wealth be called?
Without the Guru, where can the Lord's Name be found?
The wealth of the Lord's Name is the companion and helper (that goes) along;
night and day, (one) who fixes loving attention on the Lord (becomes) pure.
Without the Name of the Lord, who is ours?
Holding pleasure and pain alike, I will not let go of the Naam; (the Lord) himself forgives and unites (me with himself).
Fools are attached to gold and women;
caught in duality, they have forgotten the Naam.
Whom you forgive, (him) you make to repeat the Naam;
singing (your) praises, (he) cannot be touched by Jam's servant.
O Lord, great Giver, O Ram, O Gopal,
keep (me) as it pleases you, O Merciful One.
Through the Guru, Ram has become dear to my mind;
(my) ailments are gone, and pain has been held back.
There is no other medicine, no charm and no mantra;
the Simran of the Lord, Har Har, destroys sins.
You yourself lead (beings) astray, making them forget the Naam;
you yourself save (them), showing grace.
(Theirs is) the disease of doubt, of separateness, of another in the mind;
without the Guru, in doubt, they chant the chant of another.
They do not behold the Guru, the Primal Being;
without the Guru's Shabad, of what account is (their) life?
Beholding the Wonder (that you are, we) are struck with awe;
(you are) in every heart, in gods and men, in Sahaj Samadhi (steady absorption).
You fill every mind and uphold (all);
there is no other equal to you.
Ram, for devotion to whom (the Sants) have love, and whose Name is on their lips,
is (found) in the company of the Sants and devotees.
They break (their) bonds and (hold God) in meditation in Sahaj;
through the Guru, (one) is set free, (gaining) the Guru's knowledge of the Lord.
The pain (dealt) by Jam's servants does not touch him,
the servant who stays awake, attuned in love to the Lord's Name.
The Lord, Lover of devotion, is with his devotees;
O Nanak, (they) are liberated in the Lord's love. ॥8॥
416.2: Raag Asa, an Iktuki, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One who serves the Guru knows the Master;
(his) sorrow is erased; through the Shabad he recognises the True One.
Repeat the name of Ram, my friends and companions;
serve the True Guru, and see God with your own eyes.
In the world, mother and father are bonds;
son, daughter and wife are bonds.
Rites and religious deeds done in ego are bonds;
son and wife are bonds (when) another (love) is in the mind.
The farmers who till the land are in bonds:
(one) bears the penalty of Haumai, (and) the king demands (his) due.
Trade done without reflection is a bond;
in the spread of attachment to Maya there is no contentment.
The bankers who hoard wealth are in bonds; the wealth goes;
without devotion to the Lord, (none) is accepted.
The Vedas and debate (done) in pride are bonds;
in the bond of attachment and vice, (one) perishes.
O Nanak, (those who) take the refuge of the Lord's Name,
the True Guru has saved (them), and no bond binds them. ॥8॥
417.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 3, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Those on whose heads the smoothly dressed hair looked lovely, with vermilion in the parting,
those heads are now shorn with shears, and dust fills their throats.
They lived inside palaces; now they are not allowed even to sit near them.
Salutation, O Father, salutation!
O Primal Being, no one has found your limit; you make form after form and watch them.
When they were wed, their bridegrooms looked splendid beside them;
they came riding in palanquins inlaid with ivory;
water was waved over their heads (in welcome), and fans glittered beside them.
They received a lakh (in gifts) when they sat, and a lakh when they stood;
they ate coconut and dates, and enjoyed their beds.
Now ropes are put round their necks, and their strings of pearls are breaking.
Wealth and youth, which kept them steeped in delight, have both become their enemies;
the order was given to the henchmen, and they carried them off, robbed of honour.
If it pleases him, (the Lord) gives greatness; if it pleases him, he gives punishment.
If one remembers (the Lord) beforehand, why should one receive punishment?
The rulers had lost their senses in revelry, in shows and in pleasures;
now that Babur's rule has been proclaimed, even a prince gets no bread to eat.
Some (the Muslims) lose the times of their prayers; some (the Hindus) lose their worship;
without their sacred cooking squares, how can the Hindu women bathe and put on the frontal mark?
They never remembered Ram; now they are not allowed even to say Khuda.
Some come back to their homes, and meeting one another ask how each one fares;
for some this is what was written: they sit and weep over their sorrows.
Whatever pleases him comes to pass; O Nanak, what can mortals do? ॥7॥
417.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Where are those games, the stables and the horses? Where are the kettledrums and the shehnais?
Where are those sword-belts of fine wool? Where are those red tunics?
Where are those mirrors and the handsome faces? They are not seen here (any more).
This world is yours; you are its Master.
In a moment (the Lord) sets up and pulls down; he shares out wealth and gives it to others.
Where are those houses, gateways, pavilions and palaces? Where are those handsome serais?
Where is that easeful bed, and the woman the sight of whom kept sleep away?
Where are the betel leaves and the betel-sellers, and the women of the harem? They have vanished like shadows.
Many have been ruined on account of this wealth; this wealth has brought many to ruin.
It cannot be amassed without sin, and at death it does not go with (anyone).
Whom the Creator himself would lead astray, he first takes away (his) goodness.
When they heard that the Mir was marching on them, millions of pirs tried to hold (him) back;
(yet) shrines and abodes and mansions solid as stone were burnt, and the princes were cut to pieces and left in the dust.
Not one Mughal went blind, and no one worked any miracle.
There was battle between the Mughals and the Pathans, and the sword was wielded on the field;
they (the Mughals) aimed and fired their guns, they (the Pathans) drove on their elephants.
Those whose letter was torn in the (Lord's) court had to die, brother.
The Hindu women and the Muslim women, the wives of the Bhattis and of the Thakurs:
some had their robes torn from head to foot, some came to dwell in the cremation ground;
those whose handsome (husbands) did not come home, how did they pass the night?
The Creator himself does and causes (all) to be done; to whom should (this) be told?
Pain and pleasure come in your will; to whom should we go and weep?
The Lord of the Hukam drives (all) by his Hukam and is pleased; O Nanak, what is written is received. ॥7॥
418.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa Kafi, Ghar 8, Ashtapadis, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
As the herdsman (stays a while) at the pasture, so is (our stay in) the world;
men practise falsehood when they build houses and homes.
Wake up, wake up, you sleepers; the trader is departing.
Houses would be built to last for ever if one were to stay (here for ever);
the body falls, the soul will depart; if only one understood!
Why do you cry, alas, alas? (The Lord) who is, he alone will be.
You will weep for him (who has died); who will weep for you?
You beat (your breasts) in vain, O brothers; you practise falsehood.
He (the dead one) does not hear (you) at all; you only make the people hear.
O Nanak, the one by whom (the soul) sleeps, he alone wakes it;
if (one) understands his own home, then sleep does not come.
If the one departing has taken any wealth along with him,
then gather wealth (too): look, reflect and understand.
Trade, and gain (life's) purpose, lest you regret;
give up faults and practise virtues; in this way gain the essence.
Make dharma the soil and truth the seed: farm such a crop;
then you will be known as (true) traders, and take your profit with you.
If (God's) grace comes, the True Guru is met, and (one) understands this teaching;
he utters the Name, hears the Name, and deals in the Name alone.
As there is profit and loss (in trade), so has (the world's) way always gone on;
O Nanak, whatever pleases him is (true) greatness. ॥10॥
418.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
I have searched the four directions; no one is mine.
If it pleases you, O Master, you are mine and I am yours.
I have no second door; before whom should I bow in salutation?
You alone are my Master; your True Name is on my lips.
(Some) serve the Siddhas, (wishing to be) Siddhas and pirs, and beg for riddhis and siddhis (riches and miraculous powers);
may I never forget the one Name, through the wisdom of the True Guru.
Yogis, pleasure-seekers and wearers of patched coats, why do they roam through foreign lands?
They do not recognise the Guru's Shabad, the sublime essence that pervades all.
Pandits, teachers and astrologers read the Puranas every day;
they do not know the treasure within: Brahm (God) is hidden in the heart.
Some ascetics practise austerities in the forest, and ever dwell at tiraths (places of pilgrimage);
in their dark (tamasi) nature they do not know themselves; why have they become renunciants?
Some hold back their seed with effort and call themselves jatis (celibates);
without the Guru's Shabad they are not set free; in doubt they come and go.
Some householders, servants (of the Lord) and seekers hold to the Guru's teaching;
they keep the Naam, giving and purity firm, and stay awake in the Lord's devotion.
Through the Guru (the Lord's) door and home are known; one who goes (to the Guru) recognises (them).
O Nanak, (such a one) does not forget the Name; his mind is content in the True One. ॥8॥
419.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Merge desire into the mind itself; through the True One the terrifying world-ocean is crossed.
From the beginning, through the ages, you are merciful; O Master, (I seek) your refuge.
You are the Giver, we are beggars; O Lord, grant (us) the sight of you.
Meditate on the Naam through the Guru, and the temple of the mind is drenched (in love).
If false greed is given up, then (one) recognises the True One;
if one merges in the Guru's Shabad, one knows the highest aim.
This mind is a king, greedy, lured on by greed;
through the Guru greed is driven out, and (one comes into) harmony with the Lord.
If a crop is sown in saline soil, how can (one) reap a profit?
The manmukh is not drenched in the True One; the false (one) is sunk in falsehood.
Give up greed, you blind ones; in greed there is great pain.
(When) the True Master dwells in the mind, the poison of Haumai is destroyed.
Give up duality, the crooked path, or you will be robbed, brother;
night and day, praise the Naam in the refuge of the True Guru.
The manmukh is a stone, a rock; cursed (is his) insipid life:
however long (a stone) is kept in water, it stays dry within.
The Lord's Name is the treasure; the perfect Guru has given (it);
O Nanak, (one who has it) does not forget the Name; he churns and drinks the Amrit. ॥8॥
419.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Those bound to depart are going on their way, having left the (true) road;
the world toils and frets over its affairs; the True One has not pleased it.
Why wander now, what is there to search for? The Guru's Shabad has shown (the Lord);
(I) have cast off possessiveness and attachment, and come into (my) own home.
The True One is met through truth; through falsehood he is not found;
fixing the mind on the True One, one does not come (into birth) again.
Why do you weep for those who have died? You do not know how to weep.
Weep as you praise the True One, and recognise (his) Hukam.
Know that (each one) has come with his allowance written by the Hukam;
if the Hukam is recognised, the profit (of life) comes into one's hands.
By the Hukam (one) goes (from here) robed in honour, and is pleasing in the Lord's court;
by the Hukam too, in God's prison, blows fall on the head.
This is the profit: let truth and justice dwell in the mind;
what is written is what one receives; (so) let pride be cast away.
The self-willed are struck on the head and worn away in strife;
the false (world), plundered by the cheat (Maya), is bound and driven off.
Those who enshrine the Master in the heart do not repent;
(he) is the forgiver of sins, and they live by the Shabad.
Nanak begs for the True (Naam), which is earned by toil through the Guru;
(O Lord,) I have none but you; look on (me) with your glance of grace. ॥9॥
420.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Why should I go and search the forest? In my own home is a green forest.
Coming home through the Shabad, (the mind) quickly settles in the True One.
Wherever I look, there he is; no other is known.
By doing the Guru's work, (the Lord's) mansion is recognised.
When the True One himself unites (one with himself), then he is dear to the mind;
(one) walks ever in (his) will, and merges in (his) embrace.
When the True Master dwells in the mind, he alone stays dwelling in the mind;
he himself bestows glories, and however much he gives, (his store) does not run short.
Waiting on this one and that, how is (one) to reach the Lord's court?
If one boards a boat of stone, it sinks him in the sea.
Let us sell our own mind (to the Guru), and give our head along with it;
(then), searching our own home, we recognise through the Guru the real thing (the Naam).
What is called birth and death was made by that Creator;
those who lost self-conceit and stayed dead (to self while living) have not had to die again.
That work alone is to be done which is ordained from the Source;
if, giving the mind to the True Guru, one meets (the Lord), who has ever put a price on (such a one)?
That Master is the assayer of jewels; it is he who has set (their) worth.
O Nanak, (one in whose) mind the Master dwells (receives) true glory. ॥8॥
420.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Those who have forgotten the Naam, led astray by the doubt of duality,
have left the root and clung to the branches; what will they gain? Ashes.
How can one be set free without the Naam? If anyone would understand (this):
become Gurmukh, and one is set free; the manmukh has lost (his) honour.
Those who have served the One, O brother, have perfect understanding;
(such) servants stay in the refuge of the Lord, the Pure One, who is from the beginning, from the start of the ages.
My Master is One; there is no other, O brother;
by (his) grace, through the True One, peace has been found.
Without the Guru none has found (the Lord), however many may say (otherwise) and have it said;
(the Guru) himself shows the way, and makes true devotion firm (in the heart).
Even if the manmukh is taught, he still goes off into the wilds.
Without the Lord's Name he will not be set free; he dies and sinks into hell.
He is born and dies and is made to wander, (yet) does not take the Lord's Name;
without serving the Guru, he is of no worth.
As is the service (the Lord) makes one do, such too are (one's) deeds;
he himself does (all); whom else can one tell? He beholds his own greatness.
The Guru's service is done only by the one whom (the Lord) himself has do it;
O Nanak, by giving one's head one is set free, and (such a one) gains honour in the Lord's court. ॥8॥
421.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Master, you are beautiful and wise; beautiful (too) is the Guru's Bani;
it is by great good fortune that the True Guru is met, and (through him) the state of nirvana, where desire is stilled, is attained.
I am the servant of (your) servants; we are your little servants;
as you keep me, so I live; (let your) Name be in my mouth.
Great is the thirst for the sight of (you); by (your) will alone does one please (your) mind;
glories are in my Master's hands; by (his) will alone is honour obtained.
The True One is not to be thought far away; he is within (all).
Wherever I look, there he pervades; by whom can (his) worth be told?
He himself makes, he himself destroys, and he beholds his own greatness.
Becoming Gurmukh, one beholds (him); in this way (his) worth is known.
One who does the Guru's work gains the profit while still alive;
if it is written (in one's lot) from the past, only then is the True Guru found.
The manmukhs suffer loss every day; led astray, they wander about.
the manmukh, blind, does not remember (the Lord); how can he gain the sight of (him)?
Only then is one's coming into the world (counted worth while), when one fixes one's attention on the True One;
meeting the Guru, they become the Paaras, and merge (their) light in the (Lord's) Light.
Day and night (such a one) stays unattached, doing the work given from the Source.
O Nanak, contented in the Naam, they are dyed in (love of) the Lord's feet. ॥8॥
421.2: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
However much is said of (the Lord), I do not know his limit.
For me who have no support, you alone are the support; you are my mighty strength.
Nanak's prayer is this: to live at peace in the True Naam.
When self-conceit goes, understanding dawns, and through the Guru's Shabad comes union (with the Lord).
When Haumai and pride are cast away, true understanding is gained;
when the mind is won over to the Master, he gives the support of the True (Naam).
To stay contented in the Naam day and night: that is the true service.
No obstacle comes in the way of one who walks in the Hukam of the Lord of the Will.
Whoever walks in the Hukam of the Lord of the Will is placed in (his) treasury;
the counterfeit find no place (there), and stay mixed with the impure.
Day by day let the Genuine One be cherished (in the heart); (so) the true merchandise is gained.
The counterfeit do not come into (his) sight; they are taken and burnt in the fire.
Those who have recognised their own self are one with the Supreme Self;
the One alone is the tree of Amrit, and its fruit is Amrit.
Those who have tasted the fruit of Amrit stay fulfilled in the True One;
they have neither doubt nor separation (from him); their tongues are steeped in the Lord's savour.
(O mortal,) by the Hukam, through the joining of (your past deeds), you have come (into the world); walk ever in (the will of) the Lord of the Will.
May Nanak, who is without virtue, be given virtue, the True (Naam) and glory. ॥8॥
421.3: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(One whose) mind is dyed in the Lord's Name, (who) has spoken (the praise of) the True One,
what do people lose when (such a one) has become pleasing to you?
As long as there is life and breath, let us meditate on the True One;
by singing the Lord's virtues the profit is gained, and peace is found.
Your service is true; grant (it to me), O Merciful One.
Praising you, I live; you are my prop and my support.
(I am) a servant at (your) door, a doorkeeper; you know (my) pain.
Devotion to you is a wonder; (through it) you take away pain.
Through the Guru one comes to know that in the Lord's court, in (his) presence, (it is) the Naam (that is accepted).
the time (of one's life) is true and accepted, (if) one recognises the Shabad.
They practise truth, contentment and love, and (take) the Lord's Name as provisions for the road;
they cast vices out of the mind, (and) the True One gives (them) the True (Naam).
True love for the True One, the True One himself has kindled;
he himself does justice, as it pleases him.
O True One, give (me) the true gift; (the Lord) is merciful;
I serve him day and night; (his) Name is priceless.
You are exalted and I am lowly, (yet) I am called (your) servant.
Says Nanak: (O Lord,) cast your glance of grace, that I, who am separated, may find the True One. ॥8॥
422.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
How can coming and going cease? How can union (with the Lord) take place?
Great is the pain of birth and death, (with) constant dread in duality.
Without the Naam, what life is it? Shame on (such) cleverness; it is cursed,
(for one who) has not served the True Guru, the Saadh, and has not loved devotion to the Lord.
Coming and going ceases only when the Perfect Guru is found;
(he) gives as capital the wealth that is the Lord's Name, and false doubt perishes.
(Such a one) stays joined with the Sants, and sings (the Lord's) praise, (saying), Blessed, blessed;
through the Guru he finds the Lord, the Primal Being, beyond the farthest beyond.
An actor has put on a show: the world is (such) a play;
the play is watched for an instant, a moment; it takes no time to be swept away.
The game of chaupar is being played in Haumai, with falsehood and pride (for pieces);
all the world loses; only he wins who reflects on the Guru's Shabad.
Like the stick in a blind man's hand is the Lord's Name to me;
the Name of the Lord, of Hari, is (my) prop, by night, by day and at dawn.
As you keep me, so I live; the Lord's Name is (my) support.
I have found the friend who stands by (me) at the end, the gateway of liberation for (your) servant.
Repeating the Name of Murari, (I) have erased the pains of birth and death.
O Nanak, (one to whom) the Naam is never forgotten, the Perfect Guru carries across. ॥8॥
422.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 2, Ashtapadis, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(O Lord,) the Shastras, the Vedas and the Simritis are your pool; the Ganga is merged in your feet;
the intellect dwells on the three branches (the three qualities of Maya) and their root; but you are wondrous through and through.
Servant Nanak contemplates his feet, and speaks the Bani that is Amrit.
The thirty-three crore (gods) are your servants; (you are) the support of riddhis and siddhis (wealth and miraculous powers) and of the breath of life.
His forms cannot be discerned; what can I say, what can I reflect (of them)?
Within the world the three qualities (of Maya) are yours; yours are the four sources of life.
When there is (your) grace, the supreme state is attained, and (one) tells the story of the Untellable.
You are the Creator; everything is your doing; what can any mortal do?
She alone on whom you cast your glance of grace merges in the True One.
Everyone takes your Name, all the (creation) that comes and goes;
(but) when it pleases you, then (one) understands, through the Guru; the rest, self-willed, wander about in folly.
The four Vedas were given to Brahma; reading them again and again, he reflects (on them);
(yet) the poor one does not understand his Hukam, and is born now into hell, now into heaven.
(The Lord) made the kings of age upon age, whom (people) sing of as incarnations;
even they did not find his limit; what can I say, what can I reflect (of him)?
You are true; everything you have made is true; if you grant it, I speak of the True One.
She to whom you make your Truth known merges in the Naam, in Sahaj. ॥8॥
423.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The True Guru has driven out my doubt,
and has made the immaculate Name of the Lord dwell in (my) mind;
recognising the Shabad, (I) have found peace that lasts for ever.
Hear, O my mind, the wisdom that is the essence:
the Giver knows every way; the treasure of the Naam is found through the Guru.
Such is the greatness of meeting the True Guru
that he has put out the fire of the sense of mine and of craving;
absorbed in Sahaj, (I) sing the virtues of the Lord.
Without the Perfect Guru, none has known (this wisdom);
(the world) is lured by attachment to Maya, by the love of another;
through the Guru (alone) the Naam is received, and the Lord's Bani.
Service of the Guru is the excellent austerity, crowning all austerities;
(through it) the Lord, who takes away all sorrows, comes to dwell in the mind,
and (one) is seen to be truthful at the True One's door.
Through service of the Guru comes understanding of (the Lord in) the three worlds;
recognising his own self, he finds the Lord;
through the True Bani (the Lord's) mansion is attained.
Through service of the Guru (one) saves all his family lines;
(he) keeps the pure Naam enshrined in his heart;
true glory is (his) at the True One's door.
Fortunate are those whom the Guru has set to service;
night and day (the Guru) makes devotion and the True Naam firm (in them);
through the Naam all (their) family lines have been saved.
Nanak speaks a true reflection:
keep the Name of the Lord fixed in your heart;
those dyed in devotion to the Lord (find) the door of liberation. ॥8॥
423.2: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Everyone lives on hope upon hope;
one who understands (the Lord's) Hukam is freed from hope.
Many people lie asleep in (the sleep of) hope;
he alone wakes whom (the Lord himself) awakens.
The True Guru has given (me) understanding of the Naam; without the Name, the hunger (for Maya) does not go.
only through the Naam is the fire of craving put out; (but) the Naam is received only by the will of that (Lord).
In Kalyug, (the Lord's) praise (is the way); recognise the Shabad.
This is devotion; (by it) pride comes to an end.
By serving the True Guru, (one) is accepted (at the Lord's door);
know him who made hope.
What should be offered to (the Guru) who makes (us) hear the Shabad,
(and) in his grace makes the Naam dwell in the mind?
Let this head be offered (to him), losing self-conceit;
one who understands (his) Hukam has peace for ever.
(The Lord) himself does (all), and himself causes (all) to be done;
he himself, through the Guru, makes the Naam dwell (in the mind);
he himself leads astray, and himself sets (one) on the path;
through the True Shabad (one) merges in the True One.
The Shabad is true, the Bani is true,
which Gurmukhs in every age have uttered and expounded.
The self-willed (world) is led astray by attachment and doubt;
without the Name, all (the world) wanders about crazed.
In all three worlds (spreads) the one Maya;
the fool, reading and reading, has made firm (only) the love of another (than God);
he performs many rites, (yet for him) it is all sorrow.
Serving the True Guru, (the Gurmukh) has found lasting peace.
Reflecting on the Shabad, (one gains) the sweet Amrit;
having killed Haumai, (he) enjoys (it) night and day;
when (the Lord) shows grace, (he abides) in Sahaj and in bliss.
Those dyed in the Naam ever (abide) in the True One, in (his) love.
Reflecting on the Guru's Shabad, let us repeat and read of the Lord;
killing Haumai, let us repeat and read of the Lord;
let us repeat (the Name of) the Lord in (his) fear and in true love.
O Nanak, through the Guru's teaching, enshrine the Naam in the heart. ॥8॥
424.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa Kafi, Ghar 8, Ashtapadis, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
From the Guru springs (the) calm that has put out the fire of craving;
from the Guru the Naam is received, (which is) the highest glory.
Remember the one Name, O my brother.
Seeing the world burning, (I) have run to the shelter (of the Guru).
From the Guru springs wisdom, (and) reflection on the supreme essence;
from the Guru (the Lord's) house and door are found, (and) the storehouses of devotion are filled.
Through the Guru the Naam is meditated on, (and one) grasps the reflection;
through the Guru (come) devotion and praise, (and) within (dwells) the Shabad of the Infinite.
Through the Guru peace springs up, and sorrow never comes;
through the Guru Haumai is killed, (and) the mind becomes pure.
When the True Guru is met, self-conceit departs, (and) one comes to understand (the Lord in) the three worlds;
(one sees that) the pure Light is spread (everywhere), (and one's) light is merged in the Light.
(The one whom) the Perfect Guru has taught, (his) understanding has become sublime;
(his) inner self becomes cool and calm, (and) through the Naam there is peace.
The Perfect True Guru is met only when (the Lord) casts his glance of grace;
(then) all sins and wrongs are cut away, (and) then no sorrow or hindrance comes.
Glories are in (the Lord's) own hands; giving (them), he joins (one) to the Naam.
O Nanak, (the one in whose) mind the treasure of the Naam has come to dwell receives glory. ॥8॥
425.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Listen, O mind: make (the Naam) dwell within you; (the Lord) himself will come and meet (you), O my brother.
Night and day perform true devotion, (and) fix (your) consciousness on the True One.
Meditate on the one Name, and you will find peace, O my brother;
cast out Haumai and (the love of) another, (and) great will be (your) glory.
This devotion gods, men and silent sages long for, (but) without the True Guru it cannot be had.
Pandits and astrologers read (their books), (but) they gain no understanding (of it).
(The Lord) has kept everything in his own hands; nothing can be said.
what he himself gives, that alone is received; the Guru has given (me) this understanding.
All beings and creatures are his; he alone is (the Master) of all;
whom should one call bad? (One might,) if there were any other (than him).
The Hukam of the One alone prevails; the task (set) by the One alone is on (every) head.
(Those whom) he himself has set wandering have greed and vice within.
Some he himself has made Gurmukh; (they) grasp the (true) reflection;
on them he has also bestowed devotion; within (them) is the storehouse (of the Naam).
To those who have wisdom, all is the True One; understanding of the True One has dawned (on them);
though anyone try to mislead them, they are not misled, (for) they know that True One.
In the house (of the heart of the wise) the five (passions) are at work too, (but there) the five become discerning (and keep within bounds).
O Nanak, without the True Guru (these five) are not brought under control; through the Naam Haumai is killed. ॥8॥
425.2: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
All the treasure is within the home (of the heart); outside there is nothing;
(it) is found by the Guru's grace, (when) the doors within are opened.
From the True Guru the Lord is found, O brother.
The treasure of the Naam lies within; the Perfect True Guru has revealed (it).
One who becomes a buyer of the Lord('s Name) takes (it), (and) gains the jewel of reflection;
(he) opens (his) inner self, (and) with divine sight beholds the storehouse of liberation.
Within (the body) are many mansions, (in which) the soul makes its dwelling;
(it) will obtain the fruit the mind longs for, (and) there will be no more round (of birth and death).
The assayers have taken good care of the treasure (of the Naam); understanding has come (to them) from the Guru;
the Naam is a priceless treasure; some (rare) one obtains it through the Guru.
What will one find who searches outside? The treasure is within the home, O brother.
Led astray by doubt, the whole world wanders; the manmukh has lost (his) honour.
The false one, (who) leaves his own house and door (and) goes into another's house,
is caught like a thief; without the Name (he) suffers blows.
Those who have come to know their own home are at peace, O brother;
(they) have recognised Brahm (God) within; (this is) the greatness of the Guru.
(The Lord) himself makes the gift; to whom (else) can one speak? He himself gives understanding.
O Nanak, meditate on the Naam, (and) you will win glory at the True One's door. ॥8॥
426.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those who have recognised their own self have found (the Naam's) taste sweet, O brother;
tasting the Lord's elixir, those to whom the True One is dear have become free.
The Lord is pure, wholly pure; his dwelling is in the pure mind.
When (he) is praised through the Guru's teaching, (one stays) detached in the midst of Maya.
Without the Shabad one's own self is not known; all (the world) is blind, O brother.
Through the Guru's teaching there is light in the heart, (and) the Naam is a companion at the last.
(They) move in the Naam, in the Naam alone; (their) dealings are with the Naam alone.
Within (them) is the Naam, in (their) mouth is the Naam; through the Shabad (they) reflect on the Naam alone.
Let the Naam be heard, let the Naam be accepted; through the Naam alone comes glory.
One who praises the Naam for ever and ever finds (the Lord's) mansion through the Naam.
Through the Naam alone there is light in the heart; through the Naam alone glory is won;
through the Naam alone peace springs up; through the Naam alone (one finds) refuge (in the Lord).
Without the Name no one is accepted; the manmukh has lost (his) honour.
(Manmukhs) are bound and beaten in the city of Jam; (they) have wasted (their) life for nothing.
All (the world) serves the one of the Naam; through the Guru understanding of the Naam is given.
Through the Naam alone (one's) name is honoured; through the Naam alone comes glory.
He to whom (the Lord himself) gives (it) receives (the Naam); through the Guru's teaching (he) gives understanding of the Naam.
O Nanak, everything is in the power of the Naam; some (rare) one obtains (it) by perfect fortune. ॥8॥
426.2: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
The forsaken soul-brides do not reach (the Husband's) mansion, nor do (they) know the delight of the Husband;
(they) speak harshly and do not bow; the love of another is (their only) relish.
How can this mind be brought under control?
By the Guru's grace (it) is held back, (and) through an understanding lit by wisdom it comes (back to its) home.
The happy soul-brides (the Lord) has himself adorned, instilling love and affection (in them);
(they) walk in the will of the True Guru; through the Naam, Sahaj is (their) adornment.
(They) ever enjoy their own Husband, on the true bed, in love;
enchanted by the Husband's love, (they) find peace in meeting the Beloved.
(She whose) adornment is boundless wisdom is a woman of honour;
she is blessed with brothers, she is beautiful, (steeped) in the Husband's affection and love.
In the happy soul-brides the True, the Unseen, the Infinite (Lord) has placed (his) love;
with true love and affection (they) serve their own True Guru.
The happy soul-brides have made (this) their adornment: round the neck a necklace of virtues;
on the body, the fragrance of love applied; (and) within, the jewel of reflection.
Those dyed in devotion are exalted; (their) caste and honour come through the Shabad alone.
Without the Name, all are of low caste; (one without the Name) becomes a worm of filth.
All (the world) goes about crying I, I; without the Shabad the I does not go.
O Nanak, those dyed in the Naam have lost their Haumai; (they) remain merged in the True One. ॥8॥
426.3: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those dyed in the True One are pure; their glory is true for ever.
Here they are known in house after house; hereafter (their glory) shines out age after age.
O fair mind, so fond of colour, take on the true colour.
If you are dyed with the beautiful Bani, this colour will neither fade nor leave.
We are lowly, soiled and very proud; in the love of another (we are caught) in vices.
Meeting the Guru, the Paaras, (we) have turned to gold; the pure Light of the Infinite (shines within).
Without the Guru no one is dyed (in this colour); when the Guru is met, the colour takes.
Those dyed in the Guru's fear and love are merged, through praise, in the True One.
Without (the Lord's) fear the mordant (that fixes the colour) does not take, nor does the mind become pure.
Deeds done without fear are false; (such a one finds) no place at all.
He alone will be dyed whom (the Lord) himself dyes, joining (him) to the Sat Sangat.
The Sat Sangat springs from the Perfect Guru, (and in it one abides) in Sahaj, in the True One, in love.
Without the Sangat all live like beasts and cattle;
they do not know their Maker; without the Name all are thieves.
Some buy virtues, and (their) faults are sold off; through the Guru (they abide) in Sahaj and in love.
Through service of the Guru (they) have found the Name, which has come to dwell within (them).
The Giver of all is the One (Lord); (he) sets each one to (his) work.
O Nanak, (those whom) he has adorned by joining (them) to the Naam he unites (with himself) through the Shabad. ॥8॥
427.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
All (the world) longs for the Name, (but) he alone obtains (it) to whom (the Lord) is gracious.
Without the Name all is sorrow; peace is his in whose mind (the Lord) makes (the Name) dwell.
(O Lord,) you are infinite and merciful; (I am in) your refuge.
From the Perfect Guru (your Name) is received, (and) through the Naam alone comes glory.
Within and without is the One (Lord); (he) has made the creation in many forms.
By his Hukam alone (he) has (all) work done; whom else could we name, O brother?
(O Lord,) understanding and the lack of it are your making; this work is in your charge.
Some you forgive and unite (with yourself); some, the false, are beaten and thrown out of the Lord's court.
Some are pure and holy from the very start; you have joined (them) to the Naam.
Through service of the Guru peace springs up (in them); through the True Shabad (the Guru) gives (them) understanding.
Some are of crooked ways, unclean and debauched; (the Lord) himself has made them miss the Name.
They have neither attainment nor understanding, nor are they self-disciplined; they wander about unsteady and bewildered.
On whom (the Lord) casts his glance of grace, in him he instils faith.
Truth and contentment are (his) self-discipline; (his) mind is pure, (for the Lord) lets (him) hear the Shabad.
Reading accounts, one cannot reach (him); by telling and describing, (his) end is not found.
From the Guru (his) worth is known; through the True Shabad understanding comes.
Search and set right this mind and body, reflecting on the Guru's Shabad.
O Nanak, the treasure of the Naam lies within this very body; (it) is found through boundless love for the Guru. ॥8॥
427.2: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Dyed in the True One are the happy soul-brides whose adornment is the Guru's Shabad;
reflecting on the True Shabad, (they) have found that Husband in (their own) home.
(She who) through virtues has had (her) faults forgiven, (and) has fixed loving attention on the Lord,
that bride has found the Lord as (her) Husband; the Guru has brought (her) into union (with him).
Some, led astray by the doubt of duality, do not know the Husband to be ever present;
how can (those) forsaken soul-brides find (the Husband)? (Their) night passes in pain.
Those in whose mind the True One has come to dwell do the true work;
night and day (they) serve (him) in Sahaj, (and) stay merged in the True One.
The forsaken soul-brides are led astray by doubt; speaking falsehood, (they) eat poison.
(They) do not know their own Husband, (and) on an empty bed they suffer.
The True Master is One; O mind, see that (you) are not led astray by doubt.
(If you) serve (him) by asking the Guru, (you will) enshrine the pure True One in (your) mind.
The happy soul-bride, shedding Haumai and self-conceit, has found the Husband for ever;
night and day (she) holds fast to the Husband, (and) finds peace on the true bed.
(Those who) went (from the world) crying mine, mine got nothing in their hands.
The forsaken soul-bride has no (place in the Husband's) mansion; at the last (she) went away repenting.
That Husband of mine is the One; fix loving attention on the One alone.
Says Nanak: O bride, if (you) long for peace, enshrine the Name of the Lord in (your) mind. ॥8॥
428.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Those whom he has given the Amrit to taste have found its savour, in Sahaj and in love.
The True One is carefree; he has not a speck of greed.
The true Amrit is raining down; (he) puts (it) into the mouths of the Gurmukhs.
(Their) mind stays ever green, (and they) sing the virtues of the Lord in Sahaj.
The self-willed (brides) are ever forsaken soul-brides; standing at the door, (they) wail.
Those who have not known the delight of the Husband do just what was written (for them) from the start.
The Gurmukh sows Truth, (and in him) Truth springs up; the True Name is (his) trade.
Those whom he has set to this profit, (to them he) gives the storehouses of devotion.
The Gurmukh (brides) are ever happy soul-brides; (the Lord's) fear and devotion are (their) adornment.
Night and day (they) enjoy their own Husband, (and) keep the True One fixed in (their) heart.
Those who have enjoyed their own Husband, to them I offer myself;
shedding self-conceit from within, (they) stay ever with the Husband.
In the Husband's love and affection, (their) body and mind are cool (and their) faces bright.
Having killed Haumai and craving, (their) bed is a bed of ease, (and) the Husband delights in (them).
(She into whose heart's) home (the Lord), in his grace, has come through boundless love for the Guru,
(that) happy soul-bride has found as Husband the one Murari alone.
He has forgiven all (her) sins; the Uniter has united (her with himself).
O Nanak, let us speak only such words that, hearing them, (the Lord) may bear (us) love. ॥8॥
428.2: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Virtue springs from the True Guru when that God unites (one with the Guru);
(then) the Naam is meditated on in Sahaj, (and) wisdom is revealed (within).
O mind, do not think the Lord is far away; see (him) ever present.
(He) ever hears and ever sees; he is wholly present in the Shabad.
Those who have recognised their own self through the Guru have meditated (on the Lord) with a single mind;
(they) ever enjoy their own Husband, (and) have found peace through the True Name.
O mind, no one is yours; reflect through the Shabad and see.
Run and fall into the Lord's refuge; (you) will find the door of liberation.
Through the Shabad (the Naam) is heard, through the Shabad it is understood, (and one) stays lovingly attuned to the True One.
Through the Shabad alone Haumai is killed, (and one) finds peace in the True mansion.
In this age the glory belongs to the Naam; without the Name there is no glory.
This glory of Maya is for four days; it is gone without delay.
Those who have forgotten the Naam are dead, (and) they go on dying.
(They) have not tasted the savour of the Lord's elixir; (they) stay sunk in filth.
Some (the Lord) himself has forgiven and united (with himself), joining (them) to the Naam night and day;
(they) live the Truth, abide in the True One, (and) merge in the True One alone.
Without the Shabad (the Lord) is neither heard nor seen; deaf and blind, the world wanders astray.
Without the Name (it) will suffer pain; (but) the Naam is received only by the will of that (Lord).
Those who have joined their mind to the Bani are pure people, and accepted (at the Lord's door).
O Nanak, they never forget the Naam; at the door of the True One they are renowned. ॥9॥
429.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Through the Shabad alone are the devotees known, whose speech is true;
self-conceit has gone from within (them), (they) have accepted the Name, (and their) union with the True One comes about.
The Name of the Lord, Har Har, is the honour of (his) servants;
fruitful is their life, (and) everyone honours them.
Haumai and the sense of mine are (the world's) caste, (and with them) great anger and pride;
if one dies through the Shabad, then (this) caste goes; (one's) light merges in the Light, (and) the Lord is met.
(I) have met the Perfect True Guru, (and) my life has borne fruit;
(I) have found the Naam, the nine treasures, (and my) storehouses are full, never to run out.
The traders in this capital who come are (those) to whom the Naam is dear;
one who becomes Gurmukh obtains (this) wealth; within such ones (dwells) reflection on the Shabad.
The proud manmukhs do not know the worth of devotion;
(the Lord) himself has led (them) astray from the start; (they) have lost the game (of life) in a gamble.
Without love there is no devotion, nor is there peace in the body.
The gift of love is received (from the Guru); through devotion as the Guru teaches, the mind is steadied.
He alone performs devotion, reflecting on the Guru's Shabad, whom (the Lord himself) moves to it;
with Haumai and duality killed, the one Name dwells in (his) heart.
The caste and honour of the devotees is the one Name; (the Lord) himself adorns (them).
(They) are ever in his refuge; as it pleases (him), so (he) brings (their) task to fulfilment.
Wondrous is devotion to Allah, the Lord; (it) is understood through reflection on the Guru('s word).
O Nanak, (one in whose) heart the Naam dwells is adorned by (the Lord's) fear, devotion and the Naam. ॥9॥
430.1: Raag Asa, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Led astray by other pleasures, (one) suffers pain without the Naam;
(he) has not met the True Guru, the Purakh, who imparts true understanding.
O my crazed mind, taste the Lord's elixir (and) enjoy its savour.
