Clinging to other pleasures, you wander about, wasting (your) life for nothing.
In this age the Gurmukhs are pure; (they) stay lovingly attuned to the True Name.
Without (the Lord's) grace nothing is obtained; what can one say?
(Those on whom it falls) recognise their own self, (and) die through the Shabad, casting the vices out of (their) mind;
(they) have run to the Guru's refuge, (and) the Forgiver has forgiven (them).
Without the Name peace is not found, nor does sorrow leave from within;
(yet) this world is gripped by attachment to Maya, led astray by the doubt of duality.
The forsaken soul-brides do not know the Husband's worth; what use is the adornment they put on?
Night and day (they) go about ever burning; the Husband does not delight in (them) on the bed.
The happy soul-brides, shedding self-conceit from within, have reached (the Husband's) mansion;
adorned with the Guru's Shabad, (they) have been united (with himself) by their own Husband.
(The manmukh) has put death out of (his) mind; attachment to Maya is pitch darkness.
The manmukhs die and die and are born, and die again, (and) are disgraced at the door of Jam.
Those whom he himself has united are united (with him), reflecting on the Guru's Shabad.
O Nanak, (those) merged in the Naam have bright faces in that True Court. ॥8॥
430.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 2, Ashtapadis, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(I) have won over the five (virtues), (and) turned away the five (passions);
(the first) five (I) have settled (within), (the other) five (I) have driven out.
In this way the city (of my body) has come to be peopled, O my brother;
sin has gone, (for) the Guru has made wisdom firm (within).
(The Guru) has set a fence of true dharma (around it);
its strong gates (are) reflection on the Guru's wisdom.
Sow the crop of the Naam, O brothers and friends;
trade in (it), and serve the Guru every day.
All the shops (of this city) are of calm, Sahaj and peace;
the banker and the traders (live) together in one place.
(Here) no one takes jizya, fine or toll,
(for) the True Guru has set the seal of the Lord's own court.
Load the merchandise of the Naam and send off (your) consignment;
through the Guru, earn the profit and come (to your true) home.
The True Guru is the banker, the Sikhs are the travelling traders;
(their) capital is the Naam, (and) cherishing the True One (in the heart) is (their) account.
He dwells in this house whom the Perfect Guru (blesses with) service;
O Nanak, (that house becomes) the unshakeable city of the Lord. ॥8॥
431.1: Raag Asavari, Ghar 3, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O my mind, love for the Lord has taken hold;
repeating (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, in the Saadh Sangat: (this is) the pure and true way of life.
(O Lord,) great is (my) thirst for the sight of you, as I think (of you) in countless ways;
be gracious, O Supreme Lord, O Lord; show mercy, O Murari.
The mind, a stranger (wandering through many births), has come and joined the Saadh's company;
the merchandise it wanted, it has found in the love of the Naam.
However many the pleasures and relishes of Maya, they perish in an instant;
(but) the devotees dyed in your Name enjoy peace in every place.
The whole world is seen to be passing; the Name of the Lord is unshakeable.
Make friends with the Saadh, and you will find an unshakeable place.
Friends, companions, sons and kin: none of them goes along (with you);
the Name of Ram alone stands by (one to the end); God is the Master of the lowly.
The lotus feet have become the ship; clinging to them, (one) has crossed the ocean (of the world).
(the one who) has met the Perfect True Guru (has) true love for God.
(O Lord,) this is the plea of your Saadh: may you not be forgotten with any breath or morsel;
whatever pleases you is good; in your will (all) affairs are set right.
The Beloved, the ocean of peace, has been met, and great bliss has welled up;
says Nanak, all sorrows are erased: God, (the Lord of) supreme bliss, has been met. ॥8॥
431.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 4, Birhare, to the measure of the Chhants, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Let us remember the Supreme Lord God, O dear one; I am a sacrifice to the sight of him.
He by remembering whom sorrows are forgotten, O dear one: how can he be forsaken?
I would sell this body to the Sant, O dear one, (who) unites (me with) the Beloved.
The pleasures and adornments of Maya are insipid; I have given them up, O my mother.
Lust, anger and greed have left (me), O dear one, as (I) fell at the True Guru's feet.
Those humble ones who are dyed in (the love of) Ram, O dear one, go nowhere else.
Those who have tasted the essence of the Lord('s Name), O dear one, remain sated and fulfilled.
O Nanak, (one who) has grasped the hem of the Saadh's robe crosses the terrifying ocean (of the world).
The pain of birth and death is cut away, O dear one, when the Lord King is met.
Beautiful, refined and wise is my God; when he shows (me) his sight, (that is) life (to me).
Beings parted from you, O Beloved, go on being born and dying, having eaten the poison (of Maya).
Only the one you unite (with yourself) meets (you), O Beloved; I fall at his feet.
The peace (that comes) in beholding your sight, O Beloved, cannot be told by the mouth.
True love does not break, O Beloved; it stays contained (in the heart) age after age.
Whatever pleases you is good, O Beloved; undying is your will.
O Nanak, those dyed in the love of Narayan, O Beloved, are intoxicated in Sahaj and in love.
You alone know all the ways (of things), O Beloved; to whom else should I speak and tell (it)?
You are the Giver of all beings; (all) wear and eat what you have given.
Pleasure and pain (come) by your order, O Beloved; there is no other place (to turn).
What you have me do, that I do, O Beloved; nothing else can be done.
All the days and nights are beautiful, O Beloved, in which the Lord's Name is repeated.
That alone is the work (one) does, O Beloved, (whose) writ (one) has had inscribed on the forehead from the start.
The One himself is at work (in all), O Beloved; he is contained in every heart.
Draw (me) up out of the well of the world, O Beloved; Nanak (has come to) the Lord's refuge. ॥8॥
432.1: Raag Asa, Patti Likhi, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Sassa: he who created the universe is the one Master of all;
those whose minds were attached (to him) kept serving (him); their coming (into the world) has borne fruit. ॥1॥
432.2: O mind, why do you go astray, O foolish mind?
When you can render the account (of your deeds), O brother, then (are you truly) learned.
432.3: Eevri: the Primal Being is the Giver (of all); he himself alone is the True One.
One who, through the Guru, understands (him) in these letters has no account (standing) on his head. ॥2॥
432.4: Oora: let us praise him whose limit has not been found.
They alone who serve (him) obtain the fruit, they who have practised the Truth. ॥3॥
432.5: Nganga: if anyone understands (true) knowledge, he alone is learned, a pandit;
if he knows the One (Lord) in all beings, then he utters no (word of) Haumai. ॥4॥
432.6: Kaka: when the hair has turned white (as the white lotus), shining without soap,
the scouts of Jam the King have come, and (one is) held bound by the chain of Maya. ॥5॥
432.7: Khakha: Khundkar (the Lord) is the King of the world, who has bought (all beings as his own) and given (them) their keep;
in whose bond the whole world is held; no one else's command holds sway. ॥6॥
432.8: Gaga: (the one who,) by mere talk of Gobind, who has kneaded and worked (the clay of the world), has grown proud,
for such a one, he (Gobind) who shaped the pots and built the kiln (of the world) has made ready the putting in (the kiln) and the taking out. ॥7॥
432.9: Ghagha: if the servant toils at (true) labour and stays attached to the Guru's Shabad,
if he knows bad and good as alike: in this way he keeps the Master in remembrance. ॥8॥
432.10: Chacha: he who created the four Vedas, the four sources (of life) and the four ages
has himself, age after age, been the yogi, the enjoyer (in the beings of) the sources, the learned one and the pandit. ॥9॥
433.1: Chhachha: the shadow (of ignorance) spreads within all; (O Lord,) doubt is of your making.
Having created doubt, he himself has led (beings) astray; (O Lord,) those on whom your grace has fallen have met the Guru. ॥10॥
433.2: Jaja: the humble beggar begs for knowledge (of God); for these alms he has wandered through the eighty-four lakh (forms of life).
The One alone takes, the One alone gives; I have heard of no other, a second. ॥11॥
433.3: Jhajha: why do you fret yourself to death, O mortal? Whatever (God) is to give, he goes on giving.
Giving and giving, he watches over (all) and runs his command, as the sustenance of beings is allotted. ॥12॥
433.4: Nyanya: when I look with attention, there is no other at all;
the One is present in every place; the One dwells in the mind. ॥13॥
433.5: Tatta: why do you busy yourselves with vain affairs, O mortal? In a ghari or a muhurat you must rise and depart.
Do not gamble away your (human) life; run and fall into the Lord's refuge. ॥14॥
433.6: Thattha: coolness has come within those whose minds are fixed on the Lord's feet;
those humble ones whose minds are so fixed have been carried across; (O Lord,) by your grace they have found peace. ॥15॥
433.7: Dadda: why do you make a show, O mortal? Whatever has come into being must all depart.
Worship him, and you will find peace; he pervades all, without a gap. ॥16॥
433.8: Dhaddha: he himself pulls down and builds up; as it pleases him, so he does.
Making (creation) again and again, he watches over it and runs his command; he carries across the one on whom he casts his glance of grace. ॥17॥
433.9: Nanna: the one in whose heart (the Lord) stays pervading, he alone sings the Lord's virtues;
the Creator himself unites (him with himself), and he is not born again. ॥18॥
433.10: Tata: the world-ocean is too deep to wade, and its far shore has not been found;
we have neither boat nor raft, (and) we will drown; carry us across, O King who carries (all) across. ॥19॥
433.11: Thatha: he is in place after place, he by whom all that is was made.
What can be called doubt, what Maya? Whatever pleases him, that alone is good. ॥20॥
433.12: Dada: let me blame no one; the fault is in my own deeds.
Whatever I did, that I received; blame should not be laid on other people. ॥21॥
433.13: Dhadha: the Lord, who has set his power (in all), the doer of wonders who made (the world's many) colours:
what he gives, all have received; according to each one's deeds his command operates. ॥22॥
433.14: Nana: (everyone) daily enjoys the gifts of the Husband (Lord); (yet I) have neither seen him nor kept him in (my heart).
In talk alone am I a happy soul-bride, O sister; (yet) the Husband has never met me. ॥23॥
433.15: Pappa: the Supreme God is the King; he made this expanse (of the world) to behold (it).
He sees, understands and knows everything; he pervades within and without. ॥24॥
433.16: Phapha: all the world is caught in the noose (of Maya), held bound by the chain of Jam;
by the Guru's grace those men have escaped who have run to the Lord's sanctuary. ॥25॥
433.17: Babba: (the Lord) has begun to play the game (of chaupar), making the four ages the (four arms of the) board;
all beings and creatures he has made the pieces, and he himself casts the dice. ॥26॥
434.1: Bhabha: those who seek (him) obtain the fruit, in whom, by the Guru's grace, the fear (of God) has taken root;
the manmukhs wander, the fools, and do not remember (him); the round of the eighty-four lakh (forms of life) is their lot. ॥27॥
434.2: Mamma: attachment (to Maya) is death; only when death came did he think of Madhusudan.
While in the body, he read (of) other things, and forgot the letter Mamma. ॥28॥
434.3: Yaya: one is never born again, if one recognises the True One;
through the Guru he speaks (of him), through the Guru he understands, through the Guru he knows the One. ॥29॥
434.4: Rara: he pervades within all, all the creatures he has made;
having created the creatures, he has set them all to their tasks; those on whom (his) grace fell have taken the Naam. ॥30॥
434.5: Lala: he who has set (beings) to their tasks, who has made the love of Maya sweet (to them):
eating and drinking, and bearing (pain) alike: by his will (this) command is laid down (for each). ॥31॥
434.6: Vava: Vasudev, the Supreme God, who put on this guise (of the world) to behold (it),
sees and tastes (all), knows everything; he pervades within and without. ॥32॥
434.7: Rarra: what is (the use of) quarrelling, O mortal? Meditate on him who is deathless;
meditate on him, merge in the True One; (I) have made (myself) a sacrifice to him. ॥33॥
434.8: Haha: there is no other giver (but him) who created beings and gave (them) sustenance.
Meditate on the Lord's Name, merge in the Lord's Name; (so) night and day the profit of the Lord's Name is earned. ॥34॥
434.9: Aira: he who himself made (the world) is doing whatever is to be done;
he acts and causes (all) to act, and knows everything; so has Nanak the poet said. ॥35॥
434.10: Raag Asa, Patti, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Ayo Angai: the whole world has come (into being); Kakhai Ghangai: it is under (the sway of) death.
Riri Lali: (people) commit sins; reading (what breeds) vices, they have forgotten virtue. ॥1॥
434.11: O mind, to what end have you read such accounts?
The account (of your deeds) still stands on your head, to be given.
434.12: Sidhan-ngaiai: you do not remember (the Lord); Nana: you have not taken the Name.
Chhachha: you are wasting away night and day, you fool; how will you get free when Jam has seized you? ॥2॥
434.13: Babba: you fail to understand, you fool; lost in doubt, your life has slipped away.
Unworthy (of it), you have had yourself named a teacher; you have taken on yourself the load of others. ॥3॥
434.14: Jaja: your light (of understanding) has been stolen, you fool; at the end, as you go, you will repent.
You do not recognise the One Shabad; again and again you will come into births. ॥4॥
434.15: O pandit, read what is written on your own head; do not teach others (the reckonings of) Maya.
The noose has fallen first (on the neck) of the teacher; afterwards he puts (it) on the pupils' necks. ॥5॥
435.1: Sassa: your self-restraint is gone, you fool; you have taken a gift from the wrong place.
The daughter of your patron is your own (daughter); by eating this grain, your life has gone (to waste). ॥6॥
435.2: Mamma: your understanding has been stolen, you fool; the great disease of Haumai has seized you.
Within your inner self you have not recognised Brahm (God); you have become dependent on Maya. ॥7॥
435.3: Kaka: you have strayed in lust and anger, you fool; clinging to (the thought of) mine, you have let the Lord slip from your mind.
You read, you ponder, you proclaim much aloud; (but) without understanding you have drowned and died. ॥8॥
435.4: Tata: you are burnt up in tamas (anger), you fool; Thatha: the place (of your heart) has been defiled.
Ghagha: you wander from house to house, you fool; Dada: (yet) you have not received the gift (of the Name). ॥9॥
435.5: Pappa: you will not reach the far shore, you fool; you are entangled in the world's show.
The True One himself has led you astray, you fool; this is the writ set on your head. ॥10॥
435.6: Bhabha: you are drowning in the world-ocean, you fool; you are sunk deep in Maya.
(One who,) by the Guru's grace, knows the One crosses over in a single ghari. ॥11॥
435.7: Vava: your turn (of human birth) has come, you fool, (yet) Vasudev has slipped from your mind.
You will not find this time (again), you fool; then you will fall into Jam's power. ॥12॥
435.8: Jhajha: you will never (have to) grieve, you fool; listen to the True Guru's teaching, and see.
Without the True Guru there is no Guru; the one without a Guru bears an evil name. ॥13॥
435.9: Dhadha: hold back (the mind) that runs about, you fool; the treasure lies within you.
If you become Gurmukh, you will drink the Lord's essence, and feed on (the treasure) lying (within) age after age. ॥14॥
435.10: Gaga: keep Gobind in your mind, you fool; no one has ever found (him) by talk.
Enshrine the Guru's feet in your heart, you fool, (and) all past sins are forgiven. ॥15॥
435.11: Haha: understand the telling of the Lord's praises, you fool; then there will be peace for ever.
However much the manmukhs read, so much suffering clings to them; without the True Guru there is no liberation. ॥16॥
435.12: Rara: keep Ram in your mind, you fool. Those in whose hearts he dwells,
who by the Guru's grace have recognised Ram, have understood and found Ram, who is beyond the three qualities. ॥17॥
435.13: (O Lord,) your limit cannot be perceived; the Lord, who is beyond telling, cannot be told.
O Nanak, those who have met the True Guru have had their account settled. ॥18॥
435.14: Raag Asa, Ghar 1, Chhants, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O innocent bride, a young girl in the bloom of youth, my Husband is full of delight.
Deep is the love between bride and Husband; with delight she loves the Merciful One.
The bride's union with her Husband comes about (when) God, the Master, himself shows grace.
With the Husband, the bed (of her heart) is made beautiful, and the seven pools (within her) brim with Amrit.
O merciful True One, show kindness and mercy, that joined to the Shabad (I) may sing (your) praises.
O Nanak, seeing the Lord, her Groom, the young bride has blossomed; there is joyous eagerness in her mind.
O young bride, made lovely in Sahaj, (hear) one prayer of love:
To my mind and body the Lord is dear; I am dyed in union with God.
Dyed in God's love, (I) make my prayer to the Lord; in the Lord's Name (the bride) dwells in peace.
(O Lord,) (the brides) recognise your virtues, and then they know God; under the sway of virtue, fault flees.
(O Lord,) without you I cannot live even a moment; by (mere) talk and hearing (my mind) finds no comfort.
O Nanak, (she who) calls out, Beloved, Beloved, has her mind drenched in the delight her tongue tastes.
O my friends and companions, my Husband is a trader.
(From him I) have bought the Lord's Name, boundless in its relish and its worth.
Priceless beyond any price, the Beloved (dwells) in the true home; if she pleases God, then the bride is good.
Some (brides) revel in delight with the Lord; I stand at the door, calling out.
The cause of all creation, the all-powerful Sridhar (the Lord), himself brings the task to fulfilment.
O Nanak, by his gracious glance the bride is a happy wife, and the Shabad gives her heart support.
In my home (of the heart) the true song of joy (is sung); God, my Friend, has come.
He enjoys (me), dyed in (his) love; (I) gave (my) mind, and (he) took it.
I gave my own mind and took the Lord as my Groom; as it pleases him, so he enjoys (me).
Placing body and mind before the Husband, through the Shabad she gains the fruit of Amrit in the fortunate home (of her heart).
He is not found by intellect, by reading of texts or by much cleverness; he is met through love, when the mind holds him dear.
Says Nanak: the Master is our Friend; we do not belong to the world's people. ॥4॥
436.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The unstruck music, the unstruck music plays, with a ringing, tinkling chime.
My mind, my mind is dyed in the love of the darling Beloved.
Night and day, dyed (in love), the detached mind has found its home in the realm of Sunn.
The Primal Being, beyond all that is beyond, the Beloved, the Unseen: the True Guru has made (me) see him.
Narayan is ever steady on his seat, in his dwelling; through reflection (on the Guru's Shabad) the mind is dyed in him.
O Nanak, within the detached ones dyed in the Name is the ringing, tinkling chime of the unstruck music.
(O friend,) tell me, by what way can one go to that city beyond reach, beyond reach?
By truth and self-restraint, by cherishing (his) virtues, the Guru's Shabad is to be lived.
Living the true Shabad, one goes to one's own home and finds the treasure of virtues.
He has no branch, no root, no leaf, no bough; he is supreme over the heads of all.
(The world) has grown weary of chanting, austerity and self-restraint, done again and again; by stubborn effort and forced control (of the senses) he is not found.
O Nanak, the Life of the world is met in Sahaj, (when) understanding is given by the True Guru.
The Guru is the ocean, a mine of jewels; in him are jewels in abundance.
Bathe in the seven pools, O my mind, and be pure.
One bathes in the pure water when it pleases God; through reflection (on the Guru's Shabad) the five (virtues) are gained.
Giving up lust, anger, deceit and Maya, he holds the True Name in his heart.
Haumai, the wave of greed, and avarice are stilled; he finds the One who is merciful to the meek.
O Nanak, no place of pilgrimage equals the Guru; the Guru is the True Gopal.
I have looked through forest after forest, and looked at all the green growth.
The three worlds, the whole world, all of it, you yourself have made.
All is of your making; you remain steadfast; there is none like you.
You are the Giver, and all are beggars at your door; whom but you should I praise?
You give gifts unasked, O Giver; the storehouses are full of devotion to you.
Without the Name of Ram there is no liberation: Nanak says this after reflection. ॥4॥
437.1: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
My mind, my mind is dyed in the love of Ram, the Beloved.
The True Master, the Primal Being, beyond all that is beyond, upholds (all).
Beyond reach, beyond the senses, boundless, without limit, the Supreme Lord is foremost of all.
He was from the beginning, from the start of the ages; he is, and he will be; know all else to be false.
(The mind) does not know the essence of rites and deeds of dharma; how then are awareness and liberation to be gained?
O Nanak, through the Guru (the mind) recognises by the Shabad (that) night and day the Name is to be meditated on.
My mind, my mind is convinced (that) the Name is the (true) friend.
Haumai, possessiveness and Maya do not go along (at the end).
Mother, father, brother, son, cleverness, wealth and wife: (none of these) goes along.
Through reflection (I) have cast off and forsaken the daughter of the ocean (Maya), (keeping her) under (my) feet.
The Primal Being has shown a wondrous play: wherever I look, there he is.
Nanak does not let go of the Lord's devotion; whatever comes to be in Sahaj, let it be.
My mind, my mind is pure, cherishing the True One.
Erasing faults, (I) walk on, with virtues as companions beside (me).
Casting off faults, (one whose) conduct is excellent is found true at the door of the True One.
(He) puts a stop to coming and going, and through the Guru reflects on the essence (of all).
(O Lord,) you are (my) friend, beloved, all-knowing companion; in the True One glory is gained.
Says Nanak: the jewel of the Name has shone forth (within); such is the Guru's teaching (I) have received.
The True One is the collyrium; applying that collyrium, (the mind) is dyed in the Niranjan (the One untouched by Maya's stain).
The Life of the world, the Giver, pervades mind and body.
The Lord, the Life of the world, the Giver, in whom the mind is dyed, is met in Sahaj when (the Guru) brings about the meeting.
In the gathering of the Saadh, in the company of the Sants, by God's gracious glance, peace is found.
The detached ones, dyed in the Lord's devotion, are rid of attachment and thirst.
O Nanak, rare are the servants, detached (from the world), who have killed Haumai and are content (in the Name). ॥4॥
438.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 2, a Chhant, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Wherever I go, you are in every place, O true Creator.
(You are) the Giver of all, who shapes (each) by their deeds, the One who takes sorrows away.
The Master who takes sorrows away, by whose doing (all) comes to pass,
destroys in a single moment sins by the millions upon millions.
The swan as a swan, the heron as a heron: he weighs every heart.
Wherever I go, you are in every place, O true Creator.
Those who meditated (on him) with one-pointed mind found peace; such are rare in the world.
Jam does not come near them; they live the Guru's Shabad and never come back defeated.
They never lose; they cherish the virtues of the Lord, Har Har; Jam does not come near them.
Birth and death are ended for those who have fallen at the Lord's feet.
Through the Guru's teaching they have gained the Lord's essence, the Lord's fruit, keeping in their hearts the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Those who meditated (on him) with one-pointed mind found peace; such are rare in the world.
To the One who created the world and set it to its work, (I am) a sacrifice.
Serve him and earn (this) profit; (so) honour is gained in the Lord's court.
In the Lord's court, honour is gained only by the one who recognises the One.
He gains the nine treasures, who through the Guru's teaching meditates on the Lord and daily speaks and tells of the Lord's virtues.
Night and day take the Name of him alone: the Lord, the most exalted, the all-pervading Being, foremost of all.
To the One who created the world and set it to its work, I am a sacrifice.
Those who take the Name look beautiful; to them come the fruits of peace; those who believe (in it) go having won (life's game).
When it pleases him, their fruit does not run short, though ages upon ages pass.
Though ages upon ages pass, O Master, their fruit does not run short.
Those who meditate on the Lord's Name know no old age, no death, no fall into hell.
Those who repeat Har Har do not wither; O Nanak, they suffer no pain.
Those who take the Name look beautiful; to them come the fruits of peace; those who believe (in it) go having won (life's game). ॥4॥
438.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, Ghar 3, a Chhant, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Listen, O black deer: why are you lost in delight in the garden (of the world)?
The poisonous fruit is sweet for four days, then it turns hot (and painful).
(That in which you are) so drunk turns hot then; without the Name it brings torment.
It is like the waves the sea throws up, like the flash of lightning (gone in a moment).
Without the Lord there is no protector, and him you have forgotten.
Says Nanak: O mind, remember the True One, (or) you will die, O black deer.
O bumblebee, hovering over the flowers, very heavy is the pain (to come).
I have asked my own Guru, true and wise in reflection.
Having reflected, I asked the True Guru about the bumblebee (of the mind), lost in delight among the creepers.
(The answer:) when the sun rises (and the night of life is over), the body falls, and (the soul) is heated like oil in the pan.
Bound on Jam's road, you take blows, O ghoul, without the Shabad.
Says Nanak: O mind, remember the True One, (or) you will die, O black bumblebee.
O my soul, a stranger (here), why do you fall into entanglements?
If the True Master dwells in the mind, why would you be caught in Jam's net?
The fish, parted (from the water), weeps from its eyes when the fisher has cast his net.
The world, Maya's attachment, seems sweet; at the end this illusion is shattered.
Worship (him) with devotion, fixing your mind on the Lord, and cast anxiety from your mind.
Says Nanak: O mind, remember the True One, O soul, a stranger (here).
When the currents of rivers are parted, they meet again only by destiny.
Age after age (this attachment) is sweet, (yet) filled with poison; a rare yogi (one detached) knows (it).
Some (rare) one knows (it) in Sahaj and recognises the Lord: the one who has kept the True Guru in mind.
Without the Lord's Name, heedless fools, strayed in doubt, waste away.
Those in whose hearts are not the Lord's Name, devotion and the True One, at the end weep and wail aloud.
Says Nanak: through the true Shabad the True One unites those long parted. ॥4॥
439.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, Ghar 1, Chhants, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
In my home (of the heart) is the true song of joy, made beautiful by the true Shabad.
The bride's union with her Husband has come about; God himself has united (her with him).
God himself united (her) and set the True (Name) in (her) mind; the bride is rapt in Sahaj.
The Guru's Shabad has adorned her, truth has made her beautiful; dyed in love, she ever delights in (her Husband).
When she sheds self-conceit and finds the Lord as her Groom, then she sets the Lord's essence in her mind.
Says Nanak: (she who is) made beautiful by the Guru's Shabad has her whole life made fruitful.
Caught in (the love of) another, the bride, strayed in doubt, does not find the Lord as her Groom.
That bride has no virtue; she wastes her life in vain.
She wastes her life in vain; the manmukh, ignorant, full of faults, pines in grief.
Serving her own True Guru, she found lasting peace; then she met the Husband, present before her.
Seeing the Husband, she blossomed, delighted within; through the true Shabad she is (absorbed) in love.
O Nanak, without the Name the bride strays in doubt; meeting her Beloved, she finds peace.
The bride whom the Guru has brought into union knew the Husband to be with her.
Within, through the Shabad, she met (him), and in Sahaj quenched (her) burning.
The Shabad quenched the burning; peace came within, and in Sahaj she tasted the Lord's essence.
Meeting her own Beloved, she ever enjoys his love; through the true Shabad her speech is sweet.
The pandits and the silent sages have worn themselves out with reading and reading; those who wear religious garb have not found liberation.
O Nanak, without devotion the world has gone mad; through the true Shabad (one) is united (with God).
Bliss has come into the mind of that bride whom the beloved Lord has united (with himself).
That bride is steeped in the Lord's essence through the Guru's boundless Shabad.
Through the boundless Shabad she has met the Beloved; ever she cherishes (his) virtues, and they dwell in (her) mind.
The bed (of her heart) became beautiful when the Husband enjoyed her; meeting the Beloved, her faults fled.
In the home where the Lord's Name is ever meditated on, the song of joy (resounds) through all four ages.
O Nanak, those dyed in the Name are ever in bliss; meeting the Lord, (all) tasks are fulfilled. ॥4॥
440.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, Ghar 3, a Chhant, by the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji).
O my friends, my dear ones, keep up devotion to the Husband Lord.
Serve your own Guru always, and receive the precious gift of the Naam.
Practise devotion to the Husband Lord, (the devotion) that pleases the beloved Husband.
If you do as you yourselves will, then the Husband's favour does not come (your way).
This path of devotion and love is hard; some rare one finds it at the Guru's door.
Says Nanak, the one on whom (the Lord) shows grace fixes his mind on devotion to the Lord.
O my mind, you who have turned renunciant, to whom do you show off your detachment?
The Lord's song of joy (sounds) ever and always within those who sing the Lord's virtues.
Practise (true) detachment, give up pretence: that Husband Lord knows everything.
In the water, on the land and in the sky, he alone is (present); the Gurmukh recognises (his) Hukam.
One who has recognised the Lord's Hukam, he alone finds every comfort.
Thus says Nanak: he is the (true) renunciant who night and day keeps his mind attuned to the Lord.
O mind, wherever you run, there the Lord is with you.
O mind, cleverness should be given up; cherish the Guru's Shabad.
That Husband Lord is ever with you; if you hold the Name of the Lord in your heart even for a moment,
your sins of birth after birth will be cut away, and in the end you will attain the supreme state.
Your bond with the True One will be tied; through the Guru, cherish (him) always.
Thus says Nanak: O mind, wherever you run, there the Lord is ever with you.
When the True Guru is met, the wandering (mind) is held still, and comes to dwell in its own home (within).
It buys the Naam, utters the Naam, and stays merged in the Naam.
The wandering (mind) is held still when the True Guru is met, and it reaches the Tenth Gate.
There the Amrit (of the Naam) is its food, and the strain of Sahaj wells up; through that Shabad (the pull of) the world is held in check.
There countless instruments (play), there is bliss for ever, and (the mind) stays merged in the True One.
Thus says Nanak: when the True Guru is met, the wandering (mind) is held still, and comes to dwell in its own home (within).
O mind, you are the very form of the Light; recognise your own source.
O mind, the dear Lord is at your side; following the Guru's teaching, take delight in his love.
If you recognise your source, you will know the Husband Lord, and understanding of death and of life will come.
If by the Guru's grace you know the One, then the love of another does not arise.
Peace has come into the mind, the music of rejoicing has sounded, and so (the mind) has been accepted.
Thus says Nanak: O mind, you are the very form of the Light; recognise your own source.
O mind, you are smeared with pride; laden with pride you will depart.
Bewitched by enchanting Maya, you will be made to wander through births again and again.
Clinging to pride you will go, O foolish mind, and at the last, when you are gone, you will repent.
The disease of pride and craving has seized you; you are wasting your life in vain.
O foolish, self-willed (mind), you do not remember (the Lord); gone on to the next world, you will repent.
Thus says Nanak: O mind, you are smeared with pride; laden with pride you will depart.
O mind, take no pride (in thinking) that you know something; through the Guru, become humble.
Within you are ignorance and an intellect of ego; through the True Shabad, wash away this filth.
Be humble before the True Guru; do not make any show of yourself.
The world is burning in its own pride; see that you do not ruin your own self (in it as well).
(Only) if you do your work in the True Guru's will (are you safe); so stay attached to the True Guru's will.
Thus says Nanak: give up self-conceit and you will find peace; O mind, remain humble.
Blessed is that moment when I met the True Guru, and that Husband Lord came into my mind.
Great bliss and Sahaj came about, and (my) mind and body found peace.
That Husband Lord came into my mind; I enshrined him in my heart, and put all my faults out of mind.
When it pleased him, virtues became manifest (in me); the True Guru himself adorned (my life).
Those people are accepted who have held fast to the one Naam and have ended the love of another.
Thus says Nanak: blessed is that moment when I met the True Guru, and that Husband Lord came into my mind.
Some beings are lost in doubt; that Husband Lord has himself led them astray.
In the love of another they wander about, doing their deeds in Haumai.
That Husband Lord has himself led them astray and set them on the wrong path; nothing is in their power.
Their good state and their bad you alone know, you who made this creation.
Your Hukam is very weighty; to some rare one you make it understood through the Guru.
Thus says Nanak: what can helpless beings do, when you lead them astray in doubt?
O my True Master, true is your greatness.
You are the Supreme Lord, the infinite Master; your power cannot be told.
True is your greatness; those in whose minds you have made it dwell sing your virtues for ever.
They sing your virtues when they are pleasing to you, and they fix their minds on the True One.
One whom you yourself unite (with you) stays absorbed (in you) through the Guru.
Thus says Nanak: O my True Master, true is your greatness. ॥10॥
442.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 1, Chhants, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
I have found life, the true life: through the Guru (the Lord) has become dear to me.
(The Guru) gives the Lord's Name, the Lord's Name, and makes it dwell in my every breath.
He has made the Name of the Lord, Har Har, dwell in my every breath, and has taken away all my fear and sorrow.
Through the Guru's word I have meditated on the Unseen One, beyond the reach of the senses, and have attained the pure, supreme state.
With unstruck melody, instruments play (within me) day after day, as I sing the True Guru's Bani.
O Nanak, God the Giver has given (this) gift, and (my) light has merged in the Light.
The self-willed, the manmukhs, have died (a spiritual death), holding Maya to be their own.
(Their mind) is buoyed one moment and sinks the next; they have fixed their minds on the stinking carcass (of the body).
They have fixed (them) on the stinking carcass, and their minds cling to what shows itself like the safflower's colour (bright, and soon gone).
Like a shadow (their mind) falls one moment to the east and the next to the west, and turns like the wheel the potter spins.
They eat sorrow, gather sorrow and live on sorrow; they have made sorrow grow and grow.
O Nanak, the hard (ocean of the world) is crossed with ease when one comes to the Guru's refuge.
My Master, my Master is beautiful, unreachable and unfathomable.
I ask for the capital of the Lord, the capital of the Lord, O my True Guru, my Banker.
One who has sought the Lord's capital and bought the Naam sings (his) virtues, and through those virtues is dear (to him).
He casts off sleep and hunger altogether, and stays absorbed in the stillness of Sunn.
Traders of one kind come (to the Guru) and take away the Lord's Name as their profit.
O Nanak, offer your mind and body to the Guru; he finds (the Name) in whose lot it is.
The ocean (of the body) is full of jewels upon jewels, of countless precious things.
Those who are attached to the Bani, the Guru's Bani, have it come into their hands.
Those attached to the Guru's Bani have the priceless, boundless jewel come into their hands.
They have found the Name of the Lord, Har Har, beyond all weighing; (O Lord,) their storehouses are full of devotion to you.
I have churned the ocean of the body and searched it, and a thing of matchless beauty has come into sight.
The Guru is Govind, and Govind is the Guru; says Nanak, there is no difference (between them), O brother. ॥4॥
442.2: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Gently, gently, drop by drop, the stream of Amrit rains down.
To the Gurmukh, to the Gurmukh, the beloved Lord comes into sight.
The Name of Ram, the saviour of the world, is dear (to him); in the Name of Ram is (his) glory.
In Kalyug the Name of Ram is the ship; through the Guru it carries (one) across.
In this world and the next, through the Name of Ram (they) live at ease; the Gurmukh's way of life is excellent.
O Nanak, (the Lord) in his mercy gives this gift, and through the Name of Ram carries (one) across.
(I) have repeated the Name of Ram, of Ram, and sorrows and sins have been destroyed and driven away.
In close bond with the Guru, in close bond with the Guru, I have meditated (on him), and have made Ram dwell in my heart.
Ram has been remembered in the heart, and the supreme state attained, since (I) came to the Guru's refuge.
The boat (of life), sinking in greed and vice, came out (safe), when the True Guru made the Naam firm (within).
The Perfect Guru has given the gift of (spiritual) life, and has fixed (my) mind on the Name of Ram.
The Merciful One himself gives (this) in his mercy; O Nanak, (it comes) in the Guru's refuge.
Hearing the Bani of the Name of Ram, (I) have won success; all (my) affairs are made fair.
With every hair, every single hair, through the Guru I meditate on Ram.
Meditating on the Name of Ram, (I) have become pure; he has no form or feature at all.
Ram, Ram alone is remembered within the heart, and all craving and hunger have been taken away.
Mind and body have grown cool, and all is adorned, (now that) through the Guru's teaching Ram has shone forth.
O Nanak, (the Lord) himself has shown grace; I am the slave of the slaves of (his) slaves.
They who have forgotten the Name of Ram, of Ram, are foolish, unfortunate manmukhs.
Within them attachment holds sway; moment after moment Maya holds on (to them).
Maya's filth has stuck (to them); they have become foolish and unfortunate, those to whom the Name of Ram is not pleasing.
The proud perform countless rites, but keep (their minds) stolen away from the Name of the Lord, of Ram.
Very hard and painful is the path of Jam, (full of) the blackness and darkness of attachment.
O Nanak, when (one) has meditated on the Naam through the Guru, then (one) finds the door of liberation.
The Name of Ram, of Ram, and Ram himself, one who is a Gurmukh comes to know through the Guru.
This mind, which wanders one moment up high and (the next) down in the netherworld, he brings into the one home.
He brings the mind into the one home, knows every state and bound (of the spiritual life), and relishes the Name of the Lord, of Ram.
The Name of Ram keeps the honour of the Lord's servant; it saved Prahlad and carried him across.
Ram, Ram, the all-pervading, the beautiful, is high above; telling his virtues, none has found their end.
O Nanak, hearing the Name of Ram, (they) are drenched (in it), and merged in the Name of Ram.
Those within whom the Name of Ram dwells have cast away all anxiety.
All wealth and all dharma have come to them, and they have found the fruit their minds longed for.
They have found the fruit the mind longed for, meditating on the Name of Ram and singing the praises of Ram's Name.
Evil thinking and bad sense have gone and understanding has come, as they fix their minds on the Name of Ram.
Fruitful has become the life, and the whole body, in which the Name of Ram has shone forth.
O Nanak, worship the Lord always, day and night; through the Guru, (one) comes to dwell in one's own home (within).
Those who have come to have faith in the Name of Ram do not fix their minds on another.
Even if the whole earth were turned to gold and given (to them), nothing but the Name pleases them.
The Name of Ram pleases their minds; they have found supreme peace, and (the Name) goes with them as their companion at the last, when they depart.
They have gathered the wealth of the Name of Ram as their capital; it neither sinks nor is lost.
In this age the Name of Ram is the raft; Jamkaal does not come near.
O Nanak, (one who) has recognised Ram through the Guru, (Ram) in his grace himself unites (him with himself).
The Name of Ram, of Ram, is true, ever true; the Gurmukh has come to know it.
That servant is engaged in the Guru's service who has offered up his mind and body.
He has given his mind and body, with great faith in his mind; for the love of the servant, the Guru unites (him with the Lord).
The Master of the meek, the Giver of all beings, is found through the Perfect Guru.
The Guru is the Sikh, and the Sikh is the Guru; (the two) are one, (and the Sikh) carries on the Guru's teaching.
(The Guru) places the mantra of the Name of Ram in the heart; O Nanak, the union (with the Lord) comes through love. ॥8॥
444.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, Ghar 2, Chhants, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Lord, Har Har, the Creator, is the destroyer of sorrow; the Lord's Name purifies the fallen.
One to whom the Lord's service is pleasing has attained the supreme state; (remembering) the Lord, Har Har, is the most excellent work.
The Lord is the excellent work: let the Lord's Name be repeated; by repeating the Lord, one becomes steady.
(That one) wipes out the sorrows of both birth and death, and in Sahaj sleeps in peace.
O Lord, Har Har, O Master, show your grace, that (we) may repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Atam Ram, the all-pervading.
The Lord, Har Har, the Creator, is the destroyer of sorrow; the Lord's Name purifies the fallen.
In Kalyug the treasure of the Lord's Name is the most excellent; let the Lord be repeated in love of the True Guru.
Through the Guru, read of the Lord; through the Guru, hear of the Lord; repeating and hearing of the Lord, sorrow departs.
Repeating the Name of the Lord, Har Har, sorrow has been destroyed; through the Lord's Name, supreme peace has been found.
The True Guru's wisdom has blazed up, there is light in the heart, and the darkness of ignorance is dispelled.
They alone have worshipped the Name of the Lord, Har Har, on whose foreheads (this) was written from the very beginning.
In Kalyug the treasure of the Lord's Name is the most excellent; let the Lord be repeated in love of the True Guru.
One in whose mind the Lord, Har Har, has become dear has found supreme peace, and earned the Lord as profit: the state beyond all desire.
He has formed love for the Lord, the Lord's Name is his companion, and doubt and coming and going are ended.
Coming and going, doubt and fear have fled, as he has sung the virtues of the Lord, Har Har Har.
The sins and sorrows of birth after birth have been washed away, and he is absorbed in the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
Those who have meditated on the Lord, as was written in their lot from the beginning: their life is fruitful and accepted.
One in whose mind the Lord, Har Har, has become dear has found supreme peace, and earned the Lord as profit: the state beyond all desire.
Those to whom the Lord seems sweet are the foremost of people; they are the exalted ones, the people of the Lord, Har Har.
Their greatness is the Lord's Name, their companion the Lord's Name; through the Guru's Shabad, they enjoy the Lord's delight.
Enjoying the Lord's delight, they stay wholly unattached; by great good fortune they have found the Lord's delight.
Blessed are they, great, true and perfect beings, who through the Guru's teaching have meditated on the Naam.
Servant Nanak begs for the dust of the Saadh's (the Guru's) feet; grief and separation in the mind are ended.
Those to whom the Lord seems sweet are the foremost of people; they are the exalted ones, the people of the Lord, Har Har. ॥4॥
445.1: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
In Satjug everyone was contentment embodied; dharma stood on all four feet, and (hearts) dwelt in meditation (on the Lord).
(People) sang the Lord with mind and body, and found supreme peace; in their hearts was the Lord, and the knowledge of the Lord's virtues.
The knowledge of (his) virtues was their wealth; through the Lord, Har Har, their lives were fulfilled, and glory came through the Guru.
Within and without (they saw) the one Lord God alone, and no other besides.
One who fixed loving attention on the Lord, Har Har, with the Lord's Name as companion, gains honour in the Lord's court.
In Satjug everyone was contentment embodied; dharma stood on all four feet, and (hearts) dwelt in meditation (on the Lord).
(Then) came the age of Treta; force took hold within (people), and they practised the disciplines of chastity and self-restraint.
The fourth foot (of dharma) slipped, and it stood on three; anger blazed in mind and heart.
In mind and heart was anger, a deadly poison; kings marched against (one another), and by fighting they reaped pain.
The sickness of possessiveness took hold within (them), and Haumai and pride grew great.
(Those on whom) my Master, the Lord, Har Har, showed grace have the poison removed through the Guru's teaching, through the Lord's Name.
(Then) came the age of Treta; force took hold within (people), and they practised the disciplines of chastity and self-restraint.
(Then) came the age of Duapar; (people) were led astray by doubt; the Lord created the gopis and Kaanh (Krishna).
They practised austerities, enduring the heat (of fires), began sacrifices and works of merit, and performed rituals and rites in plenty.
With rituals and rites performed, two feet (of dharma) slipped away, and it stood held up on two.
Warriors fought many mighty wars; in Haumai one burns and sets others burning.
(One whom) the Lord, merciful to the meek, brings to the Guru, the Saadh, has his filth washed away on meeting the True Guru.
(Then) came the age of Duapar; (people) were led astray by doubt; the Lord created the gopis and Kaanh (Krishna).
(Then) the Lord made Kalyug; three feet (of dharma) slipped away, and it stands held up on the fourth foot (alone).
(One who) lives the Guru's Shabad has found the medicine, the Lord; through the Lord's praise, the Lord bestows peace.
The season of the Lord's praise has come; the Lord's Name is (true) glory; (the Gurmukh) has made the crop of the Name of the Lord, Har Har, spring up.
In Kalyug, (whoever) sows a seed other than the Name loses all the profit and the capital (too).
Servant Nanak has found the Perfect Guru, who has made the Name shine forth in (his) mind and heart.
(Then) the Lord made Kalyug; three feet (of dharma) slipped away, and it stands held up on the fourth foot (alone). ॥4॥
446.1: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
One whose mind loves the Lord's praise has attained the supreme state; to mind and body the Lord has grown sweet.
He has found the relish of the Lord, Har Har, and through the Guru's teaching meditated on the Lord; the fortune written of old on his forehead from the start (has awoken).
Such was the fortune on his forehead from the start: through the Lord's Name he found the Husband, and through the Name he sang the Lord's virtues.
On his forehead the jewel of deep love has shone out; through his Name the Lord has made him beautiful.
His light has merged in the Light; he has found God; meeting the True Guru, his mind is won over.
One whose mind loves the Lord's praise has attained the supreme state; to mind and body the Lord has grown sweet.
Those who sang the praise of the Lord, Har Har, attained the supreme state; those servants are excellent and foremost.
We wait upon their feet and wash their feet moment by moment, those to whom the Lord is sweet.
(Those to whom) the Lord is sweet have found supreme peace; on their faces glows the lovely bloom of good fortune.
Through the Guru's teaching they sang of the Lord, put the Lord's garland upon their breast, and kept the Lord's Name at their throat.
He looks on all with one eye, seeing all alike, and recognises the all-pervading Lord (Atam Ram) in all.
Those who sang the praise of the Lord, Har Har, attained the supreme state; those servants are excellent and foremost.
One whose mind loves the Sat Sangat has a tongue steeped in the Lord; in the Sangat the Lord's relish is found.
He has worshipped the Lord, Har Har, and blossomed through the Guru's Shabad; (for him) there is no other, no second.
There is no other: the Lord alone is Amrit; one who has drunk it knows what it is.
Blessed, blessed is the Perfect Guru, (through whom) God is found; held to the Sangat, one recognises the Name.
He serves the Name alone and worships the Name alone; without the Name he has no other.
One whose mind loves the Sat Sangat has a tongue steeped in the Lord; in the Sangat the Lord's relish is found.
O Lord, O God, show mercy: carry us stones across, and lift us out through the Shabad, in your love.
Caught in the mire of attachment, we are sinking down; O Lord God, give (us) your arm to hold.
(The one to whom) God gave his arm gained the highest understanding, and that servant clung to the Guru's feet.
He repeated and worshipped the Name of the Lord, Har Har; on his face and forehead good fortune (awoke).
The Lord has shown grace to servant Nanak, and made the Lord, Har Har, sweet to his mind.
O Lord, O God, show mercy: carry us stones across, and lift us out through the Shabad, in your love. ॥4॥
447.1: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
In their minds they repeat the Naam; the Lord, Har Har, is dear to their minds; in the minds of the Lord's devotees is eager longing.
Those who have died (to self) and live (anew) drink Amrit; through the Guru's teaching, love (for the Lord) has taken hold in their minds.
In the mind is love for the Lord, Har Har, (when) the Guru shows grace; one is liberated while yet alive, and there is peace.
In life and in death they are at ease through the Lord's Name; in their minds and hearts is that Lord, Har Har.
The Lord, Har Har, has come to dwell in their minds; through the Guru's teaching the Lord has become their delight; they drink the relish of the Lord in deep draughts.
In their minds they repeat the Naam; the Lord, Har Har, is dear to their minds; in the minds of the Lord's devotees is eager longing.
In the world no one likes to die; each keeps hiding himself, lest Jam seize him and take him away.
(But) within and without is the one Lord God; this life cannot be kept (hidden from him).
How can the life be kept, when the Lord wants back what is his? The One whose thing it is takes it away.
The manmukhs wander about wailing piteously, trying every medicine and cure.
God, the Master, whose thing it is, takes it; his servants are saved (from the fear of death) by living the Shabad.
In the world no one likes to die; each keeps hiding himself, lest Jam seize him and take him away.
Death is written from the start; through the Guru it is made beautiful; the servants are saved by meditation on the Lord, Har Har.
Through the Lord they gained honour, through the Lord's Name glory; robed (in honour), they go to the Lord's court.
Robed in honour in the Lord's court, made whole through the Lord's Name, they have found peace from the Lord's Name.
The sorrows of both birth and death are wiped away (for them), and they are merged in the Name of the Lord, of Ram.
The Lord's servants and God have blended into one; the Lord's servants and God are alike.
Death is written from the start; through the Guru it is made beautiful; the servants are saved by meditation on the Lord, Har Har.
The world is born and perishes, perishing again and again; clinging (to the Lord) through the Guru, one becomes steady.
The Guru makes the mantra (of the Name) firm (within), and makes one savour the Lord with delight; the Lord lets his Amrit trickle into the mouth.
(One who) has found the relish of the Lord's Amrit is brought back to life from death, and never dies again.
Through the Name of the Lord, Har Har, he has attained the deathless state; he remains merged in the Lord's Name.
For servant Nanak the Name is the support and the prop; without the Name there is no other.
The world is born and perishes, perishing again and again; clinging (to the Lord) through the Guru, one becomes steady. ॥4॥
448.1: Raag Asa, a Chhant, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Great is my Govind, beyond reach, beyond the senses, the Primal, Stainless and Formless One.
His state cannot be told; his greatness is beyond measure; my Govind is unseen and boundless.
Govind is unseen, boundless, beyond the farthest beyond; he alone knows himself.
What can these poor creatures be called, that any could speak of you and describe you?
(O Lord,) one on whom you cast your gracious glance reflects (on you) through the Guru.
Great is my Govind, beyond reach, beyond the senses, the Primal, Stainless and Formless One.
You are the Primal Being, beyond the farthest beyond, the Creator; your far shore cannot be found.
You dwell in every heart, through all without a break, pervading all.
The Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, is within every heart; no one has found his end.
He has no form and no feature; he is unseen, beyond the senses; through the Guru the Unknowable is made known.
(Such a one) lives in bliss always, day and night, and is absorbed in the Name in Sahaj.
You are the Primal Being, beyond the farthest beyond, the Creator; your far shore cannot be found.
You are the True One, the Supreme God, imperishable for ever; O Lord, Har Har, (you are) the treasure of virtues.
The Lord God, Har Har, is One; there is no other; you yourself are the all-pervading, all-knowing Being.
You are the all-knowing Being, you are foremost; no other is as great as you.
Your Word (your Hukam) is everywhere, and you alone are at work in all; what you yourself do, that comes to pass.
The One Lord alone pervades all; through the Guru the Lord's Name is perceived.
You are the True One, the Supreme God, imperishable for ever; O Lord, Har Har, (you are) the treasure of virtues.
O Creator, you yourself are all, and all glory is yours; as it pleases you, so make (us) walk.
As it pleases you yourself, so you make (all) walk; all are held within your Word.
When it pleases you, all merge in the Word; through your Word comes glory.
Through the Guru understanding is gained and self is lost, and one stays absorbed in the Word.
Your Word is beyond the senses; it is found through the Guru; O Nanak, (the one who finds it) merges in the Name.
O Creator, you yourself are all, and all glory is yours; as it pleases you, so make (us) walk. ॥4॥
448.2: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, Ghar 4, Chhants, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
(My) eyes are moist with the Lord's Amrit, and (my) mind is dyed in (his) love.
The Lord put (my) mind to the touchstone, and it (proved) pure gold.
Through the Guru (I) am dyed deep red (with love); my mind and body are drenched (in that colour).
Servant Nanak is steeped in the musk (of the Name); his whole life is blessed, blessed.
The Lord's Bani of love has pierced my mind, like arrows with keen points.
Only one struck by the pang of the Beloved's love knows how it is borne.
He is called liberated while yet alive, who dies (to self) and, so dead, lives.
O Lord, unite servant Nanak with the True Guru, (by whom) the world (-ocean), so hard to cross, is crossed.
We, foolish and ignorant, have come to your refuge; meet (us), O Govind, whose plays are many.
Through the Perfect Guru I have found the Lord; one thing I ask: devotion to the Lord.
My mind and body have blossomed through the Shabad, repeating (the Name of) the Lord of endless waves.
Meeting the Sants, in the Sat Sangat, the Lord is found, O Nanak.
Hear (my) plea, O Lord God, kind to the lowly, O Lord King.
I beg for the shelter of the Lord's Name, that I may take the Lord, Har Har, into my mouth.
To love devotion is the Lord's age-old way; the Lord has kept (his devotees') honour.
Servant Nanak has come to (the Lord's) refuge; through the Name the Lord has carried him across. ॥4॥
449.1: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Through the Guru, searching and searching, (I) have found the Lord, my Friend.
Within the fortress of the body, (now) gold, the Lord, Har Har, is made manifest.
The Lord, Har Har, is a diamond, a jewel, and my mind and body are pierced through (by him).
By great fortune written from the start (I) have found the Lord; Nanak is steeped in (his) relish.
Every day I stand and ask the way (to my Husband), a young bride in the bloom of youth.
O Guru, make (me) remember the Name of the Lord, Har Har, (that I may) walk the Lord's path.
In my mind and body the Name is the support; (it) has burnt away the poison of Haumai.
O Lord, unite servant Nanak with the True Guru; (through him) the Lord, Har Har, Banwali, is met.
O Beloved, come and meet me through the Guru; I have been parted (from you) so long.
My mind and body are deeply forlorn; O Lord, (my) eyes are wet with (tears of love).
O Guru, show me the beloved Lord God, that meeting the Lord (my) mind may be content.
(The Guru) has set me, the fool Nanak, to a task: the Lord's work.
The Guru's frame is steeped in Amrit; he sprinkles Amrit (all around).
Those whose minds love the Guru's Bani drink deep of the Amrit and are fulfilled.
The Guru being pleased, they have found the Lord, and their being pushed about (from birth to birth) is ended.
The Lord's servant has become the Lord, Har Har; Nanak and the Lord are one. ॥4॥
449.2: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The storehouses of the Lord's devotion, which is Amrit, are with the Guru, the True Guru.
The Guru, the True Guru, is the Banker, ever true; to the Sikh he gives the Lord as his stock.
Blessed, blessed is the trader, (and blessed his) trade; the Guru, the Banker, praises him.
Says servant Nanak: they alone have found the Guru on whose foreheads (this) was written from the start.
(O Lord,) you are our true Banker, our Master; the whole world is (your) trader.
All the vessels (bodies) you yourself have fashioned; what lies within (them), O Lord, is yours.
What you put in the vessel, that alone comes out; what can any poor creature do?
On servant Nanak the Lord has bestowed the treasure of the Lord's devotion.
Which of your virtues can we tell, O Master? You are boundless, without limit.
Let (us) praise the Lord's Name day and night; this is (our) hope and support.
We are fools and know nothing at all; how can we find (your) far shore?
Servant Nanak is the Lord's slave, a water-carrier for the Lord's slaves.
Save (us) as it pleases you; we have come to your refuge, O God.
We go astray and spoil (our lives) day and night; O Lord, keep our honour.
We are children; you are (our) Guru and Father: give (us) counsel and make (us) understand.
Servant Nanak is called the Lord's slave; O Lord, keep his honour. ॥4॥
450.1: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those on whose foreheads the Lord wrote (this) from the beginning have met the True Guru.
(Their) darkness of ignorance is cut away, and the Guru's wisdom has been lit (like a lamp) in the heart.
(They) have found the Lord, the precious jewel, which never leaves (them) again.
O servant Nanak, they have worshipped the Naam, and worshipping, have met the Lord.
Those who have not remembered such a Name of the Lord: why did they come into the world?
This human birth is so hard to obtain; without the Name it all goes to waste.
One who has not sown the Lord's Name now, in the sowing season, what will he eat hereafter, when hungry?
For the manmukhs there is birth again; O Nanak, this is what pleases the Lord.
O Lord, you (are the Master of all); everyone is yours; you have created all.
Nothing at all is in anyone's hands; all walk as (you) make them walk.
Those whom you unite (with yourself), O Beloved, they alone meet you, those who are pleasing to your mind, O Lord.
O servant Nanak, (those who) have met the True Guru, (he) carries (them) across through the Lord's Name.
One sings in raags, one with the sounds of instruments, one with the Vedas, in many ways, (yet so) the Lord is not won over.
Those who have deceit and vice within: what is gained by their weeping?
The Lord, the Creator, knows everything, though one put a hand over the head of the disease (to hide it).
O Nanak, those whose hearts are made pure through the Guru win the Lord by devotion to the Lord. ॥4॥
450.2: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those within whom is the love of the Lord, Har Har, are people of refined and wise mind.
Even if outwardly they speak with a slip or a mistake, they are still most pleasing to the Lord.
The Lord's Sants have no other place (but the Lord); the Lord is the honour of those without honour.
O servant Nanak, (for the Sants) the Naam is the court where they plead; the Lord is the strength by which they are strong.
Wherever my True Guru goes and sits, that place becomes beautiful.
The Guru's Sikhs sought out that place, and took its dust and put it on their faces.
The toil of the Guru's Sikhs who meditated on the Lord's Name was accepted.
Those who have worshipped the True Guru, Nanak: the Lord makes (all the world) worship them.
O Lord, in the minds of the Guru's Sikhs is love for you, love for your Name.
They serve (him), knowing (him) for the Perfect True Guru, and (their) hunger and possessiveness depart.
All the hunger of the Guru's Sikhs is gone, and following them, many others eat (the food of the Name).
O servant Nanak, (those who) have sown the merit of the Lord, never again run short of the Lord's merit.
There is rejoicing in the minds of the Guru's Sikhs who have seen my True Guru.
If someone tells them anything of the Lord's Name, he seems sweet to the minds of the Guru's Sikhs.
The Guru's Sikhs with whom my True Guru is pleased are robed in honour in the Lord's court.
Servant Nanak has become (one with) the Lord, Har Har; the Lord, Har Har, has come to dwell in his mind. ॥4॥
451.1: Raag Asa, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Those who have met my Perfect True Guru, he makes the Lord's Name firm within them.
All the craving and hunger of one who meditates on the Lord's Name are taken away.
Jam does not come near any who keep meditating on the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
O Lord, show mercy to servant Nanak, that he may repeat the Lord's Name day after day, and through the Lord's Name carry (others) across.
Those who have meditated on the Naam through the Guru meet no obstacle again.
Those who have won the favour of the True Guru, the mighty one, are honoured by everyone.
Those who have served the beloved True Guru have peace for ever.
Those who have met the True Guru, Nanak, have met the Lord himself.
Those within whom is love (for the Lord) through the Guru: the Lord is their protector.
What slander can anyone speak of those to whom the Lord's Name is dear?
Those whose minds are reconciled with the Lord: all the wicked strike out (at them) in vain.
O servant Nanak, (those who) have meditated on the Naam: the Lord is (their) protector.
Age after age the Lord creates devotees, and has ever kept their honour.
The Lord killed the wicked Harnakhash and carried Prahlad across.
(He) turned his back on the proud and the slanderers, and turned his face to Namdev.
Servant Nanak has served such a Lord, who delivers (him) at the last. ॥4॥
451.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 5, a Chhant, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O my mind, wanderer in strange lands, O beloved, come home.
Meet the Guru, the Lord's own form, O my beloved, and the Lord will dwell in (your) home.
Enjoy delight in (his) love, O my beloved, (if) the Lord shows grace.
Guru Nanak, when pleased, O my beloved, unites (one) with the Lord.
I have not loved (him) and tasted (his) love, O my beloved.
Craving in the mind is not quenched, O my beloved; ever it hopes (for more).
Day by day youth passes, O my beloved, and Jam watches the breaths.
She is the happy bride with the jewel of fortune, O my beloved, who, O Nanak, keeps the Lord in her heart.
My eyes are steeped in (love of) the Husband, O my beloved, as the chatrik (rain-bird longs) for the raindrop.
The mind has grown cool, O my beloved, drinking the drop of the Lord (the Name).
The pain of parting in the body keeps (me) awake, O my beloved; sleep does not come at all.
I have found the Lord, my Friend, O my beloved; O Nanak, (it is) through the attunement the Guru gives.
Chet has come, and spring, O my beloved, a fine season.
Without the Husband, O my beloved, dust blows in (my) courtyard.
With hope in (my) mind, O my beloved, (I am) downcast, and (my) two eyes are fixed (on his path).
Seeing Guru Nanak, O my beloved, I have blossomed, as a mother (at the sight of) her son.
The True Guru has told (me) the stories and discourses of the Lord, O my beloved.
To the Guru I am a sacrifice, O my beloved, who has brought about (my) union with the Lord.
The Lord has made all (my) hopes come true, O my beloved; I have found the fruit the mind longed for.
The Lord is pleased, O my beloved, and servant Nanak is absorbed in the Name.
Without the beloved Lord, I will not play the game of love (with anyone).
How may I find the Guru, holding on to whom I may see the Beloved?
O Lord, dear Giver, unite (me) with the Guru; through the Guru I shall meet (you) face to face.
I have found Guru Nanak, O my beloved; such was the writ on (my) forehead from the beginning. ॥6॥
452.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, Ghar 1, Chhants, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Bliss upon bliss, great bliss (is within me): I have seen that God.
I have tasted, tasted the Lord's sweet essence.
The Lord's sweet essence has come to dwell in the mind; the True Guru is pleased, and Sahaj has come.
The home (of the heart) is peopled, songs of joy are sung, and those five villains have fled.
(We) are cooled and satisfied by the Amrit Bani; the friend, the Sant, has been the go-between (to unite us with God).
Says Nanak, my mind is reconciled with the Lord; I have seen that God with my eyes.
Adorned, adorned are my splendid doors.
My guests, my guests are the beloved Sants.
The beloved Sants have set (my) affairs right; bowing (to them), (we) have taken up (their) service.
He himself is the groom's party, himself the bride's kin, himself the Master (the groom), himself the deity (before whom the wedding is made).
He himself sets his own affair right; he himself gives the support.
Says Nanak, the Husband is seated in (my) home, and the splendid doors are adorned.
The nine treasures, the nine treasures have come into my home.
I have found everything, everything, meditating on the Naam.
I meditate on the Naam of Govind, my companion for ever, who brings Sahaj and love.
(My) anxious reckoning is wiped out, (my) running about is ended; anxiety of mind never besets (me).
Govind resounds (within), unstruck music plays, a wondrous splendour has been made.
Says Nanak, the Husband is with me; so I have found the nine treasures.
Delighted, delighted are my brothers and all my friends.
Meeting the Guru, I have won the hardest, hardest arena.
Meeting the Guru I have won; I have repeated (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har, and the wall of the fortress of doubt has broken.
I have found the treasure, a vast store of wealth; (God) himself stands by me to help me.
He alone is wise, he alone is foremost, whom God has taken as his own.
Says Nanak, when the Master is on (one's) side, then brothers and friends rejoice. ॥4॥
453.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Beyond telling, beyond telling is the story of the Lord; nothing of it can be known.
Men of godly nature and silent sages utter (his praise), resting in Sahaj.
In Sahaj they have uttered the Amrit Bani, and fixed their love on (his) lotus feet.
Repeating (the Name of) the One God, unseen and stainless, they have found the fruit the mind longed for.
Casting off pride, attachment, vice and duality, (their) light has merged in the Light.
Nanak prays: by the Guru's grace, the Lord's love is enjoyed for ever.
The Lord's Sants, the Lord's Sants are my friends, companions and helpers.
By great fortune, by great fortune I have found the Sat Sangat.
One who finds it by great fortune meditates on the Naam, and (his) pains and torments are lifted.
(One who) clings to the Guru's feet: doubt and fear flee, and he has wiped out self-conceit from within himself.
(One whom) God in his grace has united with himself never parts (from him) to go anywhere.
Nanak prays: (I am) your servant, O Lord, for ever in your refuge.
At the Lord's door, at your door, O Lord, your beloved devotees look beautiful.
To them I am a sacrifice, a sacrifice, ever a sacrifice.
Ever a sacrifice, I bow to them, meeting whom God is known.
The Perfect Purakh, the Maker of all, pervades every heart and every place.
(One who) has found the Perfect Guru and meditated on the Naam does not lose (his) life in the gamble.
Nanak prays: (I am) in your refuge; show mercy and save (me).
Endless, endless are your virtues; how many can I sing?
Your feet, the dust of your feet I gain by great fortune.
Bathing in the dust of the Lord's (feet), filth is washed away and the pains of birth and death are lifted.
Within and without, the Supreme God is ever present, ever with (us).
Through Kirtan sorrows are erased and well-being comes; (so) I shall not be cast into a womb again.
Nanak prays: in the Guru's refuge one crosses over; (so) may I be pleasing to my God. ॥4॥
453.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 4, a Chhant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The mind pierced by the Lord's lotus feet finds nothing else sweet.
Joining the company of the Sants, (one) has worshipped (him), and has seen the Lord in every heart.
(One) has seen the Lord in every heart, Amrit has come to dwell (within), and the pains of birth and death have fled.
(One) has sung of the treasure of virtues, has erased all pain, and the knot of Haumai has come undone.
The Beloved, full of Sahaj and love, does not leave (him) to go away; the mind is dyed the fast colour of madder.
O Nanak, (the mind) pierced by the Lord's lotus feet finds nothing else sweet.
As the fish is steeped in water, so (the Sants) are intoxicated with the essence of Ram.
(Those whom) the Perfect Guru has taught are pleasing to (the Lord), the life and liberation (of all).
The Master, the life and liberation (of all), the Knower of hearts, has himself attached (them) to his hem.
The Lord, the precious jewel, has shone forth (in them); he fills all, and does not leave (them) to go anywhere.
God the Master is accomplished, beautiful in form and all-knowing; his gifts never run out.
As the fish is steeped in the company of water, (so,) O Nanak, (the Sants) are intoxicated with the Lord.
As the chatrik begs for the raindrop, (so to them) the Lord is the support of life.
More than wealth, treasure, sons, brothers and friends, more than all, (the Lord) is dear (to them).
Dearer than all is (he,) the Purakh beyond all, whose state cannot be known.
(For them) the Lord is never forgotten with any breath or morsel; through the Guru's Shabad (his) love is enjoyed.
God, the Purakh, is the life of the world; the Sants drink (his) essence, and repeating (his Name), cast off doubt, attachment and pain.
As the chatrik begs for the raindrop, (so,) O Nanak, the Lord is dear (to them).
(Those who) have met their Narayan have their heart's desire fulfilled.
Meeting the valiant Guru, (their) wall of doubt has fallen.
(They) have found the Perfect Guru, as was written before (in their lot) by the Merciful to the meek, the treasure of all.
In the beginning, the middle and the end there is that God alone, the beautiful, the great Gopal.
The dust (of the feet) of the Saadh, which purifies the fallen, (brings) abundant peace, Sahaj and bliss.
O Nanak, (those who) have met the Lord Narayan have their heart's desire fulfilled. ॥4॥
454.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 6, Chhants, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Those on whom God becomes merciful, they alone repeat (the Name of) the Lord, Har Har.
O Nanak, as soon as they meet the Saadh Sangat, their love is drawn to Ram. ॥1॥
454.2: Such is the way of water's love for milk: then, (on the fire,) it lets no heat touch the milk; O mind, such is love for the Lord.
Then the bumblebee is caught in the lotus, absorbed in its fragrance, and does not stir from it for even a moment.
(So) one should not stir from love for the Lord for even a moment; all adornments and all pleasures should be offered up (to it).
Where cries of pain are heard and the path of Jam is spoken of, there, in the Saadh Sangat, one knows no fear.
Sing the praise of Govind, (sing) his virtues: he takes away all sins and sorrows.
Says Nanak: O mind, (sing) the chhants of praise of Govind, the Lord, and keep love for the Lord; O mind, such is love for the Lord.
As the fish (loves) the water and, (without it,) has no peace for even a moment, O mind, love (the Lord) like that.
As is the thirst of the chatrik, which every moment begs for the drop and calls: Rain, O beautiful cloud!
(So) one should love the Lord, give him this mind, and fix one's consciousness wholly on Murari.
One should not be proud, but fall into his refuge and be a sacrifice to the sight of him.
When the Guru is well pleased, the bride sends her true message: Meet me, my Husband, from whom I am parted.
Says Nanak: (sing) the chhants of praise of the infinite Master; one should love the Lord. O mind, love (the Lord) like that.
The chakvi loves the sun and keeps it in her thoughts; great is her longing: when shall the sun be seen?
The koel loves the mango and sings sweetly; O mind, (so) love the Lord.
One should love the Lord and not be proud; all (here) are guests for one night.
Why then have you now taken to pleasures and built up attachment? Naked (all) come and (naked they) go.
One should take the Saadh's refuge and fall at his feet, (and the mind is) steady; then the attachment you have formed will break.
Says Nanak: (sing) the chhants of praise of the merciful, all-pervading Lord; O mind, love the Lord (as the chakvi longs): when shall the sun be seen?
As the deer at night, hearing the sound (of the hunter's bell) with its ears, gives its heart (to it), O mind, love (the Lord) like that.
As a young wife, bound in love to her husband, serves her beloved, (so) one should give this mind to the Beloved.
One should give the mind to the Beloved and enjoy (union with him); (she who does so) delights in all joys and pleasures.
She has found her own Husband, has dyed herself the deep red (of love), and the Friend of ages long past has met (her).
(She says:) When the Guru became the go-between, I saw (him) with my eyes; none is seen like the Husband.
Says Nanak: O mind, (sing) the chhants of praise of the merciful, enchanting Lord; one should grasp the Lord's feet. O mind, love (him) like that. ॥4॥
455.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(The bride) wandered from forest to forest, searching, and grew weary of searching deep.
O Nanak, when the Saadh was met, the Lord was found within the mind. ॥1॥
455.2: He whom countless munis (silent sages) and many ascetics search for,
whom millions of Brahmas and men of knowledge worship, chanting their chants;
with chants, austerities, self-restraint, rites, worship, countless purifications and prostrations,
journeying over the whole earth and bathing at tiraths, (people strive) to meet him, the Immaculate One:
(O Lord,) humans, forests, grasses, beasts and birds, all of them worship you.
O merciful, beloved Gobind! O Nanak, join the Saadh Sangat: (there) liberation is gained.
Millions of Vishnu's incarnations, and Shivas with matted hair,
long for you, O merciful one; in mind and body (they feel) a boundless yearning.
O infinite, inaccessible Gobind, Master, God who fulfils all, Lord!
Gods, Siddhas, ganas and gandharvas meditate on you; yakshas and kinnars (beings of the heavens) utter your praises.
Millions of Indras and countless gods repeat (your Name), O Master, and hail your victory.
O Master of the masterless, merciful one! O Nanak, joining the Saadh Sangat one is saved.
He whom millions of goddesses serve, and Lakshmi in countless ways;
whom the hidden and the manifest worship, (and) wind and water, day and night;
on whom the stars, the moon and the sun meditate, (of whom) earth and sky sing;
on whom all the sources of life and all the tongues ever meditate;
whose Name is chanted by the Simritis and Puranas, the four Vedas and six Shastras:
