he, the purifier of the fallen, Lover of devotion, O Nanak, is met in the true company.
As much as God has made known (to me), so much has (my) tongue spoken.
Those beyond (my) knowing who serve (him) cannot be counted.
The Master is unmanifest, countless, unfathomable; he is within all and outside all.
All are beggars, he alone the Giver; he is not far, but with (all), plain to see.
He has come under the sway of his devotees; those beings who have met (him), how is their glory to be reckoned?
May Nanak receive this gift and this honour: to place (his) head at the feet of the Saadhs. ॥4॥
456.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Make the effort, O fortunate ones: remember the Lord King, Har Har,
by remembering whom, O Nanak, all comforts come, and pain, suffering and wandering doubt depart. ॥1॥
456.2: In repeating the Name of Gobind, one should never be slothful.
Meeting the company of the Saadh, one does not have to go to the city of Jam.
Pain, suffering and fear do not seize (one); remembering the Naam, (one is) ever at peace.
With every breath worship the Lord, Har Har; meditate on that God in the mind and with the mouth.
O kind, merciful one, home of all delight, treasure of virtues: in your mercy, set (me) to your service.
Nanak makes his plea and meditates on (your) feet: in repeating the Name of Gobind, one should never be slothful.
Pure is the Name of the Immaculate One, the purifier of the fallen.
The salve of the Guru's wisdom destroys the darkness of doubt.
With the salve of the Guru's wisdom (one sees that) God, the Immaculate, fills water, land and sky.
One in whose heart (he) dwells for even an instant, his every grief is wiped away.
The Master, of unfathomable wisdom, all-powerful, is the destroyer of the fear of all.
Nanak makes his plea and meditates on (his) feet: pure is the Name of the Immaculate One, the purifier of the fallen.
I have taken your shelter, O Gopal, merciful one, treasure of grace.
My support is your feet; in your refuge is (my) fulfilment.
The feet of the Lord, the Master, the Cause of causes, Har Hare, are the saviour of the fallen;
they carry (beings) across the dreadful world-ocean; remembering the Name, many have crossed.
(You are) at the beginning and at the end; beings without number search for (you). (I) have heard that the company of the Sants is the way of deliverance.
Nanak makes his plea and meditates on (your) feet: I have taken your shelter, O Gopal, merciful one, treasure of grace.
The Lord is the Lover of devotion: he himself has made this his pledged way.
Wherever the Sants worship (him), there he becomes manifest.
God himself has merged (them in himself), and with natural ease has accomplished the tasks of his devotees.
(Singing) the Lord's praise (they know) bliss and great joy, and all sorrows are forgotten.
He whose wondrous light shines in the ten directions, the One alone, is seen there.
Nanak makes his plea and meditates on (his) feet: the Lord is the Lover of devotion: he himself has made this his pledged way. ॥4॥
457.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Lasting is the marriage of the Sants: (their Husband) neither dies nor goes away.
She in whose home the Lord is the Husband enjoys (his union) for ever.
That God is imperishable, unmanifest, ever new and pure.
The Master is not far, he is ever present; he fills the ten directions, for ever and ever.
(He is) the Lord of the breath of life, from whom (the high) state and understanding come; through love for the Beloved, the Beloved grows ever dearer.
Nanak says, and through the Guru's word one comes to know it: lasting is the marriage of the Sants: (their Husband) neither dies nor goes away.
She whose Husband is Ram has great bliss (within).
Happy is that wife, and her glory is full and complete.
Honour, greatness, well-being and the Lord's praise (are hers); that God, the noble one, is with her.
All siddhis and the nine treasures are in that home; nothing is lacking, everything is (there).
Sweet is her speech, the Husband honours her; her marriage is made lasting.
Nanak says, and through the Guru's word one comes to know it: she whose Husband is Ram has great bliss (within).
Come, my friend, let us go to the Sant and give ourselves to (his) service.
I would grind (corn for him) and wash (his) feet; let us give up the self.
Giving up the self, anguish ends; let us make no show of ourselves.
Let us take (his) refuge and accept (his will): whatever he does, in that let us find comfort.
Becoming the handmaid of (his) servants, giving up listlessness, with palms joined let us keep awake day and night.
Nanak says, and through the Guru's word one comes to know it: come, my friend, let us go to the Sant and give ourselves to (his) service.
Those on whose foreheads (good) fortune (is written) are set to (his) service.
Fulfilled is the hope of those who have found the Saadh Sangat.
In the Saadh Sangat, in the Lord's love, they take to the remembrance of Gobind.
Doubt, attachment, vice and duality: all of these they have given up.
Peace, Sahaj and love have come to dwell in (their) minds; in bliss and joy they have sung (his) praises.
Nanak says, and through the Guru's word one comes to know it: those on whose foreheads (good) fortune (is written) are set to (his) service. ॥4॥
457.2: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Jamkaal says nothing to one who repeats the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
O Nanak, mind and body are at peace, and in the end Gopal is met. ॥1॥
457.3: (O Lord,) may I join the company of the Sants; save me.
With palms joined I make my plea: give (me) the Name of the Lord, Har Har.
By your mercy, may I beg for the Lord's Name, fall at (your) feet and give up pride.
May I run nowhere (else), but find (your) refuge; O God, embodiment of compassion, show mercy.
O all-powerful, indescribable, infinite, pure Master, hear this my plea.
With palms joined Nanak begs for (this) gift: put an end to (my) birth and death.
(O God, I am) a wrongdoer, without understanding, without virtue, without a protector, and lowly.
(I am) foolish, hard of heart and of no lineage; the mire of attachment has seized (me).
(On me is) the filth of deeds done in doubt, of ego and of mine-ness; death does not come to (my) mind.
(I) cling to the play of women, the pleasures of Maya and ignorance.
Youth is fading, old age grows; death, standing by, watches (my) days.
Nanak humbly prays: my hope is in you; keep (me), the lowly one, in the refuge of the Saadh.
(I) have wandered through countless births and suffered the great hardships of the life-forms.
(I) have stayed clinging to sweet pleasures and gold.
Carrying countless burdens (of sin), (I) have come wandering, and have run through many foreign lands.
Now (I) have taken the shelter of God, Murari; in the Name of the Lord are all comforts.
O beloved God, the Protector: nothing has been done, nor can be done, by me.
Says Nanak: (O God,) by your grace come peace, Sahaj and bliss, and (one) crosses the world (-ocean).
(God) has saved even those who were (devotees) in name alone; what doubt (then) for (true) devotees?
By whatever means (you can), hear the praise of the Lord, Har Har, with your ears.
O man of understanding, hearing with your ears the Bani (of his praise), you will find the treasure within your mind.
(Those) dyed in the love of the Lord, God, the Maker, sing the virtues of Ram.
If the earth were paper, the forests pens, and the wind the writer,
(even then) the end of the Infinite cannot be found. Nanak has taken the refuge of (his) feet. ॥4॥
458.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Lord, the Master of all beings: (I) have taken his refuge.
(My) life has become fearless, (and) all anxiety has lifted.
(Him I) have known as mother, father, son, friend, well-wisher, beloved and kin.
The Guru brought (me) to meet (him), and he took (me) by the hand and held (me) to his breast; the Sants speak his spotless praise.
Infinite are (his) virtues, countless his glories; (his) worth cannot be told at all.
God is One (and) many, the unseen Master; Nanak has taken his shelter.
When (God) himself became (my) helper, the world (-ocean) became the water of Amrit.
The Name of Ram is the necklace of (my) heart; the days of poison are gone.
Doubt is gone, attachment and vices are destroyed, (and) all coming into births has ceased.
The oceans of fire have become cool, holding on to the hem of the Saadh.
Govind, Gopal, the merciful, the all-powerful: with the Saadh, proclaim the Lord's victory, hail, hail.
O Nanak, meditating on the Name of the Perfect (Lord), the supreme state is gained in the Saadh Sangat.
Wherever I look, there the One alone is with (me), pervading.
He himself dwells in every heart; some rare one has realised (this).
Filling water, land and sky completely, he is contained in the worm and the elephant (alike).
In the beginning, the end and the middle he alone (is); by the Guru's grace (this) is known.
Brahm has spread out (all this), (all) is the play of Brahm; (his) servant has spoken (thus) of Govind, the treasure of virtues.
O Nanak, remember the Master, the Knower of hearts: the One Lord alone pervades (all).
Day and night have come beautiful, remembering the Name of the Lord.
With love for (his) lotus feet, impurities and sins are driven away.
Sorrow, hunger and poverty have fled; (the Guru) has shown the plain path.
Joining the Saadh Sangat, dyed in the Name, (I) have found what the mind longed for.
Seeing the sight of the Lord, the wish is fulfilled, and all the generations of the family are carried across.
Day and night there is bliss, O Nanak, remembering the Lord, Har Hare, night and day. ॥4॥
459.1: Raag Asa, Ghar 7, Chhants, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Good thoughts, the uttering of Gobind's praises, the pure company of the Saadh (be mine);
have mercy, O Lord, that I, Nanak, may not forget the Naam for even a moment. ॥1॥
459.2: In the lovely dew-soaked night the stars glitter;
(then) the Sants, the beloved ones of my Ram, are awake.
The beloved ones of Ram are ever awake, and remember the Naam night and day.
In their hearts is meditation on (God's) lotus feet; (they say:) O God, do not slip from (our) minds for even an instant.
Casting off the mind's pride, attachment and vice, they burn away sins and sorrows.
Nanak prays: the Lord's servants, (his) beloved Sants, stay awake for ever.
My lovely bed has been adorned;
joy has come to my mind on hearing that God is coming.
God, the Master who leads to peace, has met (me); (I am) brimming with eagerness, gladness and delight.
(I) have clung to (his) side, sorrows have fled, and breath, mind and body have all turned green.
Meditating on God, I have gained my heart's wish; the union and the saha (the wedding day) were reckoned auspicious.
Nanak prays: Sridhar (the Lord) has met (me), and every joy and delight has come about.
Gathering together, my friends ask: tell (us) some sign of the Husband.
Filled with the delight of (his) love, I cannot put anything into words.
The Creator's virtues are deep, hidden and boundless; even the Vedas do not find their end.
(His devotees,) meditating on the Master with devotion and love, ever sing the Lord's virtues.
Full of every virtue and of true wisdom, (the soul-bride) is pleasing to her God;
Nanak prays: dyed in (his) colour, she stays merged in love, in Sahaj.
(When his servants) begin to sing the Lord's soothing songs of joy,
(their) friends flourish, and sorrows and enemies run away.
The comforts of Sahaj bloom, and they rejoice in the Lord's Name; God himself has shown (this) mercy.
They have come to the Lord's feet, are ever awake, and have met God, Banwari.
Blessed days have come (to them); in Sahaj they have reached the feet of God, (master of) all treasures.
Nanak prays: in the Master's refuge, the Lord's servants keep (their love) to the end, for ever. ॥4॥
459.3: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Rise and get going, O traveller; why have you lingered?
Your allotted time is up; in what falsehood are you lured?
You are lured by what is false; Maya is a fraud, (yet) you commit countless sins.
The body (is to be) a heap of ashes; Jam has his eye on it; death has conquered the poor creature.
Leaving wealth and youth, you will go; your clothes and your food stay behind.
O Nanak, what one has earned goes along (with one); the record of past deeds cannot be erased.
You are caught like the deer that sees at night (the hunter's) moon-like light;
out of comforts sorrows have come, (yet) you commit sins every day.
You do not give up committing sins; with a halter round the neck, (you) are being led away.
Seeing the city of Harichand, you are cheated; on your bed you have enjoyed only what is false.
Drunk with craving, greed and ego, you are lost in pride.
O Nanak, (such) deer perish through ignorance, and (their) coming and going does not end.
The fly is dead in the sweet; how can it take flight?
The elephant lies fallen in the pit; how can it swim across?
Crossing over has become hard, (for) not for an instant did the Master come to mind.
There is no counting the pains and punishments; (one) has reaped what one did.
What was done in secret has come to light; there is disgrace here and hereafter.
O Nanak, the proud manmukh is plundered for want of the True Guru.
The Lord's servants have come to life, clinging to God's feet;
in the refuge of that Master, (he) has hugged them to his breast.
Strength, understanding, knowledge and meditation on himself (he gave), and himself had them repeat the Naam.
(God) himself became the Saadh Sangat, and himself carried the world across.
The Protector has kept them safe; (their) conduct is ever pure.
O Nanak, the Lord's Sants never go to hell; (they are) in the Lord's refuge. ॥4॥
460.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Be gone, my laziness; (my) plea is before the Lord,
that I may enjoy my own dear Husband; at God's side I am made beautiful.
At the side of the Husband, the Master, (the soul-bride) is beautiful; let us enjoy him day and night.
Calling (him) to mind with every breath, I live; beholding God, let us sing the Lord's praises.
Separation is put to shame; (I) have found (his) sight; (his) glance sprinkles Amrit.
Nanak prays: my wish is fulfilled; he whom I was searching for has met (me).
Flee, O sins: the Creator has come into the home (of the heart).
The fiends (the vices) are burned up, (for) Govind has become manifest.
The beloved Gopal, Gobind, has become manifest; (his praise) is spoken in the Saadh Sangat.
A wonder has been seen: Amrit has come to dwell (within); by the Guru's grace (God) is known.
Peace has come to the mind, the songs of rejoicing ring out; (God's) end cannot be found.
Nanak prays: in peace and Sahaj, God himself has brought about (this) union.
Remembering Narain, (one) does not see hell;
Dharam (Raj) hails (such a one), and (Jam's) messengers flee.
Worshipping the Lord in the Saadh Sangat, (they) have found contentment in dharma, patience and Sahaj.
In his kindness (God) has saved them; they have given up all attachment and possessiveness.
(God) has taken hold of them and hugged them close; the Guru has united (them with him); repeating Govind, they are satisfied.
Nanak prays: by remembering the Master, every hope is fulfilled.
When (one) has grasped the feet of (the Lord of) treasures and siddhis, what worry is left?
The God in whose power everything lies is ours.
Taking (us) by the arm, he has made (us) his own, given (us) the Naam, and, placing his hand on (our) forehead, kept (us) safe.
The world-ocean does not overpower (us): we have tasted the Lord's essence, the Amrit.
In the Saadh Sangat, dyed in the Naam, (we) have won the battle, the great wrestling ground (of the world).
Nanak prays: in the Master's refuge, (one) is not uprooted by Jam again. ॥4॥
461.1: Raag Asa, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
What you have done, day and night, has come (written) upon your forehead.
He from whom you hide (your deeds) is beside you, watching.
The Maker watches from close by; why commit sin?
Let us do good deeds and take the Naam; then one never goes to hell at all.
At all hours remember the Lord's Name: (it) goes along with you.
Says Nanak: worship (God) ever in the Saadh Sangat; the faults you have committed are wiped away.
O foolish, ignorant one, you fill your belly by cheating,
while the Lord, the Giver, goes on giving everything.
The bountiful Master is ever merciful; why forget him from the mind?
Join the Saadh Sangat and worship (him) without hesitation; so all one's generations are carried across.
For Siddhas, seekers, gods, sages and devotees, the Naam is the support.
Nanak prays: let us ever worship God, the One, the Maker (of all).
Let no falseness be practised: God is the one who tests (all).
Those who deal in falsehood and fraud are born into the world (again and again).
They alone have crossed the world-ocean who have meditated on the One,
(and,) giving up lust, anger and the slander of the blameless, have come to God's refuge.
The Master pervades the water, the land and the sky; (he is) lofty, unreachable and boundless.
Nanak prays: (he) is his servants' prop; (his) lotus feet are what they lean on.
See, (this world) is the city of Harichand; nothing (in it) is lasting.
All the pleasures of Maya, as many as there are, do not go along (with anyone).
Ever at your side, the Lord is your companion; let us cherish him day and night.
Apart from the one Lord there is nothing else; let the love of duality be burned away.
Friend, youth, wealth, everything: hold in your mind that the one God is (all of these).
Nanak prays: (God) is found by great good fortune; (those who find him) remain merged in peace and Sahaj. ॥4॥
461.2: Raag Asa, Ghar 8, a Chhant, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Maya (Kamla) is a wall of delusion, Maya is a wall of delusion; its intoxication is sharp and leads the wrong way; (in it) life is passing in vain.
(The world) is a dense, dreadful forest, a dense, dreadful forest; the thief, the mind, is plundering the house (of the heart), and night and day the sun devours (one's life).
The days devour (it) and slip away, passing without God; meet (me), O God, Lord of compassion.
Countless births and deaths have gone by; without the Beloved's company there is no liberation.
I am without lineage, beauty, fragrance or wisdom; without you, who is a mother to me?
With joined palms Nanak has come to your refuge; O beloved Master, O Narhar (the Lord), grant (me) liberation.
A fish without water, a fish without water: parted from it, its mind and body waste away; how can there be life without the beloved?
Facing (the hunter), the deer takes the arrow, facing him takes the arrow; it gives up mind, body and breath, pierced by (the hunter's) soothing sound.
O Beloved, love (for you) has taken hold; meet (me), I am forlorn; cursed is the body that stays an instant without him.
The eyelids do not close; (the mind is) at the Beloved's feet in love; night and day, O God, the mind dwells on (you).
Those dyed in (the love of) Sri Rang (the Lord) and drunk with the Naam have lost all fears and the wandering after duality.
Show kindness and mercy, O merciful, all-pervading (Lord), (that) Nanak may stay immersed in the Lord's love.
The bees hum, the bees hum, drunk on the nectar's taste and fragrance; for love they let themselves be bound in the lotus.
The chatrik's heart thirsts, the chatrik's heart thirsts; its mind hopes for the lovely drop from the cloud; drinking that heady (drop), its fever is gone.
O destroyer of fever, remover of pain, meet (me); in my mind and body the love is very deep.
O beautiful, clever, all-wise Master, with what tongue can I tell (your) virtues?
Take (me) by the arm, give (me) the Naam; as soon as you cast your glance, sins are erased.
Nanak prays: O Lord, purifier of the fallen, beholding your sight there is no anguish.
I dwell on you in my mind, O Master, I dwell on you in my mind, O Master; keep me, who have no one, in your refuge; meet (me), my breath is full of longing.
(My) attention is on (your) beautiful form, on (your) beautiful form; my mind craves the knowledge of Gopal; (you) keep the honour of the servants who beg (at your door).
God gives honour in full and tears pain away; every wish is fulfilled.
(I) am clasped to the Lord's neck, and the days are blessed; now that (I) have met the Husband, the bed is made beautiful.
God cast his glance; Murari has met (me), and all sins are destroyed.
Nanak prays: my hope is fulfilled; Sridhar (the Lord), the treasure of virtues, has met (me). ॥4॥
462.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
A Vaar with saloks; the saloks too were written by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji); (to be sung) to the tune of Tunda Asraja.
Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
To my Guru I am a sacrifice, each day a hundred times over,
who made gods out of men, and took no time in doing it. ॥1॥
463.1: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
Were a hundred moons to rise and a thousand suns to come up,
even with so much light, without the Guru there is pitch darkness. ॥2॥
463.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, those who do not keep the Guru in mind, and are clever in their own eyes,
are like barren sesame plants left forsaken in an empty field.
Left in the field, says Nanak, such plants have a hundred masters;
the poor things flower and bear pods, yet inside their bodies is only ash. ॥3॥
463.3: (God) himself made himself, and himself fashioned his Name (his glory).
Second, he made the creation, and taking his seat (within it), watched its play.
You are the Giver, you yourself the Maker; when pleased you give and bestow grace.
You know all; having given life and its garment (the body), you will take (them) back.
Taking your seat (within the creation), you have watched its play. ॥1॥
463.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
True are your lands (khand), true the universes.
True are your worlds, true the forms (in them).
True are your works, and all your thought.
True is your rule, true your court.
True is your Hukam, true your decree.
True is your grace, true its token.
True are the hundreds of thousands, the millions, who call on you.
All rest on the True One's strength, all on the True One's might.
True is your praise, true your acclaim.
True is your creation, O True King.
O Nanak, those who meditate on the True One are true;
those who die and are born (again) are raw, raw through and through. ॥1॥
463.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
His greatness is great, for his Name is great.
His greatness is great, for his justice is true.
His greatness is great, for his seat is unshakeable.
His greatness is great: he knows what (all) say.
His greatness is great: he grasps the feelings (of every heart).
His greatness is great, for he consults no one before he gives.
His greatness is great, for he is all by himself.
O Nanak, (his) work cannot be told;
all that he has made, the whole creation, is within his will. ॥2॥
463.6: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
This world is the chamber of the True One; the True One dwells in it.
Some, by his Hukam, he takes into himself; some, by that same Hukam, he brings to ruin.
Some, as it pleases him, he draws out (of Maya); others he keeps dwelling in Maya.
Nor can it be told whom he will bring through.
O Nanak, (this) is understood through the Guru by the one in whom he himself makes light. ॥3॥
463.7: O Nanak, having created the beings, (God) has seated Dharam Raj to write (their) accounts.
There (each case) is settled by truth, truth alone; those foul with sin (jajmale) are picked out and set apart.
The false find no place (there); with blackened faces they are sent off to hell.
Those dyed in your Name go (from here) having won; the cheats go having lost.
(God) has seated Dharam Raj to write (their) accounts. ॥2॥
463.8: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Wondrous are the sounds (naad), wondrous the Vedas.
Wondrous are the beings, wondrous their kinds.
Wondrous are the forms, wondrous the colours.
Wondrous are the creatures that roam naked.
Wondrous is the wind, wondrous the water.
Wondrous are the fires that play their strange games.
Wondrous is the earth, wondrous the sources of life (khaani).
Wondrous it is that mortals cling to tastes.
Wondrous is hunger, wondrous the eating.
Wondrous is the trackless waste, wondrous the road.
Wondrous it is (that he is) near, wondrous (that he is) far.
Wondrous it is (that he), ever present, watches over (all).
Seeing (his) marvels, (the mind) is lost in wonder (vismaad).
O Nanak, to understand (it) comes by perfect fortune. ॥1॥
464.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(Your) Kudrat is what is seen, (your) Kudrat what is heard; (your) Kudrat is fear, the essence of peace.
(Your) Kudrat is in the netherworlds and the skies; (your) Kudrat is all that has form.
(Your) Kudrat are the Vedas, the Puranas and the Kateb; (your) Kudrat is all thought.
(Your) Kudrat is eating, drinking and clothing; (your) Kudrat is all love.
(Your) Kudrat is in castes, kinds and colours; (your) Kudrat is in the beings of the world.
(Your) Kudrat are the good deeds, (your) Kudrat the evil; (your) Kudrat is honour and pride.
(Your) Kudrat are wind, water and fire; (your) Kudrat the earth and the dust.
All is your Kudrat; you are its Master (Kadir), the Creator; pure is your glory, (and you yourself are) pure.
O Nanak, (God) watches over (all) within his Hukam, and he alone, himself, pervades (all). ॥2॥
464.2: (Man) himself enjoyed his pleasures; (then the body) became a heap of ashes, and the bhaur (the soul) departed.
The worldly man died (vadda hoa); a chain was put round his neck, and he was driven off.
Hereafter his deeds and his repute are read out; seated, he is made to understand the reckoning of his account.
As the blows fall he finds no place (of shelter); what wailing of his is heard now?
His blind mind has wasted (this human) birth. ॥3॥
464.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
In (God's) fear the wind blows for ever.
In (God's) fear hundreds of thousands of rivers run.
In (God's) fear fire does its forced labour (begaar).
In (God's) fear the earth is pressed down under (its) load.
In (God's) fear Indra (the god of rain) goes about on his head.
In (God's) fear is the door of Dharam Raj.
In (God's) fear is the sun, in (God's) fear the moon;
travelling crores of kos, (their journey) has no end.
In (God's) fear are the Siddhas, the Buddhas, the gods and the Naths.
In (God's) fear the skies are stretched out.
In (God's) fear are warriors, the mighty and the brave.
In (God's) fear boatloads (of beings) come and go.
Upon the heads of all, fear is written as their lot.
O Nanak, only the One, the True, the Formless, is without fear. ॥1॥
464.4: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, the Formless One (alone) is without fear; so many other Rams are (but) dust (before him).
So many are the tales of Kaanh, so many the reflections on the Vedas.
So many beggars dance, and wheeling round and round keep the beat.
The players (bajaari) come into the bazaar and set out their show.
They sing (as) kings and queens, and talk wild nonsense.
(They wear) earrings worth a lakh of takas, necklaces worth a lakh of takas;
(but) the bodies they are put on, O Nanak, those bodies turn to ash.
Wisdom is not found by talk; to tell of it is as hard as iron.
It is gained only when it comes by (his) grace; all other cleverness and command come to nothing. ॥2॥
465.1: If you cast your glance of grace, then by (your) grace the True Guru is found.
This soul roamed through many births; then the True Guru made it hear the Shabad.
None is a giver as great as the True Guru; listen, all you people, every one.
Those who rid themselves of self within have found the True One by meeting the True Guru,
(the Guru) who has made (them) understand the True One, Truth itself. ॥4॥
465.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The gharis are all gopis, the pahars (of day and night) Kaanh, Gopal;
wind, water and fire are the ornaments, the moon and the sun the avatars;
the whole earth is (the play's) goods and wealth, and all the world's entanglements are the things it uses.
O Nanak, (the world,) empty of wisdom, is being robbed; Jamkaal has devoured it. ॥1॥
465.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The disciples play (the instruments), and the gurus dance;
they jig their feet and toss their heads;
the dust flies up and settles in their hair.
The onlookers watch, laugh, and make for home.
For the sake of bread they keep the beat,
and fling themselves upon the ground.
They sing as the gopis, they sing as Kaanh,
they sing as Sita and as Ram the king.
The Fearless, the Formless, whose Name is True,
whose making is all the world:
him those servants serve whom (his) grace has uplifted;
for those whose minds are eager (for him), the night (of life) is dew-soaked and sweet.
Those who have learned this teaching through reflection on the Guru's word,
the Gracious One, in his kindness, carries (them) across.
The oil-press, the spinning wheel, the grindstone, the potter's wheel,
the whirlwinds of the desert, many beyond count,
tops, churning-staves, threshing frames,
birds that wheel without pausing for breath,
creatures set on a spike and spun round:
O Nanak, of those that go round there is no count and no end.
Binding (beings) in bonds, he spins them round;
everyone dances by the deeds that have fallen to his lot.
Those who laugh as they dance depart in tears.
(Dancing,) they neither take flight (to a higher state) nor become Siddhas.
Dancing and leaping are (but) the mind's fancy;
O Nanak, those whose minds hold (God's) fear hold (his) love in their minds. ॥2॥
465.4: Your Name is Nirankar (the Formless); taking (your) Name, one does not go to hell.
Soul and body, all is his; give (of what he gives) and then eat; speak of (the giving), and (its merit) is lost.
If you want your own good, do good deeds and (still) be called lowly.
Even if a mighty man would cast it off, old age comes on, putting on its garb.
No one stays (here) when the measure (paai) of life is full. ॥5॥
465.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
With the Muslims it is the praise of the Shariat (the Islamic law); reading it again and again, they reflect:
(God's) servants are those who enter its bond (bandi) to behold (his) vision.
The Hindus praise the Praiseworthy One, through the darshans (their schools of scripture), as beautiful and boundless;
they bathe at the tiraths, make offerings (to images) and worship (them), with the scent of aloe-wood and perfumes.
The yogis, all of them, meditate on the Creator in Sunn, naming him Alakh (the Unseen);
(yet in their meditation) the One of subtle form, whose Name is Niranjan, takes the shape of a body.
In the minds of the charitable, contentment springs up at the thought of giving;
(but) giving and giving, they ask a thousandfold (in return), and the world sings their praise.
Thieves, adulterers and liars, the wicked and the sinful:
some use up what they had and go from here; they too have some task (given them).
In water and on land are beings, in the realms and the worlds, form upon form:
what they say, you alone know; they too are in your care.
O Nanak, the devotees hunger to praise (you); the True Name is (their) support.
Ever in bliss they live, day and night, (as) dust beneath the feet of the virtuous. ॥1॥
466.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The clay of a Muslim('s grave) may come to lie in the potter's lump;
shaping it, (he) makes pots and bricks of it, and as it burns (in the kiln) it cries out.
The poor thing weeps as it burns and burns, and embers keep dropping from it.
O Nanak, the Creator who made the creation, he alone knows (its secret). ॥2॥
466.2: Without the True Guru no one has found (God); without the True Guru no one has found (him).
(God) has placed himself within the True Guru, and has made this plain and proclaimed it.
One who has rid himself of attachment within is free for ever, when the True Guru is met.
Best of all is this understanding: one who has fixed his mind on the True One
has found the Giver, the Life of the world. ॥6॥
466.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
In Haumai (ego) one comes (into the world), in Haumai one goes.
In Haumai one is born, in Haumai one dies.
In Haumai one gives, in Haumai one takes.
In Haumai one earns, in Haumai one loses.
In Haumai one is (now) truthful, (now) false.
In Haumai one weighs sin and merit.
In Haumai one falls (now) into hell, (now) into heaven.
In Haumai one laughs, in Haumai one weeps.
In Haumai one is soiled (with sin), in Haumai one washes (it off).
In Haumai, (proud of) caste and kind, one loses (oneself).
In Haumai one is (now) a fool, in Haumai (now) wise,
(but) does not grasp what liberation and release are.
In Haumai one (chases) Maya, in Haumai (lives under) its shadow.
Acting in Haumai again and again, beings are born (again and again).
When one understands Haumai, then the (Lord's) door comes into sight.
Without this knowledge, one only quarrels, talking and talking.
O Nanak, this record is written by the Hukam:
as (beings) look (upon others), so their own form becomes. ॥1॥
466.4: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
Such is the nature of Haumai: (beings) do the deeds of Haumai.
These are the bonds of Haumai: (beings) fall into the life-forms again and again.
Where does Haumai spring from? By what discipline does it go?
Haumai is by this very Hukam: driven by their past deeds, (beings) wander.
Haumai is a long, lingering disease, but it has a cure as well.
If (God) shows his grace, then (beings) live by the Guru's Shabad.
Nanak says: hear, O people; by this discipline the pains (of Haumai) go. ॥2॥
466.5: Service has been done by the contented, who have meditated on none but the True One.
They have not set foot on (the path of) evil; doing good deeds, they have lived by dharma.
They have broken the world's bonds, and have taken little of grain and water.
(O Lord,) you are the great Giver of gifts; you give each day, and (your giving) ever grows.
By praising (you), they have found (you), the Great One. ॥7॥
467.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Of men, trees, tiraths, riverbanks, clouds and fields,
of islands, worlds, spheres, continents and universes,
of the sources of life, egg-born, womb-born, earth-born and sweat-born,
of lakes, mountains and creatures, he knows the measure, O Nanak.
O Nanak, having brought forth the beings, (God) takes care of them all.
The Creator who made the creation must also see to its care.
That Creator who brought forth the world takes thought for it.
To him I bow, hail to him; his court stands for ever unbroken.
O Nanak, without the True Name, what is the frontal mark, what the sacred thread? ॥1॥
467.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Lakhs of good deeds and kindnesses, lakhs of acts of merit approved (by the world),
lakhs of austerities at tiraths, yoga in the stillness of Sahaj in the wilds,
lakhs of feats of valour, the breath of life let go on the field of battle,
lakhs of ways of fixing the attention, lakhs of (discourses on) knowledge and of meditations, and the Puranas read and recited:
(before) the Creator who made the creation and wrote down (all) coming and going,
O Nanak, (all these) clevernesses are worthless; his grace is the true mark (of acceptance). ॥2॥
467.3: (O Lord,) you alone are the True Master, who have made Truth, nothing but Truth, prevail.
Whoever you give it to receives Truth; then such ones live the Truth.
Those in whose hearts (the Guru) has set Truth to dwell have found Truth through meeting the True Guru.
Fools do not know the Truth; the manmukhs have wasted their lives.
Why did (such a one) come into the world? ॥8॥
467.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
One may read and read till carts are loaded, read and read till caravans are filled (with books);
read and read till a boat is laden, read and read till pits are packed full;
one may read for as many years as there are, year upon year, read for as many months as there are;
one may read for as long as life lasts, read for as many breaths as there are:
(Even so,) O Nanak, in (God's) reckoning one thing alone counts; all else is the idle babble of Haumai. ॥1॥
467.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
However much one writes and reads, so much does one fret and burn (within).
However many tiraths one tours, so much the more one prattles.
(One) has put on many guises and given the body pain:
endure, O soul, what you have done yourself.
(One who) has eaten no grain has lost the taste (of life);
he has suffered much pain, for something other (than the Name) has pleased him.
(One) wears no clothes, and is in torment day and night.
(One) has gone astray in silence: asleep, how can he wake without the Guru?
(One) goes barefoot, and reaps what he has done.
(One) has eaten what is foul and put ash on his head:
the blind fool has lost his honour.
Without the Name, nothing is accepted.
(One) lives in the wilds, at tombs and cremation grounds:
the blind man does not know (the way), and afterwards repents.
One who meets the True Guru finds peace,
and enshrines the Lord's Name in the mind.
O Nanak, one on whom (God) casts his glance of grace finds (the Guru);
free from hope and anxiety, he burns away Haumai through the Shabad. ॥2॥
468.1: (O Lord,) your devotees are dear to your mind; singing (your) praises, they look beautiful at (your) door.
O Nanak, those without (his) grace find no shelter at the door; they wander about.
Some do not understand their own origin, and, having nothing, make much of themselves.
I am a humble minstrel (dhadhi) of low caste; others call themselves high-born.
(The company of) those who meditate on you is what I ask for. ॥9॥
468.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The king is falsehood, the subjects are falsehood, all the world is falsehood.
Pavilions are falsehood, palaces are falsehood, and he who sits in them is falsehood.
Gold is falsehood, silver is falsehood, and he who wears them is falsehood.
The body is falsehood, clothes are falsehood, and beauty beyond measure is falsehood.
Husband is falsehood, wife is falsehood; worn out (in it), they come to ruin.
The false one's love is fixed in falsehood, and he has forgotten the Creator.
With whom should one make friends? The whole world is passing away.
Falsehood is sweet, falsehood is honey; falsehood drowns the whole boatload (of beings).
Nanak humbly prays: without you, (all) is falsehood, nothing but falsehood. ॥1॥
468.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Truth is known only when the True One is in the heart;
(then) the filth of falsehood comes off, and (one) washes the body clean.
Truth is known only when (one) bears love for the True One;
hearing the Name, the mind blossoms with joy, and then one finds the door of liberation.
Truth is known only when the soul knows the (true) way of life:
making ready the earth of the body, it puts into it the Creator's seed (the Name).
Truth is known only when (one) takes true teaching (from the Guru),
knows how to show compassion to living beings, and gives something in charity and good works.
Truth is known only when (one) dwells at the tirath of the soul within,
and, having asked the True Guru, stays seated (there) and makes his home (there).
Truth is the cure for all (ills); it washes sins away and drives them out.
Nanak humbly prays before those who have Truth in their lap. ॥2॥
468.4: For me the gift (to ask for) is the dust from beneath (the Sants') feet; if it is obtained, let it be put to the forehead.
Let false greed be given up, and, single-minded, let the Unseen One be meditated on.
Such fruit is reaped as is the work one does.
If it is so written from the start, then the dust of such ones is obtained.
(Leaning on one's) small understanding, service is lost. ॥10॥
468.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
A famine of Truth has come, falsehood holds sway; in the blackness of Kalyug, (people have become) ghouls.
Those who sowed the seed (of the Name) have gone with honour; how now can split grain sprout?
Seed sprouts if it is whole, and the season too is the best of seasons.
O Nanak, without the mordant, raw cloth does not take the (fast) colour.
In the fear (of God) let (the mind) be set on the khumb, and let effort be the mordant for the cloth (of the body).
O Nanak, if (the mind) is dyed in devotion, not a trace of falsehood (remains). ॥1॥
468.6: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Greed and sin are the two, king and minister (mahta), and falsehood has become the chief (sikdar).
Lust is the deputy (naib), summoned and consulted; he sits with them, deliberating again and again.
The subjects, blind and without knowledge, stuff the fire (of the rulers' craving) with carrion (bribes).
Those (called) wise dance, play instruments, put on guises and adorn themselves.
They shout aloud, sing of battles, and expound the tales of warriors.
Foolish pandits love to amass (wealth) by cunning and argument.
The pious do pious deeds and waste them, asking (in return) for the door of liberation.
(Some) call themselves celibates but do not know the way; they leave hearth and home and sit (apart).
Everyone is perfect in his own eyes; no one calls himself lacking.
O Nanak, only when the weight of honour (from God) is put in the other pan does (one) prove truly weighed. ॥2॥
469.1: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
What is ordained, O Nanak, shall sound forth (come to light); the True One himself watches over (all).
All have made their leaps (and tried their strength), but what the Creator does, that comes to pass.
Hereafter there is no caste and no force; hereafter the beings (one meets) are new (strangers).
Those few whose honour counts in the reckoning, they alone are good. ॥3॥
469.2: Those on whom you cast your grace from the very first have then meditated on the Master.
It is not in these creatures' power to do anything; you have brought forth a world of many kinds.
Some you unite (with yourself); others you have led astray from yourself.
By the Guru's grace you are known (by the one) to whom you have made yourself understood,
and (that one) has merged, in Sahaj, in the True One. ॥11॥
469.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Sorrow has become the remedy and comfort the disease, for when there is comfort, then (your remembrance) is not there.
You are the Creator, the Doer (of all); I am nothing; when I would do (anything) myself, it does not come about. ॥1॥
469.4: I am a sacrifice to you, who dwell within your creation;
469.5: Your light is in the creation, and in every light you are known; undivided and whole, you fill all things.
You are the True Master, and lovely is your praise; whoever has offered it has crossed over.
Says Nanak, (all these are) the Creator's doings: whatever is to be done, he is doing. ॥2॥
469.6: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
The way of the yogi is knowledge; the way of the Brahmins is the Veda;
the way of the Khatri is valour; the way of the Shudra is the service of others;
the way of all is (the remembrance of) the One; if anyone knows this secret,
Nanak is his servant; he himself is (the image of) Niranjan, the Lord. ॥3॥
469.7: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
The one Krishna (the Lord) is the soul of all the gods, and the soul too of the gods of the gods;
(in all) is the soul of Vasudev (the Lord); if anyone knows this secret,
Nanak is his servant; he himself is (the image of) Niranjan, the Lord. ॥4॥
469.8: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Water stays held only within a pitcher, (yet) without water no pitcher is made;
(so) the mind stays steady only when held by wisdom, (yet) without the Guru there is no wisdom. ॥5॥
469.9: If the learned one is a sinner, the unlettered one who is good is not punished.
As are the deeds one labours at, so is the name one comes to be known by.
Let no such game be played as would make one lose on reaching the Lord's court.
Of the learned and the unlettered alike, the case is weighed hereafter;
whoever goes headstrong, by his own will, is punished hereafter. ॥12॥
470.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, the body that is the meru (the crown of all bodies, the human one) has one chariot and one charioteer;
age after age they are changed again; the wise understand this.
In Satjug the chariot is of contentment, and dharma the charioteer in front;
in Treta the chariot is of continence, and might the charioteer in front;
in Duapar the chariot is of austerity, and sat (upright conduct) the charioteer in front;
in Kalyug the chariot is of fire, and falsehood the charioteer in front. ॥1॥
470.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The Sama (Veda) calls the Master Setambar (the white-robed), who dwells in truth; (in its age, people) abide in truth;
among the gods, the Name of Ram is the sun;
by taking the Name, sins depart;
In the Yajur (Veda), Chandravali was beguiled by force, and (the Master's name) became Kaanh Krishna, the Yadav;
he brought the Parjat (tree) for the gopi, and made merry in Brindaban.
In Kalyug the Atharva Veda came (to the fore), and (the Master's) name became Khuda and Allah;
taking blue cloth, they wore garments (of it), and the Turks and Pathans held sway.
All four Vedas came to be (held) true;
those who read and ponder them find four (different) teachings (in them).
One who, worshipping with loving devotion, calls himself lowly,
470.3: I am a sacrifice to the True Guru, meeting whom (I have) kept the Master in mind;
who, giving his teaching, has given (me) the collyrium of wisdom, by which with these eyes (I) have seen the world (as it is).
Those traders who left the Master and clung to another have drowned.
The True Guru is the ship; rare is the one who has understood (this);
(him the Guru) in his grace has carried across. ॥13॥
470.4: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The simmal tree is straight, very tall and very stout;
(the birds) that come to it in hope: why do they go away disappointed?
(Because) its fruits are insipid, its flowers tasteless, and its leaves of no use.
O Nanak, sweetness and lowliness are the very core of virtues and good deeds.
Everyone bows for his own sake; no one bows for another's.
Put on the scales and weighed, the (pan) that sinks is the heavier.
The sinner who slays deer bows double;
(but) what comes of bowing the head, when (people) go on with impure hearts? ॥1॥
470.5: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(The pandit) reads the books, says the sandhya prayers, and disputes;
he worships stone (idols), and sits in trance like a heron;
lies are on his lips, (decked out) like fine ornaments;
three times a day he ponders the three-footed (Gayatri);
a rosary round his neck, a tilak on his brow;
two dhotis, and a cloth over his head.
If he knew the work of (worshipping) God,
(he would see that) all these rites are surely hollow.
Says Nanak, one should meditate (on God) with firm faith,
(but) without the True Guru one does not find the way. ॥2॥
470.6: Leaving the lovely garment (of the body) and its beauty in the world, one has to go;
the bad and the good one has done, one must oneself reap.
(One who) gave orders as his mind pleased must go hereafter by a narrow road;
stripped bare, he is driven to hell, and then he looks dreadful indeed.
Having done wrong, he must repent. ॥14॥
471.1: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Compassion the cotton, contentment the thread, continence the knots and upright conduct the twist:
such is the soul's sacred thread; O pandit, if you have it, put it on (me).
It does not break, no dirt clings to it, it is not burned, nor is it lost.
Blessed, O Nanak, are the people who go (on their way) wearing it round their necks.
(This thread) you had brought for four cowries and, seated in the chauka, put it on (your patron);
you whispered instruction in (his) ear, and the Brahmin became (his) guru.
He died, it fell away, and he went without a thread. ॥1॥
471.2: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(One commits) countless thefts, countless adulteries, countless lies and countless abuses;
countless frauds and breaches of trust, kept secret within, night and day.
From cotton the thread is spun; the Brahmin comes and twists it;
a goat is killed, cooked and eaten, and everyone says: (the thread) is on.
When it grows old it is cast aside, and then another is put on.
O Nanak, were there strength in the thread, the thread would not break. ॥2॥
471.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
By believing in the Name, honour springs up; praise (of God) is the true thread;
(with it, honour) is gained in the Lord's court; this pure thread will not break. ॥3॥
471.4: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
There is no thread on the senses, no thread (to hold him back) from women;
(so) morning after morning his beard is spat upon.
No thread on the feet, no thread on the hands;
no thread on the tongue, no thread on the eyes.
Without a thread himself he wanders about,
yet twisting threads, he puts them on others.
He takes a fee and performs marriages,
and, taking out his almanac, shows (people) the way.
Hear and see, O people, this wonder:
blind in mind, and his name is Wise. ॥4॥
471.5: When the Master grows merciful and shows grace, he will have (one) do that very work (which pleases him).
That servant alone serves whom (the Master) makes obey his Hukam.
By obeying the Hukam (he) is approved, and then he will reach the Master's mansion.
Doing what pleases the Master, he will gain the fruit his mind longed for;
then he will go to the Lord's court robed in honour. ॥15॥
471.6: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
You levy a tax on the cow and the Brahmin; by the cow-dung (you plaster with) no one crosses over.
Dhoti, tilak and rosary (you wear), (yet) you eat the grain of the mlechhas.
Indoors you worship, (outside) you read the Kateb; your way of life, brother, is the Turks'.
taking the Naam, you will cross over. ॥1॥
471.7: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Those who devour men say the namaz;
those who ply the knife have the sacred thread at their necks.
In their homes the Brahmins blow the conch;
they too relish the same flavours.
False is the capital, false the trade;
by speaking lies they get their food.
Modesty and dharma dwell far away (from them);
O Nanak, falsehood fills every place.
A tilak on the forehead, an ochre dhoti round the waist,
(and) a knife in the hand: (they are) butchers of the world.
Wearing blue clothes, they find favour (with the rulers);
taking their bread from the mlechhas, they worship the Puranas.
Their food is a goat slaughtered with the words of a foreign tongue,
(yet they say:) no one is to step onto our chauka.
The chauka is laid out and a line drawn (around it);
and the false ones come and sit upon it.
(They say:) take care, lest it be defiled, lest it be defiled;
this food of ours will be spoiled.
With defiled bodies they do wicked deeds,
and with soiled minds they rinse their mouths.
Says Nanak, let the True One be meditated on;
if there is purity, then the True One is found. ॥2॥
472.1: (God) holds everyone in his mind, and, watching (them), moves them along under his eye.
He himself bestows greatness, and he himself has (beings) do their deeds.
Greater than the great is he, and vast his earth; one by one he sets each to his task.
If he turns his look against them, he makes sultans (worth no more than) grass;
they beg at the door, and no one puts alms (in their bowl). ॥16॥
472.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If a thief robs a house, and, having robbed it, gives (the goods) for his forebears,
then in the world beyond the goods are recognised, and (so) he makes thieves of his forebears.
The hands of the go-between (the Brahmin) are cut off: such is the justice (God) does.
O Nanak, in the world beyond one receives only what one earns, toils for and gives (with one's own hands). ॥1॥
472.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
As a woman's monthly course comes to her time after time,
(so) in the mouth of the false dwells the defilement (of falsehood), and day after day he comes to grief.
They are not called pure who (merely) wash the body and sit down (as pure);
O Nanak, they alone are pure in whose mind he (God) has come to dwell. ॥2॥
472.4: (Those who have) saddled horses swift as the wind, and harems decked out in every colour,
(who) have set up houses, pavilions and mansions and sit (in them), having spread out a display,
(who) take the pleasures their minds desire, but do not know the Lord: they lose (the game of life).
Giving orders, they ate (their fill), and gazing at their palaces forgot death;
old age came upon them, undone by their youth. ॥17॥
472.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
If Sutak is to be believed in, then Sutak is everywhere:
in cow-dung and in wood, too, the worm comes to life;
of all the grains of corn there are, not one is without life;
first of all, water itself is a living thing, by which every being is kept green (alive).
How then can Sutak be kept away? Sutak falls in the very kitchen.
O Nanak, Sutak is not removed in this way; (divine) knowledge washes it off. ॥1॥
472.6: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
The Sutak of the mind is greed; the Sutak of the tongue is falsehood;
the Sutak of the eyes is gazing on the beauty of another's wife and on another's wealth;
the Sutak of the ears is that (people) backbite and it falls into the ears.
O Nanak, (such) men, (though they look as white) as swans, go bound to the city of Jam. ॥2॥
472.7: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
All Sutak is doubt (superstition); it clings to those who have gone after another (than God).
Birth and death are (God's) Hukam; by his will (a being) comes and goes.
Eating and drinking are pure: (God) has gathered sustenance and given it (to all).
O Nanak, those who have understood (this) through the Guru are touched by no Sutak. ॥3॥
473.1: Let us praise the True Guru as great, in whom are great excellences.
When the Husband Lord brought (us) together (with the Guru), then (those excellences) came into sight;
when it pleased him, (he) set them to dwell in the mind.
By his command, laying his hand on (our) forehead, he struck the evils out from within.
With the Husband Lord pleased, the nine treasures were found. ॥18॥
473.2: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
First (the Brahmin) makes himself pure, and comes and sits in the pure (chauka);
before him, the pure one, is set (food) that no one has gone near to defile.
Pure, he eats, and begins to chant a salok;
(yet the food) is thrown into a foul place (the belly): on whom does this blame fall?
Grain is a god, water is a god, fire is a god, salt (is a god);
the fifth, ghee, was added, and then (the food) became clean and holy.
(Then this) body (of the gods) met with the sinner, and was spat upon.
The mouth with which (people) do not utter the Naam, and without the Name eat dainties:
O Nanak, know it in the same way: on that mouth spittle falls. ॥1॥
473.3: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Of woman we are born, within woman we are formed, to woman we are betrothed and wed;
through woman friendships are made, through woman the way (of the world) goes on;
if a woman dies, (another) woman is sought; through woman the bonds (of kinship) are tied.
Why should she be called bad, of whom kings are born?
Of woman, woman herself is born; without woman there is no one.
O Nanak, the True One alone stands outside woman (unborn of her).
The mouth with which (God) is ever praised glows with the beauty of good fortune;
O Nanak, those faces are radiant in that True Court. ॥2॥
473.4: Everyone claims (things) as his own; the one who does not is to be sought out and singled out.
For what each has done, each must himself settle the account.
Since we are not to stay in this world, why wear ourselves out in pride?
Call no one bad: having read the letters, this is what is to be understood;
do not quarrel with a fool. ॥19॥
473.5: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
O Nanak, by speaking harshly, body and mind grow harsh.
The harsh one is known as harsh, and harsh is the harsh one's repute;
the harsh one is cast out of the Lord's court, and spittle falls on the harsh one's face;
the harsh one is called a fool, and is punished with (a beating of) shoes. ॥1॥
473.6: By the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
Those who are false within, keep up an honour outside and make a show in the world:
though they bathe at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage, their filth does not come off.
Those with silk within and rags without are the good ones in the world;
their love is set on God, and they dwell on the thought of seeing him.
In (his) love they laugh, in love they weep, and they fall silent too;
they care for no one but the True Master.
On the road (of life) they ask at his door for provisions, and eat when he gives.
There is one court and one pen, and there we and you (all) are to meet;
at that door he takes the account, and, O Nanak, (the false) are crushed as seeds are crushed for oil. ॥2॥
474.1: You yourself made the creation, and you yourself have set your power (in it).
Setting out the pieces, raw and ripe, you watch what you have made.
Whoever has come will depart; each one (goes) when his turn has come.
Why put out of mind the Master to whom our soul and breath belong?
With our own hands, by ourselves, let us put our own task in order. ॥20॥
474.2: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
What kind of love is this, that goes and attaches itself to another?
O Nanak, he is called a lover who stays ever absorbed (in the Beloved).
One who takes it as good when good comes, and turns sour when ill comes:
such a one is not called a lover; he deals by keeping accounts. ॥1॥
474.3: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
One who both bows in salute and answers back (to the Master) has gone astray from the very start.
O Nanak, both are false; neither is accepted. ॥2॥
474.4: The Master by serving whom peace is found: let us keep him ever in mind.
Since what we have done (comes back) to us, why labour at what is evil?
Let us do no evil at all, and look far ahead.
Let us cast the dice in such a way that we do not lose (the game) with the Master;
let us labour at something that brings profit. ॥21॥
474.5: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
(If) a servant is at his service, and with it is proud and quarrelsome,
(and) talks a great deal, he does not win the Master's pleasure.
If he gives up his self and serves, then he gains some honour;
O Nanak, he meets the one he serves; (so) engaged, he is accepted. ॥1॥
474.6: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
What is in the heart is what sprouts; what the mouth says is (mere) wind.
One sows poison and asks for Amrit: see what justice this is. ॥2॥
474.7: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
Friendship with the ignorant never turns out well;
as he understands, so he behaves; let anyone weigh it and see.
One thing goes into another only when what was there is set aside.
With the Master no command prevails; it is prayer, offered (to him), that befits.
Practising falsehood, falsehood alone comes of it; O Nanak, through (God's) praise (the mind) blossoms. ॥3॥
474.8: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
Friendship with the ignorant, and love for one far greater (than oneself),
are like a line drawn in water, which leaves neither place nor trace. ॥4॥
474.9: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
If one who is ignorant takes up a task, he cannot bring it to a good end;
even if he does one thing or so well, he spoils the next all the same. ॥5॥
474.10: A servant is (truly) at service if he walks as the Master wishes;
he receives great honour, and draws double wages besides.
(If) he sets himself up as the Master's equal, he then falls into disgrace;
he loses the wages he had, and is struck with shoes on the face.
He whose gifts we eat: to him let us give praise.
O Nanak, with the Master no command prevails; prayer prevails. ॥22॥
474.11: Salok, by the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
What kind of gift is it that one gets of oneself (by one's own effort)?
O Nanak, that is grace (karamat) which comes when the Master is pleased. ॥1॥
475.1: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
What kind of service is this, that does not take away the fear of the Master?
O Nanak, the one to be called a servant is he who merges into the Master. ॥2॥
475.2: O Nanak, no end is seen to the Lord's near and far shores.
He himself brings about the making, and then he himself brings about the destroying.
Round the necks of some are chains; many ride on horses.
He himself causes and he himself does; to whom am I to complain?
O Nanak, he who made the creation: it is he again who must care for it. ॥23॥
475.3: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji).
(God) himself fashioned the vessels (of the body), and he himself fills them.
Some hold milk, while others stay up on the hearth;
some lie down and sleep on quilts, while others stay standing over them (in attendance).
He sets right those, O Nanak, on whom he looks with grace. ॥1॥
475.4: By the Second Guru (Guru Angad Dev Ji).
He himself fashions, he himself makes, and he himself keeps, too, what he has brought forth;
creating beings within it, he watches them, setting up and pulling down.
To whom can we speak, O Nanak? He himself is all in all. ॥2॥
475.5: Of the greatness of the Great One, nothing at all can be said.
He is the Creator, the Master of creation, the Bountiful (Karim); he carries their sustenance to all beings.
(All beings) do the work that he himself has allotted (to them) from the very start.
O Nanak, apart from the One there is no other place;
he does whatever is his will.
475.6: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, the hymns of the Bhagats.
Kabir Ji, Namdev Ji, Ravidas Ji.
Raag Asa, the hymn of Sri Kabir Ji.
Falling at the Guru's feet, I pray and ask: for what has the soul been placed (in the body)?
For what purpose is the world born and destroyed? Tell me, and make me understand.
O divine Guru, be kind: set me on the path by which the bonds of fear are broken,
and the soul is freed at the root from the pains and pleasures of birth and death that its own deeds have brought.
(The soul) does not tear apart the nooses and bonds of Maya, and (its) mind takes no shelter in Sunn;
(it) has not recognised its own true state, free of desire; in this way (its) hardness is not ended.
(The world) that nowhere arises (apart from God), (the mind) takes to have arisen, for it cannot tell what is from what is not.
When the mind's thinking of rising and setting (birth and death) was destroyed, then it was absorbed for ever in Sahaj, its attention fixed (on God).
As, when the pot of water breaks, the reflection merges into its original (the thing it mirrored),
says Kabir: so has the delusion of the rope (taken for a snake) fled; then the mind is absorbed in Sunn. ॥4॥
476.1: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
(Those who) wear dhotis three and a half yards long and put on sacred threads of triple strands,
who have rosaries round their necks and gleaming lotas (water pots) in their hands,
cannot be called Sants of the Lord: they are the thugs of Banaras.
Such Sants do not please me,
who swallow the tree along with its branches.
(They) scour their pots before setting them (on the fire), and wash the firewood before they burn it;
they dig up the earth to make two hearths, (yet) they eat up men whole.
Those sinners go about ever doing wrong, and with their mouths call themselves Apras (those who touch no one).
For ever and ever they go about in pride, and drown their whole families (too).
To whatever (God) has set anyone, to that he is set, and he does deeds to match.
Says Kabir: one whom the True Guru meets does not come into birth again. ॥4॥
476.2: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The Father has given me comfort;
(my) bed is restful, and (he) has put Amrit in (my) mouth.
Why should I let that Father slip from my mind?
Going on (to the world beyond), I shall not lose the game (of life).
My mother (Maya) is dead, and I am at ease indeed;
I do not wear the padded coat (of the body), and the cold does not touch me.
I am a sacrifice to that Father who has given me (a new) birth,
(and) has ended my company with the five (passions).
I have slain the five and put them under my feet;
my mind and body are soaked in Simran of the Lord.
My Father is the great Gosain;
how shall I go to that Father?
When the True Guru met (me), he showed (me) the way,
(and) the Father of the world became dear to my mind.
(O God,) I am your son, and you are my Father;
the two of us have one dwelling place.
Says Kabir: (your) servant has understood the One alone;
by the Guru's grace I have come to see everything. ॥4॥
476.3: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
(They) fill one vessel with cooked fowl, and fill another vessel with water (wine);
all around sit the five yogis, and in their midst is the noseless queen.
The drum of the noseless one (Maya) beats on, loud and resounding;
(O Maya,) only some rare one of discernment has cut you down.
The noseless one dwells within all; having struck all down, she keeps looking about (for more).
(She says:) I am sister and niece to all; to the one who weds me, I am a maidservant.
My husband is truly discerning; he alone is called a Sant.
He stands firm over my head; no one else comes near me.
(The Sants) have cut off her nose, cut off her ears, and hacking her to pieces, have cast her out.
Says Kabir: she is the enemy of the Sants, and the darling of the three worlds. ॥4॥
476.4: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Yogis, celibates, ascetics, sannyasis, those who roam to many places of pilgrimage,
those who have their hair plucked out, those girdled with munj grass, the silent ones, those with matted hair: even so, in the end they must die.
So it is Ram who should be served.
One who has Ram's Name on the tongue and love (for it within): what can Jam do to him?
(Those who) know the Shastras, the Vedas, astrology and grammars by the score,
(who) know all the tantras, mantras and medicines: even so, in the end they must die.
(Those who enjoy) the pleasures of kingship, the royal canopy and the throne, many beautiful women,
betel, camphor and fragrant sandalwood: even so, in the end they must die.
I have searched the Vedas, the Puranas and the Simritis, all of them: nowhere (in them) is there escape.
Says Kabir: so I repeat (the Name of) Ram, who wipes out birth and death. ॥4॥
477.1: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The elephant plays the rebab, the ox plays the pakhavaj, the crow beats the cymbals;
putting on a dancer's robe the donkey dances, and the he-buffalo sings the songs of devotion.
The Sovereign Ram has cooked fritters of frost;
some rare one of understanding (alone) has eaten them.
Sitting at home the lion prepares betel leaves, and the bandicoot brings the folded betel;
in house after house the mice sing songs of joy, and the tortoise blows the conch.
The son of the barren woman sets out to be wed, and canopies of gold are spread;
(he) has wedded a maiden lovely in form, and the hare and the lion have sung (the couple's) praises.
Says Kabir: listen, O Sants: the ant has eaten up the mountain;
the tortoise says: I want a burning coal as well. (Thus) has this Shabad of hidden meaning been told. ॥4॥
477.2: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
(One whose) pouch is the One (Name), whose bag is the body of seventy-two (channels), the bag that has a single door,
(who) begs (for the Name) in the land of nine regions (the body itself): that yogi is the most excellent in the world.
Such a yogi obtains the nine treasures;
he takes the Brahm (the soul) that lies below (in Maya) and raises it to the Gagan.
Making wisdom his patched coat and meditation the needle, he twists the thread of the Shabad and puts it through;
making (the body of) the five elements his deerskin seat, he walks on the Guru's path.
Making compassion his ash-scraper and the body his fire-pit, he kindles the fire of (true) vision;
he keeps love for him within his heart, and stays absorbed in trance through all four ages.
All yoga is the Name of Ram, whose are the body and the breath of life.
Says Kabir: if (God) shows mercy, he grants the true mark. ॥4॥
477.3: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Where have the Hindu and the Turk (Muslim) come from? Who set these ways going?
Think it over in your heart and reflect, you wrangler: who has won heaven, and who hell?
O Qazi, which Kateb is it that you expound?
All such readers and ponderers as you have come to ruin; none has gained (true) understanding.
It is for love of woman that circumcision is done; I will not accept (it), brother.
If God had meant to make me a Turk, O brother, (my circumcision) would have come about of itself.
If one becomes a Turk by being circumcised, what is to be done about a woman?
The wife, who shares half a man's body, does not leave his side; so one had best remain a Hindu.
Leave (your arguments over) the Kateb and remember Ram, you crazed one: you are doing grievous wrong.
Kabir has taken hold of Ram's support; the Turks have worn themselves out (in argument) and lost. ॥4॥
477.4: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
As long as there is oil in the lamp and a wick in its mouth, everything can be seen;
when the oil has burnt away the wick goes out, and the house becomes empty.
O crazed one, (then) no one will keep you (in the house) even for a moment;
repeat the Name of that Ram (who stands by you).
Tell me, whose mother is she, whose father is he, which man's wife is she?
When the pot (of the body) breaks, no one asks after (you); there is only: take him out, take him out.
Sitting at the threshold the mother weeps; the brothers have taken up the bier and gone;
her hair let loose, the wife weeps; (but) the swan (the soul) goes alone.
Says Kabir: listen, O Sants, about the terrifying world-ocean:
cruel suffering falls on this man's head, and Jam does not turn away, O Lord of the world.
478.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, Chaupade Iktuke of Sri Kabir Ji.
Sanak and Sanand did not find (God's) end;
reading and reading the Vedas, Brahma wasted his life.
Churn the churning of the Lord, O my brother;
churn in Sahaj, so that the essence (the butter) is not lost.
Make the body the churning pot, and the mind within it the churning staff;
into this pot put the Shabad (as the culture that sets the milk).
The churning of the Lord is the mind's reflection (on him);
by the Guru's grace one obtains the stream of Amrit.
Says Kabir: if the King (God) casts his glance of grace,
then, holding to Ram's Name, one reaches the far shore. ॥4॥
478.2: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The wick has dried up, the oil is spent;
the drum does not sound, the actor has lain down to sleep.
The fire has gone out, no smoke rises;
the One alone pervades all, there is no other.
The string has snapped, the rebab does not play,
(the rebab through which) one went astray and spoiled one's own work.
The telling, the speaking, the saying and the getting said:
when understanding dawned, the singing (of these) was forgotten.
Says Kabir: those who crush the five (passions),
from them the supreme state is not far. ॥4॥
478.3: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
However many wrongs a son commits,
his mother keeps none of them in her mind.
O dear Ram, I am your child;
why do you not destroy my faults?
Even if (the child), in great anger, rushes at her again and again,
even then the mother does not keep it in mind.
My mind is caught in the whirl of worry;
without (your) Name, how will it cross over?
Give (this) body a pure understanding for ever,
that Kabir may dwell on (your) virtues, steadily, in Sahaj. ॥4॥
478.4: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
My Hajj, my bank of the Gomti, (is the place)
where the Lord, the Pir in yellow robes, dwells.
How beautiful the praise, Waah Waah, that (my mind) sings!
The Lord's Name is dear to my mind.
beside (him) sits the Lady Kavla (Lakshmi) as his maidservant.
My rosary at the neck is Ram on my tongue;
uttering (his) thousand names over and over, I offer (him) my salaam.
Says Kabir: I sing Ram's praises,
and teach (this) to both Hindu and Turk. ॥4॥
479.1: Raag Asa, nine Panchpade of Sri Kabir Ji, five of them Dutuke.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The gardener woman plucks leaves, (but) in every leaf there is life;
the stone for which she plucks the leaves, that stone is lifeless.
Thus the gardener woman has gone astray:
the True Guru is the deity who is awake.
The leaves are Brahma, the branch Vishnu, the flowers Shankar (Shiva);
you break off the three gods before your eyes: whose service, then, do you do?
Carving the stone, (the sculptor) made the idol, setting his foot on its chest;
if this idol is true, let it devour the one who carved it.
Rice, lentils, lapsi and crisp kasar:
the eater (the priest) has eaten them; this idol gets ashes in its mouth.
The gardener woman has gone astray, the world has gone astray, (but) I have not gone astray;
says Kabir: Ram, the Lord King, has kept me (from it) in his mercy. ॥5॥
479.2: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Twelve years passed in childhood; for twenty years (more) he did no austerity at all;
for thirty years he did no worship of God at all; then, grown old, he repented.
Crying mine, mine, (his) life has gone;
the ocean (of the body) has dried up, and the arms have lost their strength.
He builds a bank in a dried-up pool, and with his own hands fences a field already reaped;
the thief (death) came and at once carried off what the fool goes about guarding as his own.
Feet, head and hands have begun to tremble; water flows from the eyes unchecked;
no clear word comes from the tongue: and then, O brother, he hopes to practise dharma!
(On whom) the Lord shows mercy, him he attunes (to himself), and he earns the profit of the Name of the Lord, Har Har;
by the Guru's grace he found the Lord's wealth, which went with him when at the last he departed.
Says Kabir: listen, O Sants: no one has taken any other wealth along;
when the summons of Gopal, the King, came, (each) left wealth and mansions and went. ॥5॥
479.3: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
To some (the Lord) has given silks and silken robes, to some beds woven with cotton tape;
some have not even a rotten patched quilt, and in some homes (there is only) straw.
Do not envy and quarrel, O mind;
keep doing good deeds, and so earn (what you would have), O mind.
The potter kneaded one and the same clay, and gave (the pots) colours of many kinds;
in some he has set pearls and strings of pearls, and to some he has fastened sickness.
To the miser wealth is given to keep; the fool says the wealth is his;
when the rod of Jam strikes the head, in a moment (Jam) settles (the account).
The Lord's servant is called the highest devotee; obeying (his) command he finds peace;
whatever pleases him (the Lord), he accepts as true, and he enshrines (his) will in his mind.
Says Kabir: listen, O Sants: (the cry of) mine, mine, is false;
(death) tears open the cage and carries off the sparrow, and its little water pot and feeding cup are left behind. ॥5॥
480.1: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
We are humble servants of God; you (O Qazi) love power in your mind.
Allah, the First, the Master of the faith, does not command force (on anyone).
O Qazi, what you say does not become (you).
One keeps the roza, offers the namaz and recites the kalma, (yet by these) paradise is not won;
seventy Kaabas are within the heart itself, if only one knows it.
That is namaz, when one weighs (what is) justice; (that is) the kalma, when one knows (God) through understanding;
(when) he subdues the five (passions), he spreads the prayer mat, and then he recognises the faith.
Know the Master, keep compassion in your heart, and kill your pride, holding it worthless;
when one comes to know himself and (so) knows others, then he gains a share in paradise.
The clay is one, taking on many guises; in them (the one who knows) has recognised Brahm (God).
Says Kabir: (O Qazi,) leaving paradise, your mind has taken to hell. ॥5॥
480.2: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
In the city of the Gagan not one drop rains (now); where has the sound (nad) that was there merged?
Has the supreme swan (the soul) departed, taking with it the Supreme Lord, the Supreme God, Madho (who dwelt within)?
O Baba, where have they gone, who used to speak and who lived with the body,
who danced in awareness, and told tales and talked?
Where has the player gone, who made this mandar (the body, his drum)?
No saying, no word, no awareness arises (now); (death) has drawn out all the vital light.
Your companions, the ears, have grown feeble; the strength of the senses is spent;
the feet have stopped, the hands have fallen limp, no word comes from the mouth.
Worn out are the five enemies, all the thieves who roamed each after its own (pleasures);
worn out is the elephant of the mind, worn out the heart, that moved about holding the thread of (the soul's) light.
(All of them) have died, the ten fastenings have come loose, friends and brothers are all left behind;
says Kabir: whoever meditates on the Lord breaks his bonds while still alive. ॥5॥
480.3: Raag Asa, four Iktuke of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
No one has more strength than the she-serpent (Maya),
who beguiled (even) Brahma, Vishnu and Mahadev (Shiva).
Striking and killing, the she-serpent has entered even the pure water;
she who has stung the three worlds, by the Guru's grace I have seen (for what she is).
Why do you keep crying she-serpent, she-serpent, O brother?
Whoever has recognised the True One has devoured the she-serpent.
Nothing else is as hollow as the she-serpent;
when the she-serpent is conquered, what can poor Jam do?
This she-serpent is of his (the Lord's) making;
what strength or weakness can come from her (of herself)?
While she dwells (in the mind), (the soul) dwells in bodies (again and again);
by the Guru's grace Kabir has crossed over in Sahaj. ॥5॥
481.1: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
What (use) is it to recite the Simritis to a dog?
What (use) is it to sing the Lord's praises before a Saakat?
Let us dwell on Ram, Ram, Ram, and stay absorbed (in him);
(but) never, even by mistake, should we speak (of him) to a Saakat.
What (use) is it to feed camphor to a crow?
What (use) is it to give a snake milk to drink?
Meeting the Sat Sangat, discerning understanding arises;
touching the philosopher's stone, that same iron becomes gold.
The Saakat, like the dog, does all that he is made to do;
he does the deeds that were written (for him) from the beginning.
Though one takes Amrit again and again to water the neem,
says Kabir: its nature does not go. ॥5॥
481.2: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
A fort like Lanka, a moat like the ocean:
of that Ravan's house no trace is found.
What shall I ask for? Nothing stays fixed;
before my eyes the world is passing away.
