A hundred thousand sons and a hundred and twenty-five thousand grandsons:
in that Ravan's house there is no lamp, no wick.
He whose kitchen the moon and the sun kept heated,
whose clothes the fire washed, (he too did not last).
One who through the Guru's teaching makes (his mind) dwell in Ram's Name
stays steadfast, and does not go anywhere.
without Ram's Name there is no liberation. ॥5॥
481.3: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
First (came) the son, after him the mother;
the guru has fallen at the feet of the disciple.
Listen to one wonder, O brothers:
before (our) eyes a lion is herding cows.
The fish of the water has given birth in a tree;
before (our) eyes the cat has carried off the dog.
The branches, O brother, are below, the root above;
on its trunk fruits and flowers have grown.
Riding a horse, the buffalo goes to graze (it);
the bullock is outside, (while) its load has come home.
Says Kabir: whoever understands this verse,
dwelling on Ram, comes to see everything clearly.
481.4: Raag Asa, eight Tipade of Sri Kabir Ji, seven of them Dutuke and one an Iktuka.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
He who made the body from a drop and kept it (safe) in the pit of fire (of the womb),
kept (you) ten months in the mother's belly; then (once you were born) Maya clung (to you).
O mortal, why have you clung to greed and lost the jewel of (human) birth?
In the field of deeds (this body), won by (the deeds of) a past birth, you have not sown the seed (of the Name).
From a child you have grown old; what was to happen has happened;
when Jam comes and seizes you by the hair, why weep then?
You hope to live (on), while Jam watches your breaths;
the world is a juggler's show: O Kabir, remember (the Lord), and cast that die. ॥3॥
482.1: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Making my body the dyer's vat, I shall dye my mind with virtues; the five elements (in their good qualities) are my wedding guests;
I shall take the wedding rounds with Ram, the King; my soul is dyed in his love.
Sing, sing, O brides, the songs of joy:
Ram, the King, my Husband, has come to my house.
In the lotus of the navel I have set up the wedding altar, and the knowledge of God is recited (as the wedding hymn);
I have found such a groom as Ram, the King: so great is my good fortune.
Godly men and sages have come to see the wonder, the three hundred and thirty million (gods) in their sky-chariots;
says Kabir: the one Husband, God, has married me and is taking me away. ॥3॥
482.2: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
I am tormented by my mother-in-law, dear to my father-in-law, and I fear the very name of my husband's elder brother, O brother;
O friends and companions, my husband's sister holds me fast, and I burn, parted from my husband's younger brother.
My mind has gone mad, I have forgotten Ram: how shall I live my life, O brother?
(My Husband Lord) dwells on my bed, (yet) I do not see him with my eyes: to whom shall I tell this pain, O brother?
My stepfather quarrels (with me), and I am ever drunk with Maya;
when I was with my elder brother, then I was dear to my Husband.
Says Kabir: (all are caught in) the quarrel with the five (passions); quarrelling, (people) have wasted their lives;
the whole world is bound by false Maya; (but) dwelling on Ram, I have found peace. ॥3॥
482.3: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
In my house is thread, which I stretch into the warp every day; round your neck is the sacred thread.
You, for your part, read the Vedas and the Gayatri; Gobind is in my heart.
On my tongue is Bisan (Vishnu), in my eyes Narayan, and in my heart dwells Gobind.
When Mukand (the giver of liberation) questions you at Jam's door, what answer will you give then, you crazed one?
We are the cows and you our masters, the herdsmen, our keepers birth after birth;
(yet) you have never taken us across the river to graze: what kind of masters are you?
You are a Brahmin and I a weaver of Kashi; grasp what I have understood:
you go begging from kings, the lords of the earth, while my mind is fixed on the Lord. ॥3॥
482.4: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Life in the world is like a dream; life is the same as a dream.
(Yet) taking it for true, we have tied it in our knot, letting go the supreme treasure.
O Baba, (we) have given our love and attachment to Maya,
which has robbed (us) of the jewel of wisdom.
Seeing (the flame) with its eyes, the moth is caught; the foolish creature does not see the fire.
(So) the fool, clinging to gold and woman, gives no thought to the noose of death.
Reflect, and cast off your vices: he is the ship that carries (beings) across.
Says Kabir: such is the Life of the world that there is no second (like him). ॥3॥
482.5: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Many were the forms (births) I took, but now there will be no form again.
The thread, the string and all the gear are worn out; (my mind) has come under the sway of Ram's Name.
Now dancing comes no more to me;
my mind does not beat the drum.
Lust, anger and Maya I have burnt away; the pitcher of craving has burst.
The robe of lust has grown old; doubt is gone, and all of it is left behind.
I have known all beings as one; disputes and quarrels are over.
Says Kabir: I have found the Perfect One; Ram has shown his grace. ॥3॥
483.1: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
(The Qazi) keeps the roza, seeks to please Allah, and for his palate's sake kills living beings;
he looks to himself and not to others: why does he toil in vain?
O Qazi, your one Master is within you, yet you do not ponder and look.
You take no heed, you who are crazed by your creed; and so your life counts for nothing.
The Kateb say that Allah is true, and is neither woman nor man.
Reading and pondering are of no avail, O crazed one, if there is no awareness in the heart.
Allah is hidden within every body; reflect on this in your heart.
In both, Hindu and Muslim, is the One alone: Kabir proclaims it aloud. ॥3॥
483.2: Raag Asa, a Tipada Iktuka of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
I adorned myself to meet (my Husband),
but Hari, the Life of the world, the Lord of the world, has not met me.
Hari is my Husband, I am Hari's young bride;
Ram is great, and I a tiny little girl.
Bride and Husband dwell together in one place;
the bed is one, but meeting is hard.
Blessed is the wedded bride who is pleasing to her Beloved;
says Kabir: she does not come into birth again. ॥3॥
483.3: Raag Asa, Dupade of Sri Kabir Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
When the diamond (the soul) has pierced the Diamond (God), the mind, restless as the wind, stays merged in Sahaj;
this Diamond has pierced every light (every being): through the True Guru's words I have come to know (it).
Through the Lord's praise, the unstruck (Anahad) Bani,
(the soul) becomes a swan and recognises the Diamond.
Says Kabir: I have seen such a Diamond, pervading the world;
the hidden Diamond became manifest when the Guru who has reached him showed (him) to me. ॥2॥
483.4: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The first (bride) was ugly, of ill breeding and of evil ways, bad in her husband's home and bad in her parents'.
The present one is beautiful, wise and of good ways; in Sahaj I have kept her within me.
It is well that my first wedded one has died;
may the one I hold now live age after age.
Says Kabir: when the younger came, the elder lost her married fortune;
the younger now stays with me, and the elder has found another. ॥2॥
484.1: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
My young bride was named Dhania (the wealthy one);
(the holy men) have taken her and named her Ramjania (Ram's handmaid).
These shaven-headed (holy men) have laid my house waste;
they have set (my) little son to repeating Ram's Name.
Says Kabir: listen, O my mother:
these shaven-headed ones have made me lose my caste. ॥2॥
484.2: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Stop, stop, O young bride, do not draw your veil;
at the end you will not get even half (a damri).
Those before you went (from here) with their veils drawn;
take care that their way does not cling to you.
This is all the honour the veil brings:
for ten days or five, (people say) a fine bride has come.
Your veil is true only then,
if, singing the Lord's praises, you leap and dance.
Says Kabir: the bride wins only then,
when her life passes in singing the Lord's praises. ॥4॥
484.3: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Better the saw than your turning your back (on me);
hold me to your heart, hear my plea.
I am a sacrifice to you: turn your face (to me), Beloved;
why do you kill me by turning your back on me?
Even if you cleave my body, I will not draw back a limb;
even if my body falls, I will not break my love.
Between you and me there is no gap;
you are that Husband, and I that wife.
now I put no trust in you. ॥4॥
484.4: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
No one has known the secret of the Weaver,
who has brought forth the whole world and stretched it as his warp.
While you (pandits) were listening to the Vedas and the Puranas,
in that time I stretched out this little warp.
He has made the earth and the sky his loom-comb;
the moon and the sun he has set going side by side, two shuttles.
With the pair of treadles he has made one play; in that Weaver the weaver's mind is content.
The weaver has recognised his own home, and known Ram within his heart.
Says Kabir: when he breaks the loom-comb,
the Weaver blends thread into thread. ॥4॥
484.5: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
If one with filth within bathes at places of pilgrimage, he shall not go to Baikunth (heaven).
Nothing comes of satisfying people: Ram is not ignorant.
Worship Ram alone, the one divine Lord;
the true bath is service to the Guru.
If liberation came by dipping in water, frogs bathe day after day;
as are the frogs, so are those men: again and again they come into birth.
One hard of heart who dies at Banaras cannot be spared hell;
if the Lord's saint dies in Haramb (the barren land of Magahar), he carries all the people across.
Where there is no day and no night, no Veda and no Shastra, there dwells the Formless Lord.
Says Kabir: meditate on him, O men, O crazed world. ॥4॥
485.1: Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Raag Asa, the hymn of Sri Namdev Ji.
The One, in many (forms), is pervading and filling all; wherever I look, there is he.
(Beings are) bewitched by the many-coloured pictures of Maya; rare is the one who understands.
All is Gobind, all is Gobind; without Gobind there is nothing.
As on a single thread are strung beads by the hundred and the thousand, so God is woven through (all), warp and weft.
The waves, the foam and the bubbles of water are not apart from the water;
this world is the play of the Supreme Lord: on reflection, it is not other (than him).
False doubt and dream-like desires (men) have taken for true things.
The Guru taught (me) a mind set on good; on waking, my mind was convinced.
Says Namdev: look at the Lord's creation, reflecting on it in your heart:
within every heart, and evenly in all, is the one Murari alone. ॥4॥
485.2: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
I brought a pitcher and had it filled with water, to bathe the Thakur (the image of the Lord);
in the water live forty-two lakh beings; Bithal was (already) there: what should I do it for?
Wherever I go, there is Bithal,
ever at play in supreme bliss.
I brought flowers and strung a garland, to worship the Thakur;
the bumblebee has taken their fragrance first; Bithal was (already) there: what should I do it for?
I brought milk and had kheer cooked, to offer as food to the Thakur;
the calf has first made the milk his leavings; Bithal was (already) there: what should I do it for?
Below is Bithal, above is Bithal; without Bithal there is no world.
In every place and between places, prays Nama, you are filling all the earth. ॥4॥
485.3: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
My mind is the yardstick, my tongue the scissors;
measuring and measuring, I cut Jam's noose.
What would I do with caste? what with lineage?
I repeat the Name of Ram day and night.
I dye in the dyeing vat, I sew the seams;
without Ram's Name I do not live a ghari.
I worship in devotion, I sing the Lord's praises;
at all hours I meditate on my Master.
The needle is of gold, the thread of silver;
Nama's mind is attached to the Lord. ॥4॥
485.4: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
The snake sheds its slough, but does not shed its poison;
as the heron stands in the water, fixed in meditation.
while one's own mind is not pure?
The man who knows the lion's way of food (a living got by violence),
such a one is called the god of cheats.
Nama's Master has put an end to (his) strife:
drink the elixir of Ram, O stone-hearted one. ॥3॥
486.1: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
Those who come to know the Supreme Lord have no liking for (other) hopes;
Ram keeps free of care the minds of the devotees who have kept him in mind.
O mind, how will you swim across? The world-ocean is full of the water of the pleasures of the senses.
Seeing false Maya, O mind, you have gone astray.
(God) gave (me) birth in a calico printer's home, (yet) the Guru's teaching came to (me);
by the grace of the Sants, Nama has met the Lord. ॥2॥
486.2: Raag Asa, the hymn of Sri Ravidas Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The deer, the fish, the bumblebee, the moth and the elephant are each destroyed by a single failing;
how much hope (of escape) is there, then, for one in whom are five failings that cannot be subdued?
O Madho, (man) has given his love to ignorance;
(so) the lamp of (his) discernment is clouded.
The creatures of the species that move crookedly are without thought; for them to give no thought to good deeds and sins is natural;
(but) human birth is hard to come by, and still its company is with the low (vices).
Wherever beings and creatures go (to be born), in the power of their deeds,
death's noose, which cannot be cut, is upon them; no remedy avails.
O servant Ravidas, turn away (from vice) and give up doubt; the Guru's wisdom is the austerity of austerities.
O remover of your devotees' fears, grant (me) supreme bliss at the last. ॥4॥
486.3: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji.
(O God,) the Sants are your own form, and their fellowship is your life;
through the True Guru's wisdom one comes to know the Sants (as such), O God of gods.
The company of the Sants, the relish of the Sants' discourse (of God),
and love for the Sants: give (these) to me, O God of gods.
(Give me too) the conduct of the Sants, the path of the Sants, and service to the servants of the Sants.
One thing more I ask: devotion, the wish-fulfilling jewel (Chintamani);
do not let me set eyes on the unholy and the sinners.
Says Ravidas: the one who knows (this) is the one who truly knows:
the Sants and the Infinite One are not apart. ॥4॥
486.4: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji.
You are sandalwood, we are the lowly castor plant, (yet we have) a dwelling beside you;
from a lowly tree we have been raised high; (your) scent, a sweet scent, has come to dwell (in us).
O Madho, (I have taken) the refuge of your Sat Sangat;
we are full of faults, you are the doer of good.
You are silk, white and yellow; we are like wretched worms;
O Madho, may we stay joined to the Sat Sangat, as honeybees to the comb.
Low in caste, low in lineage, low is my birth;
and I have not served Ram, the Sovereign Lord, says Ravidas the Chamar (of the leather-working caste). ॥3॥
486.5: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji.
What does it matter if (my) body falls to pieces?
Only if love should go does your servant fear.
(O God,) your lotus feet are the dwelling of (my) mind;
drinking (their nectar), I have found, yes found, the wealth of beloved Ram.
Prosperity, adversity and wealth are the veils of Maya;
your servant is not lost in them.
Your servant is bound with the rope of (your) love;
says Ravidas: what good would there be in getting free (of it)? ॥3॥
487.1: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji.
Har, Har, Har, Har, Har, Har, Har:
remembering the Lord, (his) servants have crossed over, wholly saved.
Through the Lord's Name Kabir became renowned,
and the papers (of the accounts) of birth after birth were torn up.
By virtue of it Namdev gave (the Lord) milk to drink,
and so he did not come into the pains of birth in the world.
The servant Ravidas is dyed in the love of Ram;
so, through the Guru's grace, he does not go to hell.
See how this puppet of clay dances!
It looks and looks about, listens, speaks, and runs here and there.
When it gains something, it grows proud;
when Maya is gone, it begins to weep.
In mind, word and deed it is lured by tastes, sweet and sharp;
when it perishes, (the soul) goes and is absorbed somewhere (else).
Says Ravidas: the world is (a juggler's) show, O brother;
my love has been formed with the Juggler (who stages it). ॥3॥
487.2: Raag Asa, the hymn of Bhagat Dhanna Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Wandering and roaming, many births have gone by; body, mind and wealth never hold steady.
Steeped in greed, poison and lust, the greedy one has let God, the diamond, slip from his mind.
The poison fruits tasted sweet (to you), O crazed mind, and you knew nothing of noble reflection;
love of other kinds grew, away from virtue, and the warp of birth and death was stretched again.
Knowing the way (to live), you did not settle it in your heart; burning (in craving), you have fallen into Jam's net and noose.
O mind, you gathered and stored poison fruits so (much) that God, the Supreme Being, slipped from the mind.
(Those to whom) the Guru gave the wealth of entry into knowledge, their attention, faith and mind became one (with God);
they embraced loving devotion, came to know peace, and, filled and fully content, were set free.
The one in whom (God's) all-pervading Light has merged has recognised God, who cannot be deceived.
Dhanna has gained the wealth, the Upholder of the earth (Dharnidhar); meeting the humble Sants, he has merged (in him). ॥4॥
487.3: By the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Namdev's mind was absorbed in Gobind, Gobind, Gobind;
the poor calico printer, worth half a dam (a copper coin), came to be worth lakhs.
Leaving his weaving and warping, Kabir turned his love to (the Lord's) feet;
the humble weaver of a low family became an ocean of virtue.
Ravidas used to carry (dead) cattle every day; he gave up Maya,
grew renowned in the Saadh Sangat, and was granted the sight of the Lord.
Sain the barber, who ran errands (for people), came to be known in every house;
the Supreme Lord came to live in his heart, and he was numbered among the devotees.
Hearing of this, the humble Jatt (Dhanna) rose and set himself to devotion;
the Lord of the world met him face to face; most fortunate was Dhanna. ॥4॥
488.1: O my mind, why do you not remember the merciful Damodar? Know no other (as your support).
Though you run through the lands of the universe, that alone comes about which the Creator does.
In the mother's womb, in its water, he made the body with its ten doors;
giving it food, he keeps it (safe) in the fire (of the womb): such is our Master.
The she-turtle lives in the water, her young outside it; they have no wings, and (she has) no milk (for them);
(yet) the Perfect One, Supreme Bliss, the Enchanter of hearts, (cares for them): understand and see this in your mind.
A worm lies hidden inside a stone, with no way out for it;
says Dhanna: it too is in the care of the Perfect One; have no fear, O soul. ॥3॥
488.2: Raag Asa, the hymn of Sheikh Farid Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Those whose love (for God) is from the heart are the true (lovers);
those with one thing in their mind and another on their lips are called raw (in love).
(Those) steeped in the love of God (Khuda) are dyed in the colour of his sight;
those who have forgotten the Name have become a burden on the earth.
Those whom (God) has himself attached to his hem are the dervishes at (his) door;
blessed is the mother who bore them; their coming (into the world) bears fruit.
O Sustainer, you are boundless, beyond reach, without end.
Those who have known the True One: I kiss their feet.
Your shelter (is mine), O God; you are the Forgiver;
grant Sheikh Farid the alms of (your) worship (bandagi). ॥4॥
488.3: Raag Asa, the hymn of Sheikh Farid Ji.
Says Sheikh Farid: O dear one, hold fast to Allah;
this body will become dust in its humble home, the grave.
Union (with God) can be today, O Sheikh Farid, if the little cranes (the senses) that inflame the mind are held back.
If I know that we must die and not come round again,
(then) we should not waste ourselves clinging to the false world.
Let us speak the truth, speak what is right, and speak no falsehood;
the way the Guru shows, let us walk it as his disciples.
The handsome young men cross to the far bank, and (seeing it) the fair maiden's heart takes courage;
(but) those who turned to the side of gold were cut through with the saw.
O Sheikh, in this world no one's life has lasted for ever;
on the seat where we now sit, many have sat and gone.
Cranes in Katik, forest fires in Chet, lightning in Savan,
and in winter (a wife's) arms about her husband's neck look lovely.
(So) those who must go are going; reflect on this in your mind.
Six months it takes to shape (the body), a single instant to break it.
The earth asks the sky, O Farid: where have the boatmen gone?
(The answer:) they are passing their time in the graves, and the souls are bearing the reproaches. ॥8॥
